She said: "I am an old, great woman who cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt; this is for the world. As for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into a chamber of Paradise except that I descend with you." He said: "Yes." She said: "He is in the depths of the water, in the Nile, so pray to Allah that He hold back the water from him." He prayed to Allah and He held back the water from him, and he prayed that the rising of dawn be delayed until he finished the matter of Yusuf. Musa dug at that place and extracted him in a coffer of marble, and he carried him until he buried him in al-Sham. Then the road opened for them.

They set out, with Musa at their rear and Harun at their front. Pharaoh learned of them, so he gathered his people and commanded them not to go out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night.

Pharaoh went out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand, and among them were seventy thousand of the dark-coloured horses, apart from the rest of the mixed breeds. The Children of Israel proceeded until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest rise.

They looked, and behold, there was Pharaoh, and that was when the sun rose. They remained perplexed and said: "O Musa, what shall we do? What is the way out? Pharaoh is behind us and the sea is before us." Musa said: ﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. Then He revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [26:63]. He struck it but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: "Be gentle with it," so Musa struck it with his staff and said: "Split, Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah." ﴿So it split, and each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [26:63]. And there appeared in it twelve paths, one path for each tribe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Mu'awiya sent to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about a place where the sun had risen only once. He wrote back to him: "It is the place from which the sea split for the Children of Israel." [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 8/334, which mentions the remainder of the story.]

The Children of Israel plunged into the sea, each tribe in its own path, and on either side of them the water was like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were frightened, and each tribe said: "Our brothers have all drowned." So Allah revealed to the state of the water: "Become interlaced," and the water became like latticed windows so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We divided the sea for you﴾, that is, We said, and We separated the water to the right and to the left.

﴿And We saved you﴾ from the people of Pharaoh and from drowning.

﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾. This is because Pharaoh, when he reached the sea and saw it split, said to his people: "Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my enemies and my slaves who ran away, and kill them. Enter the sea!" His people were afraid to enter it, and there was no female horse among Pharaoh's horses; they were all males. So Jibril, peace be upon him, came on a female horse in heat and went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When the horses smelled her scent, they rushed into the sea after her until they all plunged into the sea. Mikail came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and saying to them: "Catch up with your companions!" When Jibril came out of the sea and the first of them was about to come out, Allah, Exalted, commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them, and He drowned them all, and that was in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾.

﴿And you were looking on﴾ at their fate.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa forty nights﴾. This is because when the Children of Israel felt safe from their enemy and entered Egypt, they had no book or law to which they could refer, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised Musa that He would send down the Torah to them. Musa said to his people: "I am going to the appointed time of my Lord, and I will bring you a book containing the explanation of what you should do and what you should avoid." So he appointed them forty nights, thirty of Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, and he appointed his brother Harun as his successor over them.

When the promised time came, Jibril came on a horse called the horse of life, which does not touch anything without it coming to life, to take Musa to his Lord. When al-Samiri saw him, and he was a goldsmith from the people of Bajaro, whose name was Mikha (and Ibn 'Abbas said: his name was Musa ibn Zafar; he was a hypocrite who had outwardly embraced Islam, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, so the love of cows had entered his heart), when he saw Jibril on that horse, he said: "This has a matter." He took a handful of the dust from the hoof-print of Jibril's horse. The Children of Israel had borrowed a great deal of ornaments from the people of Pharaoh when they wanted to leave Egypt, for a festival of theirs, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed the people of Pharaoh, so those ornaments remained in the hands of the Children of Israel. When Musa arrived, al-Samiri said: "The goods and ornaments you borrowed from the people of Pharaoh are spoils of war, and they are not lawful for you. Dig a pit and bury them in it until Musa returns, and he will see his opinion regarding them." They did that.

When the ornaments were gathered, al-Samiri fashioned them, then he threw into them the handful he had taken from the dust of Jibril's horse, and there came out a calf of gold, set with jewels, as beautiful as could be, and it lowed a lowing. Al-Suddi said: It used to low and walk, [and say:] ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾ [20:88], that is, he left it here and went out to seek him.

The Children of Israel had broken the promise, so they counted a day and a night as two days. When twenty days had passed and Musa, peace be upon him, had not returned, and they saw the calf and heard the words of al-Samiri, eight thousand men among them were seduced by the calf, and they clung to it, worshipping it besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa﴾: Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub recited "wa'adnā" without an alif throughout the Qur'an, and the rest recited "wā'adnā" with an alif, and this is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. Whoever recited without an alif said: because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the sole one who makes the promise, and the Qur'an speaks of it thus, as in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised﴾ [4:95], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise﴾ [14:22]. Whoever recited with an alif said: "The form of mufā'ala (mutual action) may come from one party, as in their saying: 'I punished the thief,' 'May Allah grant you well-being,' and 'I struck the sandal.'"

Al-Zajjaj said: "wā'adnā" is good, because acceptance and obedience stand in the position of mutual promising; so the promise is from Allah and the acceptance is from Musa.

Musa: he is Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Yasahar ibn Qahat ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub.

﴿Forty nights﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited "arbi'īn" with a kasra on the bā', and this is a dialect form, and "laylatan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz) and explanation. Time was linked to the night rather than the day because the months of the Arabs were set by the course of the moon, and the crescent appears at night. It was also said that darkness is older than light, and night was created before day. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ [36:37], and so on.

﴿Then you took the calf﴾. Abu al-'Aliya said: It was named "the calf" because they hastened (ta'ajjalū) to it before the return of Musa, peace be upon him.

﴿After him﴾: after Musa's departure to the mountain for the appointed meeting.

﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾: harming yourselves by disobedience, and placing worship in other than its proper place.

﴿Then We pardoned you﴾: that is, We left you and did not uproot you,
from his saying, peace be upon him: "Trim the moustaches and leave the beards." It was also said: We erased your sins, from the saying of the Arabs: "The wind effaced the dwellings, so they were effaced."

﴿After that﴾: that is, after your worship of the calf.

﴿So that you might be grateful﴾: in order that you might thank My pardon of you and My kindness to you.

The scholars differed concerning the reality of gratitude (shukr). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is obedience with all the limbs to the Lord of creation, openly and secretly.

Al-Hasan said: the thanks for a blessing is to mention it. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [93:11].

Al-Fadl said: the thanks for every blessing is that Allah is not disobeyed after that blessing.

Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq: The reality of gratitude is knowing the Benefactor, and that you do not regard any share for yourself in the blessing, but see it as from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [16:53]. This is indicated by what Sayf ibn Maymun narrated from al-Husayn: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Musa, peace be upon him, said: 'O Lord, how was Adam able to render thanks for what You bestowed upon him of Your blessings? You created him with Your hand, made Your angels prostrate to him, and settled him in Your Paradise.' So Allah revealed to him: 'Adam knew that all of that is from Me and from My side, and that is his gratitude.'" [85] [Rawdat al-Wa'izin (al-Fattal al-Nisaburi): p. 473; al-Shukr li-llah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya: p. 70.]

And from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Dawud, peace be upon him, said: "My God, how can I thank You when I cannot reach Your thanks except by Your blessing?" Allah, Exalted, revealed to him: "Do you not know that the blessings you have are from Me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord." He said: "Then be content with that as your gratitude."

Wahb said: Likewise Musa said: "O Lord, You have bestowed upon me abundant blessings and commanded me to thank You for them, and my thanks for every blessing from You upon me is itself a further blessing." Allah said: "O Musa, you have learned the knowledge that no knowledge escapes. It is enough from My servant that he knows that whatever blessing he has is from Me and from My side."

Al-Junayd said: The reality of gratitude is the inability to give thanks.

It is narrated of Dawud, peace be upon him, that he said: "Glory be to Him who made the servant's acknowledgment of his inability to thank Him a form of thanks, just as He made his acknowledgment of his inability to know Him a form of knowing."

Some of them said: Gratitude is that one does not see the blessing at all, but sees the Benefactor.

Abu 'Uthman al-Khayri: The truth of gratitude is that you do not praise with your tongue anyone other than the Benefactor.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Bakr al-Razi, from al-Shibli: Gratitude is humility under the vision of the favour.

It was said: Gratitude consists of five things: keeping away from evil deeds, guarding good deeds, opposing desires, offering acts of obedience, and watching over the Lord of the heavens.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qannad was asked in the mosque, in the presence of Abu Bakr ibn 'Adus, while I was present: "Who are the most grateful of the grateful?" He said: "The one who is pure from sins, who counts himself among the sinners; the one who strives in supererogatory acts beyond the obligatory ones, and counts himself among the negligent; and the one who is content with little of this world, and counts himself among the destitute. These are the most grateful of the grateful."

Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Dhu al-Nur: Gratitude to one above you is through obedience, to your equal through reciprocation, and to one below you through kindness and bounty.

﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾. Mujahid and al-Farra' said: they are one thing, and the Arabs repeat a thing when its wording differs, out of a suspicion of difference. Al-Farra' recited:

"I offered the hide to his two forearms,
and he found her words false and deceitful."

Antara said:

"I greeted a campsite whose traces had become old,
it was effaced and emptied after Umm al-Haytham."

Al-Zajjaj said: This is the correct view, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the Criterion for Musa in another place, saying: ﴿And We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion﴾ [21:48].

Al-Kisa'i said: "al-Furqan" is an epithet for "al-Kitab," meaning: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾, which distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful, between disbelief and faith, and between promise and threat. The waw was added to it as it is added to epithets, as in the saying: "So-and-so is good and tall." He recited:

"To the king, the resolute and the son of the leader,
and the lion of the battalion in the crowd."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, completed upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [6:154].

Qutrub said: He meant by it the Criterion, and there is an implicit element in the verse, its meaning being: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and Muhammad the Criterion﴾.

﴿So that you might be guided﴾ by these two books. So one of the two names was dropped, as in the poet's saying:

"You see him as if Allah were slitting his nose,
and his eyes, if his master spends the night with him, are narrowed."

Ibn 'Abbas said: By the Criterion he meant victory over the enemies, the victory that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave Musa, and the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We sent not down upon Our servant on the day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ [8:41], which is the day of Badr.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: "al-Furqan" means the splitting of the sea, which is among the great signs, as indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and saved you﴾.

﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [as a god]. So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Rabab's remark continues: "Wronged yourselves" means you harmed yourselves by taking the calf as a god. They said: "What shall we do, and what is the remedy?" He said: "So turn in repentance, return" ﴿to your Creator﴾, meaning your Originator. Abu 'Amr would reduce the hamza, dropping the vowel to a jussive-like sukun, in His saying ﴿bari'kum﴾ and ﴿yamurukum﴾ and ﴿yansurkum﴾, seeking lightness. [That is, by eliding the vowel; it is also reported from him as sukun, while the others recited without elision.] Like the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor as one who drinks uninvited.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 10/426.]

And he recited:

*When they go crooked, I say "companion, straighten them," across the desert like swimming ships.* [Sharh Shafiyat Ibn al-Hajib: 4/225, and Lisan al-'Arab: 12/432.]

He said: ﴿So kill yourselves﴾, so that the innocent would kill the guilty. ﴿That killing is best for you in the sight of your Creator.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: God, Mighty and Majestic, refused to accept the repentance of the Children of Israel except in the state they disliked, that they fight one another when they worshipped the calf.

Qatadah said: the punishment of the calf-worshippers was killing, because they had apostatized, and disbelief makes blood lawful.

Qatadah recited: ﴿fa-aqīlū anfusakum﴾, from iqalah (seeking revocation), meaning seek to have your stumble removed through repentance. When Moses intended the killing, they said: "We submit to the command of God, Exalted is He," so they sat in the courtyards hidden, and the people unsheathed daggers against them. A man would see his son, his father, his paternal uncle, his people, his friend and his neighbor, yet they could not proceed in obedience to God's command. They said: "O Moses, how shall we act?" So God sent a mist and a black cloud, so that no one could see another. It was said to them: whoever loosens his turban, or lifts his gaze to his killer, or shields himself with a hand or foot, is struck, and his repentance is rejected. So they kept killing one another until evening. When the killing increased among them, Aaron and Moses called out, wept, grieved, humbled themselves, and said: "O Lord, the Children of Israel are being destroyed, the remnant, the remnant!" Then God, Mighty and Majestic, lifted the cloud and commanded them to lay down their weapons and cease killing.

The dead were uncovered, thousands of them, and this weighed heavily on Moses. God revealed to him: "Would it not satisfy you that I admit both the killer and the killed into Paradise? Whoever among them was killed is a martyr, and whoever remains, I will expiate his sins." This is His saying ﴿Then He accepted your repentance﴾, meaning: since you did as He commanded, He accepted your repentance and pardoned you.

﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 49–54 (part 1 of 2):

And when We saved you: that is, your forefathers and ancestors. He counted it a favour upon them because they were saved by their salvation, and the virtues of fathers are the glories of sons.

As for His saying, ﴿And We saved you﴾ [2:50]: its root is "we cast you upon al-najah," and al-najah is the high and wide part of the land. This is the original meaning. Then every one who attains success was called "najin" (one who is saved), as if he had come out of narrowness and hardship into ease and comfort.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i recited: "wa-idh najjākum" (with the single letter of the root doubled and the verb in the singular).

﴿From the people of Pharaoh﴾: that is, his partisans, followers, household, his kin, and the people of his religion. Its origin is from "al-awwal," which means return, as if it returns to you (uwwal). In origin there were two hamzas, and one of them was replaced by a long vowel (madd) and lightening.

Pharaoh: he is al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and he was from the Amalekites.

﴿They inflict upon you the worst torment﴾: that is, they impose upon you and make you taste the most severe and worst torment. This is because Pharaoh made the Children of Israel servants and slaves, and divided them according to their work. One group built, another group ploughed and planted, another group served, and whoever was not in any of these occupations had to pay the poll-tax (jizya).

﴿They slaughter your sons and let your women live﴾.

Ibn Muhaysin recited with lightening: the yā' and the bā' vowelled with fatḥa in "yudhabbihūna" (in the sense of slaughter), and the doubling (tashdid) is for intensity. This is because Pharaoh saw in his dream as if a fire came from Bayt al-Maqdis until it enveloped the houses of Egypt, burned them, burned the Copts, and left the Children of Israel. This frightened him, so he summoned the magicians and soothsayers and asked them about his dream. They said: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of your destruction, the end of your kingdom, and the change of your religion." So Pharaoh ordered the killing of every boy born among the Children of Israel, and he gathered the midwives from among the people of his kingdom and said to them: "Let no boy of the Children of Israel fall into your hands except that he is killed, and let no girl be but that she is spared." He appointed people to watch them and carry this out. Death spread among the elders of the Children of Israel, so the chiefs of the Copts entered upon Pharaoh and said to him: "Death has befallen the Children of Israel, and you are slaughtering their young, while their elders die, and soon the work will fall upon us." So Pharaoh ordered that they slaughter for one year and leave for one year. Harun was born in the year in which they did not slaughter, so he was spared, and Musa was born in the year in which they did slaughter.

﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾: in your being saved from them there was a great blessing. And the word "bala' (trial)" is used in two senses:

the blessings and the calamities [...]

[Blank in the manuscript.]

﴿And when We divided the sea for you ...﴾ [Unreadable text.]

the sea: This is because when the destruction of Pharaoh drew near, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and commanded them to keep lamps lit in their houses until morning. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought out to them every illegitimate child among the Copts who were among the Children of Israel, and He brought out [from the Children of Israel every illegitimate child among them] [Supplement from al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/84; the manuscript has a blank] to the Copts, until each one of them returned to his father. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent death upon the Copts, and every firstborn died, so they were occupied with burying them [away from pursuing them until] [Supplement from Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/396] the sun rose. Musa, peace be upon him, went out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, none of them younger than twenty or older than sixty, apart from the offspring. When they wanted to set out, the wandering (al-tih) was imposed upon them, so they did not know where to go. Musa, peace be upon him, summoned the elders of the Children of Israel and asked them about that.

They said: "When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he took a covenant from his brothers that they would not leave Egypt until they took him out with them. That is why the road was closed to us." So he asked them about the location of his grave, and they did not know.

Musa stood calling out: "I beseech Allah, whoever knows where the grave of Yusuf is, to inform me of it. And whoever does not know, let his ears be deaf to my words." He kept passing between two men calling out, and they did not hear his voice, until an old woman of theirs heard him and said: "Do you see, if I guide you to his grave, will you give me whatever I ask of you?" He refused her and said: "Until I ask my Lord." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to grant her request. She said: "I am an old, great woman who cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt; this is for the world. As for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into a chamber of Paradise except that I descend with you." He said: "Yes." She said: "He is in the depths of the water, in the Nile, so pray to Allah that He hold back the water from him." He prayed to Allah and He held back the water from him, and he prayed that the rising of dawn be delayed until he finished the matter of Yusuf. Musa dug at that place and extracted him in a coffer of marble, and he carried him until he buried him in al-Sham. Then the road opened for them.

They set out, with Musa at their rear and Harun at their front. Pharaoh learned of them, so he gathered his people and commanded them not to go out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night.

Pharaoh went out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand, and among them were seventy thousand of the dark-coloured horses, apart from the rest of the mixed breeds. The Children of Israel proceeded until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest rise.

They looked, and behold, there was Pharaoh, and that was when the sun rose. They remained perplexed and said: "O Musa, what shall we do? What is the way out? Pharaoh is behind us and the sea is before us." Musa said: ﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. Then He revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [26:63]. He struck it but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: "Be gentle with it," so Musa struck it with his staff and said: "Split, Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah." ﴿So it split, and each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [26:63]. And there appeared in it twelve paths, one path for each tribe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Mu'awiya sent to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about a place where the sun had risen only once. He wrote back to him: "It is the place from which the sea split for the Children of Israel." [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 8/334, which mentions the remainder of the story.]

The Children of Israel plunged into the sea, each tribe in its own path, and on either side of them the water was like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were frightened, and each tribe said: "Our brothers have all drowned." So Allah revealed to the state of the water: "Become interlaced," and the water became like latticed windows so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We divided the sea for you﴾, that is, We said, and We separated the water to the right and to the left.

﴿And We saved you﴾ from the people of Pharaoh and from drowning.

﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾. This is because Pharaoh, when he reached the sea and saw it split, said to his people: "Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my enemies and my slaves who ran away, and kill them. Enter the sea!" His people were afraid to enter it, and there was no female horse among Pharaoh's horses; they were all males. So Jibril, peace be upon him, came on a female horse in heat and went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When the horses smelled her scent, they rushed into the sea after her until they all plunged into the sea. Mikail came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and saying to them: "Catch up with your companions!" When Jibril came out of the sea and the first of them was about to come out, Allah, Exalted, commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them, and He drowned them all, and that was in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾.

﴿And you were looking on﴾ at their fate.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa forty nights﴾. This is because when the Children of Israel felt safe from their enemy and entered Egypt, they had no book or law to which they could refer, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised Musa that He would send down the Torah to them. Musa said to his people: "I am going to the appointed time of my Lord, and I will bring you a book containing the explanation of what you should do and what you should avoid." So he appointed them forty nights, thirty of Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, and he appointed his brother Harun as his successor over them.

When the promised time came, Jibril came on a horse called the horse of life, which does not touch anything without it coming to life, to take Musa to his Lord. When al-Samiri saw him, and he was a goldsmith from the people of Bajaro, whose name was Mikha (and Ibn 'Abbas said: his name was Musa ibn Zafar; he was a hypocrite who had outwardly embraced Islam, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, so the love of cows had entered his heart), when he saw Jibril on that horse, he said: "This has a matter." He took a handful of the dust from the hoof-print of Jibril's horse. The Children of Israel had borrowed a great deal of ornaments from the people of Pharaoh when they wanted to leave Egypt, for a festival of theirs, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed the people of Pharaoh, so those ornaments remained in the hands of the Children of Israel. When Musa arrived, al-Samiri said: "The goods and ornaments you borrowed from the people of Pharaoh are spoils of war, and they are not lawful for you. Dig a pit and bury them in it until Musa returns, and he will see his opinion regarding them." They did that.

When the ornaments were gathered, al-Samiri fashioned them, then he threw into them the handful he had taken from the dust of Jibril's horse, and there came out a calf of gold, set with jewels, as beautiful as could be, and it lowed a lowing. Al-Suddi said: It used to low and walk, [and say:] ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾ [20:88], that is, he left it here and went out to seek him.

The Children of Israel had broken the promise, so they counted a day and a night as two days. When twenty days had passed and Musa, peace be upon him, had not returned, and they saw the calf and heard the words of al-Samiri, eight thousand men among them were seduced by the calf, and they clung to it, worshipping it besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa﴾: Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub recited "wa'adnā" without an alif throughout the Qur'an, and the rest recited "wā'adnā" with an alif, and this is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. Whoever recited without an alif said: because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the sole one who makes the promise, and the Qur'an speaks of it thus, as in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised﴾ [4:95], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise﴾ [14:22]. Whoever recited with an alif said: "The form of mufā'ala (mutual action) may come from one party, as in their saying: 'I punished the thief,' 'May Allah grant you well-being,' and 'I struck the sandal.'"

Al-Zajjaj said: "wā'adnā" is good, because acceptance and obedience stand in the position of mutual promising; so the promise is from Allah and the acceptance is from Musa.

Musa: he is Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Yasahar ibn Qahat ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub.

﴿Forty nights﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited "arbi'īn" with a kasra on the bā', and this is a dialect form, and "laylatan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz) and explanation. Time was linked to the night rather than the day because the months of the Arabs were set by the course of the moon, and the crescent appears at night. It was also said that darkness is older than light, and night was created before day. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ [36:37], and so on.

﴿Then you took the calf﴾. Abu al-'Aliya said: It was named "the calf" because they hastened (ta'ajjalū) to it before the return of Musa, peace be upon him.

﴿After him﴾: after Musa's departure to the mountain for the appointed meeting.

﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾: harming yourselves by disobedience, and placing worship in other than its proper place.

﴿Then We pardoned you﴾: that is, We left you and did not uproot you,
from his saying, peace be upon him: "Trim the moustaches and leave the beards." It was also said: We erased your sins, from the saying of the Arabs: "The wind effaced the dwellings, so they were effaced."

﴿After that﴾: that is, after your worship of the calf.

﴿So that you might be grateful﴾: in order that you might thank My pardon of you and My kindness to you.

The scholars differed concerning the reality of gratitude (shukr). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is obedience with all the limbs to the Lord of creation, openly and secretly.

Al-Hasan said: the thanks for a blessing is to mention it. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [93:11].

Al-Fadl said: the thanks for every blessing is that Allah is not disobeyed after that blessing.

Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq: The reality of gratitude is knowing the Benefactor, and that you do not regard any share for yourself in the blessing, but see it as from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [16:53]. This is indicated by what Sayf ibn Maymun narrated from al-Husayn: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Musa, peace be upon him, said: 'O Lord, how was Adam able to render thanks for what You bestowed upon him of Your blessings? You created him with Your hand, made Your angels prostrate to him, and settled him in Your Paradise.' So Allah revealed to him: 'Adam knew that all of that is from Me and from My side, and that is his gratitude.'" [85] [Rawdat al-Wa'izin (al-Fattal al-Nisaburi): p. 473; al-Shukr li-llah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya: p. 70.]

And from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Dawud, peace be upon him, said: "My God, how can I thank You when I cannot reach Your thanks except by Your blessing?" Allah, Exalted, revealed to him: "Do you not know that the blessings you have are from Me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord." He said: "Then be content with that as your gratitude."

Wahb said: Likewise Musa said: "O Lord, You have bestowed upon me abundant blessings and commanded me to thank You for them, and my thanks for every blessing from You upon me is itself a further blessing." Allah said: "O Musa, you have learned the knowledge that no knowledge escapes. It is enough from My servant that he knows that whatever blessing he has is from Me and from My side."

Al-Junayd said: The reality of gratitude is the inability to give thanks.

It is narrated of Dawud, peace be upon him, that he said: "Glory be to Him who made the servant's acknowledgment of his inability to thank Him a form of thanks, just as He made his acknowledgment of his inability to know Him a form of knowing."

Some of them said: Gratitude is that one does not see the blessing at all, but sees the Benefactor.

Abu 'Uthman al-Khayri: The truth of gratitude is that you do not praise with your tongue anyone other than the Benefactor.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Bakr al-Razi, from al-Shibli: Gratitude is humility under the vision of the favour.

It was said: Gratitude consists of five things: keeping away from evil deeds, guarding good deeds, opposing desires, offering acts of obedience, and watching over the Lord of the heavens.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Qannad was asked in the mosque, in the presence of Abu Bakr ibn 'Adus, while I was present: "Who are the most grateful of the grateful?" He said: "The one who is pure from sins, who counts himself among the sinners; the one who strives in supererogatory acts beyond the obligatory ones, and counts himself among the negligent; and the one who is content with little of this world, and counts himself among the destitute. These are the most grateful of the grateful."

Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Dhu al-Nur: Gratitude to one above you is through obedience, to your equal through reciprocation, and to one below you through kindness and bounty.

﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾. Mujahid and al-Farra' said: they are one thing, and the Arabs repeat a thing when its wording differs, out of a suspicion of difference. Al-Farra' recited:

"I offered the hide to his two forearms,
and he found her words false and deceitful."

Antara said:

"I greeted a campsite whose traces had become old,
it was effaced and emptied after Umm al-Haytham."

Al-Zajjaj said: This is the correct view, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the Criterion for Musa in another place, saying: ﴿And We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion﴾ [21:48].

Al-Kisa'i said: "al-Furqan" is an epithet for "al-Kitab," meaning: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾, which distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful, between disbelief and faith, and between promise and threat. The waw was added to it as it is added to epithets, as in the saying: "So-and-so is good and tall." He recited:

"To the king, the resolute and the son of the leader,
and the lion of the battalion in the crowd."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, completed upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [6:154].

Qutrub said: He meant by it the Criterion, and there is an implicit element in the verse, its meaning being: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and Muhammad the Criterion﴾.

﴿So that you might be guided﴾ by these two books. So one of the two names was dropped, as in the poet's saying:

"You see him as if Allah were slitting his nose,
and his eyes, if his master spends the night with him, are narrowed."

Ibn 'Abbas said: By the Criterion he meant victory over the enemies, the victory that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave Musa, and the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We sent not down upon Our servant on the day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ [8:41], which is the day of Badr.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: "al-Furqan" means the splitting of the sea, which is among the great signs, as indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and saved you﴾.

﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [as a god]. So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Rabab's remark continues: "Wronged yourselves" means you harmed yourselves by taking the calf as a god. They said: "What shall we do, and what is the remedy?" He said: "So turn in repentance, return" ﴿to your Creator﴾, meaning your Originator. Abu 'Amr would reduce the hamza, dropping the vowel to a jussive-like sukun, in His saying ﴿bari'kum﴾ and ﴿yamurukum﴾ and ﴿yansurkum﴾, seeking lightness. [That is, by eliding the vowel; it is also reported from him as sukun, while the others recited without elision.] Like the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor as one who drinks uninvited.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 10/426.]

And he recited:

*When they go crooked, I say "companion, straighten them," across the desert like swimming ships.* [Sharh Shafiyat Ibn al-Hajib: 4/225, and Lisan al-'Arab: 12/432.]

He said: ﴿So kill yourselves﴾, so that the innocent would kill the guilty. ﴿That killing is best for you in the sight of your Creator.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: God, Mighty and Majestic, refused to accept the repentance of the Children of Israel except in the state they disliked, that they fight one another when they worshipped the calf.

Qatadah said: the punishment of the calf-worshippers was killing, because they had apostatized, and disbelief makes blood lawful.

Qatadah recited: ﴿fa-aqīlū anfusakum﴾, from iqalah (seeking revocation), meaning seek to have your stumble removed through repentance. When Moses intended the killing, they said: "We submit to the command of God, Exalted is He," so they sat in the courtyards hidden, and the people unsheathed daggers against them. A man would see his son, his father, his paternal uncle, his people, his friend and his neighbor, yet they could not proceed in obedience to God's command. They said: "O Moses, how shall we act?" So God sent a mist and a black cloud, so that no one could see another. It was said to them: whoever loosens his turban, or lifts his gaze to his killer, or shields himself with a hand or foot, is struck, and his repentance is rejected. So they kept killing one another until evening. When the killing increased among them, Aaron and Moses called out, wept, grieved, humbled themselves, and said: "O Lord, the Children of Israel are being destroyed, the remnant, the remnant!" Then God, Mighty and Majestic, lifted the cloud and commanded them to lay down their weapons and cease killing.

The dead were uncovered, thousands of them, and this weighed heavily on Moses. God revealed to him: "Would it not satisfy you that I admit both the killer and the killed into Paradise? Whoever among them was killed is a martyr, and whoever remains, I will expiate his sins." This is His saying ﴿Then He accepted your repentance﴾, meaning: since you did as He commanded, He accepted your repentance and pardoned you.

﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 49–54 (part 1 of 2):

And when We saved you: that is, your forefathers and ancestors. He counted it a favour upon them because they were saved by their salvation, and the virtues of fathers are the glories of sons.

As for His saying, ﴿And We saved you﴾ [2:50]: its root is "we cast you upon al-najah," and al-najah is the high and wide part of the land. This is the original meaning. Then every one who attains success was called "najin" (one who is saved), as if he had come out of narrowness and hardship into ease and comfort.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i recited: "wa-idh najjākum" (with the single letter of the root doubled and the verb in the singular).

﴿From the people of Pharaoh﴾: that is, his partisans, followers, household, his kin, and the people of his religion. Its origin is from "al-awwal," which means return, as if it returns to you (uwwal). In origin there were two hamzas, and one of them was replaced by a long vowel (madd) and lightening.

Pharaoh: he is al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and he was from the Amalekites.

﴿They inflict upon you the worst torment﴾: that is, they impose upon you and make you taste the most severe and worst torment. This is because Pharaoh made the Children of Israel servants and slaves, and divided them according to their work. One group built, another group ploughed and planted, another group served, and whoever was not in any of these occupations had to pay the poll-tax (jizya).

﴿They slaughter your sons and let your women live﴾.

Ibn Muhaysin recited with lightening: the yā' and the bā' vowelled with fatḥa in "yudhabbihūna" (in the sense of slaughter), and the doubling (tashdid) is for intensity. This is because Pharaoh saw in his dream as if a fire came from Bayt al-Maqdis until it enveloped the houses of Egypt, burned them, burned the Copts, and left the Children of Israel. This frightened him, so he summoned the magicians and soothsayers and asked them about his dream. They said: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of your destruction, the end of your kingdom, and the change of your religion." So Pharaoh ordered the killing of every boy born among the Children of Israel, and he gathered the midwives from among the people of his kingdom and said to them: "Let no boy of the Children of Israel fall into your hands except that he is killed, and let no girl be but that she is spared." He appointed people to watch them and carry this out. Death spread among the elders of the Children of Israel, so the chiefs of the Copts entered upon Pharaoh and said to him: "Death has befallen the Children of Israel, and you are slaughtering their young, while their elders die, and soon the work will fall upon us." So Pharaoh ordered that they slaughter for one year and leave for one year. Harun was born in the year in which they did not slaughter, so he was spared, and Musa was born in the year in which they did slaughter.

﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾: in your being saved from them there was a great blessing. And the word "bala' (trial)" is used in two senses:

the blessings and the calamities [...]

[Blank in the manuscript.]

﴿And when We divided the sea for you ...﴾ [Unreadable text.]

the sea: This is because when the destruction of Pharaoh drew near, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and commanded them to keep lamps lit in their houses until morning. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought out to them every illegitimate child among the Copts who were among the Children of Israel, and He brought out [from the Children of Israel every illegitimate child among them] [Supplement from al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/84; the manuscript has a blank] to the Copts, until each one of them returned to his father. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent death upon the Copts, and every firstborn died, so they were occupied with burying them [away from pursuing them until] [Supplement from Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/396] the sun rose. Musa, peace be upon him, went out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, none of them younger than twenty or older than sixty, apart from the offspring. When they wanted to set out, the wandering (al-tih) was imposed upon them, so they did not know where to go. Musa, peace be upon him, summoned the elders of the Children of Israel and asked them about that.

They said: "When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he took a covenant from his brothers that they would not leave Egypt until they took him out with them. That is why the road was closed to us." So he asked them about the location of his grave, and they did not know.

Musa stood calling out: "I beseech Allah, whoever knows where the grave of Yusuf is, to inform me of it. And whoever does not know, let his ears be deaf to my words." He kept passing between two men calling out, and they did not hear his voice, until an old woman of theirs heard him and said: "Do you see, if I guide you to his grave, will you give me whatever I ask of you?" He refused her and said: "Until I ask my Lord." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to grant her request. She said: "I am an old, great woman who cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt; this is for the world. As for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into a chamber of Paradise except that I descend with you." He said: "Yes." She said: "He is in the depths of the water, in the Nile, so pray to Allah that He hold back the water from him." He prayed to Allah and He held back the water from him, and he prayed that the rising of dawn be delayed until he finished the matter of Yusuf. Musa dug at that place and extracted him in a coffer of marble, and he carried him until he buried him in al-Sham. Then the road opened for them.

They set out, with Musa at their rear and Harun at their front. Pharaoh learned of them, so he gathered his people and commanded them not to go out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night.

Pharaoh went out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand, and among them were seventy thousand of the dark-coloured horses, apart from the rest of the mixed breeds. The Children of Israel proceeded until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest rise.

They looked, and behold, there was Pharaoh, and that was when the sun rose. They remained perplexed and said: "O Musa, what shall we do? What is the way out? Pharaoh is behind us and the sea is before us." Musa said: ﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. Then He revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [26:63]. He struck it but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: "Be gentle with it," so Musa struck it with his staff and said: "Split, Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah." ﴿So it split, and each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [26:63]. And there appeared in it twelve paths, one path for each tribe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Mu'awiya sent to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about a place where the sun had risen only once. He wrote back to him: "It is the place from which the sea split for the Children of Israel." [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 8/334, which mentions the remainder of the story.]

The Children of Israel plunged into the sea, each tribe in its own path, and on either side of them the water was like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were frightened, and each tribe said: "Our brothers have all drowned." So Allah revealed to the state of the water: "Become interlaced," and the water became like latticed windows so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We divided the sea for you﴾, that is, We said, and We separated the water to the right and to the left.

﴿And We saved you﴾ from the people of Pharaoh and from drowning.

﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾. This is because Pharaoh, when he reached the sea and saw it split, said to his people: "Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my enemies and my slaves who ran away, and kill them. Enter the sea!" His people were afraid to enter it, and there was no female horse among Pharaoh's horses; they were all males. So Jibril, peace be upon him, came on a female horse in heat and went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When the horses smelled her scent, they rushed into the sea after her until they all plunged into the sea. Mikail came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and saying to them: "Catch up with your companions!" When Jibril came out of the sea and the first of them was about to come out, Allah, Exalted, commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them, and He drowned them all, and that was in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾.

﴿And you were looking on﴾ at their fate.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa forty nights﴾. This is because when the Children of Israel felt safe from their enemy and entered Egypt, they had no book or law to which they could refer, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised Musa that He would send down the Torah to them. Musa said to his people: "I am going to the appointed time of my Lord, and I will bring you a book containing the explanation of what you should do and what you should avoid." So he appointed them forty nights, thirty of Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, and he appointed his brother Harun as his successor over them.

When the promised time came, Jibril came on a horse called the horse of life, which does not touch anything without it coming to life, to take Musa to his Lord. When al-Samiri saw him, and he was a goldsmith from the people of Bajaro, whose name was Mikha (and Ibn 'Abbas said: his name was Musa ibn Zafar; he was a hypocrite who had outwardly embraced Islam, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, so the love of cows had entered his heart), when he saw Jibril on that horse, he said: "This has a matter." He took a handful of the dust from the hoof-print of Jibril's horse. The Children of Israel had borrowed a great deal of ornaments from the people of Pharaoh when they wanted to leave Egypt, for a festival of theirs, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed the people of Pharaoh, so those ornaments remained in the hands of the Children of Israel. When Musa arrived, al-Samiri said: "The goods and ornaments you borrowed from the people of Pharaoh are spoils of war, and they are not lawful for you. Dig a pit and bury them in it until Musa returns, and he will see his opinion regarding them." They did that.

When the ornaments were gathered, al-Samiri fashioned them, then he threw into them the handful he had taken from the dust of Jibril's horse, and there came out a calf of gold, set with jewels, as beautiful as could be, and it lowed a lowing. Al-Suddi said: It used to low and walk, [and say:] ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾ [20:88], that is, he left it here and went out to seek him.

He said: "The one who is pure from sins, who counts himself among the sinners; the one who strives in supererogatory acts beyond the obligatory ones, and counts himself among the negligent; and the one who is content with little of this world, and counts himself among the destitute. These are the most grateful of the grateful."

Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Dhu al-Nur: Gratitude to one above you is through obedience, to your equal through reciprocation, and to one below you through kindness and bounty.

﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾. Mujahid and al-Farra' said: they are one thing, and the Arabs repeat a thing when its wording differs, out of a suspicion of difference. Al-Farra' recited:

"I offered the hide to his two forearms,
and he found her words false and deceitful."

Antara said:

"I greeted a campsite whose traces had become old,
it was effaced and emptied after Umm al-Haytham."

Al-Zajjaj said: This is the correct view, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the Criterion for Musa in another place, saying: ﴿And We gave Musa and Harun the Criterion﴾ [21:48].

Al-Kisa'i said: "al-Furqan" is an epithet for "al-Kitab," meaning: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and the Criterion﴾, which distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful, between disbelief and faith, and between promise and threat. The waw was added to it as it is added to epithets, as in the saying: "So-and-so is good and tall." He recited:

"To the king, the resolute and the son of the leader,
and the lion of the battalion in the crowd."

The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book, completed upon the one who did good, and a detailed explanation of everything﴾ [6:154].

Qutrub said: He meant by it the Criterion, and there is an implicit element in the verse, its meaning being: ﴿And when We gave Musa the Book and Muhammad the Criterion﴾.

﴿So that you might be guided﴾ by these two books. So one of the two names was dropped, as in the poet's saying:

"You see him as if Allah were slitting his nose,
and his eyes, if his master spends the night with him, are narrowed."

Ibn 'Abbas said: By the Criterion he meant victory over the enemies, the victory that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave Musa, and the destruction of Pharaoh and his people. This is indicated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We sent not down upon Our servant on the day of the Criterion, the day the two hosts met﴾ [8:41], which is the day of Badr.

Yaman ibn Rabab said: "al-Furqan" means the splitting of the sea, which is among the great signs, as indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you and saved you﴾.

﴿And when Moses said to his people, "O my people, you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [as a god]. So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is best for you in the sight of your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Ibn Rabab's remark continues: "Wronged yourselves" means you harmed yourselves by taking the calf as a god. They said: "What shall we do, and what is the remedy?" He said: "So turn in repentance, return" ﴿to your Creator﴾, meaning your Originator. Abu 'Amr would reduce the hamza, dropping the vowel to a jussive-like sukun, in His saying ﴿bari'kum﴾ and ﴿yamurukum﴾ and ﴿yansurkum﴾, seeking lightness. [That is, by eliding the vowel; it is also reported from him as sukun, while the others recited without elision.] Like the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

*So today I drink, not bearing sin from God, nor as one who drinks uninvited.* [Lisan al-'Arab: 10/426.]

And he recited:

*When they go crooked, I say "companion, straighten them," across the desert like swimming ships.* [Sharh Shafiyat Ibn al-Hajib: 4/225, and Lisan al-'Arab: 12/432.]

He said: ﴿So kill yourselves﴾, so that the innocent would kill the guilty. ﴿That killing is best for you in the sight of your Creator.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: God, Mighty and Majestic, refused to accept the repentance of the Children of Israel except in the state they disliked, that they fight one another when they worshipped the calf.

Qatadah said: the punishment of the calf-worshippers was killing, because they had apostatized, and disbelief makes blood lawful.

Qatadah recited: ﴿fa-aqīlū anfusakum﴾, from iqalah (seeking revocation), meaning seek to have your stumble removed through repentance. When Moses intended the killing, they said: "We submit to the command of God, Exalted is He," so they sat in the courtyards hidden, and the people unsheathed daggers against them. A man would see his son, his father, his paternal uncle, his people, his friend and his neighbor, yet they could not proceed in obedience to God's command. They said: "O Moses, how shall we act?" So God sent a mist and a black cloud, so that no one could see another. It was said to them: whoever loosens his turban, or lifts his gaze to his killer, or shields himself with a hand or foot, is struck, and his repentance is rejected. So they kept killing one another until evening. When the killing increased among them, Aaron and Moses called out, wept, grieved, humbled themselves, and said: "O Lord, the Children of Israel are being destroyed, the remnant, the remnant!" Then God, Mighty and Majestic, lifted the cloud and commanded them to lay down their weapons and cease killing.

The dead were uncovered, thousands of them, and this weighed heavily on Moses. God revealed to him: "Would it not satisfy you that I admit both the killer and the killed into Paradise? Whoever among them was killed is a martyr, and whoever remains, I will expiate his sins." This is His saying ﴿Then He accepted your repentance﴾, meaning: since you did as He commanded, He accepted your repentance and pardoned you.

﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 49–54 (part 1 of 2):

And when We saved you: that is, your forefathers and ancestors. He counted it a favour upon them because they were saved by their salvation, and the virtues of fathers are the glories of sons.

As for His saying, ﴿And We saved you﴾ [2:50]: its root is "we cast you upon al-najah," and al-najah is the high and wide part of the land. This is the original meaning. Then every one who attains success was called "najin" (one who is saved), as if he had come out of narrowness and hardship into ease and comfort.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i recited: "wa-idh najjākum" (with the single letter of the root doubled and the verb in the singular).

﴿From the people of Pharaoh﴾: that is, his partisans, followers, household, his kin, and the people of his religion. Its origin is from "al-awwal," which means return, as if it returns to you (uwwal). In origin there were two hamzas, and one of them was replaced by a long vowel (madd) and lightening.

Pharaoh: he is al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan, and he was from the Amalekites.

﴿They inflict upon you the worst torment﴾: that is, they impose upon you and make you taste the most severe and worst torment. This is because Pharaoh made the Children of Israel servants and slaves, and divided them according to their work. One group built, another group ploughed and planted, another group served, and whoever was not in any of these occupations had to pay the poll-tax (jizya).

﴿They slaughter your sons and let your women live﴾.

Ibn Muhaysin recited with lightening: the yā' and the bā' vowelled with fatḥa in "yudhabbihūna" (in the sense of slaughter), and the doubling (tashdid) is for intensity. This is because Pharaoh saw in his dream as if a fire came from Bayt al-Maqdis until it enveloped the houses of Egypt, burned them, burned the Copts, and left the Children of Israel. This frightened him, so he summoned the magicians and soothsayers and asked them about his dream. They said: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of your destruction, the end of your kingdom, and the change of your religion." So Pharaoh ordered the killing of every boy born among the Children of Israel, and he gathered the midwives from among the people of his kingdom and said to them: "Let no boy of the Children of Israel fall into your hands except that he is killed, and let no girl be but that she is spared." He appointed people to watch them and carry this out. Death spread among the elders of the Children of Israel, so the chiefs of the Copts entered upon Pharaoh and said to him: "Death has befallen the Children of Israel, and you are slaughtering their young, while their elders die, and soon the work will fall upon us." So Pharaoh ordered that they slaughter for one year and leave for one year. Harun was born in the year in which they did not slaughter, so he was spared, and Musa was born in the year in which they did slaughter.

﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾: in your being saved from them there was a great blessing. And the word "bala' (trial)" is used in two senses:

the blessings and the calamities [...]

[Blank in the manuscript.]

﴿And when We divided the sea for you ...﴾ [Unreadable text.]

the sea: This is because when the destruction of Pharaoh drew near, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel, and commanded them to keep lamps lit in their houses until morning. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brought out to them every illegitimate child among the Copts who were among the Children of Israel, and He brought out [from the Children of Israel every illegitimate child among them] [Supplement from al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/84; the manuscript has a blank] to the Copts, until each one of them returned to his father. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent death upon the Copts, and every firstborn died, so they were occupied with burying them [away from pursuing them until] [Supplement from Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/396] the sun rose. Musa, peace be upon him, went out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, none of them younger than twenty or older than sixty, apart from the offspring. When they wanted to set out, the wandering (al-tih) was imposed upon them, so they did not know where to go. Musa, peace be upon him, summoned the elders of the Children of Israel and asked them about that.

They said: "When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he took a covenant from his brothers that they would not leave Egypt until they took him out with them. That is why the road was closed to us." So he asked them about the location of his grave, and they did not know.

Musa stood calling out: "I beseech Allah, whoever knows where the grave of Yusuf is, to inform me of it. And whoever does not know, let his ears be deaf to my words." He kept passing between two men calling out, and they did not hear his voice, until an old woman of theirs heard him and said: "Do you see, if I guide you to his grave, will you give me whatever I ask of you?" He refused her and said: "Until I ask my Lord." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to grant her request. She said: "I am an old, great woman who cannot walk, so carry me and take me out of Egypt; this is for the world. As for the Hereafter, I ask you that I not descend into a chamber of Paradise except that I descend with you." He said: "Yes." She said: "He is in the depths of the water, in the Nile, so pray to Allah that He hold back the water from him." He prayed to Allah and He held back the water from him, and he prayed that the rising of dawn be delayed until he finished the matter of Yusuf. Musa dug at that place and extracted him in a coffer of marble, and he carried him until he buried him in al-Sham. Then the road opened for them.

They set out, with Musa at their rear and Harun at their front. Pharaoh learned of them, so he gathered his people and commanded them not to go out in pursuit of the Children of Israel until the rooster crowed. By Allah, no rooster crowed that night.

Pharaoh went out in pursuit of the Children of Israel, and at his vanguard was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand, and among them were seventy thousand of the dark-coloured horses, apart from the rest of the mixed breeds. The Children of Israel proceeded until they reached the sea, and the water was at its highest rise.

They looked, and behold, there was Pharaoh, and that was when the sun rose. They remained perplexed and said: "O Musa, what shall we do? What is the way out? Pharaoh is behind us and the sea is before us." Musa said: ﴿By no means! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [26:62]. Then He revealed to him: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff﴾ [26:63]. He struck it but it did not obey him. Allah revealed to him: "Be gentle with it," so Musa struck it with his staff and said: "Split, Abu Khalid, by the permission of Allah." ﴿So it split, and each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [26:63]. And there appeared in it twelve paths, one path for each tribe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent the wind and the sun upon the bed of the sea until it became dry.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Mu'awiya sent to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about a place where the sun had risen only once. He wrote back to him: "It is the place from which the sea split for the Children of Israel." [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 8/334, which mentions the remainder of the story.]

The Children of Israel plunged into the sea, each tribe in its own path, and on either side of them the water was like a huge mountain, and they could not see one another. They were frightened, and each tribe said: "Our brothers have all drowned." So Allah revealed to the state of the water: "Become interlaced," and the water became like latticed windows so that they could see one another and hear one another's speech, until they crossed the sea safely. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We divided the sea for you﴾, that is, We said, and We separated the water to the right and to the left.

﴿And We saved you﴾ from the people of Pharaoh and from drowning.

﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾. This is because Pharaoh, when he reached the sea and saw it split, said to his people: "Look at the sea, it has split out of awe of me, so that I may overtake my enemies and my slaves who ran away, and kill them. Enter the sea!" His people were afraid to enter it, and there was no female horse among Pharaoh's horses; they were all males. So Jibril, peace be upon him, came on a female horse in heat and went ahead of them and plunged into the sea. When the horses smelled her scent, they rushed into the sea after her until they all plunged into the sea. Mikail came on a horse behind the people, urging them on and saying to them: "Catch up with your companions!" When Jibril came out of the sea and the first of them was about to come out, Allah, Exalted, commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them, and He drowned them all, and that was in full view of the Children of Israel. This is His saying: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh﴾.

﴿And you were looking on﴾ at their fate.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa forty nights﴾. This is because when the Children of Israel felt safe from their enemy and entered Egypt, they had no book or law to which they could refer, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, promised Musa that He would send down the Torah to them. Musa said to his people: "I am going to the appointed time of my Lord, and I will bring you a book containing the explanation of what you should do and what you should avoid." So he appointed them forty nights, thirty of Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja, and he appointed his brother Harun as his successor over them.

When the promised time came, Jibril came on a horse called the horse of life, which does not touch anything without it coming to life, to take Musa to his Lord. When al-Samiri saw him, and he was a goldsmith from the people of Bajaro, whose name was Mikha (and Ibn 'Abbas said: his name was Musa ibn Zafar; he was a hypocrite who had outwardly embraced Islam, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, so the love of cows had entered his heart), when he saw Jibril on that horse, he said: "This has a matter." He took a handful of the dust from the hoof-print of Jibril's horse. The Children of Israel had borrowed a great deal of ornaments from the people of Pharaoh when they wanted to leave Egypt, for a festival of theirs, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, destroyed the people of Pharaoh, so those ornaments remained in the hands of the Children of Israel. When Musa arrived, al-Samiri said: "The goods and ornaments you borrowed from the people of Pharaoh are spoils of war, and they are not lawful for you. Dig a pit and bury them in it until Musa returns, and he will see his opinion regarding them." They did that.

When the ornaments were gathered, al-Samiri fashioned them, then he threw into them the handful he had taken from the dust of Jibril's horse, and there came out a calf of gold, set with jewels, as beautiful as could be, and it lowed a lowing. Al-Suddi said: It used to low and walk, [and say:] ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾ [20:88], that is, he left it here and went out to seek him.

The Children of Israel had broken the promise, so they counted a day and a night as two days. When twenty days had passed and Musa, peace be upon him, had not returned, and they saw the calf and heard the words of al-Samiri, eight thousand men among them were seduced by the calf, and they clung to it, worshipping it besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And when We appointed for Musa﴾: Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub recited "wa'adnā" without an alif throughout the Qur'an, and the rest recited "wā'adnā" with an alif, and this is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. Whoever recited without an alif said: because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the sole one who makes the promise, and the Qur'an speaks of it thus, as in His saying: ﴿Allah has promised﴾ [4:95], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise﴾ [14:22]. Whoever recited with an alif said: "The form of mufā'ala (mutual action) may come from one party, as in their saying: 'I punished the thief,' 'May Allah grant you well-being,' and 'I struck the sandal.'"

Al-Zajjaj said: "wā'adnā" is good, because acceptance and obedience stand in the position of mutual promising; so the promise is from Allah and the acceptance is from Musa.

Musa: he is Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Yasahar ibn Qahat ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub.

﴿Forty nights﴾. Zayd ibn 'Ali recited "arbi'īn" with a kasra on the bā', and this is a dialect form, and "laylatan" is in the accusative as a specification (tamyīz) and explanation. Time was linked to the night rather than the day because the months of the Arabs were set by the course of the moon, and the crescent appears at night. It was also said that darkness is older than light, and night was created before day. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And a sign for them is the night; We strip from it the day﴾ [36:37], and so on.

﴿Then you took the calf﴾. Abu al-'Aliya said: It was named "the calf" because they hastened (ta'ajjalū) to it before the return of Musa, peace be upon him.

﴿After him﴾: after Musa's departure to the mountain for the appointed meeting.

﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾: harming yourselves by disobedience, and placing worship in other than its proper place.

﴿Then We pardoned you﴾: that is, We left you and did not uproot you,
from his saying, peace be upon him: "Trim the moustaches and leave the beards." It was also said: We erased your sins, from the saying of the Arabs: "The wind effaced the dwellings, so they were effaced."

﴿After that﴾: that is, after your worship of the calf.

﴿So that you might be grateful﴾: in order that you might thank My pardon of you and My kindness to you.

The scholars differed concerning the reality of gratitude (shukr). Ibn 'Abbas said: it is obedience with all the limbs to the Lord of creation, openly and secretly.

Al-Hasan said: the thanks for a blessing is to mention it. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾ [93:11].

Al-Fadl said: the thanks for every blessing is that Allah is not disobeyed after that blessing.

Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq: The reality of gratitude is knowing the Benefactor, and that you do not regard any share for yourself in the blessing, but see it as from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [16:53]. This is indicated by what Sayf ibn Maymun narrated from al-Husayn: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Musa, peace be upon him, said: 'O Lord, how was Adam able to render thanks for what You bestowed upon him of Your blessings? You created him with Your hand, made Your angels prostrate to him, and settled him in Your Paradise.' So Allah revealed to him: 'Adam knew that all of that is from Me and from My side, and that is his gratitude.'" [85] [Rawdat al-Wa'izin (al-Fattal al-Nisaburi): p. 473; al-Shukr li-llah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya: p. 70.]

And from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Dawud, peace be upon him, said: "My God, how can I thank You when I cannot reach Your thanks except by Your blessing?" Allah, Exalted, revealed to him: "Do you not know that the blessings you have are from Me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord." He said: "Then be content with that as your gratitude."

Wahb said: Likewise Musa said: "O Lord, You have bestowed upon me abundant blessings and commanded me to thank You for them, and my thanks for every blessing from You upon me is itself a further blessing." Allah said: "O Musa, you have learned the knowledge that no knowledge escapes. It is enough from My servant that he knows that whatever blessing he has is from Me and from My side."

Al-Junayd said: The reality of gratitude is the inability to give thanks.

It is narrated of Dawud, peace be upon him, that he said: "Glory be to Him who made the servant's acknowledgment of his inability to thank Him a form of thanks, just as He made his acknowledgment of his inability to know Him a form of knowing."

Some of them said: Gratitude is that one does not see the blessing at all, but sees the Benefactor.

Abu 'Uthman al-Khayri: The truth of gratitude is that you do not praise with your tongue anyone other than the Benefactor.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, from Abu Bakr al-Razi, from al-Shibli: Gratitude is humility under the vision of the favour.
