Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 94–99:

قُلْ إِنْ كانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الآية. The commentators said: The occasion of revelation of this verse is that the Jews made false claims, which God Most High related about them in His Book, such as His saying: ﴿And they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days﴾ [2:80].

And His saying: ﴿And they said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [2:111].

And His saying: ﴿We are the sons of God and His beloved﴾ [5:18]. So God Most High refuted them and established the proof against them. He said: ﴿Say, O Muhammad: If the Last Abode with God is yours exclusively, apart from the rest of mankind﴾ — exclusively, due to His saying: ﴿Exclusively for our males﴾ [6:139], His saying: ﴿Exclusively on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [7:32], and His saying: ﴿Exclusively for you, apart from the believers﴾ [33:50], meaning: specifically, apart from mankind.

﴿Then wish for death﴾, i.e., then desire it and call for it, because whoever knows that Paradise is his destination longs for it, and there is no way to enter it except after death, so they hasten it by wishing.

﴿If you are truthful﴾ in your claim, correct in your assertion. It was said that the meaning of His saying ﴿Then wish for death﴾ is: invoke death upon the lying party.

Ibn ʿAbbas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "If they had wished for death, every one of them would have choked on his own saliva, and not a Jew would have remained on the face of the earth but would have died."

Then God said: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth﴾, knowing that they are liars in their claim.

﴿And God is Knower of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning the Jews. This is one of the miracles of the Qur'an, for He challenged them, then informed that they would not do it after He had said this to them, and it was as He informed.

﴿And you will surely find them﴾ — the lam is the lam of oath, and the nun is for emphasis of the oath; its estimate is: "By God, you will surely find them, O Muhammad," meaning the Jews, ﴿most eager of people for life﴾; in the codex of Ubayy it is "for the life."

﴿And of those who associate others with God﴾ — it was said that it is connected to the previous statement, meaning: "and [more eager] than those who associate others with God." Al-Farra' said: This is like saying "he is the most generous of people," and "more generous than Hatim," i.e., "and more generous than Hatim."

And it was said: It is a new beginning and the completion of the statement at His saying "on life." He began with the conjunctive waw and implied the subject of "yawaddu" (would love), with the estimate: "And among those who associate others with God is one who loves..." as in the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"So they remained, and among them one whose tear is ever flowing, and another who sheds tears of the eye in drops."

He meant: "and among them is one whose tear is flowing." He meant by ﴿those who associate others with God﴾ the Magians.

﴿Yawaddu﴾ means: he desires and wishes.

﴿Ahadahum law yuʿammar﴾ — its estimate is: his being granted a lifespan of

﴿alfa sana﴾ (a thousand years). The commentators said: It is the greeting of the Magians among themselves: "ten thousand years," and the word "alf" (thousand) is "Nawruz" and "Mihrajan" (festivals).

God said: ﴿And he will not be removed from the punishment﴾, i.e., from the Fire.

﴿An yuʿammar﴾ — i.e., his being granted a long life. "Zahzahahu" (he removed him): "baʿadahu" (he distanced him), so "fa-zahzaha" means he distanced himself; it is used both intransitively and transitively. Dhu al-Rummah said in the transitive usage:

"O You who seize the soul from me when it is dying, and Who forgives the sin, distance me from the Fire."

And the rajaz poet said in the intransitive usage:

"O my friend, why does the darkness not move away, and why does the light of dawn not become clear?"

﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel...﴾ — the verse.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: A rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews, called ʿAbd Allah ibn Suriya, had disputed with the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about certain things. When the proof was established against him, he said: "What angel comes to you from the sky?"

He said: "Gabriel, and God never sent a Book to any prophet except that he was his ally."

He said: "That is our enemy among the angels. If Michael had been in his place, we would have believed in you, for Gabriel brings punishment, war, and misery, and he has opposed us many times. The most grievous of that to us is that God Most High revealed to our Prophet, peace be upon him, that Jerusalem will be destroyed at the hand of a man called Bukht Nasr (Nebuchadnezzar), and He informed us of the time in which it would be destroyed. When its time came, we sent a man from the strong men of the Children of Israel in pursuit of Bukht Nasr to kill him. He set out seeking him until he found him in Babylon, a poor youth without strength. Our companion took him to kill him, but Gabriel, peace be upon him, repelled him and said to our companion: 'If your Lord is the One who permitted your destruction, you will not be able to overpower him; and if it is not so, then by what right do you kill him?' Our companion believed him and returned. Then Bukht Nasr grew great and strong, attacked us, and destroyed Jerusalem. Therefore we take him as an enemy." Then God Most High revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: The Jews said: "Gabriel is our enemy; he was commanded to place prophethood among us, but he placed it among others." So God Most High revealed this verse.

Qatadah, ʿIkrimah, and al-Suddi said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) had land at the upper part of Medina, and its path passed by the schools of the Jews. When ʿUmar went to his land, he would come to them, listen to them, and speak with them. They said: "O ʿUmar, among the companions of Muhammad there is no one more beloved to us than you. They pass by here and harm us, but you do not harm us, and we hope for you." ʿUmar said: "By God, I do not love you for your love, nor do I ask you because I doubt my religion, but I enter upon you only to increase my insight in the matter of Muhammad ﷺ and to see its traces in your Book." They said: "Which of the angels brings Muhammad?"

He said: "Gabriel." They said: "That is our enemy; he informs Muhammad of our secret, and he is the bringer of punishment, collapse, drought, and hardship, whereas Michael brings fertility and peace." ʿUmar said to them: "Do you know Gabriel and deny Muhammad?!" They said: "Yes."

He said: "Then tell me about the rank of Gabriel and Michael with God, Mighty and Majestic."

They said: "Gabriel is on His right and Michael on His left, and Michael is an enemy of Gabriel." ʿUmar said: "I testify that whoever is an enemy of Gabriel is an enemy of Michael, and whoever is an enemy of Michael is an enemy of Gabriel, and whoever is an enemy of both of them, God is an enemy to him." Then ʿUmar returned to the Messenger of God ﷺ and found that Gabriel had preceded him with the revelation, so the Messenger of God ﷺ recited to him this verse and said: "Your Lord has agreed with you, O ʿUmar." ʿUmar said: "Indeed I have seen myself, after that, in the religion of God, to be firmer than stone."

God said, confirming ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him): ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel...﴾. And for "Jibril" there are seven dialects:

(Jibril) with a hamza, the vowel on the jim and ra' long and open, which is the reading of Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr, Khalaf, and the choice of Abu ʿUbayd. He said: "I saw in the codex of ʿUthman, which is called the Imam, [the letter] ya' in Jibril and Mikayl," and the ya' before the ya' indicates the hamza. The poet said:

"We witnessed, and of a battalion there is none left to us through all time except Jibril as its leader."

(Jibra'il) long, with hamza, fully pronounced, on the pattern of Jibra'il, which is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAlqamah, and Ibn Wththab.

(Jibra'il) long, with hamza, with the short vowel, on the pattern of Jibra'l, which is the reading of Talhah ibn Musarrif.

(Jibril) with hamza, short, with the short vowel on the pattern of Jibraʿl, which is the reading of Yahya ibn Adam.

(Jibrall) with hamza, short, with the doubled lam and no ya', which is the reading of Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar, and al-Aʿmash.

(Jabril) with fatha on the jim and kasra on the ra', without hamza, which is the reading of Ibn Kathir. He recited, quoting Hassan:

"And Jabril, the trustworthy of God among us, and the Holy Spirit, about whom there is no concealment."

(Jibril) with kasra on the jim and ra', without hamza, which is the reading of ʿAli, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, Abu Raja', Abu al-ʿAliyah, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, most of the people of Basra and Medina, and the choice of Abu Hatim, and it has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that.

It is narrated from Shibl, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir, who said: "I saw the Messenger of God ﷺ in a dream, reciting Jibril with kasra on the jim and ra', without hamza. So I do not recite it except in this way."

Al-Tha'labi said: "The sound and well-known [reading] from Kathir is what has preceded, and God knows best."

As for the interpretation, the scholars said: "Jabr" is the servant in Syriac, and "Il" is God, Mighty and Majestic; what supports this is what Isma'il narrated from Raja', from Mu'awiyah, traced to the Prophet, who said: "Jibril and Mikail are only like your saying ʿAbd Allah and ʿAbd al-Rahman." It was also said: Jibril is derived from the jabarut (sovereignty) of God, and Mikail from the malakut (dominion) of God.

﴿Fa-innahu﴾ — i.e., Gabriel. ﴿Nazzalahu﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an, His Book, without prior mention, as in His saying: ﴿And if God were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back any creature﴾ [35:45], meaning the earth, and His saying: ﴿until it was hidden behind the veil﴾ [38:32], meaning the sun.

﴿ʿAla qalbika﴾ — O Muhammad. ﴿Bi-idhni Allah﴾ — by the command of God.

﴿Musaddiqan﴾ — confirming, agreeing.

﴿Limā bayna yadayhi﴾ — what came before it of the books.

﴿Wa hudan wa bushra lil-mu'minin﴾. ﴿Man kana ʿaduwwan lillahi wa malaikatihi wa rusulihi wa Jibrila wa Mikal﴾ — he singled them out by mention from among the angels, and their positions are for the sake of preference and distinction, as in His saying: ﴿In both of them is fruit, and palm trees, and pomegranates﴾ [55:68]. And Mikail has four dialects: long, with hamza, fully pronounced, on the pattern of Mikaʿil, which is the reading of the people of Mecca, Kufa, and Syria.

﴿Wa Mikal﴾ — long, with hamza, short with the short vowel, like Mika'l, which is the reading of the people of Medina.

And (Mikil) with hamza, short, on the pattern of Mikʿal, which is the reading of al-Aʿmash and Ibn Muhaysin.

(Wa Mīkāl) on the pattern of mif'al, which is the reading of the people of Basra. The poet said:

"And on the day of Badr we met you, and for us was reinforcement, with victory, Jibril and Mikal."

And Jarir said:

"They worshipped the cross and denied Muhammad, and denied Jibril and denied Mikal."

The meaning of the verse: whoever is an enemy to any of these, God is an enemy to him, and the waw in it has the sense of "or," as in His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books...﴾, the verse, because whoever disbelieves in one is a disbeliever in all.

Ibn Suriya said: "O Muhammad, you have brought us nothing we recognize, and God has not sent down to you any clear sign that we might follow you by it." So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses﴾ — clear, explicit, detailing the lawful and unlawful, the limits, and the rulings.

﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾ — those who deviate from the command of God.

"O my friend, why does the darkness not move away, and why does the light of dawn not become clear?"

Ibn ʿAbbas said: A rabbi from the rabbis of the Jews, called ʿAbd Allah ibn Suriya, had disputed with the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about certain things. When the proof was established against him, he said: "What angel comes to you from the sky?"

He said: "Gabriel, and God never sent a Book to any prophet except that he was his ally."

He said: "That is our enemy among the angels. If Michael had been in his place, we would have believed in you, for Gabriel brings punishment, war, and misery, and he has opposed us many times. He set out seeking him until he found him in Babylon, a poor youth without strength. Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 100–103 (part 1 of 2):

Ayn al-Istifham (the interrogative hamza) entered upon the conjunctive waw in أَوَكُلَّما (awa-kullama, "Is it then that every time..."), just as it enters upon the fa' in His saying ﴿Will you then make the deaf hear?﴾ [Yunus 10:42] and ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as protectors?﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50], and upon thumma (then) in His saying ﴿What! And when it has occurred?﴾ [Yunus 10:51], and similar cases.

Ibn al-Sammak al-'Adawi recited it with the waw of conjunction vowelless (awkullama), and kullama in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf). ﴿They made a covenant﴾ ('ahadu 'ahdan), meaning the Jews.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned, [they disregarded] what Allah had taken from them in covenant and what He had enjoined upon them concerning him.

Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Allah has made no covenant or pact with us concerning Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse. What clarifies this is the reading of Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi: "Whenever they were given a covenant, Allah cursed them." The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:187], and so on.

Others said: The Jews made a pact that if Muhammad emerged, they would certainly believe in him and would stand with him against the polytheists of the Arabs and expel them from their lands. But when he was sent, they broke the covenant and disbelieved in him. The evidence and parallel for this is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:101].

'Ata' said: These are the covenants that existed between the Messenger of Allah and the Jews, which they broke, like the act of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. The evidence is His saying: ﴿those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant each time﴾ [al-Anfal 8:56].

*Nabadhahu* means he rejected it. In the reading of 'Abdullah, it means he broke it (naqadahu).

*Fariqun minhum* means groups of the Jews.

*Bal aktharuhum la yu'minun* ("Rather, most of them do not believe"). The root meaning of *nabadh* is to throw away and reject. Al-Zajjaj recited:

"I looked at its title and cast it away,
as you cast away a sandal worn out from your sandals."

This is an example of someone who makes light of a thing and does not act upon it. The Arabs say: "Put this behind your back, behind your ear, and under your foot," meaning: leave it and turn away from it. Allah says: ﴿and you have made Him a thing cast behind your backs﴾ [Hud 11:92]. Al-Farra' recited:

"Tamim ibn Qays, let not my need
be behind the back, nor let its answer be cared for by me."

Al-Sha'bi said: It is before them; they read it, but they cast away acting upon it.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, and adorned it with gold and silver, but they did not treat its lawful as lawful nor its unlawful as unlawful. That is the *nabdh* (casting away).

*Wattaba'u*: that is, the Jews.

*Ma tatlu al-shayatin*: that is, what the devils recited (*ma talat al-shayatin*).

Like the saying of the poet:

"When you pass by his grave, then slaughter at it
a dark-eyed camel and every hunting horse.
And sprinkle the sides of his grave with their blood,
for indeed both maidservants and sacrificial animals have wept for him."

It is related from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl that he was asked about this verse and said: It is an abbreviated and implied construction, its estimated meaning being: "and they followed what the devils had been reciting," that is, reading it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] to follow and act upon it.

'Ata' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: [it means] to narrate and speak of it.

Yaman said: [it means] to transmit it.

Al-Hasan recited *al-shayatun* with a waw in the nominative case throughout the whole Qur'an.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Kharazanji say:

He was asked about al-Hasan's reading and said: It is an art and a beauty, according to most people of literature. However, al-Asma'i claimed that he heard a Bedouin say: "The garden of so-and-so has gardens around it" (*bustanun*/*bustanun*, in the oblique plural form *bustanun*).

*'Ala mulki Sulayman*: that is, during the reign and time of Sulayman, as in the saying of Abu al-Najm:

"Then it is over the horizon like the eye of a squinting man."

That is, on the horizon.

*Al-Mulk* is the complete power and its firm establishment.

Al-Zajjaj said, regarding the story of the verse: the devils wrote sorcery and talismanic arts (*nayranjat*) in the name of Asif. "This is what Asif ibn Barkhiya taught Sulayman the king." Then they placed them under his prayer mat when Allah removed his kingdom, and Sulayman did not perceive it. When he died, they extracted them from under his prayer mat.

The people said: "It was only by this that Sulayman ruled you, so learn it." As for the scholars and righteous ones of the Children of Israel, they said: "God forbid that this should be the knowledge of Sulayman. If this were his knowledge, Sulayman would have been ruined."

As for the base people, they said: "This is the knowledge of Sulayman," and they turned to learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Blame fell upon Sulayman, and their condition remained thus until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and revealed the excuse of Sulayman (peace be upon him) through his tongue and showed his innocence of what had been charged against him. Then they said: ﴿and they followed what the devils recited﴾, to the end of the verse. This is the saying of al-Ka'bi.

Al-Suddi said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and sit in the places of hearing, listening to the speech of the angels about what would happen on earth, such as death or other things. Then they would come to the soothsayers and mix what they had heard with lies and falsehood, seventy words for every word, and inform them of that. The people wrote this down, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn knew the unseen. So Sulayman sent out among the people, gathered those books, placed them in a chest, and buried them beneath his throne, saying: "I will not hear anyone say that the devils know the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Sulayman died and the scholars who knew the matter of Sulayman had passed away, and the burying of the books had been forgotten, a later generation came, and a devil took the form of a man. He came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I guide you to a treasure that never fails?"

They said: "Yes." He said: "Dig beneath the throne." He went with them, showed them the place, and stood aside. They said: "Come closer." He said: "No, but here. If you do not find it, then kill me." This is because no devil could approach the throne without being burned. They dug and found those books. When they took them out, the devil said: "Sulayman used to control the jinn, mankind, and the birds by this." Then the devil flew off and departed. It spread among the people that Sulayman had been a sorcerer, and the Children of Israel adopted those books. That is why sorcery is found most among the Jews. When Muhammad (ﷺ) came, the Jews disputed with him by means of them, and Allah cleared Sulayman of that and revealed this verse. [See Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 1/106.]

'Ikrimah said: Sulayman (peace be upon him) would not rise one morning without a tree sprouting in his prayer niche (mihrab) in Bayt al-Maqdis. He would ask it: "What is your name?" The tree would say: "My name is such-and-such." He would say: "For what disease are you?" It would say: "For such-and-such." He would order it to be cut down and placed in the storehouse, and some of it would be planted in gardens. Then a Syrian carob tree (kharnubah) sprouted, and he said to it: "What are you?" It said: "I am the carob." He said: "For what did you sprout?" It said: "For the ruin of your mosque." Sulayman said: "Allah would not ruin it while I am alive." "You are the one upon whose face will be my death and the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis." He uprooted it, planted it in a wall of his, and it did not grow until he died. The people began to say, in their contentment: "If only we had someone like Sulayman."

The devils wrote a book and placed it in Sulayman's prayer place. They said to the people: "Shall I guide you to what he used to heal with?" They went and extracted that book, and in it was sorcery and incantations. So Allah revealed in this verse concerning what the devils and the Jews did, upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿and they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Sulayman﴾.

﴿Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾: for sorcery is disbelief.

*Wa lakinna al-shayatina kafaru*: the people of Kufa and Syria read it with the *nun* lightened and *al-shayatinu* in the nominative, and likewise in *Wa lakinna Allaha qatalahum* and *Wa lakinna Allaha rama* in al-Anfal [8:17].

The rest read it with the *nun* doubled and what follows it in the accusative. *Lakinna* is a word with two meanings: negation of a past report and affirmation of a future report. It is composed of three words: originally *la kana*, *la* as negation, *ka* as address, and *inna* in the accusative and conjunctive. The hamza was dropped because of heaviness. It may be doubled or lightened. When doubled, it puts in the accusative the nouns that follow it, as the heavy *inna* does. When lightened, it puts in the nominative what the light *inna* puts in the nominative.

*Yu'allimuna al-nasa al-sihra* ("they taught people sorcery"). Some said: *al-sihr* means knowledge and eloquence; the evidence is the saying of a poet: "Ibn al-Sami'" ... that is, the knowledgeable one (*al-'alim*).

Others said: it is deception with a thing until the one who imagines it thinks that it is a thing, though it has no reality, like a mirage that deceives the one who sees it and disappoints the one who hopes for it. Allah says: ﴿It is imagined to him, by their sorcery, that they were running﴾ [Taha 20:66].

*Wa ma unzila 'ala al-malakayni*: the position of what follows the verb "they followed" (*wattaba'u*) is governed by its meaning, as "they did not know what was revealed to the two angels." Its meaning is: "They followed what was revealed to the two angels." It is permissible for it to be in the accusative by virtue of "they followed," the estimate being: "and they followed what was revealed to the two angels." Some made *ma* a negation, and then it has no position in the sentence, meaning: sorcery was not sent down upon the two angels, as the Jews claimed; rather, they [the devils] were teaching people [...] of their own selves [a word is unreadable in the original manuscript]. The first opinion is more sound.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir read *malakayni* with a *kasra* on the *lam*. They said: The two were two men, sorcerers, who were in Babylon, from among the angels, who did not teach people sorcery. al-Hasan explained them, saying: "Two Persian men in Babylon." Babylon is Iraq. It was named Babil because of the confusion (*tabalbul*) of tongues there when the palace of Nimrod fell, that is, their dispersal.

Or, Allah tested people by the two angels at that time: whoever was wretched by learning sorcery from them would disbelieve through it; whoever was blessed by abandoning it would remain in faith. The two teachers would thereby increase in punishment for teaching. In this there is a trial of the teacher and the learner. Allah tests His servants with what He wills, as He wills, for His is the command and the judgment.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: Babil was named so because when Allah wished to make the tongues of the sons of Adam differ, He sent a wind that gathered them from every horizon to Babil. Allah confused their tongues, and no one knew what the other was saying. Then that wind scattered them in the lands. It is not declined (*la yanșarif*) because it is the name of a well-known place.

*Harut and Marut* are two Syriac names, in the genitive position as an explanation of the two angels, being in apposition to them, except that they are in the accusative because of their foreignness and definiteness. Their story, as mentioned by Ibn 'Abbas and the exegetes, is that the angels saw the evil deeds and numerous sins of the sons of Adam ascending to heaven. This was in the time of Idris. They reproached them for that and invoked [curses] upon them. They said: "These are the ones You placed on the earth and chose, and they disobey You."

Allah, mighty and majestic, said to them: "If I had sent you down to earth and placed in you what I placed in them, you would have committed what they committed."

They said: "Glory be to You, it would not be fitting for us to disobey You." Allah said: "Choose two angels from among your best, then send them down to earth." They chose Harut and Marut, who were among the most righteous and the most devoted of the angels.

Al-Kalbi said: Allah said to them: "Choose three." [They chose] 'Azza, who is Harut, and 'Azaya, who is Marut.

Their names were changed when they committed the sin, as the name of Iblis was changed, and 'Aza'il. Allah placed in them the desire He had placed in the sons of Adam. He sent them down to earth and commanded them to judge between people with truth, and forbade them from associating partners with Allah, from unjust killing, from fornication, and from drinking wine. As for 'Aza'il, when desire fell into his heart, he asked his Lord to relieve him and asked Him to raise him to heaven. He granted his request and raised him, and he prostrated for forty years. Then he raised his head, and he remained after that with his head bowed out of shyness before Allah, mighty and majestic.

As for the other two, they remained steadfast in that, and they used to become angry at people during the day. When evening came, they would mention the Greatest Name of Allah and ascend to heaven.

Qatadah said: "Not a month passed until they were tempted." They both said, all together, that this happened when they disputed one day over al-Zuhrah (Venus), who was among the most beautiful of women.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah honor his face) said: She was from the people of Persia, and she was a queen in her land. When they saw her, she captured their hearts, and they sought to seduce her, but she departed. Then she returned on the second day, and they did the same. She refused and said: "No, unless you worship what I worship, and pray to this idol, and kill a soul, and drink wine." They said: "There is no way to these things, for Allah has forbidden them to us." She departed, then returned on the third day with a cup of wine, and within themselves was the inclination toward her that was there. They sought to seduce her. She set before them what she had said the day before. They said: "Prayer to other than Allah is grave, killing a soul is grave, and the easiest of the three is drinking wine." So they gave in, had intercourse with the woman, and committed fornication. When they had finished, a man saw them, and they killed him.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: They prostrated to the idol, so Allah transformed al-Zuhrah into a star.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah honor his face), al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: She said to them: "You will not catch me until you tell me the thing by which you ascend to heaven." They said: "In the name of Allah, the Greatest." She said: "You will not catch me until you teach it to me." One of them said to his companion: "Teach it to her." He said: "I fear Allah." The other said: "Then where is the mercy of Allah?" So they taught her that. She spoke it and ascended to heaven, and Allah transformed her into a star.

According to the opinion of these people, she is al-Zuhrah herself, and they pinned it down: they said, "She is this red constellation, and her name in Persian is Nahid, and in Nabataean is Bayadhakht." What confirms the soundness of this opinion is what was narrated by Jabir from al-Tufayl from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Suhayl (Canopus), he would say: "May Allah curse Suhayl, for he was a tax-collector in Yemen, and may Allah curse al-Zuhrah, for she tempted two angels."

Mujahid said: I was with Ibn 'Umar one night, and he said to me: "Watch the constellation, meaning al-Zuhrah, and when it rises, wake me." When it rose, I woke him, and he began to look at it and to curse it severely. I said: "May Allah have mercy on you, you have cursed a star that is obedient and submissive. What is its fault that it should be cursed?" He said: "This one was a prostitute, and the two angels suffered what they suffered because of her."

Ibn 'Umar, when he saw al-Zuhrah, would say: "No welcome to her, nor any family." Abu 'Uthman [al-Marandi] narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the woman with whom the two angels were tempted was transformed, and she is this red constellation, meaning al-Zuhrah. He said: "He used to call her Bayadhakht." Others denied this opinion. They said: "al-Zuhrah is among the seven wandering planets (al-sayyarah) that Allah made supports for the world, and He swore by them, saying: ﴿So I swear by the receding, running, hiding stars﴾ [al-Takwir 81:16]."

We say: this woman who tempted Harut and Marut was a woman called Zuhrah for her beauty. When she committed prostitution, Allah transformed her into a shooting star (shihab). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw al-Zuhrah, he mentioned this woman because of the agreement of the two names, so he cursed her. Likewise Suhayl the tax-collector. And when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the star, he mentioned it and cursed it. What indicates this is what Qays ibn 'Abbad narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this story: "She was a woman who was preferred over people as al-Zuhrah is preferred over the rest of the stars." Ka'b al-Ahbar said similarly, and Allah knows best.

They said: When evening came upon Harut and Marut, after they had committed the sin, they intended to ascend to heaven, but their wings did not obey them. They knew what had befallen them, so they went to the prophet Idris (ﷺ) and told him their matter, and asked him to intercede for them with Allah, mighty and majestic. They said to him: "We have seen that there ascends for you from worship the same as ascends for all the people of the earth. So intercede for us with your Lord."

Idris did so, and Allah gave them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, knowing that it would end. So they are in Babylon, being punished.

The scholars differed about the manner of their punishment. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: They are suspended by their hair until the Hour.

Qatadah: They were bound from their feet up to the roots of their thighs.

Mujahid: A pit filled with fire, and they were placed in it, hanging upside down in chains.

'Umayr ibn Sa'd: They are upside down, being beaten with iron whips.

It is related that a man wanted to learn sorcery, so he went to Harut and Marut and found them hanging by their feet, their eyes blue, their skins blackened, with only the space of four fingers between their tongues and the water, and they were being punished with thirst. When he saw this, their state appalled him, so he said: "There is no god but Allah." It is forbidden to mention the name of Allah in that place. When they heard his words, they said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "A man from among the people." They said: "And from what nation are you?" He said: "From the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ)." They said: "Has Muhammad been sent?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Praise be to Allah," and they showed joy. The man said: "And why is your joy?" They said: "Because he is the Prophet of the Hour, and the end of our punishment has drawn near." They said: "And for this reason the angels seek forgiveness for the sons of Adam."

It is related from al-Awza'i, who said: The meaning is that Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: "O Jibril, describe Hell for me?"

Then he said: Indeed, God commanded it, and it was kindled over for a thousand years until it turned red; then it was kindled over for another thousand years until it turned yellow; then it was kindled over for another thousand years until it turned black. So it is black and dark: its flame gives no light and its embers give no glow. By the One who sent you with the truth, if a garment of the garments of the people of the Fire were shown to the people of the earth, they would all die; and if a single bucketful of its mirage were poured onto the earth, it would kill everyone who tasted it; and if a single cubit of the chain that God mentioned were placed on all the mountains of the earth, they would melt and not bear it. And if a man entered the Fire and was then brought out of it, the people of the earth would die from the stench of his smell and the disfigurement of his form and his bones. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) wept, and Jibril wept at his weeping, and said: "Do you weep, O Muhammad, when God has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?" He said: "Shall I not be a grateful servant?" [97]. "And why do you weep, O Jibril, when you are the Trustworthy Spirit, the trustee of God over His revelation?" He said: "I fear that I may be tested with what Harut and Marut were tested with. It is that which kept me from relying on my station with my Lord, lest I feel secure from His plotting." They kept weeping until they were called from the heavens: "O Jibril and O Muhammad, God has granted you security that you will disobey Him, so that He would punish you." [[Up to here in Bihar al-Anwar: 8/306, hadith 64.]] Thus Muhammad is preferred over the prophets as the excellence of Jibril is over the angels of the heavens.

﴿And they do not teach anyone﴾: "they" means the two angels; "anyone" is an indefinite noun with min as an added particle. They do not teach magic to anyone until they first advise him and forbid him, and say: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾: a test and an ordeal.

﴿So do not disbelieve﴾ by learning magic. The root of fitnah is testing. The Arabs say: "I fitanted the gold" when one puts it into fire to know its quality from its inferiority; and "the sun fatana the stone" when it blackens it.

As for why the word fitnah is singular though they are two: because fitnah is a verbal noun (masdar), and verbal nouns are not dualized or pluralized, as in their saying: "and upon their hearing" [2:7]. In the codex of Ubayy: "And they do not teach anyone until they say: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve," seven times.

Al-Suddi and Ata said: If he refuses except to learn, they say to him: "Go to this ash and urinate on it." Then a bright light rises into the sky, which is the knowledge; and something black descends until it enters his ears, resembling smoke, and that is the anger of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Mujahid said: No one can reach Harut and Marut, and a devil goes back and forth between them with each question, one contradiction each time.

Yazid ibn al-Asamm said: Al-Mukhtar was asked: "Does anyone see Harut and Marut today?" He said: "Since Babel was overturned, its other overturning, no one has seen them."

Qatadah said: Magic is of two kinds: magic that the devils teach, and magic that Harut and Marut teach, which is the statement of God, exalted, ﴿and they learn from the two what they use to separate a man from his wife﴾, namely that each one is taken from his companion and each is made hateful to the other.

Regarding "al-mar'" (the man) there are four readings. Al-Hasan read "al-marr" with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the ra, making it a substitute for the hamza. Al-Zuhri read "al-muru'" with a damma on the mim and the hamza. Ya'qub related from his grandfather: with a kasra on the mim and the hamza. The rest read: with a fatha on the mim and the hamza.

As for the manner of their teaching magic, a comprehensive report has come about it: what Hisham ibn 'Urwah related from his father from 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): she said: A woman from the people of Dumat al-Jandal came to me, seeking the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after his death, in the early period, asking him about something she had entered into concerning magic. 'A'ishah said to 'Urwah: "O nephew, I saw her weeping when she did not find the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she wept so much that I pitied her, and I feared she had perished." She said: "I had a husband who was absent from me, so I went to an old woman and complained to her of that. She said: 'If you do what I order you, I will make him come to you.' When night came, she brought me two black dogs; I mounted one and mounted the other, and before long we stood at Babel. There were two men hanging by their feet, and they said: 'What brings you?' I said: 'I want to learn magic.'"

They said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve and return." I refused and said: "No."

They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it." I went, but I was frightened and did not do it, and I returned to them. They said: "Did you do it?" I said: "Yes." They said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "I saw nothing."

They said: "You did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve." I refused. They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it."

I went, my skin prickled and I feared, then I returned and said: "I have done it." They said: "What did you see?" I said: "I saw nothing."

They said: "You lied, you did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve, for you are at the head of your affair." I refused.

They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it." I went and urinated in it, and I saw a horseman covered in iron come out of me, rise into the sky, and vanish from me until I could no longer see him. I came to them and said: "I have done it." They said: "What did you see?" I said: "I saw a horseman covered in iron come out of me and rise into the sky until I could not see him." They said: "You have spoken truly; that was your faith going out of you. Go to the woman and say to her: 'By God, I know nothing, and he said nothing to me.'" She said: "Yes indeed." They said: "You will not want anything but that it will be." Take this wheat, sow it." I sowed it and said: "Sprout," and it sprouted; I said: "Grow ears," and it grew ears; I said: "Dry," and it dried; I said: "Grind," and it ground; I said: "Bake," and it baked. When I saw that I did not want anything but that it happened, I was struck with dismay and regret, and by God, O Mother of the Believers, I never did anything at all, nor will I ever do it."

As for how it is permissible to teach magic to the angels, and the meaning of the verse and its interpretation in the correct sense: Some of them said: They did not intentionally teach magic, but they described it, explained its falsehood, and commanded people to avoid it. "Know" and "teach" have one meaning here, and in this there is wisdom: if a questioner asked about adultery, it would be necessary to inform him and to teach him that it is forbidden. Likewise, the two angels informing people and commanding them to avoid it after informing and reporting that it is disbelief and forbidden, so the wretched one learns from them, while the lawful description of them and the abandonment of their admonition and counsel remain. On this interpretation, learning magic is not disbelief; rather, practicing it is disbelief, just as one who knows adultery does not sin, but only the one who practices it sins.

The other view, and the more correct one: God, exalted, tested people through the two angels at that time, and made the test in disbelief and faith such that whoever accepted learning magic would disbelieve by learning it, and would believe by abandoning learning. This is because magic had spread throughout the whole community, and the two teachers would increase in punishment through teaching it. Thus it becomes a trial for both teacher and learner, and God may test His servants with whatever He wills, just as He tested the Children of Israel with the river in His statement: ﴿Indeed God will test you with a river﴾ [2:249]. What indicates this is His statement: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾. These two views were related by al-Zajjaj, who relied on them.

God, exalted, said: ﴿And they could not harm anyone with it﴾: "anyone" with min as an added particle, ﴿except by the permission of God﴾ [or except by the decree of God, or except by the permission of God, that is, in sight and hearing] [note from the margin of the manuscript]: that is, by His knowledge, decree, will, and creation [the magician works magic and nothing happens unless it is willed].

﴿And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them﴾: that is, magic. Ubayd ibn Umayr read: "what harms them" from adarra, yadurru.

﴿And they certainly knew﴾: meaning the Jews, ﴿that whoever purchased it﴾: chose magic, ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾: that is, in Paradise, ﴿of any portion﴾: any allotment.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾: no religion and no standing with God.

Ibn Abbas: no sustenance; and it was said: no deliverance.

Umayyah said: "They call for destruction therein; they have no portion except garments of pitch and shackles," that is, no deliverance for them.

﴿And how evil is what they sold themselves for﴾: they sold for it the portion of their souls when they chose magic and disbelief over religion and truth, ﴿if only they knew﴾. ﴿And if only they had believed﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, ﴿and feared God﴾ by avoiding Judaism and magic, ﴿a reward from God would have been better﴾ [it is also permissible to read mathuba with a fatha on the mim and the waw, like mashurah, a verbal noun from thawab; note from the margin], meaning God's reward to them, ﴿had they known﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 100–103 (part 1 of 2):

Ayn al-Istifham (the interrogative hamza) entered upon the conjunctive waw in أَوَكُلَّما (awa-kullama, "Is it then that every time..."), just as it enters upon the fa' in His saying ﴿Will you then make the deaf hear?﴾ [Yunus 10:42] and ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as protectors?﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50], and upon thumma (then) in His saying ﴿What! And when it has occurred?﴾ [Yunus 10:51], and similar cases.

Ibn al-Sammak al-'Adawi recited it with the waw of conjunction vowelless (awkullama), and kullama in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf). ﴿They made a covenant﴾ ('ahadu 'ahdan), meaning the Jews.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned, [they disregarded] what Allah had taken from them in covenant and what He had enjoined upon them concerning him.

Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Allah has made no covenant or pact with us concerning Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse. What clarifies this is the reading of Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi: "Whenever they were given a covenant, Allah cursed them." The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:187], and so on.

Others said: The Jews made a pact that if Muhammad emerged, they would certainly believe in him and would stand with him against the polytheists of the Arabs and expel them from their lands. But when he was sent, they broke the covenant and disbelieved in him. The evidence and parallel for this is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:101].

'Ata' said: These are the covenants that existed between the Messenger of Allah and the Jews, which they broke, like the act of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. The evidence is His saying: ﴿those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant each time﴾ [al-Anfal 8:56].

*Nabadhahu* means he rejected it. In the reading of 'Abdullah, it means he broke it (naqadahu).

*Fariqun minhum* means groups of the Jews.

*Bal aktharuhum la yu'minun* ("Rather, most of them do not believe"). The root meaning of *nabadh* is to throw away and reject. Al-Zajjaj recited:

"I looked at its title and cast it away,
as you cast away a sandal worn out from your sandals."

This is an example of someone who makes light of a thing and does not act upon it. The Arabs say: "Put this behind your back, behind your ear, and under your foot," meaning: leave it and turn away from it. Allah says: ﴿and you have made Him a thing cast behind your backs﴾ [Hud 11:92]. Al-Farra' recited:

"Tamim ibn Qays, let not my need
be behind the back, nor let its answer be cared for by me."

Al-Sha'bi said: It is before them; they read it, but they cast away acting upon it.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, and adorned it with gold and silver, but they did not treat its lawful as lawful nor its unlawful as unlawful. That is the *nabdh* (casting away).

*Wattaba'u*: that is, the Jews.

*Ma tatlu al-shayatin*: that is, what the devils recited (*ma talat al-shayatin*).

Like the saying of the poet:

"When you pass by his grave, then slaughter at it
a dark-eyed camel and every hunting horse.
And sprinkle the sides of his grave with their blood,
for indeed both maidservants and sacrificial animals have wept for him."

It is related from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl that he was asked about this verse and said: It is an abbreviated and implied construction, its estimated meaning being: "and they followed what the devils had been reciting," that is, reading it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] to follow and act upon it.

'Ata' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: [it means] to narrate and speak of it.

Yaman said: [it means] to transmit it.

Al-Hasan recited *al-shayatun* with a waw in the nominative case throughout the whole Qur'an.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Kharazanji say:

He was asked about al-Hasan's reading and said: It is an art and a beauty, according to most people of literature. However, al-Asma'i claimed that he heard a Bedouin say: "The garden of so-and-so has gardens around it" (*bustanun*/*bustanun*, in the oblique plural form *bustanun*).

*'Ala mulki Sulayman*: that is, during the reign and time of Sulayman, as in the saying of Abu al-Najm:

"Then it is over the horizon like the eye of a squinting man."

That is, on the horizon.

*Al-Mulk* is the complete power and its firm establishment.

Al-Zajjaj said, regarding the story of the verse: the devils wrote sorcery and talismanic arts (*nayranjat*) in the name of Asif. "This is what Asif ibn Barkhiya taught Sulayman the king." Then they placed them under his prayer mat when Allah removed his kingdom, and Sulayman did not perceive it. When he died, they extracted them from under his prayer mat.

The people said: "It was only by this that Sulayman ruled you, so learn it." As for the scholars and righteous ones of the Children of Israel, they said: "God forbid that this should be the knowledge of Sulayman. If this were his knowledge, Sulayman would have been ruined."

As for the base people, they said: "This is the knowledge of Sulayman," and they turned to learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Blame fell upon Sulayman, and their condition remained thus until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and revealed the excuse of Sulayman (peace be upon him) through his tongue and showed his innocence of what had been charged against him. Then they said: ﴿and they followed what the devils recited﴾, to the end of the verse. This is the saying of al-Ka'bi.

Al-Suddi said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and sit in the places of hearing, listening to the speech of the angels about what would happen on earth, such as death or other things. Then they would come to the soothsayers and mix what they had heard with lies and falsehood, seventy words for every word, and inform them of that. The people wrote this down, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn knew the unseen. So Sulayman sent out among the people, gathered those books, placed them in a chest, and buried them beneath his throne, saying: "I will not hear anyone say that the devils know the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Sulayman died and the scholars who knew the matter of Sulayman had passed away, and the burying of the books had been forgotten, a later generation came, and a devil took the form of a man. He came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I guide you to a treasure that never fails?"

They said: "Yes." He said: "Dig beneath the throne." He went with them, showed them the place, and stood aside. They said: "Come closer." He said: "No, but here. If you do not find it, then kill me." This is because no devil could approach the throne without being burned. They dug and found those books. When they took them out, the devil said: "Sulayman used to control the jinn, mankind, and the birds by this." Then the devil flew off and departed. It spread among the people that Sulayman had been a sorcerer, and the Children of Israel adopted those books. That is why sorcery is found most among the Jews. When Muhammad (ﷺ) came, the Jews disputed with him by means of them, and Allah cleared Sulayman of that and revealed this verse. [See Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 1/106.]

'Ikrimah said: Sulayman (peace be upon him) would not rise one morning without a tree sprouting in his prayer niche (mihrab) in Bayt al-Maqdis. He would ask it: "What is your name?" The tree would say: "My name is such-and-such." He would say: "For what disease are you?" It would say: "For such-and-such." He would order it to be cut down and placed in the storehouse, and some of it would be planted in gardens. Then a Syrian carob tree (kharnubah) sprouted, and he said to it: "What are you?" It said: "I am the carob." He said: "For what did you sprout?" It said: "For the ruin of your mosque." Sulayman said: "Allah would not ruin it while I am alive." "You are the one upon whose face will be my death and the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis." He uprooted it, planted it in a wall of his, and it did not grow until he died. The people began to say, in their contentment: "If only we had someone like Sulayman."

The devils wrote a book and placed it in Sulayman's prayer place. They said to the people: "Shall I guide you to what he used to heal with?" They went and extracted that book, and in it was sorcery and incantations. So Allah revealed in this verse concerning what the devils and the Jews did, upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿and they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Sulayman﴾.

﴿Sulayman did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾: for sorcery is disbelief.

*Wa lakinna al-shayatina kafaru*: the people of Kufa and Syria read it with the *nun* lightened and *al-shayatinu* in the nominative, and likewise in *Wa lakinna Allaha qatalahum* and *Wa lakinna Allaha rama* in al-Anfal [8:17].

The rest read it with the *nun* doubled and what follows it in the accusative. *Lakinna* is a word with two meanings: negation of a past report and affirmation of a future report. It is composed of three words: originally *la kana*, *la* as negation, *ka* as address, and *inna* in the accusative and conjunctive. The hamza was dropped because of heaviness. It may be doubled or lightened. When doubled, it puts in the accusative the nouns that follow it, as the heavy *inna* does. When lightened, it puts in the nominative what the light *inna* puts in the nominative.

*Yu'allimuna al-nasa al-sihra* ("they taught people sorcery"). Some said: *al-sihr* means knowledge and eloquence; the evidence is the saying of a poet: "Ibn al-Sami'" ... that is, the knowledgeable one (*al-'alim*).

Others said: it is deception with a thing until the one who imagines it thinks that it is a thing, though it has no reality, like a mirage that deceives the one who sees it and disappoints the one who hopes for it. Allah says: ﴿It is imagined to him, by their sorcery, that they were running﴾ [Taha 20:66].

*Wa ma unzila 'ala al-malakayni*: the position of what follows the verb "they followed" (*wattaba'u*) is governed by its meaning, as "they did not know what was revealed to the two angels." Its meaning is: "They followed what was revealed to the two angels." It is permissible for it to be in the accusative by virtue of "they followed," the estimate being: "and they followed what was revealed to the two angels." Some made *ma* a negation, and then it has no position in the sentence, meaning: sorcery was not sent down upon the two angels, as the Jews claimed; rather, they [the devils] were teaching people [...] of their own selves [a word is unreadable in the original manuscript]. The first opinion is more sound.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir read *malakayni* with a *kasra* on the *lam*. They said: The two were two men, sorcerers, who were in Babylon, from among the angels, who did not teach people sorcery. al-Hasan explained them, saying: "Two Persian men in Babylon." Babylon is Iraq. It was named Babil because of the confusion (*tabalbul*) of tongues there when the palace of Nimrod fell, that is, their dispersal.

Or, Allah tested people by the two angels at that time: whoever was wretched by learning sorcery from them would disbelieve through it; whoever was blessed by abandoning it would remain in faith. The two teachers would thereby increase in punishment for teaching. In this there is a trial of the teacher and the learner. Allah tests His servants with what He wills, as He wills, for His is the command and the judgment.

Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: Babil was named so because when Allah wished to make the tongues of the sons of Adam differ, He sent a wind that gathered them from every horizon to Babil. Allah confused their tongues, and no one knew what the other was saying. Then that wind scattered them in the lands. It is not declined (*la yanșarif*) because it is the name of a well-known place.

*Harut and Marut* are two Syriac names, in the genitive position as an explanation of the two angels, being in apposition to them, except that they are in the accusative because of their foreignness and definiteness. Their story, as mentioned by Ibn 'Abbas and the exegetes, is that the angels saw the evil deeds and numerous sins of the sons of Adam ascending to heaven. This was in the time of Idris. They reproached them for that and invoked [curses] upon them. They said: "These are the ones You placed on the earth and chose, and they disobey You."

Allah, mighty and majestic, said to them: "If I had sent you down to earth and placed in you what I placed in them, you would have committed what they committed."

They said: "Glory be to You, it would not be fitting for us to disobey You." Allah said: "Choose two angels from among your best, then send them down to earth." They chose Harut and Marut, who were among the most righteous and the most devoted of the angels.

Al-Kalbi said: Allah said to them: "Choose three." [They chose] 'Azza, who is Harut, and 'Azaya, who is Marut.

Their names were changed when they committed the sin, as the name of Iblis was changed, and 'Aza'il. Allah placed in them the desire He had placed in the sons of Adam. He sent them down to earth and commanded them to judge between people with truth, and forbade them from associating partners with Allah, from unjust killing, from fornication, and from drinking wine. As for 'Aza'il, when desire fell into his heart, he asked his Lord to relieve him and asked Him to raise him to heaven. He granted his request and raised him, and he prostrated for forty years. Then he raised his head, and he remained after that with his head bowed out of shyness before Allah, mighty and majestic.

As for the other two, they remained steadfast in that, and they used to become angry at people during the day. When evening came, they would mention the Greatest Name of Allah and ascend to heaven.

Qatadah said: "Not a month passed until they were tempted." They both said, all together, that this happened when they disputed one day over al-Zuhrah (Venus), who was among the most beautiful of women.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah honor his face) said: She was from the people of Persia, and she was a queen in her land. When they saw her, she captured their hearts, and they sought to seduce her, but she departed. Then she returned on the second day, and they did the same. She refused and said: "No, unless you worship what I worship, and pray to this idol, and kill a soul, and drink wine." They said: "There is no way to these things, for Allah has forbidden them to us." She departed, then returned on the third day with a cup of wine, and within themselves was the inclination toward her that was there. They sought to seduce her. She set before them what she had said the day before. They said: "Prayer to other than Allah is grave, killing a soul is grave, and the easiest of the three is drinking wine." So they gave in, had intercourse with the woman, and committed fornication. When they had finished, a man saw them, and they killed him.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: They prostrated to the idol, so Allah transformed al-Zuhrah into a star.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah honor his face), al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: She said to them: "You will not catch me until you tell me the thing by which you ascend to heaven." They said: "In the name of Allah, the Greatest." She said: "You will not catch me until you teach it to me." One of them said to his companion: "Teach it to her." He said: "I fear Allah." The other said: "Then where is the mercy of Allah?" So they taught her that. She spoke it and ascended to heaven, and Allah transformed her into a star.

According to the opinion of these people, she is al-Zuhrah herself, and they pinned it down: they said, "She is this red constellation, and her name in Persian is Nahid, and in Nabataean is Bayadhakht." What confirms the soundness of this opinion is what was narrated by Jabir from al-Tufayl from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Suhayl (Canopus), he would say: "May Allah curse Suhayl, for he was a tax-collector in Yemen, and may Allah curse al-Zuhrah, for she tempted two angels."

Mujahid said: I was with Ibn 'Umar one night, and he said to me: "Watch the constellation, meaning al-Zuhrah, and when it rises, wake me." When it rose, I woke him, and he began to look at it and to curse it severely. I said: "May Allah have mercy on you, you have cursed a star that is obedient and submissive. What is its fault that it should be cursed?" He said: "This one was a prostitute, and the two angels suffered what they suffered because of her."

Ibn 'Umar, when he saw al-Zuhrah, would say: "No welcome to her, nor any family." Abu 'Uthman [al-Marandi] narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the woman with whom the two angels were tempted was transformed, and she is this red constellation, meaning al-Zuhrah. He said: "He used to call her Bayadhakht." Others denied this opinion. They said: "al-Zuhrah is among the seven wandering planets (al-sayyarah) that Allah made supports for the world, and He swore by them, saying: ﴿So I swear by the receding, running, hiding stars﴾ [al-Takwir 81:16]."

We say: this woman who tempted Harut and Marut was a woman called Zuhrah for her beauty. When she committed prostitution, Allah transformed her into a shooting star (shihab). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw al-Zuhrah, he mentioned this woman because of the agreement of the two names, so he cursed her. Likewise Suhayl the tax-collector. And when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the star, he mentioned it and cursed it. What indicates this is what Qays ibn 'Abbad narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this story: "She was a woman who was preferred over people as al-Zuhrah is preferred over the rest of the stars." Ka'b al-Ahbar said similarly, and Allah knows best.

They said: When evening came upon Harut and Marut, after they had committed the sin, they intended to ascend to heaven, but their wings did not obey them. They knew what had befallen them, so they went to the prophet Idris (ﷺ) and told him their matter, and asked him to intercede for them with Allah, mighty and majestic. They said to him: "We have seen that there ascends for you from worship the same as ascends for all the people of the earth. So intercede for us with your Lord."

Idris did so, and Allah gave them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, knowing that it would end. So they are in Babylon, being punished.

The scholars differed about the manner of their punishment. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: They are suspended by their hair until the Hour.

Qatadah: They were bound from their feet up to the roots of their thighs.

Mujahid: A pit filled with fire, and they were placed in it, hanging upside down in chains.

'Umayr ibn Sa'd: They are upside down, being beaten with iron whips.

It is related that a man wanted to learn sorcery, so he went to Harut and Marut and found them hanging by their feet, their eyes blue, their skins blackened, with only the space of four fingers between their tongues and the water, and they were being punished with thirst. When he saw this, their state appalled him, so he said: "There is no god but Allah." It is forbidden to mention the name of Allah in that place. When they heard his words, they said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "A man from among the people." They said: "And from what nation are you?" He said: "From the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ)." They said: "Has Muhammad been sent?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Praise be to Allah," and they showed joy. The man said: "And why is your joy?" They said: "Because he is the Prophet of the Hour, and the end of our punishment has drawn near." They said: "And for this reason the angels seek forgiveness for the sons of Adam."

It is related from al-Awza'i, who said: The meaning is that Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said to him: "O Jibril, describe Hell for me?"

Then he said: Indeed, God commanded it, and it was kindled over for a thousand years until it turned red; then it was kindled over for another thousand years until it turned yellow; then it was kindled over for another thousand years until it turned black. So it is black and dark: its flame gives no light and its embers give no glow. By the One who sent you with the truth, if a garment of the garments of the people of the Fire were shown to the people of the earth, they would all die; and if a single bucketful of its mirage were poured onto the earth, it would kill everyone who tasted it; and if a single cubit of the chain that God mentioned were placed on all the mountains of the earth, they would melt and not bear it. And if a man entered the Fire and was then brought out of it, the people of the earth would die from the stench of his smell and the disfigurement of his form and his bones. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) wept, and Jibril wept at his weeping, and said: "Do you weep, O Muhammad, when God has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?" He said: "Shall I not be a grateful servant?" [97]. "And why do you weep, O Jibril, when you are the Trustworthy Spirit, the trustee of God over His revelation?" He said: "I fear that I may be tested with what Harut and Marut were tested with. It is that which kept me from relying on my station with my Lord, lest I feel secure from His plotting." They kept weeping until they were called from the heavens: "O Jibril and O Muhammad, God has granted you security that you will disobey Him, so that He would punish you." [[Up to here in Bihar al-Anwar: 8/306, hadith 64.]] Thus Muhammad is preferred over the prophets as the excellence of Jibril is over the angels of the heavens.

﴿And they do not teach anyone﴾: "they" means the two angels; "anyone" is an indefinite noun with min as an added particle. They do not teach magic to anyone until they first advise him and forbid him, and say: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾: a test and an ordeal.

﴿So do not disbelieve﴾ by learning magic. The root of fitnah is testing. The Arabs say: "I fitanted the gold" when one puts it into fire to know its quality from its inferiority; and "the sun fatana the stone" when it blackens it.

As for why the word fitnah is singular though they are two: because fitnah is a verbal noun (masdar), and verbal nouns are not dualized or pluralized, as in their saying: "and upon their hearing" [2:7]. In the codex of Ubayy: "And they do not teach anyone until they say: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve," seven times.

Al-Suddi and Ata said: If he refuses except to learn, they say to him: "Go to this ash and urinate on it." Then a bright light rises into the sky, which is the knowledge; and something black descends until it enters his ears, resembling smoke, and that is the anger of God, Mighty and Majestic.

Mujahid said: No one can reach Harut and Marut, and a devil goes back and forth between them with each question, one contradiction each time.

Yazid ibn al-Asamm said: Al-Mukhtar was asked: "Does anyone see Harut and Marut today?" He said: "Since Babel was overturned, its other overturning, no one has seen them."

Qatadah said: Magic is of two kinds: magic that the devils teach, and magic that Harut and Marut teach, which is the statement of God, exalted, ﴿and they learn from the two what they use to separate a man from his wife﴾, namely that each one is taken from his companion and each is made hateful to the other.

Regarding "al-mar'" (the man) there are four readings. Al-Hasan read "al-marr" with a fatha on the mim and a shadda on the ra, making it a substitute for the hamza. Al-Zuhri read "al-muru'" with a damma on the mim and the hamza. Ya'qub related from his grandfather: with a kasra on the mim and the hamza. The rest read: with a fatha on the mim and the hamza.

As for the manner of their teaching magic, a comprehensive report has come about it: what Hisham ibn 'Urwah related from his father from 'A'ishah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): she said: A woman from the people of Dumat al-Jandal came to me, seeking the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after his death, in the early period, asking him about something she had entered into concerning magic. 'A'ishah said to 'Urwah: "O nephew, I saw her weeping when she did not find the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she wept so much that I pitied her, and I feared she had perished." She said: "I had a husband who was absent from me, so I went to an old woman and complained to her of that. She said: 'If you do what I order you, I will make him come to you.' When night came, she brought me two black dogs; I mounted one and mounted the other, and before long we stood at Babel. There were two men hanging by their feet, and they said: 'What brings you?' I said: 'I want to learn magic.'"

They said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve and return." I refused and said: "No."

They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it." I went, but I was frightened and did not do it, and I returned to them. They said: "Did you do it?" I said: "Yes." They said: "Did you see anything?" I said: "I saw nothing."

They said: "You did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve." I refused. They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it."

I went, my skin prickled and I feared, then I returned and said: "I have done it." They said: "What did you see?" I said: "I saw nothing."

They said: "You lied, you did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve, for you are at the head of your affair." I refused.

They said: "Go to that oven and urinate in it." I went and urinated in it, and I saw a horseman covered in iron come out of me, rise into the sky, and vanish from me until I could no longer see him. I came to them and said: "I have done it." They said: "What did you see?" I said: "I saw a horseman covered in iron come out of me and rise into the sky until I could not see him." They said: "You have spoken truly; that was your faith going out of you. Go to the woman and say to her: 'By God, I know nothing, and he said nothing to me.'" She said: "Yes indeed." They said: "You will not want anything but that it will be." Take this wheat, sow it." I sowed it and said: "Sprout," and it sprouted; I said: "Grow ears," and it grew ears; I said: "Dry," and it dried; I said: "Grind," and it ground; I said: "Bake," and it baked. When I saw that I did not want anything but that it happened, I was struck with dismay and regret, and by God, O Mother of the Believers, I never did anything at all, nor will I ever do it."

As for how it is permissible to teach magic to the angels, and the meaning of the verse and its interpretation in the correct sense: Some of them said: They did not intentionally teach magic, but they described it, explained its falsehood, and commanded people to avoid it. "Know" and "teach" have one meaning here, and in this there is wisdom: if a questioner asked about adultery, it would be necessary to inform him and to teach him that it is forbidden. Likewise, the two angels informing people and commanding them to avoid it after informing and reporting that it is disbelief and forbidden, so the wretched one learns from them, while the lawful description of them and the abandonment of their admonition and counsel remain. On this interpretation, learning magic is not disbelief; rather, practicing it is disbelief, just as one who knows adultery does not sin, but only the one who practices it sins.

The other view, and the more correct one: God, exalted, tested people through the two angels at that time, and made the test in disbelief and faith such that whoever accepted learning magic would disbelieve by learning it, and would believe by abandoning learning. This is because magic had spread throughout the whole community, and the two teachers would increase in punishment through teaching it. Thus it becomes a trial for both teacher and learner, and God may test His servants with whatever He wills, just as He tested the Children of Israel with the river in His statement: ﴿Indeed God will test you with a river﴾ [2:249]. What indicates this is His statement: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾. These two views were related by al-Zajjaj, who relied on them.

God, exalted, said: ﴿And they could not harm anyone with it﴾: "anyone" with min as an added particle, ﴿except by the permission of God﴾ [or except by the decree of God, or except by the permission of God, that is, in sight and hearing] [note from the margin of the manuscript]: that is, by His knowledge, decree, will, and creation [the magician works magic and nothing happens unless it is willed].

﴿And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them﴾: that is, magic. Ubayd ibn Umayr read: "what harms them" from adarra, yadurru.

﴿And they certainly knew﴾: meaning the Jews, ﴿that whoever purchased it﴾: chose magic, ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾: that is, in Paradise, ﴿of any portion﴾: any allotment.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿has no share in the Hereafter﴾: no religion and no standing with God.

Ibn Abbas: no sustenance; and it was said: no deliverance.

Umayyah said: "They call for destruction therein; they have no portion except garments of pitch and shackles," that is, no deliverance for them.

﴿And how evil is what they sold themselves for﴾: they sold for it the portion of their souls when they chose magic and disbelief over religion and truth, ﴿if only they knew﴾. ﴿And if only they had believed﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, ﴿and feared God﴾ by avoiding Judaism and magic, ﴿a reward from God would have been better﴾ [it is also permissible to read mathuba with a fatha on the mim and the waw, like mashurah, a verbal noun from thawab; note from the margin], meaning God's reward to them, ﴿had they known﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 100–103 (part 1 of 2):

Ayn al-Istifham (the interrogative hamza) entered upon the conjunctive waw in أَوَكُلَّما (awa-kullama, "Is it then that every time..."), just as it enters upon the fa' in His saying ﴿Will you then make the deaf hear?﴾ [Yunus 10:42] and ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as protectors?﴾ [al-Kahf 18:50], and upon thumma (then) in His saying ﴿What! And when it has occurred?﴾ [Yunus 10:51], and similar cases.

Ibn al-Sammak al-'Adawi recited it with the waw of conjunction vowelless (awkullama), and kullama in the accusative as an adverb of time (zarf). ﴿They made a covenant﴾ ('ahadu 'ahdan), meaning the Jews.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was mentioned, [they disregarded] what Allah had taken from them in covenant and what He had enjoined upon them concerning him.

Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Allah has made no covenant or pact with us concerning Muhammad." So Allah revealed this verse. What clarifies this is the reading of Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi: "Whenever they were given a covenant, Allah cursed them." The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:187], and so on.

Others said: The Jews made a pact that if Muhammad emerged, they would certainly believe in him and would stand with him against the polytheists of the Arabs and expel them from their lands. But when he was sent, they broke the covenant and disbelieved in him. The evidence and parallel for this is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And when there came to them a Messenger from Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:101].

'Ata' said: These are the covenants that existed between the Messenger of Allah and the Jews, which they broke, like the act of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. The evidence is His saying: ﴿those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant each time﴾ [al-Anfal 8:56].

*Nabadhahu* means he rejected it. In the reading of 'Abdullah, it means he broke it (naqadahu).

*Fariqun minhum* means groups of the Jews.

*Bal aktharuhum la yu'minun* ("Rather, most of them do not believe"). The root meaning of *nabadh* is to throw away and reject. Al-Zajjaj recited:

"I looked at its title and cast it away,
as you cast away a sandal worn out from your sandals."

This is an example of someone who makes light of a thing and does not act upon it. The Arabs say: "Put this behind your back, behind your ear, and under your foot," meaning: leave it and turn away from it. Allah says: ﴿and you have made Him a thing cast behind your backs﴾ [Hud 11:92]. Al-Farra' recited:

"Tamim ibn Qays, let not my need
be behind the back, nor let its answer be cared for by me."

Al-Sha'bi said: It is before them; they read it, but they cast away acting upon it.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, and adorned it with gold and silver, but they did not treat its lawful as lawful nor its unlawful as unlawful. That is the *nabdh* (casting away).

*Wattaba'u*: that is, the Jews.

*Ma tatlu al-shayatin*: that is, what the devils recited (*ma talat al-shayatin*).

Like the saying of the poet:

"When you pass by his grave, then slaughter at it
a dark-eyed camel and every hunting horse.
And sprinkle the sides of his grave with their blood,
for indeed both maidservants and sacrificial animals have wept for him."

It is related from al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl that he was asked about this verse and said: It is an abbreviated and implied construction, its estimated meaning being: "and they followed what the devils had been reciting," that is, reading it.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] to follow and act upon it.

'Ata' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: [it means] to narrate and speak of it.

Yaman said: [it means] to transmit it.

Al-Hasan recited *al-shayatun* with a waw in the nominative case throughout the whole Qur'an.

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Kharazanji say:

He was asked about al-Hasan's reading and said: It is an art and a beauty, according to most people of literature. However, al-Asma'i claimed that he heard a Bedouin say: "The garden of so-and-so has gardens around it" (*bustanun*/*bustanun*, in the oblique plural form *bustanun*).

*'Ala mulki Sulayman*: that is, during the reign and time of Sulayman, as in the saying of Abu al-Najm:

"Then it is over the horizon like the eye of a squinting man."

That is, on the horizon.

*Al-Mulk* is the complete power and its firm establishment.

Al-Zajjaj said, regarding the story of the verse: the devils wrote sorcery and talismanic arts (*nayranjat*) in the name of Asif. "This is what Asif ibn Barkhiya taught Sulayman the king." Then they placed them under his prayer mat when Allah removed his kingdom, and Sulayman did not perceive it. When he died, they extracted them from under his prayer mat.

The people said: "It was only by this that Sulayman ruled you, so learn it." As for the scholars and righteous ones of the Children of Israel, they said: "God forbid that this should be the knowledge of Sulayman. If this were his knowledge, Sulayman would have been ruined."

As for the base people, they said: "This is the knowledge of Sulayman," and they turned to learning it and abandoned the books of their prophets. Blame fell upon Sulayman, and their condition remained thus until Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and revealed the excuse of Sulayman (peace be upon him) through his tongue and showed his innocence of what had been charged against him. Then they said: ﴿and they followed what the devils recited﴾, to the end of the verse. This is the saying of al-Ka'bi.

Al-Suddi said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven and sit in the places of hearing, listening to the speech of the angels about what would happen on earth, such as death or other things. Then they would come to the soothsayers and mix what they had heard with lies and falsehood, seventy words for every word, and inform them of that. The people wrote this down, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn knew the unseen. So Sulayman sent out among the people, gathered those books, placed them in a chest, and buried them beneath his throne, saying: "I will not hear anyone say that the devils know the unseen except that I will strike off his neck." When Sulayman died and the scholars who knew the matter of Sulayman had passed away, and the burying of the books had been forgotten, a later generation came, and a devil took the form of a man. He came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I guide you to a treasure that never fails?"

They said: "Yes." He said: "Dig beneath the throne." He went with them, showed them the place, and stood aside. They said: "Come closer." He said: "No, but here. If you do not find it, then kill me." This is because no devil could approach the throne without being burned. They dug and found those books. When they took them out, the devil said: "Sulayman used to control the jinn, mankind, and the birds by this." Then the devil flew off and departed.
