The root of dhurriyyah is "young children," derived from dharr because of their multitude; it was also said it is from dharr, meaning creation, and the hamza was lightened and doubling (tashdid) was introduced in place of the hamza, as in al-bariyyah.
It was said: it is from dharw, and in it there are three dialects:
dhurriyyah with a kasra on the dhal, which is the reading of Zayd ibn Thabit; dhurriyyah with a fatha, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; and dhurriyyah with a damma, which is the reading of the common people.
Allah said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, that is, it does not reach or attain.
﴿My covenant (ʿahdī) the wrongdoers﴾: in it there are three readings: ʿahdī al-ẓālimūn, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Talhah ibn Musarrif; ʿahdī al-ẓālimīn with the yā' made a standing (irtijāl) yā', which is the reading of Abu Raja', al-A'mash, and Hamzah; and ʿahdiya al-ẓālimīn with a fatha on the yā', which is the reading of the common people. They differed about this covenant: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said:
"My mercy."
al-Dahhak: "My obedience." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾ [2:40].
al-Suddi: "Fulfilment." Its evidence is His words: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its binding﴾ [2:27].
Mujahid: "It is not the wrongdoer who is to be obeyed in his wrongdoing."
Abu Hudhayfah: "My trust." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you pledge﴾ [16:91].
Abu 'Ubayd: "My wishes (amani)." Its evidence is His words: ﴿So complete for them their covenant until their term﴾ [9:4]. It was also said: "My faith (iman)," and its evidence is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan﴾ [36:60].
﴿And when We made the House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah.
﴿a place of return (mathaba)﴾: a place of return (marji'an); mathab and mathabah are one, like maqam and maqamah. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning a refuge and a sanctuary.
Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak: [they return] to it from every direction and perform Hajj, and they never tire of it; for no one visits it without wishing to return to it.
Qatadah and 'Ikrimah: "a gathering place." Talhah ibn Musarrif recited: "mathabat" in the plural.
﴿for the people and a sanctuary (amnan)﴾: a place of safety, where they are secure.
Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever commits an offence outside the Haram and then takes refuge in the Haram is secure from being attacked within it; but he is not sheltered, nor mixed with, nor traded with, and he is kept apart; when he leaves it, the legal punishment (hadd) is carried out upon him. And whoever commits an offence within the Haram, the legal punishment is carried out upon him within it.
﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾: Shaybah, Ibn 'Amir, Nafi', al-A'raj, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Salam recited: "wa-attakhadha" with a fatha on the kha', as a statement; and the rest recited with a kasra, as a command.
Ibn Kaysan said: They mention that the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ passed by the Station, and with him was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this not the station of our father Ibrahim?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then should we not take it as a place of prayer?"
He said: "I have not been commanded to do that."
[105] [[Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 37; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/174.]]
Then the sun had not set on that day before this was revealed: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾.
From Anas ibn Malik: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "My Lord agreed with me in three things."
I said: "Would that you took the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer," and Allah sent down: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾. And I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked come in to you; if only you would screen the Mothers of the Believers." So Allah sent down the verse of hijab. He said:
"And something reached me that happened between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﴿ﷺ﴾, so I rebuked them and I kept saying to them: 'Either you refrain from the Messenger of Allah, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you,' until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers."
And Umm Salamah said: "O 'Umar, is there not in the Messenger of Allah what would make his wives content, that you should admonish them like this?" And she fell silent, so Allah sent down: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, believing﴾ [66:5], the verse.
They differed about the meaning of His words: ﴿from the station of Ibrahim﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The whole Haram is the station of Ibrahim."
Yaman: "The whole mosque is the station of Ibrahim."
Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Suddi: "It is prayer beside the station of Ibrahim; they were commanded to pray beside it, and they were not commanded to wipe it or kiss it."
As for its story and the beginning of his affair:
Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim brought Isma'il and Hajar and placed them in Mecca, and he remained in that state for a period, and the Jurhumites settled there, and Isma'il married a woman from them, and Hajar died. Ibrahim asked Sarah's permission to visit Hajar, and she gave him permission, but stipulated that he should not stay. Ibrahim came, and Hajar had died, so he went to Isma'il's house. He said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He is not here; he has gone hunting." Isma'il used to leave the Haram, hunt, and then return. Ibrahim said to her: "Do you have any hospitality? Do you have food or drink?" She said: "I have nothing, and no one with me has anything."
Ibrahim said: "When your husband comes, greet him, and say to him: 'Let him change the threshold of his door.'" Ibrahim left, and Isma'il came and smelled his father's scent. He said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?"
She said: "An old man came to me, with such-and-such a description," as if she belittled his description. He said: "What did he say to you?"
She said: "He said to me: 'Give my greetings to your husband, and tell him: let him change the threshold of his door.'" So he divorced her and married another. Ibrahim remained as long as Allah willed, then asked Sarah's permission to visit Isma'il, and she permitted him, stipulating that he should not stay. Ibrahim came until he reached Isma'il's house.
Ibrahim said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He has gone hunting, and he will come now, God willing; dismount, may Allah have mercy on you."
He said to her: "Do you have hospitality?"
She said: "Yes," and she brought milk and meat, and he prayed for blessing for them. Had she brought bread of wheat, barley or dates that day, the land of Allah would have been wheat, barley and dates. She said to him: "Dismount until I wash your head." He did not dismount, so she brought the Station and he put it under his right side, and he placed his foot upon it, and she washed the right side of his head. Then she moved the Station to his left side, and the mark of his foot remained upon it, and she washed the left side of his head. He said to her: "When your husband comes, greet him and say to him: 'The threshold of your door has been made right.'" When Isma'il came, he smelled his father's scent and said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man, the most handsome of people in appearance and the most fragrant in scent. He said to me such-and-such, and I said to him such-and-such, and I washed his head, and this is the place of his feet on the Station." He said to her: "That was Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/181, ed. al-A'lami, Beirut.]]
Anas ibn Malik said: "I saw in the Station the mark of his fingers, his heel and the sole of his foot, except that the wiping of people's hands has removed it."
Nafi' ibn Shaybah said: "I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: I bear witness three times that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ say: 'The Corner (stone) and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Allah extinguished their light, and had He not extinguished their light, they would have lit up what is between the east and the west.'" [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 8/36; Musnad Ahmad: 2/213.]]
﴿We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾: that is, We commanded them and entrusted them.
﴿that purify My House﴾, the Ka'bah: that is, build it upon purity and monotheism.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umar, 'Ata' and Muqatil said: ﴿purify My House﴾ from idols, doubts and false speech. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "What is this? Do you know where you are?"
al-Awza'i from 'Uhdah ibn Abi Lubabah from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed Allah revealed to me: O brother of the messengers, O brother of the warners, warn your people that they should not enter any of My houses except with sound hearts, truthful tongues, pure hands and chaste private parts; and that they should not enter any of My houses while anyone among them has a wrong against another, for I curse him as long as he stands before Me praying, until he returns that wrong to its people. Then I will be his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, he will be among My friends and chosen ones, and his neighbour will be with the Prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/933; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/115.]]
Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: its meaning is "fumigate it and perfume it." [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/114.]]
Makhul from Mu'adh ibn Jabal from the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾, who said: "Keep your mosques away from your boys [[In the sources the word 'ghilmanakum' does not occur; what occurs is: 'keep your mosques away from your children and your insane persons...']] - meaning your children and your insane - and draw your swords, raise your voices, your punishments, your disputes, your selling and your buying; perfume them on the day of your Friday gathering, and place at their doors what is in front of you." [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 20/132; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/247, no. 750.]]
al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ja'far and the people of Medina recited ﴿baytiya﴾ with a fatha on the yā'; the others recited it with a sukun.
This is the attribution of the House to Himself, Glorified is He, for distinction and honour.
﴿for those who circle (al-ta'ifin)﴾ around it, and they are those who come to it from the horizons of the earth. ﴿and those who remain (al-'akifin)﴾, that is, those who stay in it, and they are the residents of the Haram. ﴿and those who bow (al-ruka')﴾: plural of rak'i. ﴿the prostrating (al-sujud)﴾: plural of sajid, like qa'id and qu'ud.
'Ata' said: If one is circling, he is among the tai'in; if he is sitting, he is among the 'akifin; and if he is praying, he is among the ruka' and sujud.
al-Awza'i from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed, every day and night, one hundred and twenty mercies descend upon this House: sixty for those who circle it, forty for those who pray, and twenty for those who look upon it." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 34/388.]]
﴿And when Ibrahim said: My Lord, make this﴾, meaning Mecca or the Haram,
﴿a secure city (baladan amina)﴾: that is, a place where it is safe, where its people are secure.
﴿and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. al-Akhfash said: "Man amana (those who believe) is a substitute for ahlahu (its people) by way of clarification, as one says: 'I took the wealth, two-thirds of it, and I saw the people, some of them.' This is substitution of part for whole, like His words: ﴿And for Allah is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ [3:97]."
Allah said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for him a little﴾: I will sustain him until the end of his term, because He, Exalted is He, promised provision to all creatures, the disbeliever and the believer alike; and it was restricted to "little" because the enjoyment of this world is little. Mu'awiyah and Ibn 'Amir recited: ﴿fa-amti'hu﴾ with a damma on the alif and a sukun on the mim, lightly; and Ubayy recited: "fa-numti'uhu qaliran thumma nadtarruhu" with the nun.
﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ with the alif joined and a fatha on the ra', in the form of a supplication from Ibrahim (peace be upon him); and the rest recited ﴿fa-umatti'uhu﴾ with a damma on the alif and shaddah, and ﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ as a statement: that is, Paradise in the Hereafter, ﴿to the punishment of the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place of return to which you come.
﴿And when Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, and Isma'il﴾: the narrators related from various chains about the building of the Ka'bah, and I have gathered their accounts and arranged them to be finer in expression and closer to understanding.
They said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the place of the House two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out from beneath it. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Adam down to the earth, his head touched the sky until he became bald, and he bequeathed baldness to his children; and the beasts of the earth fled from his height, and from that day they became wild. He used to hear the speech of the people of heaven, their supplication and their glorification, and he was at ease with them, but the angels feared him and his soul was troubled. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reduced him to sixty cubits by his own cubit. When Adam lost what he used to hear of the voices and glorification of the angels, he became lonely and complained of that to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Allah sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, the speech being cut off, with two doors of green emerald, an eastern door and a western door, and Allah sent down in it lamps from Paradise, and placed it at the site of the House until now. Then He said: "O Adam, I have sent down for you a house which you shall circle as one circles around My Throne, and pray beside it as one prays beside My Throne."
Then He sent down the Black Stone to him. He wiped his tears with it, and it had been white, but when menstruating women touched it in the Jahiliyyah, it became black.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Black Stone is a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and had it not been touched by the polytheists with their impurities, no one with an ailment would touch it without Allah, exalted is He, curing him." [110] [[In the margin of the manuscript: qayyada: qaddara (decreed, determined).]]

Adam set out from the land of India toward Makkah on foot, and Allah appointed for him an angel [[With variation in al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/587, hadith 3803, and al-Ahd al-Muhammadiyya: 224.]] to guide him to the House.

It was said to Mujahid: "O Abu'l-Hajjaj, why did he not ride?"

He said: "What would he have carried? By Allah, his stride was a three-day journey, and every place his foot touched became a settlement, and what lay beyond it was deserts and wastelands. He came to Makkah, performed Hajj to the House, and carried out the rites. When he had finished, the angels met him and said: 'May your Hajj be accepted, O Adam; we performed Hajj to this House two thousand years before you.'"

Ibn Abbas said: Adam performed forty Hajjs from India to Makkah on foot. This was the beginning of the affair of the Ka'bah, and it remained so until the time of the Flood. Then Allah raised it to the fourth heaven, and it is the Bayt al-Ma'mur, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and they do not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. Allah sent Jibril, who concealed the Black Stone on Mount Abu Qubays to preserve it from the Flood. The site of the House remained empty until the time of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Then, after Isma'il and Ishaq were born to him, Allah commanded Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to build a house for Him in which He would be worshipped and remembered. Ibrahim did not know where it had been concealed, so he asked Allah to show him its location. Allah sent to him al-Sakinah to guide him to the site of the House; it was a rushing wind with two heads, resembling a serpent. Ibrahim followed it until they reached Makkah. Allah then coiled al-Sakinah over the site of the House as a serpent coils around a shield, and Ibrahim was commanded to build where al-Sakinah settled, and he built it. This is the view of Ali and al-Hasan ibn Abi'l-Hasan.

Ibn Abbas also said: Allah sent a cloud the size of the Ka'bah, which kept moving while Ibrahim walked beneath its shadow through darkness, until it reached Makkah and stopped over the site of the House. He was called: "O Ibrahim, build in its shade; do not add to it or subtract from it." So he built according to its shadow.

Some of them said: Allah sent Jibril to guide him to the site, and this is His saying: ﴿And when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 26.]]. Ibrahim and Isma'il then built the House: Ibrahim was building while Isma'il handed him the stones.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu'l-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qattan al-Balkhi, who was a scholar of the Qur'an, say: Ibrahim understood Syriac and Isma'il understood Arabic, and each of them understood what his companion said and what could be pronounced. Ibrahim would say to Isma'il: "Habli kunyan," meaning: "Hand me the stone," and Isma'il would say: "Hak al-hajar, khudhhu," meaning: "Here is the stone, take it."

They said: The place of the stone remained, so Isma'il went to it, and Jibril brought a stone from heaven. Isma'il came back to find that Ibrahim had already set the stone in its place, and he said to him: "Who brought you this?"

He said: "It was brought to me by One who did not rely on your building." Thus they completed the House, and this is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim and Isma'il raised the foundations of the House﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 127.]].

Ibn Abbas said: That means the original foundations of the House that existed before.

Al-Kalbi and Abu Ubaydah said: Its foundations (asas), whose singular is qa'idah. They built it from five mountains: Tur Sinai [... Tur Sina and al-Judi] [[Unreadable words.]], and they built its foundations from Hira'.

When Ibrahim reached the place of the Black Stone, he said to Isma'il: "Bring me a fine stone that will be a sign for the people." Isma'il brought him a stone, and he said: "Bring me a stone better than this." So Isma'il went off searching, and Abu Qubays [[In the margin of the manuscript: a mountain in Makkah.]] called out: "O Ibrahim, there is a deposit for you with me; take it." He took the Black Stone and placed it in its position.

It was also said: Allah extended to Ibrahim and Isma'il seven angels to help them build the House. When they had finished building it, they said: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾, that is, accept from us our building of the House. ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ of our intentions.

﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims﴾, that is, monotheists, obedient and sincere to You.

Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Jamilah read: ﴿Muslimin﴾ with a kasrah on the mim, in the plural.

﴿And from our descendants﴾, that is, our offspring, ﴿a Muslim community﴾ submitting to You. ﴿And show us﴾, that is, teach us, ﴿our rites﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿that you may judge among the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: what Allah has taught you. There are four readings of this word:

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿Wa-arihim manasikahum﴾, referring it back to the community.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Qatadah, Ibn Kathir and Ruways read it with a sukun on the ra' throughout the Qur'an.

Abu Amr read it with the vowel of the ra' weakly pronounced (ikhtilas) with the kasrah of the waw.

The rest read it with a kasrah on the ra', the original form being arana with a hamzah, which was dropped for lightness.

Whoever reads with the jazm says: the hamzah was dropped along with its vowel, and the ra' remained sukun in its state, and he cites the saying of al-Suddi: "Arina idawat Abdillah namla'uha min ma'i Zamzam, inna al-qawm qad zami'u" (Show us the water-vessel of Abdullah that we may fill it from the water of Zamzam, for the people are thirsty).

Whoever reads with a kasrah has transferred the vowel of the dropped hamzah to the ra'.

As for Abu Amr, he sought lightness.

Al-Qasim ibn Sallam reported from Shuja' ibn Abi Nasr, who said, and he was trustworthy and truthful, that he saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream, and he mentioned to him several things from Abu Amr's reading, and he did not dispute with him except over two letters: one of them is this, and the other is: ﴿What We abrogate of a verse or cause to be forgotten﴾ read with a hamzah.

﴿Manasikana﴾: the laws of our religion and the signs of our pilgrimage.

Mujahid said: our slaughtering places. The nusuk is the sacrifice, and the root of nusk is worship; a worshipper is called nasik. The poet says:

"I was concealed, much in devotion (tanassuk), / then my curtains were torn away and I had no devotion left."

Allah answered their supplication and sent Jibril, who showed them the rites on the Day of Arafah. When he reached Arafat, he said to Ibrahim: "Have you recognized (araft), O Ibrahim?"

He said: "Yes." So the day was called Arafah and the place Arafat.

﴿And turn to us﴾, that is, pardon us and turn toward us with compassion and mercy.

﴿Indeed You are the Ever-Returning, the Merciful﴾: the one who pardons greatly, who returns with mercy to His servants. ﴿The Merciful.﴾

﴿Our Lord, and raise among them﴾, that is, among the Muslim community of the descendants of Ibrahim and Isma'il.

It was also said: among the people of Makkah, ﴿a messenger﴾, that is, one sent, and it is the form fa'ul from risalah (message).

Al-Ibn al-Anbari said: It may be that its origin is from their saying: a she-camel is "mirsal" and "rasl" when she is easy-paced and goes ahead of the she-camels.

A group sent without restraint is called "rusl," its plural being "arsal." And it is said: the people came "irsalan," meaning some following others; from this the milk is called "rasl," because it flows (yursal) from the udder. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/131.]]

﴿Who recites to them Your verses﴾, that is, Your Book; the plural of ayah, which is a sign.

It was said: an ayah is a group of letters.

Al-Shaybani said: it is their saying: "kharaja al-qawm bi-ma fihim," meaning they went out with their whole group.

﴿And teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾. Some said: the ayah here is the Book, and it is joined to it in a different wording, as in the verse of al-Hutay'ah:

"Ala habbadha Hind wa-ardun biha Hind / wa-Hind tafsil ataa min dunihā al-nā'y wa'l-bu'd"

Mujahid: it means the wisdom, the understanding of the Qur'an.

Muqatil: it is the admonitions of the Qur'an and what it contains of rulings, and the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful.

Ibn Qutaybah: it is knowledge and action; a man is not called wise until he combines them.

On the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Biridi: every word that admonishes you, or restrains you, or directs you to nobility, or forbids you from what is ugly, is wisdom (hikmah) and wise sayings (hikam). From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed, among poetry there is wisdom." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/865, and Lisan al-Arab: 12/141.]]

On the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub: wisdom is every correct speech that brings forth a correct action or a correct state.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh: wisdom is one of the soldiers of Allah, which He sends to the hearts of the knowers until the heat of this world is cooled from them. It was said: wisdom is placing things in their proper places. It was said: wisdom and judgment are whatever it is obligatory upon you to do.

The poet says:

"I have said a word whose speaker is not reproached: / silence is judgment, and few are those who practise it."

That is, it is obligatory to act by silence.

It was said: it means shirk and sins. It was also said: it means taking the zakat of their wealth.

Ibn Kaysan said: they will be testified to on the Day of Resurrection as upright when they bear witness that the prophets conveyed the message, based on His saying: ﴿Thus We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 143.]].

﴿Indeed You are the Almighty﴾. Ibn Abbas: al-Aziz is the one for whom there is no equal; its proof is His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [[Surat al-Shura: 11.]].

Al-Kalbi: al-Aziz is the one who takes vengeance on whomever He wills; its proof is His saying: ﴿And Allah is Almighty, Possessor of retribution﴾ [[Surat Ali Imran: 4.]].

Al-Kisa'i: al-Aziz is the Overpowering; its proof is His saying: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾ [[Surat Sad: 23.]], meaning: he overcame me.

It is said in the proverb: "Min 'azīz" (from one who overpowers).

Ibn Kaysan: al-Aziz is the one whom nothing can incapacitate; its proof is His saying: ﴿Nor is there anything in the heavens or on the earth that could ever cause Him to fail﴾ [[Fatir: 44.]].

Al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah: al-Aziz is the Inaccessible, whom no hand can reach, so none of His decrees is turned back and He is not overcome in what He wills; its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾ [[Surat Hud: 107.]].

It is also said: it means the one who grants might (al-mu'izz), the form fa'il in the sense of maf'il; its proof is His saying: ﴿and You grant honor to whom You will﴾ [[Surat Ali Imran: 26.]].

It is also said: it means the Strong; its proof is His saying: ﴿then We strengthened [them] with a third﴾ [[Ya-Sin: 14.]], meaning: We strengthened. The root of 'izzah in the language is hardness; it is said: the flesh of the she-camel "ta'azzaza" when it became firm, and it is said: "'azza 'alayya," meaning it was hard and difficult for me. Abu Amr recited:

"A camel that, when lean, has firm flesh, / and when driven with its mates, does not despair."

So Allah answered Ibrahim's supplication and sent among them Muhammad, the master of the prophets. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed I was the servant of Allah in the Mother of the Book, the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still between clay and water. I will inform you of that: it is the supplication of Ibrahim, the glad tidings of Isa (peace be upon them) to his people, and the vision of my mother, who saw that a light came out from her which illuminated the palaces of Syria; thus the mothers of the prophets see." [112] [[With variation in Musnad Ahmad: 4/127, and Fath al-Bari: 6/426.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 124–129 (part 1 of 2):

Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Ibrahim﴾ (in the nominative) and ﴿rabbahu﴾ (in the accusative), on the sense of "asked" and "called upon." It was said to him: "From where do you have this?" He said: "Ibn 'Abbas taught it to me." This is not strong, because of the bi- (ba') in His words ﴿with words﴾. The rest recited it in the accusative, and they understood the meaning of "trial" (ibtila', al-ibtila', trial and testing) as choosing and examining in a matter, and this is the correct reading. As for ﴿Ibrahim﴾ (ʾIbrāhīm), there are four dialectal forms. Ibn al-Zubayr recited: "Ibrahām" with one alif between the ha' and the mim; Abu Bakr recited "Ibrāhim"; and Zayd ibn 'Amr used to say in his prayer: "I seek refuge with what Ibrahim sought refuge in, when he said:
"I turn to You, O Allah, humbly, submitting..." [[Its opening: facing the qibla while standing.]]
Abdullah ibn 'Amir al-Yahsubi recited: "Ibrāhām" with two alifs, and the rest recited: ﴿Ibrahim﴾. [... Yahya ibn Sa'id said] [[A group of words missing from the manuscript.]] al-Ansari: "He recited Ibrāhām and Ibrāhīm, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down both, just as He sent down Ya'qub and Isra'il, and 'Isa and al-Masih, and Muhammad and Ahmad."
al-Rabi' ibn 'Amir: "It is written in the mushafs of the people of al-Sham as Ibrāhām with an alif, and in others with a yā'."
Ibrahim is a non-Arabic name, and for this reason it is not declined. He is Ibrahim ibn Nazih ibn Nahur ibn Sarukh ibn Ar'aw ibn Falikh ibn Manabir ibn al-Shalikh ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sam ibn Nuh. They differed about his dwelling: some of them said he was in [Bakshkar] [[Thus in the manuscript.]], and a group said Harran, but his father moved him to Babylon, the land of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. They also differed about the "words" with which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was tried:
From Ibn 'Abbas: they are thirty portions (sahm), and they are the laws of Islam; no one was tested with this whole religion and fulfilled all of it except Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him).
﴿fa-atammahunna﴾: so He gave him the acquittal (al-bara'a). He said: ﴿And Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ [53:37]. It is ten in Bara'a: ﴿those who repent, those who worship﴾ [9:112], the verse; and ten in al-Ahzab: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾ [33:35], the verse; and ten in al-Mu'minun: ﴿A questioner asked... Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [70:1; 23:1], and His words ﴿except those who pray﴾ [70:22].
Tawus narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: He tested him with ten things, which are of the fitrah (natural disposition) and purity: five in the head and five in the body. Those in the head are: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. Those in the body are: trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleansing with water (istinja').
Mujahid: they are the signs in His words: ﴿I am making you a leader for the people﴾ [2:124], to the end of the story.
al-Rabi' and Qatadah: the rites of Hajj.
al-Hasan: He tested him with seven things: He tested him with the stars, the moon, and the sun, and he did well in that and knew that his Lord is Everlasting and does not cease; He tested him with the fire, and he endured that; He tested him with the sacrifice of his son, and he endured that; and with circumcision, and he endured that; and with the migration, and he endured that.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they are the words of Ibrahim and Isma'il when they raised the House: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾ [2:127], and they raised it with "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest."
Yaman: they are his argument with his people. Allah said: ﴿And his people argued with him﴾, to His words, ﴿And that is Our argument which We gave to Ibrahim against his people﴾ [6:83].
Abu Rawq: they are his words (peace be upon him): ﴿He who created me, and He guides me﴾ [26:78], the verses. Some of them said: Allah tested him in his wealth, his children, and his self; he gave his wealth to guests, his children to sacrifice, his self to the fire, and his heart to the Most Merciful, so He took him as a friend (khalil). It was also said: they are the portions of Islam, and they are ten: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, which is the creed (milla) and prayer, which is the bridge... He said: [and zakat] [[An unreadable word; the reading we have adopted seems likely.]], which is purification, and fasting, which is the shield, and Hajj, which is the law, and jihad, which is victory, and obedience, which is protection, and the community, which is affection, and enjoining good, which is fulfilment, and forbidding evil, which is the proof. ﴿fa-atammahunna﴾.
Qatadah said: "He performed them."
al-Rabi': "He fulfilled them."
al-Dahhak: [... their oaths] [[An unreadable word.]], Yaman: "He acted upon them." Allah said: ﴿Indeed I am making you, O Ibrahim, a leader for the people﴾, so that they may follow you; and its root is from umm, which means intention.
He said: ﴿And from my offspring﴾, meaning from my children also. So make them leaders who will be followed. The root of dhurriyyah is "young children," derived from dharr because of their multitude; it was also said it is from dharr, meaning creation, and the hamza was lightened and doubling (tashdid) was introduced in place of the hamza, as in al-bariyyah.
It was said: it is from dharw, and in it there are three dialects:
dhurriyyah with a kasra on the dhal, which is the reading of Zayd ibn Thabit; dhurriyyah with a fatha, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; and dhurriyyah with a damma, which is the reading of the common people.
Allah said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, that is, it does not reach or attain.
﴿My covenant (ʿahdī) the wrongdoers﴾: in it there are three readings: ʿahdī al-ẓālimūn, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Talhah ibn Musarrif; ʿahdī al-ẓālimīn with the yā' made a standing (irtijāl) yā', which is the reading of Abu Raja', al-A'mash, and Hamzah; and ʿahdiya al-ẓālimīn with a fatha on the yā', which is the reading of the common people. They differed about this covenant: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said:
"My mercy."
al-Dahhak: "My obedience." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾ [2:40].
al-Suddi: "Fulfilment." Its evidence is His words: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its binding﴾ [2:27].
Mujahid: "It is not the wrongdoer who is to be obeyed in his wrongdoing."
Abu Hudhayfah: "My trust." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you pledge﴾ [16:91].
Abu 'Ubayd: "My wishes (amani)." Its evidence is His words: ﴿So complete for them their covenant until their term﴾ [9:4]. It was also said: "My faith (iman)," and its evidence is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan﴾ [36:60].
﴿And when We made the House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah.
﴿a place of return (mathaba)﴾: a place of return (marji'an); mathab and mathabah are one, like maqam and maqamah. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning a refuge and a sanctuary.
Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak: [they return] to it from every direction and perform Hajj, and they never tire of it; for no one visits it without wishing to return to it.
Qatadah and 'Ikrimah: "a gathering place." Talhah ibn Musarrif recited: "mathabat" in the plural.
﴿for the people and a sanctuary (amnan)﴾: a place of safety, where they are secure.
Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever commits an offence outside the Haram and then takes refuge in the Haram is secure from being attacked within it; but he is not sheltered, nor mixed with, nor traded with, and he is kept apart; when he leaves it, the legal punishment (hadd) is carried out upon him. And whoever commits an offence within the Haram, the legal punishment is carried out upon him within it.
﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾: Shaybah, Ibn 'Amir, Nafi', al-A'raj, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Salam recited: "wa-attakhadha" with a fatha on the kha', as a statement; and the rest recited with a kasra, as a command.
Ibn Kaysan said: They mention that the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ passed by the Station, and with him was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this not the station of our father Ibrahim?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then should we not take it as a place of prayer?"
He said: "I have not been commanded to do that."
[105] [[Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 37; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/174.]]
Then the sun had not set on that day before this was revealed: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾.
From Anas ibn Malik: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "My Lord agreed with me in three things."
I said: "Would that you took the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer," and Allah sent down: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾. And I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked come in to you; if only you would screen the Mothers of the Believers." So Allah sent down the verse of hijab. He said:
"And something reached me that happened between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﴿ﷺ﴾, so I rebuked them and I kept saying to them: 'Either you refrain from the Messenger of Allah, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you,' until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers."
And Umm Salamah said: "O 'Umar, is there not in the Messenger of Allah what would make his wives content, that you should admonish them like this?" And she fell silent, so Allah sent down: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, believing﴾ [66:5], the verse.
They differed about the meaning of His words: ﴿from the station of Ibrahim﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The whole Haram is the station of Ibrahim."
Yaman: "The whole mosque is the station of Ibrahim."
Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Suddi: "It is prayer beside the station of Ibrahim; they were commanded to pray beside it, and they were not commanded to wipe it or kiss it."
As for its story and the beginning of his affair:
Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim brought Isma'il and Hajar and placed them in Mecca, and he remained in that state for a period, and the Jurhumites settled there, and Isma'il married a woman from them, and Hajar died. Ibrahim asked Sarah's permission to visit Hajar, and she gave him permission, but stipulated that he should not stay. Ibrahim came, and Hajar had died, so he went to Isma'il's house. He said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He is not here; he has gone hunting." Isma'il used to leave the Haram, hunt, and then return. Ibrahim said to her: "Do you have any hospitality? Do you have food or drink?" She said: "I have nothing, and no one with me has anything."
Ibrahim said: "When your husband comes, greet him, and say to him: 'Let him change the threshold of his door.'" Ibrahim left, and Isma'il came and smelled his father's scent. He said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?"
She said: "An old man came to me, with such-and-such a description," as if she belittled his description. He said: "What did he say to you?"
She said: "He said to me: 'Give my greetings to your husband, and tell him: let him change the threshold of his door.'" So he divorced her and married another. Ibrahim remained as long as Allah willed, then asked Sarah's permission to visit Isma'il, and she permitted him, stipulating that he should not stay. Ibrahim came until he reached Isma'il's house.
Ibrahim said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He has gone hunting, and he will come now, God willing; dismount, may Allah have mercy on you."
He said to her: "Do you have hospitality?"
She said: "Yes," and she brought milk and meat, and he prayed for blessing for them. Had she brought bread of wheat, barley or dates that day, the land of Allah would have been wheat, barley and dates. She said to him: "Dismount until I wash your head." He did not dismount, so she brought the Station and he put it under his right side, and he placed his foot upon it, and she washed the right side of his head. Then she moved the Station to his left side, and the mark of his foot remained upon it, and she washed the left side of his head. He said to her: "When your husband comes, greet him and say to him: 'The threshold of your door has been made right.'" When Isma'il came, he smelled his father's scent and said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man, the most handsome of people in appearance and the most fragrant in scent. He said to me such-and-such, and I said to him such-and-such, and I washed his head, and this is the place of his feet on the Station." He said to her: "That was Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/181, ed. al-A'lami, Beirut.]]
Anas ibn Malik said: "I saw in the Station the mark of his fingers, his heel and the sole of his foot, except that the wiping of people's hands has removed it."
Nafi' ibn Shaybah said: "I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: I bear witness three times that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ say: 'The Corner (stone) and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Allah extinguished their light, and had He not extinguished their light, they would have lit up what is between the east and the west.'" [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 8/36; Musnad Ahmad: 2/213.]]
﴿We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾: that is, We commanded them and entrusted them.
﴿that purify My House﴾, the Ka'bah: that is, build it upon purity and monotheism.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umar, 'Ata' and Muqatil said: ﴿purify My House﴾ from idols, doubts and false speech. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "What is this? Do you know where you are?"
al-Awza'i from 'Uhdah ibn Abi Lubabah from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed Allah revealed to me: O brother of the messengers, O brother of the warners, warn your people that they should not enter any of My houses except with sound hearts, truthful tongues, pure hands and chaste private parts; and that they should not enter any of My houses while anyone among them has a wrong against another, for I curse him as long as he stands before Me praying, until he returns that wrong to its people. Then I will be his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, he will be among My friends and chosen ones, and his neighbour will be with the Prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/933; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/115.]]
Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: its meaning is "fumigate it and perfume it." [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/114.]]
Makhul from Mu'adh ibn Jabal from the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾, who said: "Keep your mosques away from your boys [[In the sources the word 'ghilmanakum' does not occur; what occurs is: 'keep your mosques away from your children and your insane persons...']] - meaning your children and your insane - and draw your swords, raise your voices, your punishments, your disputes, your selling and your buying; perfume them on the day of your Friday gathering, and place at their doors what is in front of you." [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 20/132; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/247, no. 750.]]
al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ja'far and the people of Medina recited ﴿baytiya﴾ with a fatha on the yā'; the others recited it with a sukun.
This is the attribution of the House to Himself, Glorified is He, for distinction and honour.
﴿for those who circle (al-ta'ifin)﴾ around it, and they are those who come to it from the horizons of the earth. ﴿and those who remain (al-'akifin)﴾, that is, those who stay in it, and they are the residents of the Haram. ﴿and those who bow (al-ruka')﴾: plural of rak'i. ﴿the prostrating (al-sujud)﴾: plural of sajid, like qa'id and qu'ud.
'Ata' said: If one is circling, he is among the tai'in; if he is sitting, he is among the 'akifin; and if he is praying, he is among the ruka' and sujud.
al-Awza'i from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed, every day and night, one hundred and twenty mercies descend upon this House: sixty for those who circle it, forty for those who pray, and twenty for those who look upon it." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 34/388.]]
﴿And when Ibrahim said: My Lord, make this﴾, meaning Mecca or the Haram,
﴿a secure city (baladan amina)﴾: that is, a place where it is safe, where its people are secure.
﴿and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. al-Akhfash said: "Man amana (those who believe) is a substitute for ahlahu (its people) by way of clarification, as one says: 'I took the wealth, two-thirds of it, and I saw the people, some of them.' This is substitution of part for whole, like His words: ﴿And for Allah is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ [3:97]."
Allah said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for him a little﴾: I will sustain him until the end of his term, because He, Exalted is He, promised provision to all creatures, the disbeliever and the believer alike; and it was restricted to "little" because the enjoyment of this world is little. Mu'awiyah and Ibn 'Amir recited: ﴿fa-amti'hu﴾ with a damma on the alif and a sukun on the mim, lightly; and Ubayy recited: "fa-numti'uhu qaliran thumma nadtarruhu" with the nun.
﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ with the alif joined and a fatha on the ra', in the form of a supplication from Ibrahim (peace be upon him); and the rest recited ﴿fa-umatti'uhu﴾ with a damma on the alif and shaddah, and ﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ as a statement: that is, Paradise in the Hereafter, ﴿to the punishment of the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place of return to which you come.
﴿And when Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, and Isma'il﴾: the narrators related from various chains about the building of the Ka'bah, and I have gathered their accounts and arranged them to be finer in expression and closer to understanding.
They said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the place of the House two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out from beneath it. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Adam down to the earth, his head touched the sky until he became bald, and he bequeathed baldness to his children; and the beasts of the earth fled from his height, and from that day they became wild. He used to hear the speech of the people of heaven, their supplication and their glorification, and he was at ease with them, but the angels feared him and his soul was troubled. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reduced him to sixty cubits by his own cubit. When Adam lost what he used to hear of the voices and glorification of the angels, he became lonely and complained of that to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Allah sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, the speech being cut off, with two doors of green emerald, an eastern door and a western door, and Allah sent down in it lamps from Paradise, and placed it at the site of the House until now. Then He said: "O Adam, I have sent down for you a house which you shall circle as one circles around My Throne, and pray beside it as one prays beside My Throne."
Then He sent down the Black Stone to him. He wiped his tears with it, and it had been white, but when menstruating women touched it in the Jahiliyyah, it became black.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Black Stone is a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and had it not been touched by the polytheists with their impurities, no one with an ailment would touch it without Allah, exalted is He, curing him." [110] [[In the margin of the manuscript: qayyada: qaddara (decreed, determined).]]

Adam set out from the land of India toward Makkah on foot, and Allah appointed for him an angel [[With variation in al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/587, hadith 3803, and al-Ahd al-Muhammadiyya: 224.]] to guide him to the House.

It was said to Mujahid: "O Abu'l-Hajjaj, why did he not ride?"

He said: "What would he have carried? By Allah, his stride was a three-day journey, and every place his foot touched became a settlement, and what lay beyond it was deserts and wastelands. He came to Makkah, performed Hajj to the House, and carried out the rites. When he had finished, the angels met him and said: 'May your Hajj be accepted, O Adam; we performed Hajj to this House two thousand years before you.'"

Ibn Abbas said: Adam performed forty Hajjs from India to Makkah on foot. This was the beginning of the affair of the Ka'bah, and it remained so until the time of the Flood. Then Allah raised it to the fourth heaven, and it is the Bayt al-Ma'mur, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and they do not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. Allah sent Jibril, who concealed the Black Stone on Mount Abu Qubays to preserve it from the Flood. The site of the House remained empty until the time of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Then, after Isma'il and Ishaq were born to him, Allah commanded Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to build a house for Him in which He would be worshipped and remembered. Ibrahim did not know where it had been concealed, so he asked Allah to show him its location. Allah sent to him al-Sakinah to guide him to the site of the House; it was a rushing wind with two heads, resembling a serpent. Ibrahim followed it until they reached Makkah. Allah then coiled al-Sakinah over the site of the House as a serpent coils around a shield, and Ibrahim was commanded to build where al-Sakinah settled, and he built it. This is the view of Ali and al-Hasan ibn Abi'l-Hasan.

Ibn Abbas also said: Allah sent a cloud the size of the Ka'bah, which kept moving while Ibrahim walked beneath its shadow through darkness, until it reached Makkah and stopped over the site of the House. He was called: "O Ibrahim, build in its shade; do not add to it or subtract from it." So he built according to its shadow.

Some of them said: Allah sent Jibril to guide him to the site, and this is His saying: ﴿And when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 26.]]. Ibrahim and Isma'il then built the House: Ibrahim was building while Isma'il handed him the stones.

Al-Tha'alabi said: I heard Abu'l-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qattan al-Balkhi, who was a scholar of the Qur'an, say: Ibrahim understood Syriac and Isma'il understood Arabic, and each of them understood what his companion said and what could be pronounced. Ibrahim would say to Isma'il: "Habli kunyan," meaning: "Hand me the stone," and Isma'il would say: "Hak al-hajar, khudhhu," meaning: "Here is the stone, take it."

They said: The place of the stone remained, so Isma'il went to it, and Jibril brought a stone from heaven. Isma'il came back to find that Ibrahim had already set the stone in its place, and he said to him: "Who brought you this?"

He said: "It was brought to me by One who did not rely on your building." Thus they completed the House, and this is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim and Isma'il raised the foundations of the House﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 127.]].

Ibn Abbas said: That means the original foundations of the House that existed before.

Al-Kalbi and Abu Ubaydah said: Its foundations (asas), whose singular is qa'idah. They built it from five mountains: Tur Sinai [... Tur Sina and al-Judi] [[Unreadable words.]], and they built its foundations from Hira'.

When Ibrahim reached the place of the Black Stone, he said to Isma'il: "Bring me a fine stone that will be a sign for the people." Isma'il brought him a stone, and he said: "Bring me a stone better than this." So Isma'il went off searching, and Abu Qubays [[In the margin of the manuscript: a mountain in Makkah.]] called out: "O Ibrahim, there is a deposit for you with me; take it." He took the Black Stone and placed it in its position.

It was also said: Allah extended to Ibrahim and Isma'il seven angels to help them build the House. When they had finished building it, they said: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾, that is, accept from us our building of the House. ﴿Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ of our intentions.

﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims﴾, that is, monotheists, obedient and sincere to You.

Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Jamilah read: ﴿Muslimin﴾ with a kasrah on the mim, in the plural.

﴿And from our descendants﴾, that is, our offspring, ﴿a Muslim community﴾ submitting to You. ﴿And show us﴾, that is, teach us, ﴿our rites﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿that you may judge among the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: what Allah has taught you. There are four readings of this word:

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿Wa-arihim manasikahum﴾, referring it back to the community.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Qatadah, Ibn Kathir and Ruways read it with a sukun on the ra' throughout the Qur'an.

Abu Amr read it with the vowel of the ra' weakly pronounced (ikhtilas) with the kasrah of the waw.

The rest read it with a kasrah on the ra', the original form being arana with a hamzah, which was dropped for lightness.

Whoever reads with the jazm says: the hamzah was dropped along with its vowel, and the ra' remained sukun in its state, and he cites the saying of al-Suddi: "Arina idawat Abdillah namla'uha min ma'i Zamzam, inna al-qawm qad zami'u" (Show us the water-vessel of Abdullah that we may fill it from the water of Zamzam, for the people are thirsty).

Whoever reads with a kasrah has transferred the vowel of the dropped hamzah to the ra'.

As for Abu Amr, he sought lightness.

Al-Qasim ibn Sallam reported from Shuja' ibn Abi Nasr, who said, and he was trustworthy and truthful, that he saw the Prophet ﷺ in a dream, and he mentioned to him several things from Abu Amr's reading, and he did not dispute with him except over two letters: one of them is this, and the other is: ﴿What We abrogate of a verse or cause to be forgotten﴾ read with a hamzah.

﴿Manasikana﴾: the laws of our religion and the signs of our pilgrimage.

Mujahid said: our slaughtering places. The nusuk is the sacrifice, and the root of nusk is worship; a worshipper is called nasik. The poet says:

"I was concealed, much in devotion (tanassuk), / then my curtains were torn away and I had no devotion left."

Allah answered their supplication and sent Jibril, who showed them the rites on the Day of Arafah. When he reached Arafat, he said to Ibrahim: "Have you recognized (araft), O Ibrahim?"

He said: "Yes." So the day was called Arafah and the place Arafat.

﴿And turn to us﴾, that is, pardon us and turn toward us with compassion and mercy.

﴿Indeed You are the Ever-Returning, the Merciful﴾: the one who pardons greatly, who returns with mercy to His servants. ﴿The Merciful.﴾

﴿Our Lord, and raise among them﴾, that is, among the Muslim community of the descendants of Ibrahim and Isma'il.

It was also said: among the people of Makkah, ﴿a messenger﴾, that is, one sent, and it is the form fa'ul from risalah (message).

Al-Ibn al-Anbari said: It may be that its origin is from their saying: a she-camel is "mirsal" and "rasl" when she is easy-paced and goes ahead of the she-camels.

A group sent without restraint is called "rusl," its plural being "arsal." And it is said: the people came "irsalan," meaning some following others; from this the milk is called "rasl," because it flows (yursal) from the udder. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/131.]]

﴿Who recites to them Your verses﴾, that is, Your Book; the plural of ayah, which is a sign.

It was said: an ayah is a group of letters.

Al-Shaybani said: it is their saying: "kharaja al-qawm bi-ma fihim," meaning they went out with their whole group.

﴿And teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾. Some said: the ayah here is the Book, and it is joined to it in a different wording, as in the verse of al-Hutay'ah:

"Ala habbadha Hind wa-ardun biha Hind / wa-Hind tafsil ataa min dunihā al-nā'y wa'l-bu'd"

Mujahid: it means the wisdom, the understanding of the Qur'an.

Muqatil: it is the admonitions of the Qur'an and what it contains of rulings, and the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful.

Ibn Qutaybah: it is knowledge and action; a man is not called wise until he combines them.

On the authority of Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Biridi: every word that admonishes you, or restrains you, or directs you to nobility, or forbids you from what is ugly, is wisdom (hikmah) and wise sayings (hikam). From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed, among poetry there is wisdom." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/865, and Lisan al-Arab: 12/141.]]

On the authority of Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub: wisdom is every correct speech that brings forth a correct action or a correct state.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh: wisdom is one of the soldiers of Allah, which He sends to the hearts of the knowers until the heat of this world is cooled from them. It was said: wisdom is placing things in their proper places. It was said: wisdom and judgment are whatever it is obligatory upon you to do.

The poet says:

"I have said a word whose speaker is not reproached: / silence is judgment, and few are those who practise it."

That is, it is obligatory to act by silence.

It was said: it means shirk and sins. It was also said: it means taking the zakat of their wealth.

Ibn Kaysan said: they will be testified to on the Day of Resurrection as upright when they bear witness that the prophets conveyed the message, based on His saying: ﴿Thus We have made you a middle community, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 143.]].

﴿Indeed You are the Almighty﴾. Ibn Abbas: al-Aziz is the one for whom there is no equal; its proof is His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [[Surat al-Shura: 11.]].

Al-Kalbi: al-Aziz is the one who takes vengeance on whomever He wills; its proof is His saying: ﴿And Allah is Almighty, Possessor of retribution﴾ [[Surat Ali Imran: 4.]].

Al-Kisa'i: al-Aziz is the Overpowering; its proof is His saying: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾ [[Surat Sad: 23.]], meaning: he overcame me.

It is said in the proverb: "Min 'azīz" (from one who overpowers).

Ibn Kaysan: al-Aziz is the one whom nothing can incapacitate; its proof is His saying: ﴿Nor is there anything in the heavens or on the earth that could ever cause Him to fail﴾ [[Fatir: 44.]].

Al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah: al-Aziz is the Inaccessible, whom no hand can reach, so none of His decrees is turned back and He is not overcome in what He wills; its proof is His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾ [[Surat Hud: 107.]].

It is also said: it means the one who grants might (al-mu'izz), the form fa'il in the sense of maf'il; its proof is His saying: ﴿and You grant honor to whom You will﴾ [[Surat Ali Imran: 26.]].

It is also said: it means the Strong; its proof is His saying: ﴿then We strengthened [them] with a third﴾ [[Ya-Sin: 14.]], meaning: We strengthened. The root of 'izzah in the language is hardness; it is said: the flesh of the she-camel "ta'azzaza" when it became firm, and it is said: "'azza 'alayya," meaning it was hard and difficult for me. Abu Amr recited:

"A camel that, when lean, has firm flesh, / and when driven with its mates, does not despair."

So Allah answered Ibrahim's supplication and sent among them Muhammad, the master of the prophets. For this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Indeed I was the servant of Allah in the Mother of the Book, the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still between clay and water. I will inform you of that: it is the supplication of Ibrahim, the glad tidings of Isa (peace be upon them) to his people, and the vision of my mother, who saw that a light came out from her which illuminated the palaces of Syria; thus the mothers of the prophets see." [112] [[With variation in Musnad Ahmad: 4/127, and Fath al-Bari: 6/426.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 124–129 (part 1 of 2):

Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd recited: ﴿Ibrahim﴾ (in the nominative) and ﴿rabbahu﴾ (in the accusative), on the sense of "asked" and "called upon." It was said to him: "From where do you have this?" He said: "Ibn 'Abbas taught it to me." This is not strong, because of the bi- (ba') in His words ﴿with words﴾. The rest recited it in the accusative, and they understood the meaning of "trial" (ibtila', al-ibtila', trial and testing) as choosing and examining in a matter, and this is the correct reading. As for ﴿Ibrahim﴾ (ʾIbrāhīm), there are four dialectal forms. Ibn al-Zubayr recited: "Ibrahām" with one alif between the ha' and the mim; Abu Bakr recited "Ibrāhim"; and Zayd ibn 'Amr used to say in his prayer: "I seek refuge with what Ibrahim sought refuge in, when he said:
"I turn to You, O Allah, humbly, submitting..." [[Its opening: facing the qibla while standing.]]
Abdullah ibn 'Amir al-Yahsubi recited: "Ibrāhām" with two alifs, and the rest recited: ﴿Ibrahim﴾. [... Yahya ibn Sa'id said] [[A group of words missing from the manuscript.]] al-Ansari: "He recited Ibrāhām and Ibrāhīm, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down both, just as He sent down Ya'qub and Isra'il, and 'Isa and al-Masih, and Muhammad and Ahmad."
al-Rabi' ibn 'Amir: "It is written in the mushafs of the people of al-Sham as Ibrāhām with an alif, and in others with a yā'."
Ibrahim is a non-Arabic name, and for this reason it is not declined. He is Ibrahim ibn Nazih ibn Nahur ibn Sarukh ibn Ar'aw ibn Falikh ibn Manabir ibn al-Shalikh ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sam ibn Nuh. They differed about his dwelling: some of them said he was in [Bakshkar] [[Thus in the manuscript.]], and a group said Harran, but his father moved him to Babylon, the land of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. They also differed about the "words" with which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was tried:
From Ibn 'Abbas: they are thirty portions (sahm), and they are the laws of Islam; no one was tested with this whole religion and fulfilled all of it except Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him).
﴿fa-atammahunna﴾: so He gave him the acquittal (al-bara'a). He said: ﴿And Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ [53:37]. It is ten in Bara'a: ﴿those who repent, those who worship﴾ [9:112], the verse; and ten in al-Ahzab: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾ [33:35], the verse; and ten in al-Mu'minun: ﴿A questioner asked... Certainly the believers have succeeded﴾ [70:1; 23:1], and His words ﴿except those who pray﴾ [70:22].
Tawus narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: He tested him with ten things, which are of the fitrah (natural disposition) and purity: five in the head and five in the body. Those in the head are: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water into the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. Those in the body are: trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, and cleansing with water (istinja').
Mujahid: they are the signs in His words: ﴿I am making you a leader for the people﴾ [2:124], to the end of the story.
al-Rabi' and Qatadah: the rites of Hajj.
al-Hasan: He tested him with seven things: He tested him with the stars, the moon, and the sun, and he did well in that and knew that his Lord is Everlasting and does not cease; He tested him with the fire, and he endured that; He tested him with the sacrifice of his son, and he endured that; and with circumcision, and he endured that; and with the migration, and he endured that.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they are the words of Ibrahim and Isma'il when they raised the House: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾ [2:127], and they raised it with "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest."
Yaman: they are his argument with his people. Allah said: ﴿And his people argued with him﴾, to His words, ﴿And that is Our argument which We gave to Ibrahim against his people﴾ [6:83].
Abu Rawq: they are his words (peace be upon him): ﴿He who created me, and He guides me﴾ [26:78], the verses. Some of them said: Allah tested him in his wealth, his children, and his self; he gave his wealth to guests, his children to sacrifice, his self to the fire, and his heart to the Most Merciful, so He took him as a friend (khalil). It was also said: they are the portions of Islam, and they are ten: the testimony that there is no god but Allah, which is the creed (milla) and prayer, which is the bridge... He said: [and zakat] [[An unreadable word; the reading we have adopted seems likely.]], which is purification, and fasting, which is the shield, and Hajj, which is the law, and jihad, which is victory, and obedience, which is protection, and the community, which is affection, and enjoining good, which is fulfilment, and forbidding evil, which is the proof. ﴿fa-atammahunna﴾.
Qatadah said: "He performed them."
al-Rabi': "He fulfilled them."
al-Dahhak: [... their oaths] [[An unreadable word.]], Yaman: "He acted upon them." Allah said: ﴿Indeed I am making you, O Ibrahim, a leader for the people﴾, so that they may follow you; and its root is from umm, which means intention.
He said: ﴿And from my offspring﴾, meaning from my children also. So make them leaders who will be followed. The root of dhurriyyah is "young children," derived from dharr because of their multitude; it was also said it is from dharr, meaning creation, and the hamza was lightened and doubling (tashdid) was introduced in place of the hamza, as in al-bariyyah.
It was said: it is from dharw, and in it there are three dialects:
dhurriyyah with a kasra on the dhal, which is the reading of Zayd ibn Thabit; dhurriyyah with a fatha, which is the reading of Abu Ja'far; and dhurriyyah with a damma, which is the reading of the common people.
Allah said: ﴿My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers﴾, that is, it does not reach or attain.
﴿My covenant (ʿahdī) the wrongdoers﴾: in it there are three readings: ʿahdī al-ẓālimūn, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and Talhah ibn Musarrif; ʿahdī al-ẓālimīn with the yā' made a standing (irtijāl) yā', which is the reading of Abu Raja', al-A'mash, and Hamzah; and ʿahdiya al-ẓālimīn with a fatha on the yā', which is the reading of the common people. They differed about this covenant: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said:
"My mercy."
al-Dahhak: "My obedience." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾ [2:40].
al-Suddi: "Fulfilment." Its evidence is His words: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its binding﴾ [2:27].
Mujahid: "It is not the wrongdoer who is to be obeyed in his wrongdoing."
Abu Hudhayfah: "My trust." Its evidence is His words: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you pledge﴾ [16:91].
Abu 'Ubayd: "My wishes (amani)." Its evidence is His words: ﴿So complete for them their covenant until their term﴾ [9:4]. It was also said: "My faith (iman)," and its evidence is His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan﴾ [36:60].
﴿And when We made the House﴾, meaning the Ka'bah.
﴿a place of return (mathaba)﴾: a place of return (marji'an); mathab and mathabah are one, like maqam and maqamah. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning a refuge and a sanctuary.
Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak: [they return] to it from every direction and perform Hajj, and they never tire of it; for no one visits it without wishing to return to it.
Qatadah and 'Ikrimah: "a gathering place." Talhah ibn Musarrif recited: "mathabat" in the plural.
﴿for the people and a sanctuary (amnan)﴾: a place of safety, where they are secure.
Ibn 'Abbas said: whoever commits an offence outside the Haram and then takes refuge in the Haram is secure from being attacked within it; but he is not sheltered, nor mixed with, nor traded with, and he is kept apart; when he leaves it, the legal punishment (hadd) is carried out upon him. And whoever commits an offence within the Haram, the legal punishment is carried out upon him within it.
﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾: Shaybah, Ibn 'Amir, Nafi', al-A'raj, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Salam recited: "wa-attakhadha" with a fatha on the kha', as a statement; and the rest recited with a kasra, as a command.
Ibn Kaysan said: They mention that the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ passed by the Station, and with him was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this not the station of our father Ibrahim?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then should we not take it as a place of prayer?"
He said: "I have not been commanded to do that."
[105] [[Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 37; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/174.]]
Then the sun had not set on that day before this was revealed: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾.
From Anas ibn Malik: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "My Lord agreed with me in three things."
I said: "Would that you took the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer," and Allah sent down: ﴿And take, from the station of Ibrahim, a place of prayer﴾. And I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked come in to you; if only you would screen the Mothers of the Believers." So Allah sent down the verse of hijab. He said:
"And something reached me that happened between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet ﴿ﷺ﴾, so I rebuked them and I kept saying to them: 'Either you refrain from the Messenger of Allah, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you,' until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers."
And Umm Salamah said: "O 'Umar, is there not in the Messenger of Allah what would make his wives content, that you should admonish them like this?" And she fell silent, so Allah sent down: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you, submissive, believing﴾ [66:5], the verse.
They differed about the meaning of His words: ﴿from the station of Ibrahim﴾. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The whole Haram is the station of Ibrahim."
Yaman: "The whole mosque is the station of Ibrahim."
Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Suddi: "It is prayer beside the station of Ibrahim; they were commanded to pray beside it, and they were not commanded to wipe it or kiss it."
As for its story and the beginning of his affair:
Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Ibrahim brought Isma'il and Hajar and placed them in Mecca, and he remained in that state for a period, and the Jurhumites settled there, and Isma'il married a woman from them, and Hajar died. Ibrahim asked Sarah's permission to visit Hajar, and she gave him permission, but stipulated that he should not stay. Ibrahim came, and Hajar had died, so he went to Isma'il's house. He said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He is not here; he has gone hunting." Isma'il used to leave the Haram, hunt, and then return. Ibrahim said to her: "Do you have any hospitality? Do you have food or drink?" She said: "I have nothing, and no one with me has anything."
Ibrahim said: "When your husband comes, greet him, and say to him: 'Let him change the threshold of his door.'" Ibrahim left, and Isma'il came and smelled his father's scent. He said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?"
She said: "An old man came to me, with such-and-such a description," as if she belittled his description. He said: "What did he say to you?"
She said: "He said to me: 'Give my greetings to your husband, and tell him: let him change the threshold of his door.'" So he divorced her and married another. Ibrahim remained as long as Allah willed, then asked Sarah's permission to visit Isma'il, and she permitted him, stipulating that he should not stay. Ibrahim came until he reached Isma'il's house.
Ibrahim said to his wife: "Where is your husband?"
She said: "He has gone hunting, and he will come now, God willing; dismount, may Allah have mercy on you."
He said to her: "Do you have hospitality?"
She said: "Yes," and she brought milk and meat, and he prayed for blessing for them. Had she brought bread of wheat, barley or dates that day, the land of Allah would have been wheat, barley and dates. She said to him: "Dismount until I wash your head." He did not dismount, so she brought the Station and he put it under his right side, and he placed his foot upon it, and she washed the right side of his head. Then she moved the Station to his left side, and the mark of his foot remained upon it, and she washed the left side of his head. He said to her: "When your husband comes, greet him and say to him: 'The threshold of your door has been made right.'" When Isma'il came, he smelled his father's scent and said to his wife: "Has anyone come to you?" She said: "Yes, an old man, the most handsome of people in appearance and the most fragrant in scent. He said to me such-and-such, and I said to him such-and-such, and I washed his head, and this is the place of his feet on the Station." He said to her: "That was Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 1/181, ed. al-A'lami, Beirut.]]
Anas ibn Malik said: "I saw in the Station the mark of his fingers, his heel and the sole of his foot, except that the wiping of people's hands has removed it."
Nafi' ibn Shaybah said: "I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar say: I bear witness three times that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ say: 'The Corner (stone) and the Station are two rubies from the rubies of Paradise. Allah extinguished their light, and had He not extinguished their light, they would have lit up what is between the east and the west.'" [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 8/36; Musnad Ahmad: 2/213.]]
﴿We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il﴾: that is, We commanded them and entrusted them.
﴿that purify My House﴾, the Ka'bah: that is, build it upon purity and monotheism.
Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umar, 'Ata' and Muqatil said: ﴿purify My House﴾ from idols, doubts and false speech. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "What is this? Do you know where you are?"
al-Awza'i from 'Uhdah ibn Abi Lubabah from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed Allah revealed to me: O brother of the messengers, O brother of the warners, warn your people that they should not enter any of My houses except with sound hearts, truthful tongues, pure hands and chaste private parts; and that they should not enter any of My houses while anyone among them has a wrong against another, for I curse him as long as he stands before Me praying, until he returns that wrong to its people. Then I will be his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, he will be among My friends and chosen ones, and his neighbour will be with the Prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/933; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/115.]]
Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: its meaning is "fumigate it and perfume it." [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/114.]]
Makhul from Mu'adh ibn Jabal from the Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾, who said: "Keep your mosques away from your boys [[In the sources the word 'ghilmanakum' does not occur; what occurs is: 'keep your mosques away from your children and your insane persons...']] - meaning your children and your insane - and draw your swords, raise your voices, your punishments, your disputes, your selling and your buying; perfume them on the day of your Friday gathering, and place at their doors what is in front of you." [[Al-Majmu' of al-Nawawi: 20/132; Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/247, no. 750.]]
al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ja'far and the people of Medina recited ﴿baytiya﴾ with a fatha on the yā'; the others recited it with a sukun.
This is the attribution of the House to Himself, Glorified is He, for distinction and honour.
﴿for those who circle (al-ta'ifin)﴾ around it, and they are those who come to it from the horizons of the earth. ﴿and those who remain (al-'akifin)﴾, that is, those who stay in it, and they are the residents of the Haram. ﴿and those who bow (al-ruka')﴾: plural of rak'i. ﴿the prostrating (al-sujud)﴾: plural of sajid, like qa'id and qu'ud.
'Ata' said: If one is circling, he is among the tai'in; if he is sitting, he is among the 'akifin; and if he is praying, he is among the ruka' and sujud.
al-Awza'i from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﴿ﷺ﴾ said: "Indeed, every day and night, one hundred and twenty mercies descend upon this House: sixty for those who circle it, forty for those who pray, and twenty for those who look upon it." [[Tarikh Dimashq: 34/388.]]
﴿And when Ibrahim said: My Lord, make this﴾, meaning Mecca or the Haram,
﴿a secure city (baladan amina)﴾: that is, a place where it is safe, where its people are secure.
﴿and provide its people with fruits, those of them who believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. al-Akhfash said: "Man amana (those who believe) is a substitute for ahlahu (its people) by way of clarification, as one says: 'I took the wealth, two-thirds of it, and I saw the people, some of them.' This is substitution of part for whole, like His words: ﴿And for Allah is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ [3:97]."
Allah said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, I will provide for him a little﴾: I will sustain him until the end of his term, because He, Exalted is He, promised provision to all creatures, the disbeliever and the believer alike; and it was restricted to "little" because the enjoyment of this world is little. Mu'awiyah and Ibn 'Amir recited: ﴿fa-amti'hu﴾ with a damma on the alif and a sukun on the mim, lightly; and Ubayy recited: "fa-numti'uhu qaliran thumma nadtarruhu" with the nun.
﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ with the alif joined and a fatha on the ra', in the form of a supplication from Ibrahim (peace be upon him); and the rest recited ﴿fa-umatti'uhu﴾ with a damma on the alif and shaddah, and ﴿thumma adtarruhu﴾ as a statement: that is, Paradise in the Hereafter, ﴿to the punishment of the Fire; and wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place of return to which you come.
﴿And when Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, and Isma'il﴾: the narrators related from various chains about the building of the Ka'bah, and I have gathered their accounts and arranged them to be finer in expression and closer to understanding.
They said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the place of the House two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out from beneath it. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Adam down to the earth, his head touched the sky until he became bald, and he bequeathed baldness to his children; and the beasts of the earth fled from his height, and from that day they became wild. He used to hear the speech of the people of heaven, their supplication and their glorification, and he was at ease with them, but the angels feared him and his soul was troubled. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reduced him to sixty cubits by his own cubit. When Adam lost what he used to hear of the voices and glorification of the angels, he became lonely and complained of that to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So Allah sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, the speech being cut off, with two doors of green emerald, an eastern door and a western door, and Allah sent down in it lamps from Paradise, and placed it at the site of the House until now. Then He said: "O Adam, I have sent down for you a house which you shall circle as one circles around My Throne, and pray beside it as one prays beside My Throne."
Then He sent down the Black Stone to him. He wiped his tears with it, and it had been white, but when menstruating women touched it in the Jahiliyyah, it became black.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Black Stone is a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and had it not been touched by the polytheists with their impurities, no one with an ailment would touch it without Allah, exalted is He, curing him." [110] [[In the margin of the manuscript: qayyada: qaddara (decreed, determined).]]

Adam set out from the land of India toward Makkah on foot, and Allah appointed for him an angel [[With variation in al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/587, hadith 3803, and al-Ahd al-Muhammadiyya: 224.]] to guide him to the House.

It was said to Mujahid: "O Abu'l-Hajjaj, why did he not ride?"

He said: "What would he have carried? By Allah, his stride was a three-day journey, and every place his foot touched became a settlement, and what lay beyond it was deserts and wastelands. He came to Makkah, performed Hajj to the House, and carried out the rites. When he had finished, the angels met him and said: 'May your Hajj be accepted, O Adam; we performed Hajj to this House two thousand years before you.'"
