Al-A'mash recited: fala rafuth ('ala al-jami') (without the tanwin and a different vowel pattern, applied to all).

The commentators differed in interpreting "rafath."

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, al-Hasan, 'Amr ibn Dinar, Qatadah, Ibrahim, al-Rabi', al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak said: "rafath" is sexual intercourse.

Tawus and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "rafath" is allusion to women concerning intercourse, and mentioning it in front of [...] [an unreadable word in the manuscript].

'Ata' said: "rafath" is a man saying to a woman, while in the state of ihram, "If you become free, I will have you."

Abu Husayn ibn Qays said: I accompanied Ibn 'Abbas on the Hajj, and I was his close friend. When we had entered ihram, Ibn 'Abbas struck his camel's tail, so it turned, and he was chanting rajaz and saying:
"And they walk with us in a sway,
if the bird tells the truth, we shall have [her] in the evening."
[[al-Mabsut li-l-Sarakhsi: 4/6.]]

I said to him: "Do you engage in rafath while you are in ihram?"
He said: "Rafath is only what is said in the presence of women."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Rafath is sexual intercourse, kissing, touching, and speaking to her with obscene words; that is how it is."

Some said: "rafath" is obscenity and foul speech.

As for fusuq: Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Rabi', al-Zuhri, and al-Qurazi said: "fusuq" is all acts of disobedience to God.

Al-Dahhak said: it is mutual insulting by nicknames, as evidenced by the saying: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames; wretched is the name of wickedness after faith﴾ (49:11).

Ibn Zayd said: it is [...] [an unreadable word in the manuscript] by idols; the Prophet ﷺ forbade that when he performed Hajj, and taught his community the rites. Its evidence is the saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned, for it is indeed wickedness﴾ (6:121), and His saying: ﴿that which has been dedicated to other than God﴾ (5:3; 16:115).

Ibrahim, Mujahid, and 'Ata' said: it is reviling. Evidence for it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Reviling a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/223.]]

Ibn 'Umar said: it is what God forbade the one in ihram, such as hunting, trimming the nails, shaving the hair, and similar things.

As for jidal (quarreling): Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn Muhammad, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, 'Ata' ibn Yasar, Mu'adh ibn Abi Rabah, and Qatadah said: jidal is that you dispute with your companion and contend with him until you overcome him.

Ibn 'Umar said: it is [mutual] cursing and contention.

Al-Qurazi said: when the Quraysh gathered at Mina, one group would say, "Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj," and the other would say, "Our Hajj is more complete than yours."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: it is that some of them say, "The Hajj is today," and others say, "The Hajj is tomorrow."

Ibn Zayd said: they used to stand at different places, disputing, each one claiming that his station was the station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). God cut this off when He taught His Prophet ﷺ its rites.

Muqatil said: the Prophet ﷺ said in the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Whoever does not have an offering with him, let him leave ihram and make it an 'umrah." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/40; Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 384.]]

They said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have declared ihram for the Hajj," and that was their dispute.

Mujahid said: its meaning is: "there is no doubt about the Hajj, that it is in Dhu al-Hijjah," so the intercalation (nasi') was abolished, and the Hajj became fixed as it is today.

The scholars of meanings [ahl al-ma'ani] said: the wording is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition, meaning: do not engage in obscenity, do not commit wickedness, and do not quarrel. This is like His saying: ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾ (2:2), meaning: do not doubt it.

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever performs the Hajj to this House, and does not engage in obscenity nor in wickedness, will come out from his sins as on the day his mother bore him." [[al-Majmu' by Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi: 7/351-3; Kanz al-'Ummal: 5/7.]]

On the authority of Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, who said: I and Sufyan al-Thawri used to perform tawaf together, and Sufyan withdrew while I remained in the tawaf. I entered the Hijr and prayed near the water spout (al-mizab). While I was prostrating, I heard speech between the curtains of the House and the stones, and it was saying: "I complain to God and then to You of what [...] does, and the tawaf-performers around me, from their jesting in conversation [and their noise and their enthusiasm]." Wuhayb said: I interpreted it as the House complaining to Gabriel.

﴿And whatever good you do, God knows it﴾, meaning He will reward you for it.

﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety.﴾

The commentators said: some people from Yemen used to perform the Hajj without provisions, saying, "We rely upon God," and saying, "We are going to the House of God; will He not feed us?" [...] They began by wronging the people and seizing their property. So God commanded them to take provisions, and not to wrong people, and not to be a burden upon people. So He said: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾, and they would thereby keep their faces (from begging).

The commentators said: [provisions are] biscuit, oil, parched grain (sawiq), dates, and similar things.

Nafi' related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: when they entered ihram, they would have with them provisions, which they threw away, and they [competed] for the provision of the Hereafter. So God revealed: ﴿And take provision﴾; He forbade them from that and commanded them to safeguard provisions, and to take provisions for one who had none. So He commanded them to piety by restraining from wrongdoing. He said: ﴿for the best provision is piety.﴾

The people of allusion [ahl al-isharah] said: God reminded them of the journey of the Hereafter and urged them to take provision for both abodes, for piety is the provision of the Hereafter.

The poet said:
Death is a surging sea whose waves
in which the cunning of the swimmer vanishes.

Another said:
A person will not accompany him into his grave
except piety and righteous deeds.

Al-A'sha said:
If you do not depart with provision of piety,
and meet after death one who has provisioned himself,
you will regret not being like him,
and that you did not prepare as he prepared. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/412.]]

Malik ibn Dinar said: one of the reciters of Basra died, and we joked during the funeral and then departed. Then Sa'dun the Majnun climbed up, recited in the graveyard, and called out to the ascetics, and he began to recite:
"No, O army of the living, this is the army of the dead;
they answered the lesser call, and they await the greater.
They yearn over provision, and provision is nothing but hospitality;
they say to you: prepare, for this is the end of the world."

God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And fear Me, O people of understanding﴾, meaning those of intellects.

The Sacred Month for the sacred month. It was revealed concerning the 'umrah of the making-up (al-qada'), and that was because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made a treaty with the people of Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, that he would turn back that year and return the following year, on condition that they would vacate Makkah for him for three days, so that he and his companions could enter, perform 'umrah, circumambulate the House, and do whatever they wished, on condition that they would not enter except with the weapons of travelers, and would not leave with anyone of the people of Makkah accompanying them. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned back that year and returned the following year in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and they entered Makkah, performed 'umrah, circumambulated, sacrificed, and remained for three days. Then God revealed: "The sacred month" – Dhu al-Qa'dah, in which you entered Makkah, performed 'umrah, and completed your rites and circumambulation, in the year seven – "for the sacred month" – Dhu al-Qa'dah, in which you were prevented from the House and were hindered from your purpose, in the year six.

"The month" is in the nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in His words "for the sacred month." "Al-hurumat" is the plural of hurmah, like "al-zulumat" is the plural of zulmah and "al-hujurat" is the plural of hujrah. Hurmah is that which must be preserved and whose violation must be avoided. The plural "hurumat" is used because He meant the sacred month, the sacred land, and the sanctity of the state of ihram. "Qisas" (retaliation) means equivalence and parity: it is that the doer be treated as he did. "Whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you" (fa-man i'tada 'alaykum fa-i'tadu 'alayhi, qatiluhu bi-mithli ma i'tada 'alaykum). Thus the recompense is named by the name of the initial act [[In the margin of the manuscript: al-i'tida'.]] in correspondence with the conditional clause. "And fear God, and know that God is with the God-fearing. And spend in the way of God, and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," the verse. Know that "al-tahlukah" is a verbal noun meaning destruction, and it is of the form tafʿilah from halak (perishing).

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Khazarnaji say: I know of no verbal noun in the speech of the Arabs on the pattern tafʿulah with a damma on the ʿayn except this one.

Some said: al-tahlukah is everything whose outcome becomes destruction.

The meaning of His words "do not cast with your own hands" is: do not proceed in that. It is said of anyone who begins a deed: "he has cast his hands into it." Labid said, describing the sun:

"Until, when it cast a hand into the disbeliever / and concealed the flaws of the frontiers with its darkness" [[Majma' al-Bayan: 1/515; ajanna: concealed; ʿawarat al-thughur: its gaps.]]

That is, it began to set.

Al-Mubarrad said: "do not cast with your own hands" means yourselves; he expressed the whole by the part, as in His words, "That is for what your own hands have sent forward" and "for what your hands have earned." The "bi" in "bi-aydikum" is superfluous, as in "it grows with the oil." The poet said:

"And indeed I filled Nasib's [[Nasib: a man's name.]] skin with displeasure, / for a friend indeed blames."

He means: I filled his skin with displeasure.

They said: The Arabs say of a person "he cast his hand" only in evil.

The scholars differed concerning the interpretation of this verse.

Some said: This is about miserliness and withholding expenditure. He says: "And spend in the way of God," and do not withhold spending in the way of God, for withholding at the time of spending in the way of God is destruction. This is the view of Hudhayfah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Kaysan.

Ibn ʿAbbas said concerning this verse: Spend in the way of God even if you have only an arrow or a spearhead, and let none of you say, "I do not find anything."  [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/362.]]

al-Suddi said: "Then spend in the way of God even by a mithqal." "And do not cast with your own hands into destruction": do not say, "I have nothing."

Mujahid: "We do not forbid you expenditure in the right, out of fear of poverty."

al-Hasan: They used to travel and go on raids without spending from their wealth, so God revealed this verse.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded the people to prepare for the pilgrimage – it was said: for the 'umrah – in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and whenever he intended a journey his herald would proclaim it, informing them so that they might prepare the necessities of travel, when he commanded them to make ready, some men of the Bedouins present in Madinah stood before him and said: "O Messenger of God, with what shall we prepare? By God, we have neither provision nor wealth to prepare with, and no one will feed us." So God revealed this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When God commanded spending, some men said: "We have been commanded to spend in the way of God; if we spend our wealth, we will remain poor and destitute." So God said: "And do not cast with your own hands into destruction," meaning: spend, and do not fear poverty, for I am the Provider and will replace it for you.

al-Khalil ibn ʿAbd Allah, from ʿAli, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, Jabir, and ʿImran ibn Husayn, all narrate from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expenditure in the way of God while remaining in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham; and whoever fights himself in the way of God and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham" [70] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/305; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/236.]]. Then he recited this verse: "And God multiplies for whom He wills" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 261.]].

al-Nadr ibn ʿAziz narrated from ʿIkrimah concerning "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction": "Do not aim at the wicked part of it, of which you spend."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: Men used to go out in expeditions that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) dispatched without provision, so either they were cut off, or they were dependents; so God commanded them to spend on themselves in the way of God. And if you do not have what you can spend, do not go out yourself without provision or strength, and so cast yourself into destruction. And "destruction" is that one perish from hunger or thirst. Then he said to the one who withholds and is stingy: "And do good; indeed God loves the good-doers."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The people used to be on the path of God, and a man would take provision, and his provision would be better than another's, so people would spend from his provision until nothing remained of it, and he wished to console his companion. So God revealed this verse.

Some said: This verse was revealed concerning abandoning jihad.

Zayd ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam ibn ʿImran, said: We raided Constantinople, and over the people of Egypt was ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, a companion of the Messenger of God, and over the people of Syria was Fadalah ibn ʿUbayd, a companion of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and over the main body was ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid. He said: We stood in ranks, and I never saw ranks wider or longer than them, while the Romans had their backs pressed against the wall of the city. He said: A man from among us charged the Roman ranks until he broke through them, then came out toward us retreating, and the people cried out and said: "Glory be to God! He has cast himself with his own hands into destruction!"

Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said: You interpret this verse in this way – that a man charges fighting seeking martyrdom, or does something harmful to himself. We are more knowing of this verse; it was revealed concerning us, the group of the Ansar. When God had honored His religion and granted victory to His Messenger, we said among ourselves [O assembly of the Ansar] [[So in the original.]] secretly from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "We have left our families and our wealth until Islam spread and God granted victory to His Prophet. The war has laid down its burdens. If we return to our families and children and stay with them, we will repair what was lost of them." So God revealed concerning us: "And spend in the way of God, and do not cast with your own hands into destruction."

And "destruction" is staying with family and wealth and abandoning jihad.

Abu ʿImran said: Abu Ayyub continued to fight in the way of God until he was buried in Constantinople [[Cf. Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/279.]].

Abu al-Jawza narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Destruction" is the punishment of God, the Mighty and Majestic; meaning: do not abandon jihad, lest you be punished. Its evidence is His words, "If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment" [[Surah al-Tawbah: 39.]].

From [Yazid] ibn Abi Unaysah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three are from the essence of faith: refraining from one who says, 'There is no god but God' – do not declare him an unbeliever for a sin, nor expel him from Islam for a deed; jihad continues since God the Mighty and Majestic sent me until the last of my community fights the Dajjal, [which is not nullified by] tyranny or justice; and faith in predestination" [71] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/569; Nasb al-Rayah: 4/221.]].

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without having fought and without having resolved in himself to fight, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy" [72] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/259; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/562; al-Mustadrak: 2/79.]].

Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sufyan said: It is the man who advances between the two ranks and charges the people alone.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and ʿUbaydah al-Salmani said: Casting oneself into destruction is despair of the mercy of God.

Abu Qilabah said: It is the man who commits a sin and says, "I am ruined; there is no repentance," so he despairs of God's mercy and plunges into disobedience. So God forbade them from that.

Yaman ibn Ruʾab and al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah said: A man "casts his hands" when he submits to destruction and despairs of salvation.

From Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from [his father], concerning this verse, "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction," it was said to him: Is it the man who charges a battalion of a thousand with the sword? He said: No, rather it is the man who commits a sin, then casts his hands and says, "There is no repentance for me."

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿA'ishah, said: Habib ibn al-Harith came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man who has many sins." He said: "Repent to God, O Habib." He said: "O Messenger of God, I repent, then I return." He said: "Whenever you sin, repent." He said: "Then, O Messenger of God, my sins will multiply." He said: "The pardon of God is greater than your sins, O Habib ibn al-Harith" [73] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/200; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/123.]].

Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said concerning this verse, "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction": [it means] by evil opinion of God; "and think well of God; indeed God loves the good-doers" [means] think well of Him.

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib, who said: We entered upon Abu Nuwas al-Hasan ibn Hani to visit him in his illness in which he died, and with us was Salih ibn ʿAli al-Hashimi. Salih said to him: "Repent to God, O Abu ʿAli, for you are at the first day of the days of the Hereafter and the last day of the days of this world, and between you and God there are faults." He said: "Prop me up. You threaten me with God? Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to me from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'My intercession is only made for the people of major sins from my community. Do you think I would not be among them?'" [74] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/190, with variation.]]

And Hammad narrated to us from Thabit, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two men will come out of the Fire and be presented before God, the Mighty and Majestic. Then they will be commanded back to the Fire. One of them turns and says: 'My Lord, this was not my hope.' God says: 'And what was your hope?' He says: 'My hope was that when You bring me out of it, You would not return me to it.' So God, the Mighty and Majestic, has mercy on him and admits him to Paradise" [75] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/70, 285; Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/99.]].

"And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God."

Ibn Abi Ishaq read: (al-hijj) with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ throughout the Qur'an, and it is the dialect of Tamim and Qays Ghaylan.

It is mentioned from Talhah ibn Musarrif: with the kasrah here and in Surah Al ʿImran, and with the fathah in the rest of the Qur'an.

Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and ʿAsim, by the narration of Hafs, read it with the kasrah in Al ʿImran and with the fathah in the rest of the Qur'an.

The rest read it with the fathah throughout the Qur'an, and it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, with no difference between them in meaning, like "rattl" and "rattl" with a fathah and a kasrah [......] [[A blank in the manuscript, the meaning being complete.]].

Abu Mu'adh said: (al-hajj) with the fathah is a verbal noun, and al-hijj with the kasrah is a noun, like "qism" and "qism," "shurb" and "shurb," "suqy" and "suqy." And in the Codex of ʿAbd Allah: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God, at the House."

ʿAlqamah and Ibrahim read: "wa-atimmu al-hajja wal-ʿumrata."

The commentators differed concerning completing them.

Some said: The meaning is: complete the Hajj and 'Umrah with their rites, their limits, and their sunnah. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAlqamah, Ibrahim, and Mujahid.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning this verse: Whoever enters the state of ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah is not permitted to exit until he completes it. The completion of Hajj is the day of sacrifice, when he throws the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and then circumambulates the House, and he has then exited from his ihram entirely. The completion of 'Umrah is when he circumambulates the House and goes between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and then he has exited. The obligatory elements of Hajj are four: the ihram, standing at ʿArafah, the circumambulation of ifadah, and the circumambulation and sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. The obligatory elements of 'Umrah are all four: the obligatory ihram, the circumambulation, the sa'y, and the shaving or shortening, and the minimum is three hairs.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Tawus narrated: The completion of Hajj and 'Umrah is that one enters ihram for both separately... [[An unreadable word.]] ...

Shu'bah narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salamah, who said: A man came to ʿAli and said: "Tell me about the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God.'" He said: "That you enter ihram from your household's dwelling."

Qatadah said: [Completing the 'umrah] is that one performs 'umrah outside the months of Hajj; and if one remains in the months of Hajj and then performs Hajj, it is tamattu', and upon him is a sacrifice if he finds one, or fasting. And completing Hajj is that one performs all its rites so that no penalty of qiran or tamattu' is incurred by him.

Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: The Messenger of God said: "An 'umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj" [76] [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi: 4/346; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 4/7.]].

al-Dahhak said: Its completion [is that] the expenditure be lawful, and one refrains from what God has forbidden.

Sufyan said: Its completion is that one sets out from his land for the two (Hajj and 'Umrah) alone, not intending anything else, and does not set out for trade or for some need; until, when you are near Makkah, you say: "If only I had performed Hajj or 'Umrah." That suffices, but the completion is that one sets out for them and does not set out for other than them.

Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Ba'li [as in the original] narrated from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God said: "A time will come upon the people when the wealthy among them will perform Hajj for recreation, their middle class for trade, their reciters for show and reputation, and their poor for begging" [77] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 5/133, no. 12362; Tarikh Baghdad: 10/295.]].

In this sense ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: "The delegations are many and the pilgrims are few."

The ruling of the verse

The jurists differed concerning 'umrah. A group said: it is a good sunnah and not an obligatory duty; this is the view of Ahmad, Malik ibn Anas, Abu Thawr, and the old opinion of al-Shafi'i, and it is the choice of Jarir ibn Muhammad al-Tabari. They argued by the reading of al-Sha'bi, "wa-atimmu al-hajja wal-ʿumratu lillah," in the nominative.

And by what was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about 'umrah: "Is it obligatory or not?" and [he said]: "That you perform 'umrah is better for you." And that the Hajj is an obligation for the emigrant, and 'umrah is voluntary. They also said: When God mentioned the obligation of Hajj, He did not mention 'umrah with it. And the Mighty One said: "And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House" [[Surah Al ʿImran: 97.]].

Others said: 'Umrah is obligatory, and it is the lesser Hajj. This is the view of ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, ʿAta', Qatadah, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, and the new opinion and the more correct view of al-Shafi'i, and the choice of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. They argued with the reading of the majority, "wal-ʿumrata," in the accusative, meaning: complete the obligation of Hajj and 'umrah.

And by what was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection" [78] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/205, no. 926; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 5/181.]].

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "By God, 'umrah is indeed obligatory alongside Hajj in the Book of God: 'And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God.'" Ibn ʿUmar said: "There is no one of God's creation except that upon him is an obligatory Hajj and 'umrah, if he is able to a way to it, as God the Exalted said. Whoever adds beyond that, it is good and voluntary."

Masruq said: "We were commanded in the Book of God with four: establishing the prayer, giving the zakah, Hajj, and 'umrah. So 'umrah was placed in relation to Hajj as zakah is in relation to prayer." Then he recited this verse: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 194–197 (part 2 of 3):

Abd al-Malik ibn Sulayman said: A man asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the Prophet (ﷺ), whether ʿumrah is obligatory (fard) or voluntary (tatawwu'). He said: "It is obligatory." The man said: "But al-Sha'bi says it is voluntary." He said: "Al-Sha'bi has lied." Then he recited ﴿And complete the Hajj and the ʿUmrah for Allah﴾. Whoever says that ʿumrah is not obligatory interprets the verse to mean: complete them once you have entered upon them, and he did not intend that beginning the entry into them is obligatory for him. This is like one who volunteers for Hajj: there is no disagreement that once he has entered into ihram it is incumbent upon him to proceed with it and complete it, though it was not obligatory for him to begin entering it. Likewise ʿumrah. [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/286.]

Similarly, Ibn Wahb narrated from Zayd, who said: "ʿUmrah is not obligatory upon anyone among the people." I said to him: "[What about] the words of Allah, ﴿And complete the Hajj and the ʿUmrah for Allah﴾?" He said: "No one among creation should, once he has begun a matter, fail to complete it; and once he has set out upon it, it is not proper for him to exit it [i.e., cancel it] on a day and then return, just as if he fasts a day, it is not proper for him to break his fast at midday." The proof of this interpretation is His saying, ﴿Then fulfil to them their covenant until their term﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4]. He did not intend by it beginning, but rather completing what had passed of the covenant and agreement. Whoever makes ʿumrah obligatory interprets "completion" to mean beginning and obligating, i.e., establish them and perform them. The proof of this is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And when Abraham was tried by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 124], meaning he performed them and carried them out; and His saying, ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 187], meaning: then begin the fast and complete it, because it is mentioned after eating, drinking and dawn. This is the most correct and clearest view, because it combines the two meanings and keeps the verse in its general sense: its meaning is "begin the ʿumrah, and when you have entered into it, complete it," so it encompasses both aspects of completion. Also, the aspects of it are more numerous, and the reports concerning the obligation of Hajj and ʿumrah together are more apparent and more widely known.

From Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, my father is an old man who cannot perform Hajj or ʿumrah, nor can he ride [a mount]." He said: "Perform Hajj and ʿumrah on behalf of your father." [79] [Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah: 4/459; Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah: 4/346.]

Abu al-Mushfiq said: "I met the Prophet (ﷺ) at ʿArafah, and I drew close to him until my camel's neck and his camel's neck were entwined. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed that will save me from the punishment of Allah and admit me into Paradise.' He said: 'Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayer, pay the obligatory zakah, perform Hajj and ʿumrah, fast Ramadan, and whatever you like people to do to you, do to them; and whatever you dislike people doing to you, leave them from it.'" [80]

ʿAsim, from Shaqiq, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Follow up Hajj with ʿumrah, for they remove poverty and destitution and sins as the bellows removes the impurity of iron, gold and silver; and the accepted Hajj has no reward but Paradise." [81] [Musnad Ahmad: 3/446–447; Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/964.]

On performing Hajj alone (ifrad):

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ʿAʾishah: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed Hajj alone (afrada).

Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ʿAʾishah, who said: "We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeing nothing but Hajj."

Hammad, from Hisham, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, who said: "We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arriving at the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever wishes to enter ihram for Hajj, let him do so; and whoever wishes to enter ihram for ʿumrah, let him do so for ʿumrah.'" [82] [al-Sharh al-Kabir: 3/230; Sharh Maʿani al-Athar: 2/202.] Ifrad is that one enters ihram for Hajj from the miqat and finishes with it, then enters ihram for ʿumrah from Makkah. This is the choice of al-Shafiʿi and his companions.

On combining Hajj and ʿumrah (qiran):

ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Suhayb, Humayd al-Tawil and Yahya ibn Ishaq, all from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Labbayka ʿumrah wa-hajjan, labbayka ʿumrah wa-hajjan.'" [83]

Humayd ibn Hilal said: I heard Mutarrif say: ʿImran ibn al-Husayn said to me: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) combined a Hajj and an ʿumrah, then he died before forbidding them and before the Qur'an was revealed prohibiting them."

From Abu Wa'il, who said: Qays ibn Maʿbad said: "I was a Bedouin Christian, then I embraced Islam, and I was eager for jihad, but I found Hajj and ʿumrah prescribed upon me. I came to a man of my tribe called HurayM ibn ʿAbd Allah and asked him, and he said: 'Combine them, then slaughter what is easy of the offering (hady),' so I entered ihram for both. Then I came to al-ʿUdhayb, where Sulayman ibn Rabi'ah and Zayd ibn Suhan met me while I was in ihram for both, and one of them said to the other: 'This one is no more knowledgeable than a [stray] camel.' So I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have embraced Islam and I am eager for jihad, and I found Hajj and ʿumrah prescribed upon me, so I went to Hurayim ibn ʿAbd Allah, and he said: combine them, then slaughter what is easy of the offering, and I entered ihram for both. When I reached al-ʿUdhayb, Sulayman ibn Rabi'ah and Zayd met me, and one of them said to the other: "This one is no more knowledgeable than a [stray] camel." ʿUmar said: "You have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet (ﷺ)."

ʿAli ibn al-Hasan, from ʿUthman ibn al-Hakam: ʿUthman forbade mut'ah and forbade combining Hajj and ʿumrah. ʿAli said: "Labbayka with Hajj and ʿumrah together." ʿUthman said: "Will you do it while I forbid it?" ʿAli said: "I would not leave the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for anyone among the people." [84] [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Sahih 2/151, Dar al-Fikr edition, and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 5/148.]

The Qur'an did not forbid combining Hajj and ʿumrah together from the miqat; this is the choice of Abu Hanifah and his companions.

On ﴿But if you are held back, then [offer] what is easy of the offering﴾: The scholars differed over the meaning of "ihsar" (being prevented), for which Allah has prescribed ﴿what is easy of the offering﴾ upon the one afflicted with it in his Hajj and ʿumrah.

Some said: it is every hindrance or obstacle that prevents the muhrim and restrains him from the act that Allah has obligated upon him in his ihram and from reaching the Sacred House, whatever it may be: illness, injury, fracture, fear, an enemy, a scorpion sting, loss of provisions, his mount going astray, or other excuses. He remains in his state of ihram where he is and sends his offering, or [sends] from the offering; and when the offering is slaughtered he exits ihram. This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Hasan, Mujahid, ʿAta', Qatadah, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Muqatil and al-Kalbi, and the position of the people of Iraq. They argued that ihsar in the speech of the Arabs is the creation of a cause such as illness and the like, not coercion and domination; but preventing by an enemy through imprisonment and coercion by a dominating authority is ḥaṣr, not iḥṣār. Thus said al-Kisa'i, Abu ʿUbaydah and al-Farra': whatever is by illness or loss of provisions is called ḥaṣr, so he is muḥṣar; and whatever is by fear of an enemy or imprisonment is called ḥaṣr, so he is maḥṣūr. The proof is His saying, ﴿And We made Hell a prison (ḥaṣīr) for the disbelievers﴾, meaning a confinement. They said: We made the enemy's confinement an ihsar only by analogy with illness, since it has its ruling, [so there is no] clear evidence. [Thus in the original.]

Others said: rather, it is that an enemy or a coercive person from among the children of Adam prevents one from reaching the House; as for illness and other excuses, they do not fall within this verse.

This is the view of Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and the position of al-Shafiʿi and the people of Madinah. They argued that this verse was revealed concerning the story of al-Hudaybiyah, and that was ihsar by an enemy. The proof is His words in the context of the verse, ﴿and when you are secure﴾, which can only be from fear.

And in a hadith: "There is no ihsar except by the confinement of an enemy." [85] [Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/293.]

Tha'lab said: The Arabs say "ḥaṣartu al-rajul ʿan ḥājatihi" (I restrained the man from his need), so he is maḥṣūr; and "aḥṣarahu al-ʿaduww" (the enemy restrained him) when he prevented him from traveling, so he is muḥṣar. Yunus narrated from Abu ʿAmr that he said: "If you prevent him from every direction, then you have aḥṣartahu."

Al-Shafiʿi said: If one is restrained by an enemy, whether a disbelieving or a Muslim enemy, or by an authority that imprisons him, he slaughters an offering for his restraint where he was restrained, within the sacred territory or outside it, and exits ihram, with nothing further due unless it was obligatory, in which case he makes it up. If he does not find an offering to buy, or he is poor, there are two opinions: one, that he does not exit ihram except with an offering; and the other, that he exits when he is unable to obtain it, and brings it when he is able.

Some jurists said: If its substitution is not accepted and he owes food or fasting, then whatever is due upon the muhrim from his body, compensation, offering or charity, is not valid except within the Sacred Precinct, for the poor of its people, except in two places. One of them: the offering of the one restrained by an enemy, for he slaughters it where he was detained and exits ihram. The other: one who drives an offering for a purpose and it is injured on the way, so he slaughters it and leaves it between it and the poor; it is not permissible for him or for his associates to eat anything of it, even if they are poor.

If what he drove was for a purpose, such as being a qarin or a mutamatti', it is permissible for him to eat and to feed others. This is the meaning and ruling of ihsar. As for illness and what resembles it, he may seek treatment as far as necessary and pay a ransom, then make it an ʿumrah, and perform Hajj in the following year and offer an offering. His saying ﴿fa-ma istaysara﴾ means: upon him is what is easy. Its place is in the nominative case; and if you wish, you may take it to be in the accusative, meaning "whatever is easy." As for ﴿mina al-hady﴾ like "jadiyyat al-sarj" (the saddle-buckles), whose plural is "jadi"; so said Abu ʿAmr, who said: "I do not know a third instance of this in the language."

Al-Aʿraj recited (al-Hadiyyi) with a kasrah on the dal and shaddah on the ya in the whole Qur'an, on the meaning of the passive participle.

ʿIsmah narrated from ʿAsim: with shaddah on the hady in the position of nominative and genitive, and with a light pronunciation in the accusative, like His saying ﴿hadyan baligha al-Kaʿbah﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 95] and ﴿wa-la al-hady wa-la al-qala'id﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 2]. Both of these refer to what is sent as an offering to the houses of Allah, and it was so named because it is drawn near to Allah in the manner of a gift (hadiyyah) that a person sends to another, seeking nearness by what he sends.

They differed over the interpretation of His saying ﴿fa-ma istaysara min al-hady﴾.

ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas said: a sheep (shah).

Ibn ʿUmar said: "What is easy of the offering" refers to camels and cattle: one camel rather than another camel, one cow rather than another cow, one age rather than another age; and he denied that a sheep is part of the offering. The strongest and most correct view is the view of those who said it is a sheep, because it is closer to ease, and because Allah called the sheep a hady in His saying ﴿hadyan baligha al-Ka'bah﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 95], and in the gazelle there is a sheep's equivalent.

﴿And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice (mahill)﴾. They differed over the place at which the offering of the one restrained reaches its place. Some said: it is its slaughter or sacrifice at the place where he is restrained, whether within the ḥill (permitted territory) or the ḥaram (sacred territory); and the meaning of "its place" is the time at which its slaughter and consumption and benefit become lawful. Like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) about the meat that was given in charity to Barirah: he said, "Bring it near, for it has reached its place." meaning it has reached the place of its good and lawfulness through the gift to us after it had been charity to Barirah. This is according to the view of those who made ihsar the restraint of an enemy. Evidence for it is the act of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions at al-Hudaybiyah, when they were prevented from the House and slaughtered their offerings there, and al-Hudaybiyah is not within the Sacred Precinct.

Al-Zuhri narrated from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, concerning the story of al-Hudaybiyah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote the treaty between himself and the polytheists of Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, he said to his companions: "Arise, slaughter, and shave." He said: By Allah, none of them stood up until he said that three times; when none of them stood up, he went in to Umm Salamah and mentioned that to her. Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, go out, then speak to none of them a word until you slaughter your camel and call your barber, and he shaves you." So he went out and did not speak until he had done that. When they saw that, they stood up and slaughtered, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly [killed] others out of grief. [86] [Nayl al-Awtar of al-Shawkani: 8/187; Musnad Ahmad: 4/331.]

Others said: the place of sacrifice for the offering of the one restrained is not lawful for him other than there; so if he is a pilgrim, its place is the Day of Sacrifice, and if he is a ʿumrah performer, its place is the day its offering reaches the Haram.

Ibrahim al-Ju'fi narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, who said: "We set out in ihram for ʿumrah, and among us was al-Aswad ibn Yazid, until we reached Dhat al-Suqauf. One of our companions was stung by a scorpion, which distressed him, and he did not know what to do. Some of us went out to the road looking, and there was a caravan in which was ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud. They asked him about it, and he said: 'Let him send an offering to Makkah, and make between you and it a sign; when the offering is slaughtered, let him exit ihram, and he owes the making-up of his ʿumrah.'"

﴿Whoever among you is ill﴾: the meaning of the verse "And do not shave your heads" applies to the state of ihram, except when a man is compelled to shave, either because of an illness that requires treatment, ﴿or has an affliction of the head﴾ such as lice or headache, so he shaves or pays a ransom: ﴿then a ransom of fasting﴾. This verse was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn Hujrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by me during the time of al-Hudaybiyah, and I had a thick head of hair in which were lice and nits, and they were scattering on my face (and I was ugly), so he turned to me. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do the lice of your head harm you?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Then shave your head." [87] [Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/208; Sahih Muslim: 4/21.] So Allah revealed: ﴿Whoever among you is ill or has an affliction of the head, then a ransom of fasting﴾, three days.

﴿Or charity﴾ to six needy persons, half a ṣāʿ for each needy person; ﴿or sacrifice (nusuk)﴾, or an animal for slaughter, its singular being nusukah.

Al-Hasan recited ﴿aw nusk﴾ with lightening, and it is the dialect of Tamim.

The scholars said: The highest of them is a camel, the middle is a cow, and the lowest is a sheep; and he has the choice among these three, doing whichever he wishes.

Anas and ʿIkrimah said: ﴿fa-fidyah min siyam﴾ is ten days, ﴿or charity to ten needy persons, for each needy person a mudd of wheat or a mudd of dates﴾, ﴿or sacrifice﴾ which is a sheep. The first view is the correct one and the well-known one. As for this [obligation], it is to be performed; they agreed that he fasts wherever in the lands he wishes.

As for the sacrifice and the food, some said: it must be in Makkah. Others said: wherever he wishes, and this is the correct view, because it is stated in general terms in the verse and does not specify one place over another.

﴿But when you are secure﴾: from your fear and when you are recovered from your illness.

﴿Then whoever enjoys the ʿumrah until Hajj﴾: they differed over this enjoyment (tamattu'). Some said: its meaning is: whoever is restrained until the year of Hajj, then comes to Makkah and exits ihram by performing an ʿumrah, and enjoys his exit from ihram thereby, so he completes the ʿumrah until the following year, then performs Hajj and offers an offering; so both the exit from ihram from which he exited and his second ihram from the following year together. This is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.

Others said: its meaning is ﴿when you are secure﴾, and you have exited from your ihram after the restraint, and they did not say "an ʿumrah by which you exit from your ihram for your Hajj." And if you exit when you are informed of the offering and postpone the ʿumrah until the following year, then perform ʿumrah in the months of Hajj, you have exited, and you enjoy your exit until your Hajj; then upon you is what is easy of the offering. This is the view of ʿAlqamah, Ibrahim and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Similarly, ʿAbd Allah ibn Salamah narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him.

﴿When you are secure, then whoever enjoys the ʿumrah...﴾, the verse: if he delays the ʿumrah until he combines it with Hajj, then upon him is an offering.

Al-Suddi said: its meaning is: whoever cancels a Hajj into an ʿumrah, making it an ʿumrah, and enjoys his ʿumrah until Hajj, then upon him is what is easy of the offering.

Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAta' and a group said: it is the man who arrives as a pilgrim (muʿtamir) from one of the horizons during the months of Hajj; when he has completed his ʿumrah, he remains in a state of non-ihram (ḥalāl) in Makkah until the time of Hajj arrives, and performs Hajj in that same year; so he is enjoying the non-ihram until his ihram for Hajj. The meaning of tamattu' is thus the non-ihram through ʿumrah: he remains lawful and does what the lawful person does, then performs Hajj after his exit from ʿumrah without returning to the miqat. The meaning of tamattu' is enjoyment (al-talaththudh), and its root is provision (al-tazawwud); al-matā' is provision, then every enjoyment was called tamattu'.

The jurists said: The tamattu' that makes an offering obligatory is that four conditions be gathered in it: that he enters ihram in the months of Hajj, that he exits from the ʿumrah in the months of Hajj, that he enters ihram for Hajj in that same year from Makkah and does not return to the miqat; and some of our companions added: that he be from outside the Haram. Whoever violates any of these conditions, the offering falls from him and he is not a mutamatti'.

﴿Then whoever does not find [an offering], then a fast of three days during Hajj and seven when you return to your families﴾.

The commentators said: he fasts one day before Tarwiyah, and the day of ʿArafah, and does not delay the last of them beyond the day of ʿArafah.

Tawus and Mujahid said: if he fasts them during the months of Hajj, they are sufficient.

﴿That is ten complete﴾: the mention of "complete" is for emphasis,

like the saying of al-A'sha:

Al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan), commentary on Surah 2, verses 194–197 (part 3 of 3)

Three at dawn, and that is enough for me,
and six when the evening overtakes me.
That makes nine in the day, my Lord,
and drinking beyond quenching is a disease. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/403.]]

Al-Farazdaq said:
Three and two, and they are five,
and a sixth that inclines toward my arrows. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/403; Fath al-Qadir: 1/197.]]

Some said: "complete" refers to the sacrificial offering (hady). It was also said: it refers to the reward. It was also said: it means complete in its conditions and limits. It was also said: the wording is a report but its judgment is a command, meaning: perform them and do not diminish them.

﴿That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque﴾, meaning, as one who is not from the people of the Haram (the sacred precinct).

Ikrimah said: this refers to the area beyond the mawaqit (the fixed places of entering the state of ihram) up to Mecca.

Ibn Juraij said: "those present at the Sacred Mosque" are the people of 'Arafat and al-Raji'; they sacrifice and offer hady.

﴿And fear God, and know that God is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿The Hajj is in known months﴾. Al-Farra' said:
Its meaning is: the time of the Hajj is in known months. This is like saying: "The cold is two months and the heat is two months," meaning in them [there are] two months. I heard al-Kisa'i say: "The hunting season is two months, and the cloak [...] two months: the time of hunting and a time when [...]."

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that the months of the Hajj are known months, and they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: God assigned these [months] to the Hajj, and the rest of the months to the 'umrah (minor pilgrimage). It is not permissible for anyone to enter ihram for the Hajj except in the months of the Hajj, whereas for the 'umrah one may enter ihram in any month. The last of these months is the day of 'Arafat. Some reports have come concerning the interpretation of "the months of the Hajj" as "ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah," and in others "nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah." Whoever says "nine" expresses it in terms of days, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "The Hajj is 'Arafat." [[Bada'i al-Sana'i: 2/176; Nasb al-Raya: 3/187.]] Whoever stands at 'Arafat on the day of 'Arafat, whether by night or by day, has completed his Hajj. Whoever says "ten" expresses it in terms of nights, so whoever does not reach it by the break of dawn on the day of sacrifice (yawm al-nahr) has missed the Hajj. The months are dated by nights.

Al-Farra' related: the Arabs say, "We fasted ten," intending nights, though fasting occurs only by day. There is therefore no contradiction in these reports. God said "months," though they are two months and part of a third, because it is a period of time, and the Arabs refer to a period by its few or many parts. They say, "I came to you on Thursday," though he came only at a particular hour of it. They say, "Today is two days since I have seen him," though it is one day and part of another. They say, "I visited you this year."

Some of our companions said: two or more is a plurality (jama'ah), because plurality means joining one thing to another. We say: it is permissible to call two, by themselves, a plurality; and it is permissible to call two and part of a third a plurality. God called two a plurality in His saying: ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾ (66:4), and He did not say "your heart."

'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others said: He meant by "the months" Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah [in full], because after 'Arafat there remain for the pilgrim matters he must perform, such as stoning (al-ramy), shaving (al-halq), sacrificing (al-nahr), and staying overnight at Mina; so they are in the ruling of the Hajj.

The ruling of the verse:
Whoever enters ihram for the Hajj before the months of the Hajj, that does not suffice as his Hajj, and it becomes an 'umrah, like one who enters prayer before its time, so it becomes a voluntary prayer. This is the view of 'Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, and the school of al-Awza'i and al-Shafi'i.

Malik, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, and Muhammad said: it is disliked for him to do so, and if he does, it is valid for him. The evidence of al-Shafi'i and his companions is the saying ﴿The Hajj is in known months﴾. It specified these months for the obligation of the Hajj within them. If entering ihram for the Hajj outside these months were valid and permitted, this specification would have no benefit, just as the prayers were tied to fixed times and it is not permitted to precede them.

﴿So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj in them﴾, meaning: whoever makes obligatory upon himself the Hajj, ihram, and talbiyah (the pilgrim's call) within them, ﴿there shall be no obscenity (rafath), no wickedness (fusuq), and no quarreling (jidal)﴾.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, and Ya'qub recited: al-rafath and al-fusuq with nominative and tanwin, and jidal in the accusative.

Like the saying of Umayyah:
So there is no idle talk nor sin in them,
and what they stood for, for them is a lasting [reward/affair].

Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi recited: ﴿la rafatha wa la fusuqa﴾ in the accusative, and ﴿wa la jidalun﴾ in the nominative with tanwin.

Like the saying of al-Akhfash:
This is your [young] grandfather exactly,
may I have no mother or father if that is so.

Abu Ja'far recited kulluha (all of it) in the nominative with tanwin. The rest recited kullaha in the accusative without tanwin.

The Arabs say both of these forms in speech. Whoever makes some nominative and some accusative combines both readings.

Al-A'mash recited: fala rafuth ('ala al-jami') (without the tanwin and a different vowel pattern, applied to all).

The commentators differed in interpreting "rafath."

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, al-Hasan, 'Amr ibn Dinar, Qatadah, Ibrahim, al-Rabi', al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak said: "rafath" is sexual intercourse.

Tawus and Abu al-'Aliyah said: "rafath" is allusion to women concerning intercourse, and mentioning it in front of [...] [an unreadable word in the manuscript].

'Ata' said: "rafath" is a man saying to a woman, while in the state of ihram, "If you become free, I will have you."

Abu Husayn ibn Qays said: I accompanied Ibn 'Abbas on the Hajj, and I was his close friend. When we had entered ihram, Ibn 'Abbas struck his camel's tail, so it turned, and he was chanting rajaz and saying:
"And they walk with us in a sway,
if the bird tells the truth, we shall have [her] in the evening."
[[al-Mabsut li-l-Sarakhsi: 4/6.]]

I said to him: "Do you engage in rafath while you are in ihram?"
He said: "Rafath is only what is said in the presence of women."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Rafath is sexual intercourse, kissing, touching, and speaking to her with obscene words; that is how it is."

Some said: "rafath" is obscenity and foul speech.

As for fusuq: Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Rabi', al-Zuhri, and al-Qurazi said: "fusuq" is all acts of disobedience to God.

Al-Dahhak said: it is mutual insulting by nicknames, as evidenced by the saying: ﴿And do not insult one another by nicknames; wretched is the name of wickedness after faith﴾ (49:11).

Ibn Zayd said: it is [...] [an unreadable word in the manuscript] by idols; the Prophet ﷺ forbade that when he performed Hajj, and taught his community the rites. Its evidence is the saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned, for it is indeed wickedness﴾ (6:121), and His saying: ﴿that which has been dedicated to other than God﴾ (5:3; 16:115).

Ibrahim, Mujahid, and 'Ata' said: it is reviling. Evidence for it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Reviling a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief." [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 1/223.]]

Ibn 'Umar said: it is what God forbade the one in ihram, such as hunting, trimming the nails, shaving the hair, and similar things.

As for jidal (quarreling): Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Amr ibn Muhammad, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, al-Zuhri, 'Ata' ibn Yasar, Mu'adh ibn Abi Rabah, and Qatadah said: jidal is that you dispute with your companion and contend with him until you overcome him.

Ibn 'Umar said: it is [mutual] cursing and contention.

Al-Qurazi said: when the Quraysh gathered at Mina, one group would say, "Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj," and the other would say, "Our Hajj is more complete than yours."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: it is that some of them say, "The Hajj is today," and others say, "The Hajj is tomorrow."

Ibn Zayd said: they used to stand at different places, disputing, each one claiming that his station was the station of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). God cut this off when He taught His Prophet ﷺ its rites.

Muqatil said: the Prophet ﷺ said in the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Whoever does not have an offering with him, let him leave ihram and make it an 'umrah." [[Sahih Muslim: 4/40; Musnad Abi al-Ja'd: 384.]]

They said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have declared ihram for the Hajj," and that was their dispute.

Mujahid said: its meaning is: "there is no doubt about the Hajj, that it is in Dhu al-Hijjah," so the intercalation (nasi') was abolished, and the Hajj became fixed as it is today.

The scholars of meanings [ahl al-ma'ani] said: the wording is a negation, but its meaning is a prohibition, meaning: do not engage in obscenity, do not commit wickedness, and do not quarrel. This is like His saying: ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾ (2:2), meaning: do not doubt it.

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever performs the Hajj to this House, and does not engage in obscenity nor in wickedness, will come out from his sins as on the day his mother bore him." [[al-Majmu' by Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi: 7/351-3; Kanz al-'Ummal: 5/7.]]

On the authority of Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, who said: I and Sufyan al-Thawri used to perform tawaf together, and Sufyan withdrew while I remained in the tawaf. I entered the Hijr and prayed near the water spout (al-mizab). While I was prostrating, I heard speech between the curtains of the House and the stones, and it was saying: "I complain to God and then to You of what [...] does, and the tawaf-performers around me, from their jesting in conversation [and their noise and their enthusiasm]." Wuhayb said: I interpreted it as the House complaining to Gabriel.

﴿And whatever good you do, God knows it﴾, meaning He will reward you for it.

﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety.﴾

The commentators said: some people from Yemen used to perform the Hajj without provisions, saying, "We rely upon God," and saying, "We are going to the House of God; will He not feed us?" [...] They began by wronging the people and seizing their property. So God commanded them to take provisions, and not to wrong people, and not to be a burden upon people. So He said: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾, and they would thereby keep their faces (from begging).

The commentators said: [provisions are] biscuit, oil, parched grain (sawiq), dates, and similar things.

Nafi' related from Ibn 'Umar, who said: when they entered ihram, they would have with them provisions, which they threw away, and they [competed] for the provision of the Hereafter. So God revealed: ﴿And take provision﴾; He forbade them from that and commanded them to safeguard provisions, and to take provisions for one who had none. So He commanded them to piety by restraining from wrongdoing. He said: ﴿for the best provision is piety.﴾

The people of allusion [ahl al-isharah] said: God reminded them of the journey of the Hereafter and urged them to take provision for both abodes, for piety is the provision of the Hereafter.

The poet said:
Death is a surging sea whose waves
in which the cunning of the swimmer vanishes.

Another said:
A person will not accompany him into his grave
except piety and righteous deeds.

Al-A'sha said:
If you do not depart with provision of piety,
and meet after death one who has provisioned himself,
you will regret not being like him,
and that you did not prepare as he prepared. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/412.]]

Malik ibn Dinar said: one of the reciters of Basra died, and we joked during the funeral and then departed. Then Sa'dun the Majnun climbed up, recited in the graveyard, and called out to the ascetics, and he began to recite:
"No, O army of the living, this is the army of the dead;
they answered the lesser call, and they await the greater.
They yearn over provision, and provision is nothing but hospitality;
they say to you: prepare, for this is the end of the world."

God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And fear Me, O people of understanding﴾, meaning those of intellects.

The Sacred Month for the sacred month. It was revealed concerning the 'umrah of the making-up (al-qada'), and that was because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made a treaty with the people of Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, that he would turn back that year and return the following year, on condition that they would vacate Makkah for him for three days, so that he and his companions could enter, perform 'umrah, circumambulate the House, and do whatever they wished, on condition that they would not enter except with the weapons of travelers, and would not leave with anyone of the people of Makkah accompanying them. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned back that year and returned the following year in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and they entered Makkah, performed 'umrah, circumambulated, sacrificed, and remained for three days. Then God revealed: "The sacred month" – Dhu al-Qa'dah, in which you entered Makkah, performed 'umrah, and completed your rites and circumambulation, in the year seven – "for the sacred month" – Dhu al-Qa'dah, in which you were prevented from the House and were hindered from your purpose, in the year six.

"The month" is in the nominative as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in His words "for the sacred month." "Al-hurumat" is the plural of hurmah, like "al-zulumat" is the plural of zulmah and "al-hujurat" is the plural of hujrah. Hurmah is that which must be preserved and whose violation must be avoided. The plural "hurumat" is used because He meant the sacred month, the sacred land, and the sanctity of the state of ihram. "Qisas" (retaliation) means equivalence and parity: it is that the doer be treated as he did. "Whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you" (fa-man i'tada 'alaykum fa-i'tadu 'alayhi, qatiluhu bi-mithli ma i'tada 'alaykum). Thus the recompense is named by the name of the initial act [[In the margin of the manuscript: al-i'tida'.]] in correspondence with the conditional clause. "And fear God, and know that God is with the God-fearing. And spend in the way of God, and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," the verse. Know that "al-tahlukah" is a verbal noun meaning destruction, and it is of the form tafʿilah from halak (perishing).

Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Hamid al-Khazarnaji say: I know of no verbal noun in the speech of the Arabs on the pattern tafʿulah with a damma on the ʿayn except this one.

Some said: al-tahlukah is everything whose outcome becomes destruction.

The meaning of His words "do not cast with your own hands" is: do not proceed in that. It is said of anyone who begins a deed: "he has cast his hands into it." Labid said, describing the sun:

"Until, when it cast a hand into the disbeliever / and concealed the flaws of the frontiers with its darkness" [[Majma' al-Bayan: 1/515; ajanna: concealed; ʿawarat al-thughur: its gaps.]]

That is, it began to set.

Al-Mubarrad said: "do not cast with your own hands" means yourselves; he expressed the whole by the part, as in His words, "That is for what your own hands have sent forward" and "for what your hands have earned." The "bi" in "bi-aydikum" is superfluous, as in "it grows with the oil." The poet said:

"And indeed I filled Nasib's [[Nasib: a man's name.]] skin with displeasure, / for a friend indeed blames."

He means: I filled his skin with displeasure.

They said: The Arabs say of a person "he cast his hand" only in evil.

The scholars differed concerning the interpretation of this verse.

Some said: This is about miserliness and withholding expenditure. He says: "And spend in the way of God," and do not withhold spending in the way of God, for withholding at the time of spending in the way of God is destruction. This is the view of Hudhayfah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Kaysan.

Ibn ʿAbbas said concerning this verse: Spend in the way of God even if you have only an arrow or a spearhead, and let none of you say, "I do not find anything."  [[Cf. Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/362.]]

al-Suddi said: "Then spend in the way of God even by a mithqal." "And do not cast with your own hands into destruction": do not say, "I have nothing."

Mujahid: "We do not forbid you expenditure in the right, out of fear of poverty."

al-Hasan: They used to travel and go on raids without spending from their wealth, so God revealed this verse.

al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded the people to prepare for the pilgrimage – it was said: for the 'umrah – in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and whenever he intended a journey his herald would proclaim it, informing them so that they might prepare the necessities of travel, when he commanded them to make ready, some men of the Bedouins present in Madinah stood before him and said: "O Messenger of God, with what shall we prepare? By God, we have neither provision nor wealth to prepare with, and no one will feed us." So God revealed this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When God commanded spending, some men said: "We have been commanded to spend in the way of God; if we spend our wealth, we will remain poor and destitute." So God said: "And do not cast with your own hands into destruction," meaning: spend, and do not fear poverty, for I am the Provider and will replace it for you.

al-Khalil ibn ʿAbd Allah, from ʿAli, Abu al-Darda', Abu Hurayrah, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, Jabir, and ʿImran ibn Husayn, all narrate from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sends an expenditure in the way of God while remaining in his house, for him is seven hundred dirhams for every dirham; and whoever fights himself in the way of God and spends in that cause, for him on the Day of Resurrection is seven hundred thousand dirhams for every dirham" [70] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/305; al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/236.]]. Then he recited this verse: "And God multiplies for whom He wills" [[Surah al-Baqarah: 261.]].

al-Nadr ibn ʿAziz narrated from ʿIkrimah concerning "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction": "Do not aim at the wicked part of it, of which you spend."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: Men used to go out in expeditions that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) dispatched without provision, so either they were cut off, or they were dependents; so God commanded them to spend on themselves in the way of God. And if you do not have what you can spend, do not go out yourself without provision or strength, and so cast yourself into destruction. And "destruction" is that one perish from hunger or thirst. Then he said to the one who withholds and is stingy: "And do good; indeed God loves the good-doers."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: The people used to be on the path of God, and a man would take provision, and his provision would be better than another's, so people would spend from his provision until nothing remained of it, and he wished to console his companion. So God revealed this verse.

Some said: This verse was revealed concerning abandoning jihad.

Zayd ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam ibn ʿImran, said: We raided Constantinople, and over the people of Egypt was ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir, a companion of the Messenger of God, and over the people of Syria was Fadalah ibn ʿUbayd, a companion of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and over the main body was ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid. He said: We stood in ranks, and I never saw ranks wider or longer than them, while the Romans had their backs pressed against the wall of the city. He said: A man from among us charged the Roman ranks until he broke through them, then came out toward us retreating, and the people cried out and said: "Glory be to God! He has cast himself with his own hands into destruction!"

Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said: You interpret this verse in this way – that a man charges fighting seeking martyrdom, or does something harmful to himself. We are more knowing of this verse; it was revealed concerning us, the group of the Ansar. When God had honored His religion and granted victory to His Messenger, we said among ourselves [O assembly of the Ansar] [[So in the original.]] secretly from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "We have left our families and our wealth until Islam spread and God granted victory to His Prophet. The war has laid down its burdens. If we return to our families and children and stay with them, we will repair what was lost of them." So God revealed concerning us: "And spend in the way of God, and do not cast with your own hands into destruction."

And "destruction" is staying with family and wealth and abandoning jihad.

Abu ʿImran said: Abu Ayyub continued to fight in the way of God until he was buried in Constantinople [[Cf. Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/279.]].

Abu al-Jawza narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Destruction" is the punishment of God, the Mighty and Majestic; meaning: do not abandon jihad, lest you be punished. Its evidence is His words, "If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment" [[Surah al-Tawbah: 39.]].

From [Yazid] ibn Abi Unaysah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three are from the essence of faith: refraining from one who says, 'There is no god but God' – do not declare him an unbeliever for a sin, nor expel him from Islam for a deed; jihad continues since God the Mighty and Majestic sent me until the last of my community fights the Dajjal, [which is not nullified by] tyranny or justice; and faith in predestination" [71] [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/569; Nasb al-Rayah: 4/221.]].

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without having fought and without having resolved in himself to fight, dies upon a branch of hypocrisy" [72] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/259; Sunan Abi Dawud: 1/562; al-Mustadrak: 2/79.]].

Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sufyan said: It is the man who advances between the two ranks and charges the people alone.

Muhammad ibn Sirin and ʿUbaydah al-Salmani said: Casting oneself into destruction is despair of the mercy of God.

Abu Qilabah said: It is the man who commits a sin and says, "I am ruined; there is no repentance," so he despairs of God's mercy and plunges into disobedience. So God forbade them from that.

Yaman ibn Ruʾab and al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah said: A man "casts his hands" when he submits to destruction and despairs of salvation.

From Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from [his father], concerning this verse, "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction," it was said to him: Is it the man who charges a battalion of a thousand with the sword? He said: No, rather it is the man who commits a sin, then casts his hands and says, "There is no repentance for me."

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿA'ishah, said: Habib ibn al-Harith came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man who has many sins." He said: "Repent to God, O Habib." He said: "O Messenger of God, I repent, then I return." He said: "Whenever you sin, repent." He said: "Then, O Messenger of God, my sins will multiply." He said: "The pardon of God is greater than your sins, O Habib ibn al-Harith" [73] [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/200; al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 5/123.]].

Fudayl ibn ʿIyad said concerning this verse, "and do not cast with your own hands into destruction": [it means] by evil opinion of God; "and think well of God; indeed God loves the good-doers" [means] think well of Him.

From Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib, who said: We entered upon Abu Nuwas al-Hasan ibn Hani to visit him in his illness in which he died, and with us was Salih ibn ʿAli al-Hashimi. Salih said to him: "Repent to God, O Abu ʿAli, for you are at the first day of the days of the Hereafter and the last day of the days of this world, and between you and God there are faults." He said: "Prop me up. You threaten me with God? Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to me from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'My intercession is only made for the people of major sins from my community. Do you think I would not be among them?'" [74] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/190, with variation.]]

And Hammad narrated to us from Thabit, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two men will come out of the Fire and be presented before God, the Mighty and Majestic. Then they will be commanded back to the Fire. One of them turns and says: 'My Lord, this was not my hope.' God says: 'And what was your hope?' He says: 'My hope was that when You bring me out of it, You would not return me to it.' So God, the Mighty and Majestic, has mercy on him and admits him to Paradise" [75] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/70, 285; Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/99.]].

"And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God."

Ibn Abi Ishaq read: (al-hijj) with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ throughout the Qur'an, and it is the dialect of Tamim and Qays Ghaylan.

It is mentioned from Talhah ibn Musarrif: with the kasrah here and in Surah Al ʿImran, and with the fathah in the rest of the Qur'an.

Abu Ja'far, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and ʿAsim, by the narration of Hafs, read it with the kasrah in Al ʿImran and with the fathah in the rest of the Qur'an.

The rest read it with the fathah throughout the Qur'an, and it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, with no difference between them in meaning, like "rattl" and "rattl" with a fathah and a kasrah [......] [[A blank in the manuscript, the meaning being complete.]].

Abu Mu'adh said: (al-hajj) with the fathah is a verbal noun, and al-hijj with the kasrah is a noun, like "qism" and "qism," "shurb" and "shurb," "suqy" and "suqy." And in the Codex of ʿAbd Allah: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God, at the House."

ʿAlqamah and Ibrahim read: "wa-atimmu al-hajja wal-ʿumrata."

The commentators differed concerning completing them.

Some said: The meaning is: complete the Hajj and 'Umrah with their rites, their limits, and their sunnah. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAlqamah, Ibrahim, and Mujahid.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning this verse: Whoever enters the state of ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah is not permitted to exit until he completes it. The completion of Hajj is the day of sacrifice, when he throws the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah and then circumambulates the House, and he has then exited from his ihram entirely. The completion of 'Umrah is when he circumambulates the House and goes between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and then he has exited. The obligatory elements of Hajj are four: the ihram, standing at ʿArafah, the circumambulation of ifadah, and the circumambulation and sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. The obligatory elements of 'Umrah are all four: the obligatory ihram, the circumambulation, the sa'y, and the shaving or shortening, and the minimum is three hairs.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Tawus narrated: The completion of Hajj and 'Umrah is that one enters ihram for both separately... [[An unreadable word.]] ...

Shu'bah narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salamah, who said: A man came to ʿAli and said: "Tell me about the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God.'" He said: "That you enter ihram from your household's dwelling."

Qatadah said: [Completing the 'umrah] is that one performs 'umrah outside the months of Hajj; and if one remains in the months of Hajj and then performs Hajj, it is tamattu', and upon him is a sacrifice if he finds one, or fasting. And completing Hajj is that one performs all its rites so that no penalty of qiran or tamattu' is incurred by him.

Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: The Messenger of God said: "An 'umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj" [76] [[Sunan al-Bayhaqi: 4/346; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 4/7.]].

al-Dahhak said: Its completion [is that] the expenditure be lawful, and one refrains from what God has forbidden.

Sufyan said: Its completion is that one sets out from his land for the two (Hajj and 'Umrah) alone, not intending anything else, and does not set out for trade or for some need; until, when you are near Makkah, you say: "If only I had performed Hajj or 'Umrah." That suffices, but the completion is that one sets out for them and does not set out for other than them.

Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Ba'li [as in the original] narrated from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God said: "A time will come upon the people when the wealthy among them will perform Hajj for recreation, their middle class for trade, their reciters for show and reputation, and their poor for begging" [77] [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 5/133, no. 12362; Tarikh Baghdad: 10/295.]].

In this sense ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: "The delegations are many and the pilgrims are few."

The ruling of the verse

The jurists differed concerning 'umrah. A group said: it is a good sunnah and not an obligatory duty; this is the view of Ahmad, Malik ibn Anas, Abu Thawr, and the old opinion of al-Shafi'i, and it is the choice of Jarir ibn Muhammad al-Tabari. They argued by the reading of al-Sha'bi, "wa-atimmu al-hajja wal-ʿumratu lillah," in the nominative.

And by what was narrated by Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he was asked about 'umrah: "Is it obligatory or not?" and [he said]: "That you perform 'umrah is better for you." And that the Hajj is an obligation for the emigrant, and 'umrah is voluntary. They also said: When God mentioned the obligation of Hajj, He did not mention 'umrah with it. And the Mighty One said: "And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House" [[Surah Al ʿImran: 97.]].

Others said: 'Umrah is obligatory, and it is the lesser Hajj. This is the view of ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, ʿAta', Qatadah, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah, and the new opinion and the more correct view of al-Shafi'i, and the choice of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. They argued with the reading of the majority, "wal-ʿumrata," in the accusative, meaning: complete the obligation of Hajj and 'umrah.

And by what was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection" [78] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 2/205, no. 926; Sunan al-Nasa'i: 5/181.]].

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "By God, 'umrah is indeed obligatory alongside Hajj in the Book of God: 'And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God.'" Ibn ʿUmar said: "There is no one of God's creation except that upon him is an obligatory Hajj and 'umrah, if he is able to a way to it, as God the Exalted said. Whoever adds beyond that, it is good and voluntary."

Masruq said: "We were commanded in the Book of God with four: establishing the prayer, giving the zakah, Hajj, and 'umrah. So 'umrah was placed in relation to Hajj as zakah is in relation to prayer." Then he recited this verse: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for God."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 194–197 (part 2 of 3):

Abd al-Malik ibn Sulayman said: A man asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the Prophet (ﷺ), whether ʿumrah is obligatory (fard) or voluntary (tatawwu'). He said: "It is obligatory." The man said: "But al-Sha'bi says it is voluntary." He said: "Al-Sha'bi has lied." Then he recited ﴿And complete the Hajj and the ʿUmrah for Allah﴾. Whoever says that ʿumrah is not obligatory interprets the verse to mean: complete them once you have entered upon them, and he did not intend that beginning the entry into them is obligatory for him. This is like one who volunteers for Hajj: there is no disagreement that once he has entered into ihram it is incumbent upon him to proceed with it and complete it, though it was not obligatory for him to begin entering it. Likewise ʿumrah. [See Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/286.]

Similarly, Ibn Wahb narrated from Zayd, who said: "ʿUmrah is not obligatory upon anyone among the people." I said to him: "[What about] the words of Allah, ﴿And complete the Hajj and the ʿUmrah for Allah﴾?" He said: "No one among creation should, once he has begun a matter, fail to complete it; and once he has set out upon it, it is not proper for him to exit it [i.e., cancel it] on a day and then return, just as if he fasts a day, it is not proper for him to break his fast at midday." The proof of this interpretation is His saying, ﴿Then fulfil to them their covenant until their term﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4]. He did not intend by it beginning, but rather completing what had passed of the covenant and agreement. Whoever makes ʿumrah obligatory interprets "completion" to mean beginning and obligating, i.e., establish them and perform them.
