ʿAsim al-Ahwal narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of Islam is like a tree that is firm: its root is faith in God, its trunk is the five prayers, its bark is the fasting of Ramadan, its fruit is hajj and ʿumrah, its drink is wudu' and ghusl from impurity, its branches are kindness to parents and maintaining ties of kinship, its leaves are abstaining from what God has forbidden, its fruit is good deeds, and its roots are the remembrance of God, exalted is He."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Just as a tree is neither beautiful nor sound except with green leaves, so Islam is not sound except with abstaining from what God has forbidden and with good deeds." [104]

*Kaffah* means "all together." It derives from *kafaftu al-shay'*, when I restrained it and gathered part of it to part of it. From this comes the word *kuffah* for the hem of a shirt, because it restrains it from spreading out. Every elongated object has its edge called *kuffah* with a damma, and every round object has its edge called *kiffah* with a kasra, like the pan of a scale. From this also comes the word *kaffah* for the palm together with the fingers, because one restrains with it from the rest of the body. A man who is *makfuf* is one whose sight has been restrained from looking. So the meaning of *al-kaffah* is that one reaches it and restrains it from going beyond it.

﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, meaning his incitements and urgings, in what has been made clear to you concerning the prohibition of the Sabbath, camel meat and other things. ﴿Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.﴾

Al-Shaʿbi narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: ʿUmar came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "We hear narrations from the Jews [which have taken hold of our hearts]. [The manuscript text is illegible, and the addition is from Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/148.] Should we write some of them down?" He said: "Are you bewildered, as the Jews and Christians were bewildered? I have brought it to you white and pure. Had Moses been alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me." [105] [[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/484.]]

﴿And if you slip﴾. Ibn Hayyan said: "You err." al-Suddi said: "You go astray." Yaman said: "You deviate."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "It means shirk."

Qatadah said: God revealed this verse while knowing that some would slip away from the people, so He announced it beforehand and warned about it, so that God would have proof against His creation.

Abu al-Sammak [al-ʿUdhri] [[As in the original.]] read *zalilتم* with a kasra on the lam, and both are dialectal forms. The root of the letter is from *zalaq* (slipping).

﴿After the clear proofs have come to you﴾, meaning faith, the Qur'an, the commands and the prohibitions. ﴿Then know that God is Mighty﴾ in His favour, ﴿Wise﴾ in His command. ﴿Do they await﴾, meaning, do those who abandon entering into peace completely and who follow the footsteps of Satan await anything? It is said *nazartuhu* and *intazartuhu* with the same meaning. A poet said:

"While we were awaiting him, he came to us,
hanging a waterskin and a shepherd's firestriker."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/370.]]

That is, we awaited him and expected him. But when *al-nazar* is accompanied by mention of the face, it can only mean seeing.

﴿Except that God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾. *Zulal* is the plural of *zullah*. Qatadah read *fi ẓilal*. It has two possibilities. The first: it is the plural of *zullah*, as *zullah* and *zulal* are like *jullah* and *jilal*, and *zill* with the plural *zilal* is like *hilah* and *hilal*. The second: it is the plural of *zill* from the clouds, which is the white thin cloud, named so because it covers (*yanʿam*), that is, it conceals.

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning God's words ﴿God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾: He said: "God comes in His canopies of clouds, which have been split into openings," and some of them raised it.

[[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/446.]]

Salamah ibn Wahram narrated that Ikrimah informed him that Ibn ʿAbbas informed him from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Among the clouds are openings through which God, mighty and majestic, comes, surrounded by angels." [106] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/446; and Tahdhib al-Kamal: 2/196.]] This is His words: ﴿Except that God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In a covering of clouds, so that the people of the earth do not look at them." Al-Dahhak said: "In [a side] [[As in the original.]] of the clouds."

Mujahid said: "It is a form other than clouds, and it was only for the Children of Israel in their wandering."

[[Ibid.: 2/447.]]

Muqatil said: "Like a shade, white. This is His words: ﴿And the day the sky will split apart with clouds﴾." [[Surah al-Furqan: 25.]]

﴿And the angels﴾.

Ibn Jaʿfar read it in the genitive, conjoined to *al-ghamam* (the clouds), with the meaning "with the angels." The Arabs say: "The commander came with the army," meaning with the army. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/25.]]

The rest read it in the nominative, with the meaning: "Except that God and the angels should come to them in canopies of clouds." What supports this is the reading of Abu Hatim and ʿAbdullah: ﴿Do they await except that God and the angels should come to them?﴾

﴿In canopies of clouds.﴾

Abu al-ʿAliyah and al-Rabi' said: "The angels will come to them in canopies of clouds, and God, exalted is He, will come as He wills."

Muʿadh read: *fi zulal maʿa al-ghamam wa qaḍaʾ al-amr* with *al-madd* (the lengthened form), intending the verbal noun, and mentioning clarification of the meaning of *al-ityan* (coming).

The people differed concerning this. Some said: *fi* here means *bi*, and interchange of prepositions is common and well known in Arabic speech. The meaning of the verse is: "Except that God should come to them with canopies of clouds and with the angels, or with the angels." With this interpretation the difficulty is removed and the matter is made easy. The rest left the verse as it is, since it is apparent.

Then they differed in its interpretation. A group explained it as the coming which is movement from one place to another, and they included in this, "without how," the apparent meaning of reports that had come down whose interpretation they did not know. This is not an acceptable view, because it ascribes a place to God, glorified is He. Whatever occupies a place must be bounded, finite and needy and poor, and God is exalted far above that.

One of the verifying and successful scholars, I think it is ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: "Whoever claims that God is from something, or in something, or upon something, has committed heresy, because if He were from something He would be created, if He were in something He would be enclosed, and if He were upon something He would be carried."

[[With variation, in al-Tawhid of al-Saduq: 178, no. 9.]]

Another group refrained from delving into the meaning of *al-ityan* and said: "We believe in its outward form and stop at its explanation, because we have been forbidden to say about the Book of God what we do not know, and neither God nor His Messenger has informed us of the reality of its meaning."

Yahya said: "This is among the hidden matters that are not to be explained." Malik, al-Awza'i, Muhammad and Ishaq and a group of the scholars used to say concerning this and similar matters: "Pass them on as they came, without how."

Some claimed that there is an implied or abbreviated element in the verse, and its meaning is: "Except that the command of God should come to them," which is the reckoning and the punishment. What supports this is His words: ﴿And the matter is decided﴾ (the verse), meaning: the punishment is due and the reckoning is finished. They said this is like His words: ﴿And ask the town﴾. [[Surah Yunus: 82.]] The Arabs say: "The governor cut the thief," meaning his hand, though he only did that by his command.

It is also said: "Two khutbahs came to us from Bani Umayyah," meaning their rule.

On this interpretation is His words: ﴿But God threw﴾. [[Surah al-Anfal: 17.]] Because God said that. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan al-Basri.

A group of the people of spiritual realities said: "God brings about an action which He calls *ityan*, as you have heard. Why not call it *nuzul* (descent)? His actions are without instrument or cause."

Al-Tha'labi said: "I say: it is possible that the meaning of *ityan* here refers to recompense, so recompense is called *ityan*, just as threat and punishment in the story of Nimrod are called *ityan*. The Mighty One said: ﴿So God came at them from the foundations, and the roof fell on them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾. [[Surah al-Nahl: 26.]]

He said in the story of the Banu al-Nadir: ﴿So God came at them from where they had not expected﴾. [[Surah al-Hashr: 2.]] ﴿And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, and sufficient are We as reckoners﴾. [[Surah al-Anbiya': 47.]] These meanings are admitted for *ityan* because the basic sense of *ityan*, according to the people of the language, is the intention to walk toward something. So the verse means: "Do they await anything except that God should manifest something contrary to His actions with a people among His creatures, so that He intends to requite them, decrees their destruction as He decrees, and carries out upon them what He wills?" This is supported by what Salih, the client of al-Tawamah, narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, mighty and majestic, will be in canopies of clouds with the angels, and He will speak with clear and eloquent speech, saying: 'Be silent. I have been silent for you since I created you. I see your deeds and I hear your words. It is only your own deeds that will return to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.'" [108] [[With variation, in al-Ahadith al-Tiwal: 98, no. 36; and he narrated it with its chain from Muhammad ibn Ka'b from Abu Hurayrah.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 204–210 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world pleases you...﴾ (the verse, etc.).

Al-Kalbi, al-Suddi, Muqatil and Ata said: this verse was revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/425.]] al-Thaqafi, an ally of the Banu Abi Zuhra, whose name was Ubayy. He was called al-Akhnas because on the Day of Badr he withdrew (akhnasa) with three hundred men of the Banu Zuhra from fighting the Prophet (ﷺ), and they turned back at al-Juhfa. He said to them: "O Banu Zuhra, Muhammad is the son of your sister. If he is truthful, you will not overcome him, and you are the most fortunate of people by his truthfulness. And if he is a liar, you are the most entitled to restrain from him because of your kinship, and the rabble of the Arabs have been sufficient for you against him."

They said: "The opinion you have expressed is excellent. Proceed as you wish and we will follow you." He said: "When the people are called to depart [I will then], I will withdraw with you, so follow me." He did so, they did so, and he was named al-Akhnas for that. He was a man sweet of speech and pleasant of appearance. He would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [professing loyalty and displaying] Islam, informing him that he loved him, and swearing by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to that. But he was a hypocrite. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would bring him close and turn to him, not knowing that he concealed the opposite of what he showed. Then there was enmity between him and the Thaqif, so he attacked them by night, destroyed their livestock and burned their crops. He had a fine outward appearance and an evil inner nature.

Al-Suddi said: He passed by a field of crops belonging to the Muslims and some donkeys, so he burned the crop and hamstrung the donkeys.

Muqatil said: He went out toward al-Ta'if to demand his due from a debtor, so he burned for him [a field] ... [[An illegible word.]] and hamstrung for him ... [[An illegible word.]] Allah revealed these verses concerning him.

Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: These verses, up to His saying ﴿And Allah is Compassionate toward the servants﴾, were revealed concerning the expedition of al-Raji'. That was because the Quraysh disbelievers sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in Medina, saying: "We have embraced Islam, so send to us some men of your companions' scholars who will teach us your religion." This was a deception on their part. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Habib ibn Adi al-Ansari, Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, Khalid ibn Bukayr, Abdullah ibn Tariq ibn Shihab al-Bali, and Zayd ibn al-Dathina, and he appointed over them Asim ibn Thabit ibn al-Aqlah al-Ansari. They set out intending Makkah, and they stopped at Batn al-Raji' between Makkah and Medina. They had with them dates of ajwa. They ate, and an old woman passed by and saw the date pits, so she returned to her people in Makkah and said: "The people of Yathrib, companions of Muhammad, have taken this road." Seventy men mounted with their spears and surrounded them and fought them. They killed Marthad, Khalid and Abdullah ibn Tariq. Asim ibn Thabit scattered his quiver, which had seven arrows in it, and with them he killed a man from the great leaders of the polytheists. Then he said: "O Allah, I have defended Your religion at the beginning of the day, so protect my flesh at the end of the night." Then the polytheists surrounded him and killed him.

When they had killed him, they wanted to cut off his head to sell it to Sulafa bint Sa'd ibn Uhayd, who had vowed when her son was struck at the Battle of Uhud: "If I am able to get the head of Asim, I will surely drink wine from his skull (qahf)." So Allah sent a swarm of hornets (dabr), which are wasps, and they shielded Asim, and they could not reach him. For this reason it was called "the protection of the hornets (hima al-dabr)." When they were prevented from reaching him, he (one of them) said: "Leave him until evening, when it passes away from him, and we will take him." But a black cloud came, and it rained a heavy rain [like water-skins], and Allah sent the torrent, which carried Asim away and took him off [......] [[An illegible word.]] and carried him ... fifty [[An illegible word.]] of the polytheists into the Fire. He said: Asim had made a vow to Allah that he would never touch a polytheist nor be touched by one, ever. [Tanajjusan] [[So in the original.]] from him. When the news reached Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "The hornets protected him! How wondrous is Allah's protection of the believing servant. Asim had vowed that no polytheist would touch him, nor would he touch a polytheist, ever, so Allah prevented them after his death just as He had prevented them during his life."

The polytheists captured Khubayb ibn Adi and Zayd ibn al-Dathina and took them to Makkah. As for Habib, the Banu al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought him in order to kill him with their own hands, and Habib was the one who had killed al-Harith ibn Amir at Uhud. While Khubayb was with the daughters of al-Harith, he borrowed a razor from one of them in order to shave for the killing. The woman was unaware, and she had a child who was crawling toward Habib. He had seated the child on his thigh with the razor in his hand, so the woman screamed. Habib said: "Do you fear that I will kill him? Treachery is not our way." The woman said: "I have never seen a prisoner better than Habib. I saw him when there was not a date in Makkah, and yet in his hand was a bunch of grapes which he was eating. It was only a provision that Allah had provided to Habib."

Then they took him out of the sacred precinct (haram) to kill him, and they wanted to crucify him. He said: "Leave me to pray two rak'ahs." So they left him, and he prayed two rak'ahs. Thus the custom became established that the one killed in cold blood (sabran) should pray two rak'ahs. Then he said: "Were it not that they would say Habib was fearful, I would have prolonged it." And he recited:

"I do not care, when I am killed as a Muslim,
On whichever side I fall for the sake of Allah, is my death,
And that is for the sake of the Deity, and if He wills,
He will bless the joints of a torn-apart body."

That is: a piece cut apart.

Then he said: "O Allah, count them, and destroy them, one by one." Then they crucified him alive. He said: "O Allah, You know that there is no one around me who can convey my greetings to Your Messenger, so convey them to him for me." Then a man from the polytheists, called Abu Sarwa'a, came to him carrying a spear, and placed it between Habib's breasts. Habib said to him: "Fear Allah." But that only increased him in arrogance, so he thrust it through him.

That is the meaning of His saying ﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," ...﴾ the verse. It refers to Salaman.

As for Zayd ibn al-Dathina, Safwan ibn Umayya bought him in order to kill him in revenge for his father, Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. Then he sent him with a freedman of his named Qastas to al-Tan'im to kill him. A group of the Quraysh gathered, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. When Zayd came forward to be killed, Abu Sufyan said to him: "I beseech you by Allah, O Zayd, would you love that Muhammad were now in your place, that we would strike off his neck, and that you were in your family?" He said: "By Allah, I would not love that Muhammad, at this moment, be in the place he is in, where a thorn might pierce him and harm him, while I sit among my family."

Abu Sufyan said: "I have never seen among people anyone who loves another as the companions of Muhammad love Muhammad." Then Qastas killed him.

When this news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), he said to his companions: "Which of you will take Khubayb down from his cross, and he will have Paradise?" Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: "I, O Messenger of Allah," and his companion al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. The two of them went out walking at night and hiding by day, until they reached al-Tan'im at night. Around the cross there were forty polytheists sleeping [drunken]. They took him down, and he was fresh and flexible, not a thing had changed in him after forty days, and his hand was over his wound dyed with blood. His color was the color of blood, and his scent was the scent of musk. Al-Zubayr carried him on his horse and set off. The disbelievers woke and found that Habib was missing, so they informed the Quraysh, and seventy of them mounted. When they caught up with the two, al-Zubayr threw Habib, and the earth swallowed him up. Thus he was named "the one swallowed by the earth (bali' al-ard)."

Al-Zubayr said: "What has emboldened you against us, O assembly of the Quraysh?" Then he lifted the turban from his head and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, and my mother is Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. We are two lions crouching, defending their cub. If you wish, we will shoot at you; if you wish, we will fight you hand to hand; and if you wish, you may depart." So they returned to Makkah.

Al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Jibril was with him. He said: "O Muhammad, the angels are indeed boasting of these two of your companions." Some hypocrites among the companions of Habib said: "Woe to these slain men who perished, because they sat in their houses, and did not carry out the message of their master." So Allah revealed concerning al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, Habib and his believing companions, and concerning those among the hypocrites who reviled them [[In full in Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 1/199–201.]] ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the life of this world pleases you, O Muhammad,﴾ i.e., you find it good, and it becomes great in your heart. From this comes "ujb" (wonder/admiration), because it is greatness in the self.

In reports, "a'jabani kadha" (this pleased me) denotes approval and love, and "ajibtu min kadha" (I was amazed at this) denotes disapproval and aversion. The root meaning of ujb is that which has never been the like of its kind; this was stated by al-Mufaddal.

﴿And he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart﴾ means: the hypocrite's saying, "By Allah, I truly believe in you and love you."

Ibn Muhaysin recited: ﴿wa-yashhadu Allahu﴾ with a fatha on the ya' and the ha', and a raf' on the ha' [i.e., "and Allah bears witness"]. The meaning is: he shows a matter and speaks a statement, while Allah knows the contrary of it from him. In the codex (mushaf) of Ubayy it reads ﴿wa-yastashhidu Allaha﴾ (and he calls Allah to witness), which is an argument for the qira'a (recitation variant) of the general reciters.

﴿And he is the most contentious of adversaries﴾ means: the most intense in hostility.

It is said of this: "lamadta, ya hadha, wa-anta talidu laddan wa-ladadan" (you were contentious, O you, and you contend with great contentiousness). And when you want to say that he overcame his opponent, you say: "laddahu yaludduhu laddan" (he overcame him in contention).

It is said: "rajulun alladd" (a man who is contentious), and "imra'atun laddа'" (a woman who is contentious), and "rijalun wa-nisa'un lud" (men and women who are contentious).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that you may warn with it a contentious people﴾ [[Surah Maryam: 97.]]

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most hateful of men to Allah is the most contentious adversary." [101] [[Mawahib al-Jalil: 7/167; and Musnad Ahmad: 6/55.]]

A poet said:

"Indeed, beneath the rocks are resolve and generosity,
And an adversary most contentious, one who locks up arguments."

And a rajaz poet said:

"He contends against the contentious champions of men."

Al-Zajjaj said: its derivation is from "ludayday al-'unuq," which are the two sides of the neck. Its interpretation is that whichever way he takes, from the right or from the left, in the arenas of dispute, he overcomes in that.

Al-Khisam is the verbal noun of "khasamtuhu khisaman wa-mukhasamatan" (I disputed with him), as Abu Ubayda stated. Al-Zajjaj said: it is the plural of khasm, as one says khasm, khisam, khusum, like bahr, bihar, buhur. The reality of "khusuma" is probing deeply into the investigation of a thing and pressing upon it, and for this reason the corners of containers are called khusum.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿alladd al-khisam﴾ means "the most crooked of disputants."

Mujahid said: "The most upright in his persistence in dispute."

Al-Hasan said: "He is one who speaks falsely."

Qatada said: "He is one severe in disobedience to Allah, who argues with falsehood, knowledgeable in speech, ignorant in action, speaking with wisdom yet committing sin."

﴿And when he turns away﴾ means: he turns his back and turns away from you.

Al-Hasan said: "He turns away from his statement which he had given."

Ibn Juraij said: "He becomes angry." Al-Dahhak said: "He gains authority and becomes a governor."

﴿He strives in the land﴾ means: he works in it. It is said: "So-and-so yas'a li-'iyalihi" (strives for his dependents), i.e., he works in a way that benefits them through spending.

From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"And he strove for Kinda with striving that is not idle,
Qays, so he harmed its enemy and built for it."

It is also said: he traveled and walked.

﴿To cause corruption therein﴾.

Ibn Juraij said: "Severing kinship ties and shedding the blood of Muslims." And the women [...] "al-fasad" (corruption) is the name for all acts of disobedience.

﴿And to destroy the crops and the offspring﴾.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Abi Ishaq recited ﴿wa-yuhlika﴾ with a raf' on the kaf as a beginning (mubtada'). But the general reciters read it with a nasb (accusative), and the recitation of Ubayy supports it: "wa-li-yuhlika" (so that he may destroy).

The exegetes said: "al-harth" is what you cultivate of plants, and "al-nasl" is the offspring of every animal, and of people among them.

Al-Nadr ibn Adi related from Mujahid concerning His saying ﴿And when he turns away, he strives...﴾ the verse, that he said: "When he turns away, he fears, so he acts with aggression. And when he is a scholar, Allah withholds the rain and destroys the crops and the offspring."

﴿And Allah does not love corruption﴾.

From Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Cutting a dirham is from corruption in the land."

Qatada, from Ata: a man called al-Ala' ibn Munabbih entered the state of ihram in a robe, and the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded him to remove it.

Qatada said: "I said to Ata: 'We used to hear that he tore it.'" Ata said: "Indeed Allah does not love corruption."

﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," he is seized by pride...﴾ means: he is afraid of Allah, [but] pride takes him. ﴿He is seized by pride to sin﴾ means: the pride and partisanship of the Jahiliyya carry him to act with sin, and pride, strength and protection. It is also said: its meaning is ﴿he is seized by pride to the sin that is in his heart﴾, just as the letter ha' takes the place of the lam, as in the verse of Antara, who likens it to the Lord:

"As if a lord or a bound, pent-up thing,
Whose sides are scorched by the fire of a copper pot."

That is, He created the inclination out of fear of Hell, meaning: its torment of Hell suffices him.

﴿And evil is the resting place﴾: al-mihad is the bed.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "Among the greatest of sins with Allah is that it is said to a servant, 'Fear Allah,' and he replies, 'Attend to yourself.'"

﴿And among the people is one who sells﴾ (yashri), i.e., sells, ﴿his soul, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, i.e., seeking the good pleasure of Allah.

Al-Kisa'i read ﴿mardat Allah﴾ with imala (inclination) throughout the entire Qur'an.

﴿And Allah is Compassionate toward the servants﴾.

Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: this verse was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad when they sold themselves to bring down Habib from the cross upon which he was crucified, and the story has already passed.

Most of the exegetes said: it was revealed concerning Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Makhzumi, a client of Abdullah [ibn Jud'an] al-Taymi. The polytheists seized him along with a group of believers and beat them. Suhayb said to them: "I am an old man. It will not harm you whether you are from your own people or from others. Will you take my wealth and leave me and my religion?" They agreed to that. He had stipulated for them a riding camel and provisions. He remained in Makkah for as long as Allah willed, then he set out for Medina, and Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) met him with some men.

Abu Bakr said to him: "Your transaction has profited, Abu Yahya." Suhayb said: "And yours, so do not lose by your harm." [[Some of the Arabic here is as in the original.]] Abu Bakr said: "Allah the Exalted revealed such-and-such concerning you," and he recited to him this verse.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Ata said: Suhayb came migrating toward the Prophet (ﷺ), and a group of the polytheists of Quraysh followed him. He dismounted from his riding camel, and [took out] what was in his quiver, then said: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know that I am among the best of you in archery. By Allah, I will not make an arrow from what is in my quiver except that it will be in the heart of a man. And by Allah, they will not reach me until I have shot every arrow in my quiver. Then I will strike with my sword what remains in my hand. Then do as you wish. And if you wish, I will show you my wealth [and my property] in Makkah, and you will let my path go free."

They said: "Yes." He did that, and Allah revealed this verse.

Qatada said: "They are not the people of Harura, the ones who exited from the religion of Allah the Exalted, but they are the Muhajirun and the Ansar."

Al-Hasan said: "Do you know concerning whom this verse was revealed? [It was revealed] concerning a Muslim who met a disbeliever, and said to him: 'Say, there is no god but Allah. If you say it, your property and your blood will be protected, except by its right.' He refused to say it. The Muslim said: 'By Allah, I will surely sell myself to Allah.' So he advanced and fought until he was killed."

Al-Mughira said: "Umar sent an army, and they besieged a fortress. A man from Bajila advanced and fought alone until he was killed. The people said: 'He cast himself into destruction with his own hand.' This reached Umar, and he said: 'They have lied. Does not Allah say, ﴿And among the people is one who sells his soul...﴾' the verse?"

Some of them said: this verse was revealed concerning the enjoining of good and the forbidding of evil.

Ibn Abbas said: "I see here one who, when he is commanded to fear Allah, is seized by pride to sin." He said: "[This is so], and I sell my soul, and I see one who sells his soul seeking the pleasure of Allah, who stands up and commands this one to fear Allah. When he does not accept, he is seized by pride to sin. Then he says: 'Here I am, selling my soul to fight him,' so the two men are killed for that."

When Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) recited this verse, he would say: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, the two have fought!"

Al-Khalil said: Umar ibn al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, ﴿And among the people is one who sells his soul...﴾ the verse. Umar said: ﴿Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return﴾. A man stood up enjoining good and forbidding evil, and he was killed.

Hammad ibn Salama, from Abu Ghalib, from Abu Umama, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the best jihad is a word of truth before an oppressive ruler."

Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The master of the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection is Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and a man who stood up before an oppressive ruler, commanded him and forbade him, and was killed for it." [102]

Al-Tha'labi said: "I saw in the books that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to migrate, he left Ali ibn Abi Talib in Makkah to settle his debts and return the deposits that were with him. On the night he went out toward the cave, while the polytheists had surrounded the house, he commanded him to sleep on his bed (ﷺ), and said to him: 'Wrap yourself in my green Hadrami cloak and sleep on my bed, for no harm will reach you from them, if Allah wills.' Ali did so. Then Allah revealed to Jibril and Mika'il: 'Indeed I have made you brothers, and I have made the life of one of you longer than the life of the other. Which of you will prefer his companion with life?' Both of them chose life. Allah the Exalted revealed to them: 'Would that you had been like Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)! I made him a brother to Muhammad (ﷺ), and he slept on his bed, giving himself up for him and preferring him with life. Descend to the earth and protect him from his enemy.' They descended: Jibril was at the head of Ali, and Mika'il at his feet, and Jibril was calling: 'Bakh bakh! Who is like you, O son of Abi Talib!' Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic called out to the angels, and revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ), while he was heading toward Medina, concerning Ali (peace be upon him): ﴿And among the people is one who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾." [103] [[See Usd al-Ghaba: 4/25; al-Mustadrak ala al-Sahihayn: 3/132; Musnad Ahmad: 1/331; and Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/140.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, when the Prophet (ﷺ) fled from the polytheists to the cave with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and ʿAli slept in the Prophet's (ﷺ) bed.

﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace completely﴾. It was revealed concerning the believers among the People of the Book, ʿAbdullah ibn Salam al-Nadri and his companions. They had held the Sabbath in esteem and disliked camel meat and camel milk after they had embraced Islam, and they said: "O Messenger of God, the Torah is the Book of God, so let us observe it in our night prayers." Then God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace completely﴾, meaning, into Islam. This was said by Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. What supports this is the verse of al-Kindi: "I called my tribe to peace when I saw them turning their backs on us," meaning, I called them to Islam when they had apostatised. He said this when Kindah apostatised with al-Ash'ath ibn Qays after the death of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Tawus said: "It means into the religion."

Mujahid said: "It means in the rulings of the people of Islam and their deeds, all of them." Rabi' said: "It means in obedience." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "It means in all kinds of righteousness." All of these are close in meaning. Its origin is from submission and yielding, and that is why reconciliation is called *silm*. Zuhayr said:

"You have both been asked, if we attain peace widely,
with wealth and kindness, we shall submit in the matter."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/440.]]

Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: "In this verse, Islam has eight shares: prayer is a share, zakat is a share, fasting is a share, hajj is a share, ʿumrah is a share, jihad is a share, enjoining good is a share, and forbidding evil is a share. Whoever has no share has failed."

The readers differed concerning *al-silm*. Al-Aʿmash and Ibn ʿAbbas read it with a kasra on the sin here, and in al-Anfal and Surah Muhammad (ﷺ). The people of the Hijaz and al-Kisa'i read all of them with a fatha, and this is the choice of Abu ʿUbayd, because ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn [Abza] narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite all of them with a fatha. Hamzah and Khalaf read it with a fatha in al-Anfal and with a kasra elsewhere. The rest read it with a kasra here and with a fatha elsewhere, and this is the choice of Abu Hatim. Both are dialectal forms.

ʿAsim al-Ahwal narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of Islam is like a tree that is firm: its root is faith in God, its trunk is the five prayers, its bark is the fasting of Ramadan, its fruit is hajj and ʿumrah, its drink is wudu' and ghusl from impurity, its branches are kindness to parents and maintaining ties of kinship, its leaves are abstaining from what God has forbidden, its fruit is good deeds, and its roots are the remembrance of God, exalted is He."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Just as a tree is neither beautiful nor sound except with green leaves, so Islam is not sound except with abstaining from what God has forbidden and with good deeds." [104]

*Kaffah* means "all together." It derives from *kafaftu al-shay'*, when I restrained it and gathered part of it to part of it. From this comes the word *kuffah* for the hem of a shirt, because it restrains it from spreading out. Every elongated object has its edge called *kuffah* with a damma, and every round object has its edge called *kiffah* with a kasra, like the pan of a scale. From this also comes the word *kaffah* for the palm together with the fingers, because one restrains with it from the rest of the body. A man who is *makfuf* is one whose sight has been restrained from looking. So the meaning of *al-kaffah* is that one reaches it and restrains it from going beyond it.

﴿And do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾, meaning his incitements and urgings, in what has been made clear to you concerning the prohibition of the Sabbath, camel meat and other things. ﴿Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you.﴾

Al-Shaʿbi narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah: ʿUmar came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "We hear narrations from the Jews [which have taken hold of our hearts]. [The manuscript text is illegible, and the addition is from Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/148.] Should we write some of them down?" He said: "Are you bewildered, as the Jews and Christians were bewildered? I have brought it to you white and pure. Had Moses been alive, he would have had no choice but to follow me." [105] [[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/484.]]

﴿And if you slip﴾. Ibn Hayyan said: "You err." al-Suddi said: "You go astray." Yaman said: "You deviate."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "It means shirk."

Qatadah said: God revealed this verse while knowing that some would slip away from the people, so He announced it beforehand and warned about it, so that God would have proof against His creation.

Abu al-Sammak [al-ʿUdhri] [[As in the original.]] read *zalilتم* with a kasra on the lam, and both are dialectal forms. The root of the letter is from *zalaq* (slipping).

﴿After the clear proofs have come to you﴾, meaning faith, the Qur'an, the commands and the prohibitions. ﴿Then know that God is Mighty﴾ in His favour, ﴿Wise﴾ in His command. ﴿Do they await﴾, meaning, do those who abandon entering into peace completely and who follow the footsteps of Satan await anything? It is said *nazartuhu* and *intazartuhu* with the same meaning. A poet said:

"While we were awaiting him, he came to us,
hanging a waterskin and a shepherd's firestriker."

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/370.]]

That is, we awaited him and expected him. But when *al-nazar* is accompanied by mention of the face, it can only mean seeing.

﴿Except that God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾. *Zulal* is the plural of *zullah*. Qatadah read *fi ẓilal*. It has two possibilities. The first: it is the plural of *zullah*, as *zullah* and *zulal* are like *jullah* and *jilal*, and *zill* with the plural *zilal* is like *hilah* and *hilal*. The second: it is the plural of *zill* from the clouds, which is the white thin cloud, named so because it covers (*yanʿam*), that is, it conceals.

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning God's words ﴿God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾: He said: "God comes in His canopies of clouds, which have been split into openings," and some of them raised it.

[[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/446.]]

Salamah ibn Wahram narrated that Ikrimah informed him that Ibn ʿAbbas informed him from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Among the clouds are openings through which God, mighty and majestic, comes, surrounded by angels." [106] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/446; and Tahdhib al-Kamal: 2/196.]] This is His words: ﴿Except that God should come to them in canopies of clouds﴾.

Al-Hasan said: "In a covering of clouds, so that the people of the earth do not look at them." Al-Dahhak said: "In [a side] [[As in the original.]] of the clouds."

Mujahid said: "It is a form other than clouds, and it was only for the Children of Israel in their wandering."

[[Ibid.: 2/447.]]

Muqatil said: "Like a shade, white. This is His words: ﴿And the day the sky will split apart with clouds﴾." [[Surah al-Furqan: 25.]]

﴿And the angels﴾.

Ibn Jaʿfar read it in the genitive, conjoined to *al-ghamam* (the clouds), with the meaning "with the angels." The Arabs say: "The commander came with the army," meaning with the army. [[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/25.]]

The rest read it in the nominative, with the meaning: "Except that God and the angels should come to them in canopies of clouds." What supports this is the reading of Abu Hatim and ʿAbdullah: ﴿Do they await except that God and the angels should come to them?﴾

﴿In canopies of clouds.﴾

Abu al-ʿAliyah and al-Rabi' said: "The angels will come to them in canopies of clouds, and God, exalted is He, will come as He wills."

Muʿadh read: *fi zulal maʿa al-ghamam wa qaḍaʾ al-amr* with *al-madd* (the lengthened form), intending the verbal noun, and mentioning clarification of the meaning of *al-ityan* (coming).

The people differed concerning this. Some said: *fi* here means *bi*, and interchange of prepositions is common and well known in Arabic speech. The meaning of the verse is: "Except that God should come to them with canopies of clouds and with the angels, or with the angels." With this interpretation the difficulty is removed and the matter is made easy. The rest left the verse as it is, since it is apparent.

Then they differed in its interpretation. A group explained it as the coming which is movement from one place to another, and they included in this, "without how," the apparent meaning of reports that had come down whose interpretation they did not know. This is not an acceptable view, because it ascribes a place to God, glorified is He. Whatever occupies a place must be bounded, finite and needy and poor, and God is exalted far above that.

One of the verifying and successful scholars, I think it is ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), said: "Whoever claims that God is from something, or in something, or upon something, has committed heresy, because if He were from something He would be created, if He were in something He would be enclosed, and if He were upon something He would be carried."

[[With variation, in al-Tawhid of al-Saduq: 178, no. 9.]]

Another group refrained from delving into the meaning of *al-ityan* and said: "We believe in its outward form and stop at its explanation, because we have been forbidden to say about the Book of God what we do not know, and neither God nor His Messenger has informed us of the reality of its meaning."

Yahya said: "This is among the hidden matters that are not to be explained." Malik, al-Awza'i, Muhammad and Ishaq and a group of the scholars used to say concerning this and similar matters: "Pass them on as they came, without how."

Some claimed that there is an implied or abbreviated element in the verse, and its meaning is: "Except that the command of God should come to them," which is the reckoning and the punishment. What supports this is His words: ﴿And the matter is decided﴾ (the verse), meaning: the punishment is due and the reckoning is finished. They said this is like His words: ﴿And ask the town﴾. [[Surah Yunus: 82.]] The Arabs say: "The governor cut the thief," meaning his hand, though he only did that by his command.

It is also said: "Two khutbahs came to us from Bani Umayyah," meaning their rule.

On this interpretation is His words: ﴿But God threw﴾. [[Surah al-Anfal: 17.]] Because God said that. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Hasan al-Basri.

A group of the people of spiritual realities said: "God brings about an action which He calls *ityan*, as you have heard. Why not call it *nuzul* (descent)? His actions are without instrument or cause."

Al-Tha'labi said: "I say: it is possible that the meaning of *ityan* here refers to recompense, so recompense is called *ityan*, just as threat and punishment in the story of Nimrod are called *ityan*. The Mighty One said: ﴿So God came at them from the foundations, and the roof fell on them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive﴾. [[Surah al-Nahl: 26.]]

He said in the story of the Banu al-Nadir: ﴿So God came at them from where they had not expected﴾. [[Surah al-Hashr: 2.]] ﴿And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it, and sufficient are We as reckoners﴾. [[Surah al-Anbiya': 47.]] These meanings are admitted for *ityan* because the basic sense of *ityan*, according to the people of the language, is the intention to walk toward something. So the verse means: "Do they await anything except that God should manifest something contrary to His actions with a people among His creatures, so that He intends to requite them, decrees their destruction as He decrees, and carries out upon them what He wills?" This is supported by what Salih, the client of al-Tawamah, narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, mighty and majestic, will be in canopies of clouds with the angels, and He will speak with clear and eloquent speech, saying: 'Be silent. I have been silent for you since I created you. I see your deeds and I hear your words. It is only your own deeds that will return to you. Whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.'" [108] [[With variation, in al-Ahadith al-Tiwal: 98, no. 36; and he narrated it with its chain from Muhammad ibn Ka'b from Abu Hurayrah.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 211–215:

Ask the Children of Israel (*Sal Bani Isra'il*), meaning: ask, O Muhammad, the Jews of Madinah, how many clear signs (*ayah bayyinah*), that is, manifest proofs, such as the staff in the hand, the white hand, the splitting of the sea and others, We gave to their fathers and forebears.

﴿And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah﴾, meaning changes the Book of Allah, ﴿after it has come to him, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment. The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve﴾, the verse. Some said: this verse was revealed concerning the polytheists of the Arabs, Abu Jahl and his companions, who enjoyed the comforts that were brought to them in this world of wealth and forgot the Day of Return, ﴿and they mock﴾ the believers who turn away from the world and devote themselves to obedience and worship, saying: "If Muhammad were a prophet, our nobles would have followed him, but only the poor followed him, such as Abu 'Ammarah, Suhayb, 'Ammar, Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Bilal, Khabbab and their like." This is the meaning of the narration of al-Kalbi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who enjoyed comfort in this world and mocked the weak believers and the poor emigrants, saying: "Look at these people whom Muhammad claims he will prevail through."

'Ata' said: it was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews and their delegations from the Banu Qurayzah, al-Nadir and al-Qaynuqa', who mocked the poor emigrants, so Allah promised them that He would give them the wealth of the Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir without fighting, the easiest and most facile thing. [Allah] said: ﴿Where are those who disbelieve in the life of this world?﴾ This is according to the view of Mujahid.

(Zayyana) is read with a fatha on the zay and the ya', on the meaning that Allah made it attractive. The verb was made masculine for two reasons. The first is that the feminine marking of "al-hayah" (life) is not real, since the meaning of life, enduring, and living is one. The second is that it separated the feminine noun from the verb, so the masculine was applied, as in the saying of the poet:

"Indeed, a man whom one of you (women) deceives,
after me and after you, in this world, is deluded."

[Zad al-Masir: 1/305; Lisan al-Arab: 5/11.]

﴿And they mock those who believe﴾ because of their poverty.

It is narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever humiliates a believing man or woman, or belittles him for his poverty and lack of means, Allah will expose him on the Day of Resurrection and then disgrace him. And whoever slanders a believing man or woman, or says about him what is not in him, Allah will station him on a hill of fire until he comes out of what he said about him. Indeed the believer is greater in the sight of Allah and more honoured by Him than a near angel. There is nothing more beloved to Allah than a believing man or woman who repents. Indeed the believer [man] is recognised in the heaven just as a man recognises his family and children." [109] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/29.]]

And from Ibrahim ibn Adham, who said: 'Abbad ibn Kathir ibn Qays narrated to us, who said: A man wearing a fine garment came and sat with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then a man wearing [lamar] [[as in the manuscript.]] came and sat with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He (the first man) gathered his garments around himself. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Is it all this disgust at your Muslim brother? Were you afraid that something of his poverty would befall you, or of your wealth, something would befall him?" He said to the Prophet: "I apologise to Allah and to His Messenger. Indeed the soul commands evil, and Satan plots against me. I bear witness, O Messenger of Allah, that half of my wealth is his." The man said: "I do not want that." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "And why?" He said: "Lest my heart be corrupted as his heart was corrupted." [110]

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Do not belittle anyone among the Muslims, for the least of the Muslims is great in the sight of Allah." Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "Evil is the people among whom, if a believer becomes wealthy, they envy him, and if he becomes poor among them, they humiliate him."

﴿And those who are mindful of Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

It is narrated from Abu Dhar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Abu Dhar, raise your eyes to the most exalted man you see in the mosque." I looked and saw a man sitting, wearing a fine garment, so I said: "This one." He said: "O Abu Dhar, raise your eyes to the lowliest man you see in the mosque." I looked and saw a weak man wearing worn-out clothes, so I said: "This one." The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, this one, in the sight of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, is better than the filling of the earth with the likes of that one." [111] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/170.]]

﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means abundantly, without loss and without [hindaz] [[as in the manuscript.]], because whatever is subject to reckoning is little.

Al-Dahhak said: it means without consequence. He provides for him in this world and does not call him to account or punish him in the Hereafter.

It has been said that this refers back to Allah, and on this view it allows two meanings. The first is that He is not obligated, and He is not held to account regarding what He provides, and it is not said to Him: "Why did You give this and withhold that? Why did You give this more than that?" because He has no partner in what He possesses, and no equal disputing with Him.

The other meaning is that He does not fear the exhaustion of His treasuries, so as to need to account for what goes out of them, when accounting is done by the giver in order to reach the appropriate measure of giving, so as not to exceed in giving to the point of harming Himself. He has no need of reckoning, because He is the Knowing, the Rich, who does not fear the exhaustion of His treasuries, for they are between the "kaf" and the "nun" (i.e., His command "Be" and it is).

﴿Mankind was one community﴾, the verse. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: mankind, from the time of the death of Adam until the sending of Nuh (peace be upon him), was one community upon one religion, which was disbelief. They were all disbelievers, like the beasts. ﴿So Allah sent Nuh and Ibrahim and others of the prophets﴾.

Qatadah and 'Ikrimah said: mankind, from the time of Adam until the sending of Nuh, was one community, and there were ten centuries between Adam and Nuh, all upon one law of truth and guidance. Then they differed in the time of Nuh, ﴿so Allah sent to them Nuh﴾, who was the first prophet sent, ﴿then He sent after him the prophets﴾.

Al-Kalbi and al-Waqidi said: the people of Nuh's ark were all believers, then they differed after the death of Nuh.

﴿So Allah sent the prophets﴾. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: mankind in the time of Ibrahim was one community, all disbelievers, and Ibrahim's offspring were in jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). ﴿So Allah sent to them Ibrahim and other prophets﴾.

Al-Rabi' narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy, who said: mankind, when they were presented to Adam and were brought out from his loins and acknowledged servitude, were one community, all Muslims, and they had never been one community other than on that day. Then they differed after Adam, so Allah sent the messengers and revealed the books. Likewise, in the recitation of Ubayy and 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq: ﴿So they differed, and Allah sent the prophets﴾.

Muhammad ibn Yasar and Mujahid said: ﴿Mankind was one community﴾ means Adam alone, who was named "the one" because he bears the offspring and is the father of mankind. Then Allah created Hawwa' (Eve) and spread from the two of them mankind, who spread and multiplied. They were all Muslims until Qabil killed Habil. Then they differed at that time, so Allah sent [prophets] at that time.

Al-Tha'labi said: I saw in some tafsirs: mankind was one community in [Paradise], with no commander over them and no prohibition, ﴿so Allah sent the prophets﴾. Their total was one hundred and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers among them were three hundred and thirteen, and those mentioned by name in the Qur'an are twenty-eight prophets.

﴿Bearers of good tidings﴾ of reward to those who believe and obey, ﴿and warners﴾ who warn of punishment to those who disbelieve and disobey.

Musa ibn 'Ubayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Thabit, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon the prophets and messengers of Allah, for Allah sent them just as He sent me." [112] [[Fadl al-Salat 'ala al-Nabi by al-Jahdhami: 48; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/523.]]

﴿And He sent down with them the Book﴾, that is, the books; He sent down with them the Book ﴿with truth﴾, with justice and truthfulness, ﴿to judge between the people﴾. The common reading is with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the kaf (*liyahkuma*, "that it may judge"), and it occurs in the Qur'an in four places: here, in Al 'Imran, and two places in al-Nur.

Abu Ja'far al-Qari' and 'Asim al-Jahdari read all of them with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the kaf (*liyuhkama*, "that it may be judged"), because the Book is the judge in reality; it is what judges. The common reading has two explanations. One is that it is figurative speech, as in His saying: ﴿This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth﴾. The other is that its meaning is: that each prophet should judge by his book, and when he judges by the Book, it is as if the Book judges.

﴿Concerning that over which they differed﴾, ﴿and none differed over it﴾, that is, over the Book, ﴿except those who were given it﴾, that is, received it, and they are the Jews and Christians, ﴿after clear proofs had come to them﴾, meaning the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel.

Al-Farra' said: their differing has two meanings. One is that some of them disbelieved in the book of others, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 150.]] the verse [ ... ] [[unreadable word.]] and some of them declared others to be disbelievers. The other is their distortion and alteration of the Book of Allah the Exalted, as in His saying: ﴿They distort words from their places﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 46.]].

It has been said: this verse refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his book. The People of the Book differed concerning it after clear proofs had come to them, namely the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their books, ﴿out of insolent envy among themselves﴾, out of injustice and jealousy. ﴿So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed﴾, as in His saying: "Who guided us to this" and His saying: "They return to what they had said of truth, by His permission," by His knowledge and His will concerning them.

Ibn Zayd said concerning this verse: They differed about the prayer. Some pray facing the east, some face the west, and some face Bayt al-Maqdis, so Allah guided us to the Ka'bah. They differed about fasting: some fast part of a day, and some fast part of a night, so Allah guided us to the month of Ramadan. They differed about Friday: the Jews took Saturday and the Christians took Sunday, so Allah guided us to it. They differed about Ibrahim: the Jews said he was a Jew, and the Christians said he was a Christian, so Allah guided us to the truth in that. They differed about 'Isa: the Jews made him a son, and the Christians made him a lord, so Allah guided us to the truth regarding him. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/361.]]

﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾.

﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while the example of those who passed away before you has not yet come to you?﴾, the verse. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this verse was revealed concerning the Battle of the Trench, when the Muslims were afflicted with what befell them of hardship and difficulty [and heat and cold] and narrowness of living and various kinds of harm, as He said: ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾. It was also said that it was revealed concerning the Battle of Uhud, and its parallel is in Al 'Imran: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove﴾.

And it was said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions said to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "How long will you kill yourselves and not possess your wealth? If Muhammad were a prophet, he would not have been subjected to captivity and killing." So they said: "Undoubtedly, whoever among us is killed enters Paradise." So they said: "How long will you wish for yourselves falsehood [and you have heard] this verse."

'Ata' said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Madinah, the hardship intensified upon them, because they had left without wealth, so their lands and wealth were in the hands of the polytheists. So they preferred the pleasure of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and the pleasure of His Messenger (ﷺ). The Jews openly showed enmity to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a group of the wealthy secretly concealed hypocrisy. So Allah revealed, to comfort their hearts: ﴿Or did you think...﴾

"Am" here is an inceptive particle with no interrogation. The alif and mim are a connective; its meaning is "a'hasibtum" (did you think), as al-Farra' said.

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is "bal hasibtum" (rather, did you think), as in the saying of the poet:

"She appeared like the horn of the sun in the brightness of the forenoon,
and her form, or are you more graceful in the eye?"

[Lisan al-Arab: 14/54.]

That is, "bal anta" (rather, you). Everything in the Qur'an of this kind follows this path and this interpretation. The meaning of the verse is: did you suppose, while the Messenger (was among you), that you would enter Paradise, ﴿and the example has not yet come to you﴾, meaning "and it has not come to you," and its substance is like His exalted saying: ﴿And others from among them who have not yet joined them﴾. And al-Nabighah said:

"The time of departure has drawn near, but our riding beasts
have not yet stood by our saddles, as if it had already come."

[Lisan al-Arab: 3/346, "afad"; likewise in al-Mughni: 1/171.]

That is, "lam tazal" (they have not yet stood).

﴿The example of those who passed away before you﴾, who passed on, from the prophets and believers [and their way] [[as in the manuscript.]].

Then He mentioned what befell them, saying: ﴿Hardship touched them﴾, meaning poverty, harm, adversity and affliction, ﴿and adversity﴾, meaning illness and disease, ﴿and they were shaken﴾, that is, they were moved by various kinds of trials and calamities, and frightened, ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him said: "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ Those trials were such that they were slow to receive provision. Allah said: ﴿Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near﴾.

The reciters differed over His exalted saying ﴿yaqula al-Rasul﴾ (until the Messenger says). Mujahid read it with a fatha and a damma [on the lam]; al-A'raj: "yaqulu" with a raf'; and the others read it with a nasb. The one who reads with a nasb does so according to the apparent sense of the speech, because "hatta" (until) puts the following verb in the subjunctive. The one who reads with a raf' does so because its meaning is "hatta qala al-Rasul" (until the Messenger said). When the verb that follows "hatta" has the meaning of the past but the form of the present, you have the choice of raf' or nasb. The raf' is because "hatta" does not govern a past verb, and the nasb is by implying "an" (the light "an") according to the Basrans, and by "al-sarf" (the conversion) according to the Kufans. [Like your saying:] "We travelled until we enter Makkah" with raf', meaning "until we entered it." If it has the meaning of the future, then only the nasb is used.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Between Makkah and al-Ta'if there are found seventy [prophets] dead, whose cause of death was hunger and toil. Wahb also said: I read in a book of a man [among the Disciples]: "When the path of affliction leads you, then be content, for it has led you on the path of the prophets and the righteous. And when the path of ease leads you, then weep for yourself, [for it has] diverted you from their path."

[Shu'bah, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah], from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Which people are most severely tested?" He said: "The prophets, then the most excellent of people, then those next in excellence. A man is tested according to the measure of his religion. If his religion is firm, his trial is intensified, and if there is softness in his religion, then it is according to that measure. Affliction does not cease to befall the servant until He leaves him walking on the earth with no sin upon him." [113] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/174.]]

And from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Dhahl, who said: The minister of 'Isa (peace be upon him), a rider, was one day seized by a predator which devoured him. 'Isa said: "O Lord! My minister in Your religion, and my helper against the Children of Israel, and my successor, You have set Your dog upon him, and it devoured him." He said: "Yes. He had an exalted station with Me. I did not find his deeds reached it, so I tested him with that to bring him to that station."

﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾, the verse.

It was revealed concerning 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was an elderly man with wealth. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, with what should I give charity, and to whom should I give charity?" So Allah (ﷺ) revealed: ﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾.

There are two possibilities in the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of "dha" in the phrase "madha": one is that "madha" means "ayy shay'" (what thing), and it is [governed by] His saying "yunfiqun" (they spend), and its implied sense is: "They ask you what thing they should spend." The other is that it is in the nominative case with "ma" (what), and the meaning is: "They ask you, what is it that they spend?" ﴿Say: whatever you spend of good﴾, that is, wealth, ﴿is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveller﴾, ﴿and whatever good you do, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾, Knowing of it with knowledge of the teachings of the religion. This was before the zakat was obligated, and then the zakat abrogated (naskh) this verse.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 211–215:

Ask the Children of Israel (*Sal Bani Isra'il*), meaning: ask, O Muhammad, the Jews of Madinah, how many clear signs (*ayah bayyinah*), that is, manifest proofs, such as the staff in the hand, the white hand, the splitting of the sea and others, We gave to their fathers and forebears.

﴿And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah﴾, meaning changes the Book of Allah, ﴿after it has come to him, then indeed Allah is severe in punishment. 'Ata' said: it was revealed concerning the leaders of the Jews and their delegations from the Banu Qurayzah, al-Nadir and al-Qaynuqa', who mocked the poor emigrants, so Allah promised them that He would give them the wealth of the Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir without fighting, the easiest and most facile thing. [Allah] said: ﴿Where are those who disbelieve in the life of this world?﴾ This is according to the view of Mujahid.
