One group said: it is what a person's tongue utters of oaths quickly and hastily, so that his speech passes with it without binding or intention, like the saying of one who says: "No, by Allah," "Yes, by Allah," "No, by Allah," and the like. For this there is no expiation and no sin.

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Aisha, concerning ﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, said: it is a person's saying "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah." On this view are al-Sha'bi, 'Ikrimah, and Mujahid in the report of al-Hakam. al-Farazdaq said:

*You are not held accountable for laghw that you say, when you did not intend resolute oaths that bind.*

(Mufradat Gharib al-Qur'an: 452, where it reads "'aqidat al-'aza'im"; so also in al-Qurtubi's Tafsir.)

Others said: the laghw of an oath is that a person swears to a thing he believes to be true, then it becomes clear that it is otherwise. This is an error on his part without intention, and there is no expiation for him and no sin. This is the view of al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Abu Malik, Qatadah, al-Rabi', Zurarah ibn Awfa, Makhul, al-Suddi, and Ibn 'Abbas in the report of al-Walibi; and from Ahmad in the report of Ibn Abi Najih.

'Ali and Tawus said: laghw is the oath in a state of anger and irritation, without resolve or binding. The like of this was related by 'Ata' from Wasim from Ibn 'Abbas. The evidence for it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no oath in anger." (135) Some said: it is the oath in disobedience, which Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not hold one accountable for breaking; rather, he breaks his oath and expiates. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others said: there is no expiation for it.

Masruq said: concerning the man who swears to disobedience, there is no expiation for him; the expiation is repentance from the steps of Satan. The like was related by 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Sha'bi said: concerning the man who swears to disobedience, his expiation is that he repent from it. Thus every oath that it is not lawful for you to fulfil, there is no expiation in it, for if you had commanded him to expiate, you would have commanded him to complete his words. The evidence for this is what 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb related from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows concerning what he does not own, there is no vow for him; and whoever swears to disobey Allah, there is no oath for him." (136)

'Amrah related from 'Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears to sever kinship or to disobey, his righteousness is to break it and retract his oath." (137)

Hammad related from Ibrahim, who said: the laghw of an oath is that a man attaches his speech by swearing: "By Allah, I will surely not eat," or "I will surely not drink," and the like, without intending the oath and without wishing to swear. For this there is no expiation. The evidence for it is what 'Awf al-A'rabi related from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a group of people shooting arrows at a target, and a man among them shot and said: "By Allah, I hit it and missed." The companion who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The man has broken his oath." He said: "By Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No. The oaths of archers are laghw; there is no expiation for them nor punishment." (138)

'Aisha said: the oaths of laghw are those in jest, in dispute, and in quarrel, and in a statement that the heart does not bind itself to.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the supplication of the swearer against himself, like his saying: "May Allah blind my sight if I do not do such-and-such," "May He expel me from my wealth if I do not see you tomorrow," or he says: "He is a disbeliever if he does such-and-such." All this is laghw when it is with the tongue alone and not the heart, and Allah does not hold him accountable for it unless it comes from his heart. If it were otherwise, they would all be ruined. The evidence for it is His saying: ﴿And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man has always been hasty. And if Allah hastened for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾.

al-Dahhak said: it is the oath that requires expiation, and it was called laghw because expiation removes the sin from it. Its meaning is: "Allah will not hold you accountable for sin in the oath when you expiate." Al-Mughirah said, from Ibrahim: it is the man who swears concerning a thing and then forgets and breaks it [by Allah], so Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not hold him accountable for it. The evidence for it is His saying (ﷺ): "The error and forgetfulness of my community have been lifted, and what they have been compelled to." (139)

﴿But He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, meaning: you resolved, intended, and purposed, because the earning of the heart is the binding upon a thing and the intention.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾, the verse.

Know that oaths are of several kinds. Among them is an oath to an act of obedience, such as: "By Allah, I will surely pray," "I will surely fast," "I will surely perform Hajj," "I will surely give charity," and the like. If it is obligatory upon him, then it is obligatory for him not to break it; if he breaks it, then he owes expiation, because it was already obligatory upon him, so he has affirmed it further by the oath. If it is voluntary, there are two views: one, that he owes expiation for breaking it; the second, that he must fulfil what he said, and nothing else suffices for him. Among them is an oath to disobedience, whose ruling and disagreement we have already mentioned. Among them is an oath to what is permissible, and it is of two kinds: about the past and about the future. An oath about the future is, for example, saying: "By Allah, I will do such-and-such," or "By Allah, I will not do such-and-such." If he breaks such an oath, expiation is due without disagreement. An oath about the past is, for example, saying: "By Allah, such-and-such certainly happened," when it did not, or "such-and-such did not happen," when it did, while he knows it. This is the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus) which plunges its swearer into sin, because he deliberately committed the wrong. Expiation is due for it according to us; Abu Hanifah said: expiation is not due for it, and it is treated like laghw.

Then know that what is sworn by is of several kinds. One kind is an oath that is explicit and binding both outwardly and inwardly, and expiation is due upon breaking it, such as the saying: "By Allah," "by Allah," "by Allah" (wa-llahi, wa-billahi, wa-tallahi). These are explicit oaths, and intention is not considered in them. The second kind is swearing by an attribute of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, such as: "By the power of Allah," "by the greatness of Allah," "by the speech of Allah," "by the knowledge of Allah," and the like. The ruling for this is exactly the same as the first kind. The third kind is swearing by the ambiguous forms of oath, such as: "Ayman Allah," "Haqq Allah," "Qasam Allah," "La'amr Allah," and the like. In these intention is considered: if he intended an oath, it is an oath; if he says: "I did not intend an oath," his word is accepted concerning it. The fourth kind is swearing by other than Allah, such as saying: "By the Ka'bah," "by the prayer," "by the tablet," "by the pen," "by the right of Muhammad," "by my father," "by my life," "by the head of so-and-so," and the like. This is not an oath, and expiation is not due upon breaking it, but it is a disliked oath. Al-Shafi'i said: the meaning is that it is [ ... ] (an unclear statement).

'Abd Allah ibn Dinar said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: "The Quraysh used to swear by their fathers, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever is swearing, let him swear by Allah, and do not swear by your fathers.'" (140)

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard ['Umar] (a addition required by context) saying: "And by my father," so he forbade him from that. 'Umar said: "After that I never swore by it, mentioning it or relating it."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 222–225 (part 1 of 2):

*Wa-yas'alūnaka ʿani l-maḥīḍ* (They ask you about menstruation), the verse. ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿd Bashīr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "I have never seen a people better than the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They did not ask the Prophet about thirteen matters until the Qur'an revealed their mention:
﴿They ask you about the sacred month﴾ [2:217]
﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾; say: ﴿Whatever you spend of good﴾ [2:215]
﴿They ask you what they should spend﴾; say: ﴿The surplus﴾ [2:219]
﴿They ask you about the crescents﴾ [2:189]
﴿They ask you about wine and gambling﴾ [2:219]
﴿They ask you about orphans﴾ [2:220]
﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾ [2:222]
﴿They ask you about the Hour, when it will take place﴾; say: ﴿Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ [7:187]
﴿And when My servants ask you about Me﴾ [2:186]
﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ [8:1]
﴿They ask you about the Spirit﴾ [17:85]
﴿They ask you about Dhu l-Qarnayn﴾ [18:83]
﴿They ask you about the mountains﴾ [20:105]."

The exegetes said: In the Jahiliyyah, when a woman menstruated, the Arabs would not eat with her, drink with her, or share a house with her, nor sit with her on a bed, in the manner of the Magians and the Jews.

Abū l-Daḥdāḥ Thābit ibn al-Daḥdāḥ asked the Messenger of Allah about this and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how should we deal with women when they menstruate?" So Allah revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾, i.e., the ḥayḍ (menstruation). It is a verbal noun from your saying ḥāḍat al-mar'ah taḥīḍu ḥayḍan wa-maḥīḍan, like *al-sayr* and *al-masīr*, *al-ʿaysh* and *al-maʿīsh*, *al-kayl* and *al-makīl*. The root meaning of ḥayḍ is "gushing forth"; it is said: ḥāḍat al-thamarah when something like blood flowed from it.

﴿Say: It is an affliction﴾, i.e., filth, as said by Qatādah and al-Suddī. Mujāhid and al-Kalbī said: it is blood. *Al-adhā* is whatever is general and disliked in a thing.

﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾. Know that menstruation prevents nine things: from prayer, both permissibility and obligation; from fasting, permissibility; then she must make up the fast but does not have to make up the prayer.

ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from Muʿādah al-ʿAdawiyyah: a woman asked ʿĀ'ishah, saying: "The menstruating woman makes up the fast but does not make up the prayer." ʿĀ'ishah said to her: "Are you a Ḥarūriyyah?" She said: "I am not a Ḥarūriyyah, but I ask." ʿĀ'ishah said: "This would happen to us in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer."

ʿIyāḍ, from Abū Saʿīd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have not seen those deficient in intellect and religion who take away the understanding of a prudent man more than one of them." They said to him: "What is the deficiency of our intellect and religion, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Is not the testimony of a woman equal to half the testimony of a man? That is the deficiency of her intellect. Is it not that when a woman menstruates she neither prays nor fasts? They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'That is the deficiency of her religion.'"

She is also prohibited from reciting the Qur'an, though Mālik granted some leniency in it if the period is long, out of concern for forgetting the Qur'an; the jurists disagree with him. She is prohibited from touching the muṣḥaf, entering the mosque, and remaining in i'tikāf therein, from circumambulating the House, from counting the ʿiddah by it, and from intercourse. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾.

When this verse was revealed, the Muslims turned to menstruating women, expelled them from the houses, and kept away from them; when they had bathed, they brought them back into the house. Some Bedouins of Medina came and complained about the menstruating women being separated from them, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, the cold is severe and the garments are few. If we give the women garments, we and the household will be left in cold; and if we give the garments to the menstruating women, they will perish. Not all of us have the means for this, so widen it for all of them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "You were only commanded to keep away from intercourse with them when they menstruate, and He did not command you to expel them from the houses as the non-Arabs do." And he recited this verse to them.

Al-Nāṣirī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating, and a child is conceived from it, and he is afflicted with leprosy, let him blame none but himself. And whoever cups on Saturday and Wednesday, and suffers clear harm, let him blame none but himself." [131] [Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid: 4/299; al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ of al-Ṭabarānī: 3/326; neither of them contains the matter of cupping.]

If he has intercourse with her, he sins and is liable for expiation (kaffārah), and it is what Ibn Abī l-Mukhāriq narrated from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ that a man had intercourse with his wife while she was menstruating; he said: "If it was pure blood, let him give a dinar in charity; if it was yellowish, half a dinar." [Sunan al-Dārimī: 1/255.]

There is no harm in making the menstruating woman serve, touching her body while she wears a wrapper, and enjoying her above the waist-wrapper.

Masrūq was asked: "What is lawful for a man from his wife when she is menstruating?" He said: "Everything except intercourse."

On the authority of Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: ʿĀ'ishah was lying down with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in one garment, and she jumped up sharply. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "What is wrong with you? Perhaps you have menstruated"—meaning the menstrual period. She said: "Yes." He said: "Tighten your wrapper around you, then return to your bed." [132] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 1/259.]

Muʿādh ibn Hishām, from his father, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salamah, that Zaynab bint Abī Salamah related that Umm Salamah related to her, saying: "While I was lying down with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the khamīlah, I menstruated; I slipped away and took the clothes of my menses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Have you menstruated?' I said: 'Yes.' He called me, and I lay down with him in the khamīlah." [al-Sunan of al-Nasāʾī: 1/150; Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī: 1/75, 83.]

On the authority of Yazīdah, a freedwoman of Maymūnah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, from Maymūnah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would touch one of his wives while she was menstruating, if she had a wrapper reaching to the middle of the thighs or the knees. [al-Muḥallā of Ibn Ḥazm: 10/78.]

Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿĀ'ishah, who said: "I and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to bathe from one vessel while we were both in a state of major impurity (junub). I would delouse the head of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in i'tikāf in the mosque and I was menstruating. And when I was menstruating he would command me to tie my wrapper, then he would touch me."

Thābit ibn ʿUbaydah, from al-Qāsim, from ʿĀ'ishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hand me the mat." She said: "I am menstruating." He said: "Your menstruation is not in your hand." [Musnad Aḥmad: 6/45, 112; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: 1/168.]

And on the authority of Sharīḥ, who said: It was said to ʿĀ'ishah: "Does a woman eat with her husband while she is menstruating?" She said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would call me and I would eat with him while I was menstruating. He would take the bone, bite from it and swear that I should take it, so I would take it and bite from it. Then I would put it down, and he would take it and bite from it, placing his mouth where I had placed my mouth on the bone. He would ask for a drink, swear that I should drink first, so I would take it and drink, then I would put it down, and he would take it and drink, placing his mouth where I had placed my mouth on the cup."

These reports indicate that what is meant by keeping away from menstruation is intercourse with them. The Magians and the Jews used to avoid menstruating women in everything, while the Christians would have intercourse with them and paid no regard to menstruation. So Allah the Exalted enjoined moderation between these two matters, and the best of matters is the middle one.

Thābit, from Anas, who said: Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿They ask you about menstruation﴾, the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do everything except intercourse." This reached the Jews, who said: "What does this man want? He has left nothing of our affairs without opposing us in it." Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and ʿAbbād ibn Bishr came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews have said such and such. Shall we not have intercourse with them?" The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed, and they thought he was displeased with them. So they went out, and a gift of milk was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He sent after them and gave them to drink, and they knew that he was not displeased with them.

﴿And do not approach them﴾, i.e., do not have intercourse with them, ﴿until they are purified﴾. Ibn Muḥayṣin, al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, Khumarawayh, and al-Kisāʾī read *yaṭṭahhurna* with doubled ṭāʾ and hāʾ, meaning they bathe. This is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, *ḥattā yatatahharna* with the tāʾ, which is the original form. The rest read *yaṭhurna* without doubling, meaning ﴿until they are purified﴾ from their menses and the blood stops.

The jurists differed concerning when intercourse with a menstruating woman becomes lawful. Abū Ḥanīfah and his two companions said: If a woman menstruates for ten days, intercourse with her becomes lawful without her bathing. If she becomes pure before ten days, intercourse with her is not lawful except by one of three things: that she bathes, or that the time of the prayer passes for her, in which case she is judged by that as a pure woman regarding the obligation of prayer during that time, or that she performs tayammum when water is unavailable.

Mujāhid, Ṭāwūs, and ʿAṭāʾ said: If the menstruating woman becomes pure from the blood and her husband is overcome by desire, then if she washes her private part and performs ablution, he may come to her.

al-Shāfiʿī said: Intercourse with a menstruating woman is not lawful except at the time when the blood stops and she bathes. This is the view of Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, Sulaymān ibn Yasār, al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, Ibn Shihāb, al-Layth ibn Saʿd, and Zufar. al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: If a man has intercourse with his wife after the blood stops and before she bathes, he is liable for expiation like one who has intercourse with a menstruating woman. So whoever reads ﴿until they are purified﴾ with doubling has an argument for those who permit it. The proof that her intercourse is not lawful until she bathes is that Allah the Mighty and Majestic made the lawfulness of intercourse with her conditional on two things, so she is not lawful before both are fulfilled: His words ﴿until they are purified﴾ and His words ﴿but when they have purified themselves﴾, i.e., bathed. Its evidence is His words ﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾, and a person should not exert himself in what he has no part in; bathing is her action, while the stopping of the blood is not her action. It is also indicated by His words in al-Nisāʾ and al-Māʾidah: ﴿And if you are in a state of major impurity, purify yourselves﴾, where *iṭṭahhara* is one form, which is bathing. ﴿But when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where Allah has commanded you﴾, i.e., from where He commanded you to keep away from them, which is the private part. This was said by Mujāhid, Ibrāhīm, Qatādah, and ʿIkrimah.

al-Wālibī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, says: "Have intercourse with them in the private part, and do not go beyond it to anything else. Whoever does any of that has transgressed." [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 2/526.]

al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿUbayd: "You were forbidden from it, and fear the back passages." He said "from where Allah has commanded you" because the prohibition is also a command to abandon what is forbidden.

Others said: His words ﴿then come to them﴾ mean from the direction in which Allah has commanded you to approach them, which is the time of purity; as if He said: come to them at the time of their purity, not at the time of their menses. This is the view of Ibn Razīn, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and the narration of ʿAṭiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbās.

Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah: "Come to them in a lawful manner, not in debauchery."

Ibn Kaysān: "Do not come to them while fasting, nor while in i'tikāf, nor while in iḥrām. Come to them, approach them; their intimacy with you is lawful."

al-Farrāʾ: "Like your saying: I came to the land from its place of coming, i.e., from the direction from which it is approached."

al-Wāqidī: "Its meaning is ﴿from where Allah has commanded you﴾, which is the private part. Its parallel in the surah of the Angels and al-Aḥqāf is ﴿Show me what they have created from the earth﴾, i.e., in the earth; and His words ﴿when it is called to prayer on the day of Friday﴾, i.e., on the day of Friday."

﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves﴾. Mujāhid, from Ibn Razīn, and al-Kalbī said: ﴿those who repent﴾ from sins, ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from the back passages of women, by not coming to them there.

And he said: Whoever comes to a woman in her back passage is not among those who purify themselves, for the back passage of a woman is like that of a man.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: ﴿those who repent﴾ from sins, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from polytheism and ignorance.

I was once with Abū l-ʿĀliyah when he performed ablution well. I said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves﴾. He said: "Purification with water is good, but they are those who purify themselves from sins."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿those who repent﴾ from polytheism, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from sins.

And on the authority of Abū l-ʿĀliyah also: ﴿those who repent﴾ from disbelief, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ through faith.

Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿those who repent﴾ from sins, not returning to them; and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ here, who have not committed them.

al-Thaʿlabī said: I heard Abū l-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥabīb say: I asked Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qannād about this verse, and he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who repent﴾ from the major sins, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from the minor sins. ﴿Those who repent﴾ from actions, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from words. ﴿Those who repent﴾ from words and actions, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from contracts and concealment. ﴿Those who repent﴾ from sins, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from transgressions. ﴿Those who repent﴾ from offenses, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from the impurity of hidden things. ﴿Those who repent﴾ from sins, and ﴿those who purify themselves﴾ from defects.

The one who repents (al-tawwāb) is the one who, whenever he sins, repents; its parallel is His words ﴿For indeed He is ever Forgiving to those who repent often﴾ [17:25].

Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man from those before you, from the Children of Israel, passed by a skull, looked at it and said: 'O my Lord, You are You, and I am I. You are the one who repeatedly forgives, and I am the one who repeatedly sins.' Then he fell prostrate, and it was said to him: 'Raise your head; I am the one who repeatedly forgives, and you are the one who repeatedly sins.' He raised his head, and he was forgiven." [133] [Kanz al-ʿUmmāl: 4/226, no. 10276.]

﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾, the verse.

Jaʿfar ibn Abī l-Mughīrah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, said: ʿUmar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined." He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount last night, and he did not answer me at all." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾, meaning: come from the front and from behind, and beware of the back passage and menstruation. [Musnad Aḥmad: 1/297.]

Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The Jews used to say: "Whoever has intercourse with his wife from behind, in her front, his child will be cross-eyed." This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The Jews have lied." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: 3/156.]

Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, said: This tribe of the Anṣār were people of idols, along with this tribe of Jews, who were people of the Book, and they regarded the Jews as having superiority over them in knowledge, so they would follow much of their practice. It was the custom of the People of the Book not to come to women except on one side, which is the easiest for the woman. This tribe of the Anṣār would adopt that from their practice. And this tribe of Quraysh would treat women in a wicked manner, and they enjoyed them from the front, from behind, and lying down. When the Emigrants came to Medina, a man of them married a woman of the Anṣār, and he went to do that with her, and she rejected it and said: "We were only approached on one side. If you wish, do so; otherwise, keep away from me." The matter spread between them until it reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth﴾, meaning the place of offspring. [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr: 1/268.] They said: ﴿your tilth however you wish﴾ means from behind, from the front, and lying down.

al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, the two Muqātils, and al-Kalbī said: The Emigrants, the Anṣār, and the Jews discussed the coming of men to women in a gathering of theirs. The Emigrants said: "We come to them seated, standing, lying down, and from in front of them and from behind them, provided the place of entry is one, namely the private part." The Jews criticized them and said: "You are nothing but like cattle. We come to them in one posture only. We find in the Torah that every mode of approach to women other than lying down is filth in the sight of God, and from it comes squinting and madness." The Muslims mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, in our time of ignorance and after we embraced Islam, we used to come to women however we wished. The Jews criticized that for us and claimed that we were such and such." So Allah the Mighty and Majestic refuted the Jews and revealed a concession for them: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾, i.e., how you wish, where you wish, and when you wish, provided it is in one [place of entry]. [Asbāb al-Nuzūl of al-Wāḥidī: 49.]

*Anna* ("how" / "where") is an interrogative particle, and it may be a question about the manner or the place.

Sa'īd ibn al-Musayyab said: This concerns withdrawal (ʿazl), meaning: if you wish, withdraw, and if you wish, do not withdraw.

Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from a man, said: Ibn Mas'ud said, "One consults the free woman about coitus interruptus (al-'azl), but one does not consult the slave woman."

This verse is evidence for the prohibition of anal intercourse with women, because the anus is a place of excrement (al-farth), not a place of tilth (al-harth). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾. This is one of the subtle figures of speech of the Qur'an, where tilth (al-harth) is used to express the vagina (al-farj). So He said: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾, meaning a place of cultivation and the source of offspring. By "tilth" He meant the field that is sown, but since women are among the causes of tilling, they were called tilth.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the construction of the verse is "your women are like a tilth for you", as in His saying: ﴿until, when He made it fire﴾, meaning "like fire". The poet said:

*The scent is musk, the faces are dinars, and the fingertips are henna.*

The Arabs call women "tilth." Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama said: My father recited to me:

*When locusts eat the crops of a people, my tilth's concern is the locusts' eating.*

Al-Tha'labi said: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sadusi recited to me, saying: Abu Mansur Muhalhal ibn Ali al-'Azzi recited to me, saying: my father recited to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya recited to us:

*How lovely are the righteous offspring, the blessing of Allah's gift. They are the progeny, and by them the trees are the planted crop.*

*Allah grants us blessings in what He wills. The lands are for us tillable fields.*

*Upon us is the sowing in them, and upon Allah is the growing.*

(This is as it stands in the manuscript; there seems to be a flaw in it. Cf. the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 3/93.)

Some jurists erred in the interpretation of this verse and clung to the apparent meaning of a report which Abu 'Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from the narrators of al-Dinawari, related to us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Hayyani Abu Bakr al-Tarsusi and Ishaq al-Ghurawi, from Malik ibn Anas, from Nafi', who said: I used to hold the mushaf for Ibn 'Umar, and he recited this verse: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾. He said: "Do you know concerning what this verse was revealed?" I said: "No." He said: "It was revealed concerning a man who came to his wife from behind during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and that was difficult for him, so the verse ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾ was revealed."

As for the interpretation of Ibn 'Umar's report, it is what 'Ata' related from Musa ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan, from his father, that he met Salim ibn 'Abd Allah and said: "O Abu 'Umar, what did the narrator of Nafi' relate from 'Abd Allah?" He said: "And what is it?" He said: "He claimed that he did not see any harm in having intercourse with women from behind." He said: "The servant lied and erred. 'Abd Allah only said: 'They are approached in their vaginas, from behind.'"

The evidence for the prohibition of the anus is what 'Ikrimah related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning His saying: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾: "Tilth only occurs where growth occurs." And from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah is not shy of the truth. Do not approach women in their anuses."

Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Cursed is the one who approaches his wife in her anus."

﴿And send ahead for yourselves﴾: meaning, seek offspring. It was also said: marry chaste women so that the child will be righteous and pure. It was also said: it is a rebuke of excess.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three children who have not reached puberty, the Fire will not touch him except as an oath's fulfilment (tahillat al-qasam)." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, two?" He said: "And two." Then he said: "We thought that if one had been said, he would have said one."

Shahr ibn 'Atiyyah, from 'Ata', concerning ﴿and send ahead for yourselves﴾, said: it is the saying of the basmala at intercourse. Mujahid said concerning ﴿and send ahead for yourselves﴾: meaning, when one approaches his wife, let him supplicate.

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When one of you wishes to approach his wife, let him say: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us, and keep Satan away from what You provide us.' If a child is decreed between them, Satan will not harm it." (Musnad Ahmad: 1/217; Sahih al-Bukhari: 4/94.)

Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: it means the good and righteous deed, as evidenced by the context of the verse: ﴿And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him﴾. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿send ahead for yourselves﴾ means in everything Allah has made lawful for you and in what He has obligated you to, for your affirmation of Allah and His Messenger in everything He has made lawful for you and forbidden to you, and what you have been made to worship, is a true advance (qadam sidq) for you with your Lord. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. ﴿And know that you will meet Him﴾, so He will recompense you for your deeds.

﴿And give good tidings to the believers. And do not make Allah an obstacle (ʿurḍa) for your oaths...﴾ the verse. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, forbidding him from severing ties with his brother-in-law (khatan), Bashir ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, because there was something between them. 'Abd Allah swore that he would not enter upon him, nor speak to him, nor reconcile with him or with an adversary of his, and he kept saying:

*I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it. So it is not lawful for me unless my oath is fulfilled.*

So Allah revealed this verse.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) when he swore that he would not support his son 'Abd al-Rahman until he became Muslim. Ibn Jurayj said: I was told that it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah when he engaged in the slander (hadith al-ifk).

The root of "ʿurḍa" is strength and power, and from it comes the name for a mount prepared and readied for travel: "ʿurḍa," because of its strength over it. It is said: "I readied my she-camel for that," meaning I took it for that. Aws ibn Hajar said:

*And a brown camel like a stallion, one day I readied her for my saddle, and in her is vigour and sway.*

(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/98.)

Then it was said of anything that is suitable for a thing that it is ʿurḍa for it, until they said of a woman: she is ʿurḍa for marriage when she is fit for it and strong enough for it. It is said: so-and-so is ʿurḍa for vigil and war. Hassan said:

*Allah has said: "I have made ready a host, the Ansar, who are fit for the encounter."*

(Sahih Muslim: 7/165.)

The commentators said: This concerns a man who swears by Allah the Exalted that he will not maintain ties of kinship, nor speak to his relatives, or that he will not give charity in goodness, or that he will reconcile between two persons, and they disobey him or accuse him, or one of them does, so he swears by Allah that he will not reconcile between them. So Allah commanded him to break his oath (yahnath) and to do that secretly and expiate his oath. The meaning of the verse is: "Do not make Allah a cause and an obstacle preventing you from righteousness and piety." One of you says, "I have sworn by Allah," and so he holds his oath as a reason for abandoning righteousness and reform. This is His saying: ﴿that you be righteous and fear Allah and reconcile between people, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. Its meaning is "that you not be righteous," like His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 176), meaning "lest you go astray." Imru' al-Qays said:

*So I said: "By Allah's oath, I shall not rise from sitting, even if they cut off my head before you and my joints."*

(Al-Sihah of al-Jawhari: 6/2222.)

What clarifies this verse is what Sama' related from al-Husayn, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you swear an oath and see something better than it, then do what is better and expiate your oath." (134)

Sinan ibn Habib said: I said to Sa'd ibn Humayr: "My female client, who used to live with me, disobeyed me, so I swore that she would not live with me." He said: "This is from the work of Satan. Expiate your oath and let her live with you." Then he recited: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾.

﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾. The origin of "laghw" (inadvertence, idle talk) in Arabic speech is what is dropped and not counted. Dhu al-Rummah said:

*And he casts between them the Mari as laghw, what was dropped in the hundred of the young camels.*

(Al-Sihah: 6/2484, where it reads "yahlik bayniha" and in al-Lisan "yahlik wasatiha"; the rest as in al-Sihah.)

He means by "the hundred" those camels driven as blood-money, when one of them sets down a young camel that he does not put forward. "Al-Mari" is attributed to Imru' al-Qays ibn Zayd ibn Manat ibn Tamim. Al-Muthaqqib al-'Abdi said:

*Or a hundred whose young are made laghw, and the width of the hundred is the hard ground.*

(Al-Sihah: 3/1089.)

"Laghw" and "lagha'" in speech are what has no good in it and no meaning. Its counterpart in the language is "safw" (the pure part) of so-and-so with you, and "safa" it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who turn away from idle talk﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun: 3), and He said: ﴿They hear therein no laghw﴾ (Surah Maryam: 62). Umayyah said:

*There is no laghw nor sin therein, and what they utter for them is lasting.*

(Lisan al-'Arab: 12/6.)

Al-'Ajjaj said:

*And many a flock of pilgrims restraining their anger, from laghw and obscene speech.*

(Al-Sihah: 1/283.)

The scholars differed concerning the laghw of oaths mentioned in this verse. One group said: it is what a person's tongue utters of oaths quickly and hastily, so that his speech passes with it without binding or intention, like the saying of one who says: "No, by Allah," "Yes, by Allah," "No, by Allah," and the like. For this there is no expiation and no sin.

Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'Aisha, concerning ﴿Allah does not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths﴾, said: it is a person's saying "No, by Allah" and "Yes, by Allah." On this view are al-Sha'bi, 'Ikrimah, and Mujahid in the report of al-Hakam. al-Farazdaq said:

*You are not held accountable for laghw that you say, when you did not intend resolute oaths that bind.*

(Mufradat Gharib al-Qur'an: 452, where it reads "'aqidat al-'aza'im"; so also in al-Qurtubi's Tafsir.)

Others said: the laghw of an oath is that a person swears to a thing he believes to be true, then it becomes clear that it is otherwise. This is an error on his part without intention, and there is no expiation for him and no sin. This is the view of al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Abu Malik, Qatadah, al-Rabi', Zurarah ibn Awfa, Makhul, al-Suddi, and Ibn 'Abbas in the report of al-Walibi; and from Ahmad in the report of Ibn Abi Najih.

'Ali and Tawus said: laghw is the oath in a state of anger and irritation, without resolve or binding. The like of this was related by 'Ata' from Wasim from Ibn 'Abbas. The evidence for it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no oath in anger." (135) Some said: it is the oath in disobedience, which Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not hold one accountable for breaking; rather, he breaks his oath and expiates. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others said: there is no expiation for it.

Masruq said: concerning the man who swears to disobedience, there is no expiation for him; the expiation is repentance from the steps of Satan. The like was related by 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Sha'bi said: concerning the man who swears to disobedience, his expiation is that he repent from it. Thus every oath that it is not lawful for you to fulfil, there is no expiation in it, for if you had commanded him to expiate, you would have commanded him to complete his words. The evidence for this is what 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb related from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows concerning what he does not own, there is no vow for him; and whoever swears to disobey Allah, there is no oath for him." (136)

'Amrah related from 'Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears to sever kinship or to disobey, his righteousness is to break it and retract his oath." (137)

Hammad related from Ibrahim, who said: the laghw of an oath is that a man attaches his speech by swearing: "By Allah, I will surely not eat," or "I will surely not drink," and the like, without intending the oath and without wishing to swear. For this there is no expiation. The evidence for it is what 'Awf al-A'rabi related from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a group of people shooting arrows at a target, and a man among them shot and said: "By Allah, I hit it and missed." The companion who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The man has broken his oath." He said: "By Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No. The oaths of archers are laghw; there is no expiation for them nor punishment." (138)

'Aisha said: the oaths of laghw are those in jest, in dispute, and in quarrel, and in a statement that the heart does not bind itself to.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the supplication of the swearer against himself, like his saying: "May Allah blind my sight if I do not do such-and-such," "May He expel me from my wealth if I do not see you tomorrow," or he says: "He is a disbeliever if he does such-and-such." All this is laghw when it is with the tongue alone and not the heart, and Allah does not hold him accountable for it unless it comes from his heart. If it were otherwise, they would all be ruined. The evidence for it is His saying: ﴿And man supplicates for evil as he supplicates for good, and man has always been hasty. And if Allah hastened for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾.

al-Dahhak said: it is the oath that requires expiation, and it was called laghw because expiation removes the sin from it. Its meaning is: "Allah will not hold you accountable for sin in the oath when you expiate." Al-Mughirah said, from Ibrahim: it is the man who swears concerning a thing and then forgets and breaks it [by Allah], so Allah the Mighty and Majestic does not hold him accountable for it. The evidence for it is His saying (ﷺ): "The error and forgetfulness of my community have been lifted, and what they have been compelled to." (139)

﴿But He holds you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾, meaning: you resolved, intended, and purposed, because the earning of the heart is the binding upon a thing and the intention.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾, the verse.

Know that oaths are of several kinds. Among them is an oath to an act of obedience, such as: "By Allah, I will surely pray," "I will surely fast," "I will surely perform Hajj," "I will surely give charity," and the like. If it is obligatory upon him, then it is obligatory for him not to break it; if he breaks it, then he owes expiation, because it was already obligatory upon him, so he has affirmed it further by the oath. If it is voluntary, there are two views: one, that he owes expiation for breaking it; the second, that he must fulfil what he said, and nothing else suffices for him. Among them is an oath to disobedience, whose ruling and disagreement we have already mentioned. Among them is an oath to what is permissible, and it is of two kinds: about the past and about the future. An oath about the future is, for example, saying: "By Allah, I will do such-and-such," or "By Allah, I will not do such-and-such." If he breaks such an oath, expiation is due without disagreement. An oath about the past is, for example, saying: "By Allah, such-and-such certainly happened," when it did not, or "such-and-such did not happen," when it did, while he knows it. This is the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus) which plunges its swearer into sin, because he deliberately committed the wrong. Expiation is due for it according to us; Abu Hanifah said: expiation is not due for it, and it is treated like laghw.

Then know that what is sworn by is of several kinds. One kind is an oath that is explicit and binding both outwardly and inwardly, and expiation is due upon breaking it, such as the saying: "By Allah," "by Allah," "by Allah" (wa-llahi, wa-billahi, wa-tallahi). These are explicit oaths, and intention is not considered in them. The second kind is swearing by an attribute of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, such as: "By the power of Allah," "by the greatness of Allah," "by the speech of Allah," "by the knowledge of Allah," and the like. The ruling for this is exactly the same as the first kind. The third kind is swearing by the ambiguous forms of oath, such as: "Ayman Allah," "Haqq Allah," "Qasam Allah," "La'amr Allah," and the like. In these intention is considered: if he intended an oath, it is an oath; if he says: "I did not intend an oath," his word is accepted concerning it. The fourth kind is swearing by other than Allah, such as saying: "By the Ka'bah," "by the prayer," "by the tablet," "by the pen," "by the right of Muhammad," "by my father," "by my life," "by the head of so-and-so," and the like. This is not an oath, and expiation is not due upon breaking it, but it is a disliked oath. Al-Shafi'i said: the meaning is that it is [ ... ] (an unclear statement).

'Abd Allah ibn Dinar said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: "The Quraysh used to swear by their fathers, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever is swearing, let him swear by Allah, and do not swear by your fathers.'" (140)

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard ['Umar] (a addition required by context) saying: "And by my father," so he forbade him from that. 'Umar said: "After that I never swore by it, mentioning it or relating it."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 226–229 (part 1 of 2):

لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months﴾.

Qatada said: Ila' (oath of abstention) was the divorce of the people of the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: That was among the harms of the people of the Jahiliyya. A man would not desire a woman, nor would he like her to marry another; he would swear that he would never approach her, and he would leave her in that state, neither unmarried nor married. They did this in the Jahiliyya and in Islam. So God made the term by which a man would know about his wife four months, and God revealed: ﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "li-lladhina ala min nisa'ihim" (in the past tense). Ibn 'Abbas recited: "li-lladhina yuqsimuna min nisa'ihim" (those who swear).

Al-Ila' means the oath. It is said: "ala yuli, ila'" (he swore). al-Khansa' said:
"So I swore to grieve over the dead, or to ask the wailing woman about her possessions" [Zad al-Masir: 4/204; Kitab al-'Ayn: 8/349; Lisan al-'Arab: 15/465].

Its noun is al-alya. A poet said:
"Upon me is an oath and fasting; its wing-keeper refuses to restrain itself"

It has four dialect forms: aliyya, alwa, lalwa and alwa. The meaning of the verse, "for those who swear off," is that they withdraw from their wives. The object is omitted, the context being sufficient to indicate it. Al-tarabbus means waiting and pausing. Some claimed it is inverted (from al-tarassud), saying: al-tarabbus means patience. For example, a man swears that he will not approach his wife, saying to her: "By God, I will not have intercourse with you," or "my bed will not join your bed," and similar expressions of intercourse. Whenever a man swears to his wife and thereby refrains from intercourse with her for more than four months without any impediment in his body or wealth, that is an ila'. What is less than four months is not an ila'.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) used to say: "Ila' is an oath made in anger; if one swears in a state of contentment, it is not an ila'." The majority of jurists apply it to deliberate oaths, and they make ila' binding on every oath that prevents intercourse, whether in contentment or anger. If he swears an ila', and then has intercourse before four months pass, he expiates his oath and there is nothing upon him. The nukul (the penalty for failing to fulfil) applies if he does not have intercourse until four months have passed. The jurists differed regarding this. Some said: when four months pass and he does not fulfil it, she is divorced from him by a single revocable divorce, and she is free to decide her own affairs. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad ibn Thabit, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Kalbi and Abu Hanifa. Ibn 'Abbas's statement supports it: "The resolute divorce is the completion of four months."

Others said: when four months pass and the man is still refraining, if the woman is chaste and does not demand her right to intercourse, there is nothing upon the man and no divorce occurs, and they remain married as they were. If she demands her right, the judge stops her husband, and he must either fulfil or divorce. If he refuses both the return (to marital relations) and divorce, the judge divorces him on his behalf. It is said: he keeps him in detention indefinitely until he divorces. The whole of this view that they mention, of the stopping, is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Abu al-Darda', Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayda, Ahmad, Ishaq and the majority of the people of hadith.

Yunus al-Sawwaf said: I came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He said: "From where?" I said: "From Kufa." He said: "They say about ila', when four months have passed, [there is nothing upon him], and not four years, until if he returns [he should divorce]," and he disregards intercourse. If he is incapable of intercourse because of illness, impotence or the like, he returns by his tongue and calls witnesses.

He also said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say: "He is held to his word in every case; if he returns, he owes expiation for his oath according to the jurists." Except al-Hasan, Ibrahim and Qatada, who dropped the expiation from the one who swore if he returns, based on His saying: ﴿But if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibrahim said: "This applies to the forfeiture of the right by it, not to the expiation."

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾, that is, they are determined and sincere and intend it. Ibn 'Abbas recited: "wa in 'azamu al-sirah," which is also divorce.

﴿Then indeed God is All-Hearing of their saying, All-Knowing of their intentions﴾. This indicates that she is not divorced after the four months pass unless her husband or the ruler divorces her, because the verse makes the resolve a condition, and because hearing implies [ ... ] [[Unreadable word in the manuscript.]]. The saying is what is heard, and the hearing relates to the divorce; and God knows best.

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾. The verse was revealed concerning the case of... Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Kalbi said: At the beginning of Islam, if a man divorced his wife three times while she was pregnant, he had more right to take her back as long as she had not given birth, until God abrogated that with His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that﴾, and so on. Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah al-Ghifari divorced his wife Qutayla while she was pregnant.

Muqatil said: It was Malik ibn al-Ashdaq, a man from al-Ta'if. They all said: the man was unaware of this, and she did not inform him of it. When he learned of her pregnancy, he took her back and returned her to his house. She gave birth and died, and her child died. Concerning this God revealed this verse: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those released from the bonds of their husbands. It derives from the saying: "I released the thing from my hand" (atlaqtu al-shay' min yadi) and "I let it loose" (talaqtuhu) when I let it go. However, because the two words were used so much, they distinguished between them, so that tatliq is restricted to wives; and the Qur'an was revealed in that manner: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. The noun from it is talaq. It is said: "al-rajul talaqa al-mar'a" and "tallaqat" and "taliqat," all together. Its origin is from the saying: "inṭalaqa al-rajul" when a man goes forth unrestrained. The course that a horse or other animal runs without being restrained is called talq.

﴿Wait by themselves﴾: they await, and do not remarry. ﴿Three periods﴾: plural of qar', like qar' (sg.) and its small plural quru' and large plurals aqra' and qara'. The jurists differed regarding the qurū'.

Some people said: they are menstruations. This is the view of 'Ali, 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and the position of Sufyan, Abu Hanifa and the people of Kufa. They argued by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the woman suffering istihada: "Leave off prayer during the days of your menses" [141] [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/220]. Prayer is left only during menstruation. A rajaz verse recited by Tha'lab, from Ibn al-A'rabi, says:
"He has periods like the periods of the menstruating woman" [We have not found it with these words; see Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 1/484; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/448; Gharib al-Hadith: 1/34].
It means that his enmity flares up at known times, just as a woman menstruates at known times. Whoever holds this view says: a woman is not lawful to husbands and does not exit her 'idda until the third menstruation is complete. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Ali said concerning a man who divorces his wife once or twice: the husband may not take her back until she has bathed from the third menstruation and prayer becomes lawful for her.

Others said: they are the periods of purity (tuhr), the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i and the people of Medina. They argued by the saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their 'idda﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when Ibn 'Umar divorced a woman while she was menstruating, to 'Umar: "Tell him to take her back; when she becomes pure, let him divorce or keep her." The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them [at their waiting period]﴾. So he (ﷺ) informed that the 'idda is the periods of purity from menstruation, and he recited: "fa-tallaquhunna li-'iddatihinna" (divorce them for their waiting period), which means that he divorces her while she is pure, because then she begins her 'idda; if he divorced her during menstruation, she would not begin her 'idda until after the menstruation. What indicates that the qurū' are the periods of purity is the statement of the poet, al-A'sha:
"And every year you undertake a raid, and the determination of your raids pulls its farthest reach,
Leaving wealth behind, and in the tribe there is elevation, for what was lost among them of the quru' of your women."
[Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 2/603; al-Sihah li-l-Jawhari: 1/64].
The qar' in this verse means the purity, because he went out on raids and did not approach his women, so their quru' (periods of purity) were lost. Whoever holds this view says: when a woman has her third menstruation, her 'idda is complete and she is lawful for marriage. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa and 'Amra, from 'A'isha, who said: "When the divorced woman enters the third menstruation, she has separated from her husband and is lawful for husbands." 'Amra said: 'A'isha used to say: "The qar' is the purity, not the menstruation." Ibn Shihab said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: "I did not meet any of our jurists except that he says this," meaning the saying of 'A'isha: "The periods (aqra') are the purities."

This disagreement arose because qar' in the lexicon is one of the words with opposite meanings, suitable for both meanings together. One says: "aqra'at al-mar'a" when she menstruated, and "aqra'at" when she became pure; she is "tuqri" (in the state of menstruation or purity). They differed regarding its root. Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubayda said: it is the time of a thing's arrival and departure. It is said: "raja'a fulan li-qari'ihi" (he returned at his appointed time), i.e., the time at which he returns; and "hadha qari' al-riyah" (this is the time of the winds' blowing) [Zad al-Masir: 1/232].
Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:
"I disliked the slaughter of the Bani Shulayl, when the winds blow at their appointed time."
That is, at its time. It is said: "aqra'at al-nujum" when the stars rose, and "aqra'at" when they set.
Kathir said:
"When the Pleiades have risen, and the sky perceives that they have set."
So qar' applies to both, because menstruation comes at a time and purity comes at a time. It is also said: it is from [qara' al-ma' fi al-hawd, meaning gathering it], as in the verse of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:
"Two forearms of a she-camel when the young one has been weaned, white-skinned and lean, that has not carried a foetus."
That is, she did not conceive, and her womb did not close over a child. The Arabs say: "ma qara'at al-naqa bi-la qurt," meaning the she-camel does not close her womb over an offspring. From this is their saying: "qara'tu al-Qur'an," meaning I pronounced it collected. This is the choice of al-Zajjaj. He said: "From it is qaraytu al-ma' fi al-miqra' (I gathered the water in the cistern)," leaving out the hamza, though the original form has the hamza. So qar' is the retention and gathering of blood, and it occurs both in purity and in menstruation together; but the preference is for purity, because it collects and retains the blood, while menstruation loosens and releases it; and God knows best.

Ruling of the verse

Know that its wording is a report but its meaning is a command, like His saying: ﴿And mothers shall suckle their children﴾ and similar. The 'idda is of two kinds: the 'idda of a divorced woman and the 'idda of a widow. The 'idda of a divorced woman is of three types: the 'idda of a menstruating woman is three quru'; the 'idda of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth; and the 'idda of a young girl who has not menstruated and an elderly woman who has despaired of menstruation is three months. The 'idda of a widow is of two kinds: if she is pregnant, her 'idda is until she gives birth; otherwise her 'idda is four months and ten days. The 'idda of slave women is half of that which applies to free women, and among the periods there are two quru'; there is no half-'idda for one who has not been consummated when her husband dies, so her 'idda is four months and ten days ...

﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. 'Ikrima and Ibrahim said: this means menstruation, that is, a woman observing her 'idda while the man wishes to take her back, and she says: "I have menstruated a third time." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and Muqatil said: it means pregnancy in the child. So the meaning of the verse is: it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, of menstruation and pregnancy, to nullify the husband's right of return and the child, for a woman is trusted regarding her private parts.

﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾, and ﴿their husbands﴾, that is, their spouses. It is the plural of ba'l, like fuhula, dhukura, hazula and khayyuta. It is said: "tab'ala al-mar'a" when a woman marries, and from this intercourse is called ba'al. The husband is called ba'l because he takes charge of his wife's affairs. The root of ba'l is master and owner. God said: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾ Muslim ibn Muharib read "wa-bu'ulatuhunna" with the t vowel-less due to the many vowels; the full-vowel form is more eloquent, better, more suitable and preferable.

﴿Have more right to take them back﴾, that is, to their return ﴿in that case﴾, that is, during the 'idda ﴿if they desire reconciliation, not harm﴾. This is because when a man wants to harm his wife, he divorces her once and leaves her until near the end of her 'idda, then takes her back, then leaves her for a time, then divorces her again and leaves her as he did the first time, then takes her back, leaves her for a time, then divorces her.

﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them﴾, that is, women have over their husbands a right similar to what they owe.

It is reported that the wife of Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of God, what is the right of a wife over her husband?" He said: "That he does not strike her face, that he does not disfigure her, that he feeds her what he eats, clothes her with what he wears, and does not abandon her." [142] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/100].

Al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives who own nothing for themselves." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594, hadith 1851.] "You took them under the trust of God, and made lawful their private parts by the word of God." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/73.]

From Maymuna, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best of men of my community are those best to their women, and the best of women of my community are those best to their husbands. For every woman among them there is recorded every day and night the reward of a thousand martyrs who were slain in the path of God, patient and seeking reward; and the excellence of one of them over the dark-eyed houris is like the excellence of Muhammad over the lowest man among you. The best women of my community are those who come to their husbands' pleasure in all that he desires, short of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic. The best men of my community are those who are gentle to their families as a mother is gentle to her child; there is recorded for every man among them, every day and night, the reward of a hundred martyrs slain in the path of God, seeking reward and patient."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of God, how can a woman have the reward of a thousand martyrs and a man the reward of a hundred martyrs?" He said: "Do you not know that the woman has greater reward and more excellent recompense than the man, and that God, the Mighty and Majestic, raises the man in Paradise to degrees above his degrees because of his wife's contentment with him in this world and her supplication for him? Do you not know that the greatest burden after associating partners with God is the woman who covers her husband [with ingratitude]?

Beware, fear God regarding the two weak ones, for God will ask you about them: the orphan and the woman. Whoever is kind to them has reached God and His good pleasure, and whoever wrongs them has deserved God's anger. The right of the husband over the wife is like my right over you. Whoever neglects my right has neglected the right of God, and whoever neglects the right of God has returned with the wrath of God, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination."[144]

﴿In kindness; and men have a degree over them﴾, in excellence.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it is] by what he gives her of dowry and what he spends on her of wealth. It is also said: by reason; it is said: by inheritance; it is said: by rank. Qatada said: by jihad.

From Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: While we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was among a group of his companions, a woman approached and stood over his head, then said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. I am the envoy of the women to you. There is no woman who [has heard of my departure] to you except that she is pleased with it. O Messenger of God, God is the Lord of men and the Lord of women; Adam is the father of men and the father of women; Eve is the mother of men and the mother of women. When men go out in the path of God and are slain, ﴿they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾. When they go out, they have authority over us as you know; we [are kept back] from them and serve them; do we have any share of reward?" He said: "Yes. Convey my greetings to the women and say to them: 'Obedience to the husband and acknowledgment of his right equals all that; but few of you do it.'" [145] [al-Musannaf li-'Abd al-Razzaq: 8/463].

Thabit reported from Anas, who said: They came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, the men have taken the excellence through jihad in the path of God; what deed is there for us after you that equals a deed in the path of God?"

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani reported from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked: "Is there jihad upon women?" He said: "Yes, their jihad is jealousy; they struggle against themselves. If they are patient, they are strivers, and if they are patient, they are garrisoned, and they have two rewards." [146] [We have not found it in the sources.]

It is also said: [the degree is] by divorce and return; it is said: by testimony; it is said: by the strength of worship. Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by leadership. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is ﴿and men have a degree over them﴾, that is, a virtue of right.

﴿And God is Mighty, Wise﴾.

﴿Divorce is twice﴾

Hisham ibn Urwa narrated from his father, from Aisha, that a woman came to her and complained that her husband divorced her and then took her back in order to harm her by it. In the Jahiliyya, when a man divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period (*'iddah*) ended, he was entitled to do so. Even if he divorced her a thousand times, there was no limit to divorce among them. Aisha mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then there was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, and so Allah set the limit of divorce at three.

As for the third divorce, the words of Allah the Exalted apply: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾.

It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Divorce is twice, so where is the third?" He said: ﴿Then either keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾.

The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is that the divorce in which the husband has the right of return is twice. ﴿Then keep her in kindness﴾ means he must keep her in kindness, that is, he takes her back during the third pronouncement. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾ means after it, and he should not harm her. If he divorces her once or twice, he has the greater right to take her back as long as she is within the waiting period. When the waiting period ends, she has the right to herself. It is permissible for him to remarry her by mutual consent through a new marriage contract. If he divorces her a third time, she is separated from him and has the right to herself apart from him, and she is not lawful to him ﴿until she marries another husband﴾.

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them﴾, meaning during the time of exchange and divorce, any of the gifts, bridal payments (*mahr*) or other things you have given them. Then He made an exception for *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), saying: ﴿Except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾.

This verse was revealed concerning Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. She hated him intensely, and he loved her intensely. There was a dispute between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said to her: "Return to your husband, for by Allah, I dislike that a woman should always be raising her hand to complain about her husband." So she returned to him a second time with marks of beating on her, and she complained to him again. He said to her: "Return to your husband." When she saw that her father would not take up her complaint, she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complained to him about her husband, and showed him marks of beating on her, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Thabit ibn Qays and said: "O Thabit, what is your situation with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, there is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah when he asked her, so she said: "He speaks the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I feared that he would destroy me. Release me from him, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I have given her a garden of mine, so tell her to return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "What do you say? Will you return to him his garden and have authority over your own affair?" She said: "Yes, and I do not want him." He said: "No, only the garden."

Then she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I never told you a statement today that would be revealed to you contrary tomorrow. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I hate him, so neither he nor I [can continue]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." He did so. This was the first *khul'* in Islam. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear [that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾, where "fear" means "know."

[Footnote 147 and its note in the original: the hadith is mentioned by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/186), and likewise by al-Tabari in Jami' al-Bayan (2/626) and Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba (8/81), but all of them in abridged form.]

This is supported by the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿except that they both suspect﴾. Muhajjan said:

*"So do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear that when I die I will not taste it."*

[Footnote: Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari, 2/625.]

That is, "I know." Abu Ja'far, Hamza and Ya'qub read *yukhafa* with a dammed *ya'* (i.e., ﴿except that they both be made to fear﴾), meaning that this knowledge comes from them, by analogy with the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿except that they fear﴾. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, because of Allah's words: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. He said: "He made the fear belong to others and did not say 'if both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.'" The fear here is that the woman fears temptation for herself and so disobeys Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him he will transgress against her. Allah forbade the man to take anything from a woman without her consent, except when the disobedience (*nushuz*) and bad conduct come from her. For example, she says: "By Allah, I will not fulfill any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor let you lie with me," and similar things. When she does that to him, it is permissible for him to punish her, if she brings this upon herself. It is disliked for him to take from her more than he gave her, but in legal judgment it is permissible.

This is clarified by what al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna narrated: a woman showed *nushuz* toward her husband during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) admonished her and commanded her to obey her husband, but she refused and said: "If you return me to him, by Allah I will kill myself." So he ordered her to be confined in the stable of the animals, in the house of the fodder, for three nights. Then he summoned her and said: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I have not spent nights more pleasing to my eye than these, and I have not found rest since I was with him except these nights." He said: "This, by your father, is *nushuz*." Then he said to her husband: "Separate from her, even if it be for her earrings. Separate from her for less than the ornament of her head-band, for there is no good for you in her." This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾.

Al-Farra' said: He meant by it the husband, not the wife, but He mentioned both together because they are a pair, like His words: ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, when only the young man of Moses forgot, not Moses (peace be upon him). And His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾, when they come only from the salt water and not the sweet. A poet said:

*"If you reproach me, O son of Affan, I will be reproached; and if you call me, I will protect a defended honor."*

[Footnote: al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, 3/868; the verse is by Suwayd ibn Kura'.]

Others said its meaning is: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them﴾ together. There is no blame upon the woman for *nushuz* if she fears destruction and disobedience, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives of wealth, because she is prohibited from squandering wealth without right. Nor is there blame upon the man for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly, according to her wish.

The jurists have two opinions on *khul'*:

The first: it is a dissolution of the marriage without a divorce (*faskh*). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, and the view of al-Shafi'i in his old school in Iraq, from which he later retracted in Egypt.

The second: *khul'* is a single irrevocable divorce, unless the husband intends more than that. This is the view of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), and the new view of al-Shafi'i.

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, meaning do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 226–229 (part 1 of 2):

لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months﴾.

Qatada said: Ila' (oath of abstention) was the divorce of the people of the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: That was among the harms of the people of the Jahiliyya. A man would not desire a woman, nor would he like her to marry another; he would swear that he would never approach her, and he would leave her in that state, neither unmarried nor married. They did this in the Jahiliyya and in Islam. So God made the term by which a man would know about his wife four months, and God revealed: ﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "li-lladhina ala min nisa'ihim" (in the past tense). Ibn 'Abbas recited: "li-lladhina yuqsimuna min nisa'ihim" (those who swear).

Al-Ila' means the oath. It is said: "ala yuli, ila'" (he swore). al-Khansa' said:
"So I swore to grieve over the dead, or to ask the wailing woman about her possessions" [Zad al-Masir: 4/204; Kitab al-'Ayn: 8/349; Lisan al-'Arab: 15/465].

Its noun is al-alya. A poet said:
"Upon me is an oath and fasting; its wing-keeper refuses to restrain itself"

It has four dialect forms: aliyya, alwa, lalwa and alwa. The meaning of the verse, "for those who swear off," is that they withdraw from their wives. The object is omitted, the context being sufficient to indicate it. Al-tarabbus means waiting and pausing. Some claimed it is inverted (from al-tarassud), saying: al-tarabbus means patience. For example, a man swears that he will not approach his wife, saying to her: "By God, I will not have intercourse with you," or "my bed will not join your bed," and similar expressions of intercourse. Whenever a man swears to his wife and thereby refrains from intercourse with her for more than four months without any impediment in his body or wealth, that is an ila'. What is less than four months is not an ila'.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) used to say: "Ila' is an oath made in anger; if one swears in a state of contentment, it is not an ila'." The majority of jurists apply it to deliberate oaths, and they make ila' binding on every oath that prevents intercourse, whether in contentment or anger. If he swears an ila', and then has intercourse before four months pass, he expiates his oath and there is nothing upon him. The nukul (the penalty for failing to fulfil) applies if he does not have intercourse until four months have passed. The jurists differed regarding this. Some said: when four months pass and he does not fulfil it, she is divorced from him by a single revocable divorce, and she is free to decide her own affairs. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad ibn Thabit, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Kalbi and Abu Hanifa. Ibn 'Abbas's statement supports it: "The resolute divorce is the completion of four months."

Others said: when four months pass and the man is still refraining, if the woman is chaste and does not demand her right to intercourse, there is nothing upon the man and no divorce occurs, and they remain married as they were. If she demands her right, the judge stops her husband, and he must either fulfil or divorce. If he refuses both the return (to marital relations) and divorce, the judge divorces him on his behalf. It is said: he keeps him in detention indefinitely until he divorces. The whole of this view that they mention, of the stopping, is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Abu al-Darda', Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayda, Ahmad, Ishaq and the majority of the people of hadith.

Yunus al-Sawwaf said: I came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He said: "From where?" I said: "From Kufa." He said: "They say about ila', when four months have passed, [there is nothing upon him], and not four years, until if he returns [he should divorce]," and he disregards intercourse. If he is incapable of intercourse because of illness, impotence or the like, he returns by his tongue and calls witnesses.

He also said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say: "He is held to his word in every case; if he returns, he owes expiation for his oath according to the jurists." Except al-Hasan, Ibrahim and Qatada, who dropped the expiation from the one who swore if he returns, based on His saying: ﴿But if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibrahim said: "This applies to the forfeiture of the right by it, not to the expiation."

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾, that is, they are determined and sincere and intend it. Ibn 'Abbas recited: "wa in 'azamu al-sirah," which is also divorce.

﴿Then indeed God is All-Hearing of their saying, All-Knowing of their intentions﴾. This indicates that she is not divorced after the four months pass unless her husband or the ruler divorces her, because the verse makes the resolve a condition, and because hearing implies [ ... ] [[Unreadable word in the manuscript.]]. The saying is what is heard, and the hearing relates to the divorce; and God knows best.

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾. The verse was revealed concerning the case of... Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Kalbi said: At the beginning of Islam, if a man divorced his wife three times while she was pregnant, he had more right to take her back as long as she had not given birth, until God abrogated that with His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that﴾, and so on. Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah al-Ghifari divorced his wife Qutayla while she was pregnant.

Muqatil said: It was Malik ibn al-Ashdaq, a man from al-Ta'if. They all said: the man was unaware of this, and she did not inform him of it.
