When he learned of her pregnancy, he took her back and returned her to his house. She gave birth and died, and her child died. Concerning this God revealed this verse: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those released from the bonds of their husbands. It derives from the saying: "I released the thing from my hand" (atlaqtu al-shay' min yadi) and "I let it loose" (talaqtuhu) when I let it go. However, because the two words were used so much, they distinguished between them, so that tatliq is restricted to wives; and the Qur'an was revealed in that manner: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. The noun from it is talaq. It is said: "al-rajul talaqa al-mar'a" and "tallaqat" and "taliqat," all together. Its origin is from the saying: "inṭalaqa al-rajul" when a man goes forth unrestrained. The course that a horse or other animal runs without being restrained is called talq.

﴿Wait by themselves﴾: they await, and do not remarry. ﴿Three periods﴾: plural of qar', like qar' (sg.) and its small plural quru' and large plurals aqra' and qara'. The jurists differed regarding the qurū'.

Some people said: they are menstruations. This is the view of 'Ali, 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and the position of Sufyan, Abu Hanifa and the people of Kufa. They argued by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the woman suffering istihada: "Leave off prayer during the days of your menses" [141] [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/220]. Prayer is left only during menstruation. A rajaz verse recited by Tha'lab, from Ibn al-A'rabi, says:
"He has periods like the periods of the menstruating woman" [We have not found it with these words; see Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 1/484; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/448; Gharib al-Hadith: 1/34].
It means that his enmity flares up at known times, just as a woman menstruates at known times. Whoever holds this view says: a woman is not lawful to husbands and does not exit her 'idda until the third menstruation is complete. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Ali said concerning a man who divorces his wife once or twice: the husband may not take her back until she has bathed from the third menstruation and prayer becomes lawful for her.

Others said: they are the periods of purity (tuhr), the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i and the people of Medina. They argued by the saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their 'idda﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when Ibn 'Umar divorced a woman while she was menstruating, to 'Umar: "Tell him to take her back; when she becomes pure, let him divorce or keep her." The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them [at their waiting period]﴾. So he (ﷺ) informed that the 'idda is the periods of purity from menstruation, and he recited: "fa-tallaquhunna li-'iddatihinna" (divorce them for their waiting period), which means that he divorces her while she is pure, because then she begins her 'idda; if he divorced her during menstruation, she would not begin her 'idda until after the menstruation. What indicates that the qurū' are the periods of purity is the statement of the poet, al-A'sha:
"And every year you undertake a raid, and the determination of your raids pulls its farthest reach,
Leaving wealth behind, and in the tribe there is elevation, for what was lost among them of the quru' of your women."
[Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 2/603; al-Sihah li-l-Jawhari: 1/64].
The qar' in this verse means the purity, because he went out on raids and did not approach his women, so their quru' (periods of purity) were lost. Whoever holds this view says: when a woman has her third menstruation, her 'idda is complete and she is lawful for marriage. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa and 'Amra, from 'A'isha, who said: "When the divorced woman enters the third menstruation, she has separated from her husband and is lawful for husbands." 'Amra said: 'A'isha used to say: "The qar' is the purity, not the menstruation." Ibn Shihab said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: "I did not meet any of our jurists except that he says this," meaning the saying of 'A'isha: "The periods (aqra') are the purities."

This disagreement arose because qar' in the lexicon is one of the words with opposite meanings, suitable for both meanings together. One says: "aqra'at al-mar'a" when she menstruated, and "aqra'at" when she became pure; she is "tuqri" (in the state of menstruation or purity). They differed regarding its root. Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubayda said: it is the time of a thing's arrival and departure. It is said: "raja'a fulan li-qari'ihi" (he returned at his appointed time), i.e., the time at which he returns; and "hadha qari' al-riyah" (this is the time of the winds' blowing) [Zad al-Masir: 1/232].
Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:
"I disliked the slaughter of the Bani Shulayl, when the winds blow at their appointed time."
That is, at its time. It is said: "aqra'at al-nujum" when the stars rose, and "aqra'at" when they set.
Kathir said:
"When the Pleiades have risen, and the sky perceives that they have set."
So qar' applies to both, because menstruation comes at a time and purity comes at a time. It is also said: it is from [qara' al-ma' fi al-hawd, meaning gathering it], as in the verse of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:
"Two forearms of a she-camel when the young one has been weaned, white-skinned and lean, that has not carried a foetus."
That is, she did not conceive, and her womb did not close over a child. The Arabs say: "ma qara'at al-naqa bi-la qurt," meaning the she-camel does not close her womb over an offspring. From this is their saying: "qara'tu al-Qur'an," meaning I pronounced it collected. This is the choice of al-Zajjaj. He said: "From it is qaraytu al-ma' fi al-miqra' (I gathered the water in the cistern)," leaving out the hamza, though the original form has the hamza. So qar' is the retention and gathering of blood, and it occurs both in purity and in menstruation together; but the preference is for purity, because it collects and retains the blood, while menstruation loosens and releases it; and God knows best.

Ruling of the verse

Know that its wording is a report but its meaning is a command, like His saying: ﴿And mothers shall suckle their children﴾ and similar. The 'idda is of two kinds: the 'idda of a divorced woman and the 'idda of a widow. The 'idda of a divorced woman is of three types: the 'idda of a menstruating woman is three quru'; the 'idda of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth; and the 'idda of a young girl who has not menstruated and an elderly woman who has despaired of menstruation is three months. The 'idda of a widow is of two kinds: if she is pregnant, her 'idda is until she gives birth; otherwise her 'idda is four months and ten days. The 'idda of slave women is half of that which applies to free women, and among the periods there are two quru'; there is no half-'idda for one who has not been consummated when her husband dies, so her 'idda is four months and ten days ...

﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. 'Ikrima and Ibrahim said: this means menstruation, that is, a woman observing her 'idda while the man wishes to take her back, and she says: "I have menstruated a third time." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and Muqatil said: it means pregnancy in the child. So the meaning of the verse is: it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, of menstruation and pregnancy, to nullify the husband's right of return and the child, for a woman is trusted regarding her private parts.

﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾, and ﴿their husbands﴾, that is, their spouses. It is the plural of ba'l, like fuhula, dhukura, hazula and khayyuta. It is said: "tab'ala al-mar'a" when a woman marries, and from this intercourse is called ba'al. The husband is called ba'l because he takes charge of his wife's affairs. The root of ba'l is master and owner. God said: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾ Muslim ibn Muharib read "wa-bu'ulatuhunna" with the t vowel-less due to the many vowels; the full-vowel form is more eloquent, better, more suitable and preferable.

﴿Have more right to take them back﴾, that is, to their return ﴿in that case﴾, that is, during the 'idda ﴿if they desire reconciliation, not harm﴾. This is because when a man wants to harm his wife, he divorces her once and leaves her until near the end of her 'idda, then takes her back, then leaves her for a time, then divorces her again and leaves her as he did the first time, then takes her back, leaves her for a time, then divorces her.

﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them﴾, that is, women have over their husbands a right similar to what they owe.

It is reported that the wife of Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of God, what is the right of a wife over her husband?" He said: "That he does not strike her face, that he does not disfigure her, that he feeds her what he eats, clothes her with what he wears, and does not abandon her." [142] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/100].

Al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives who own nothing for themselves." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594, hadith 1851.] "You took them under the trust of God, and made lawful their private parts by the word of God." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/73.]

From Maymuna, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best of men of my community are those best to their women, and the best of women of my community are those best to their husbands. For every woman among them there is recorded every day and night the reward of a thousand martyrs who were slain in the path of God, patient and seeking reward; and the excellence of one of them over the dark-eyed houris is like the excellence of Muhammad over the lowest man among you. The best women of my community are those who come to their husbands' pleasure in all that he desires, short of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic. The best men of my community are those who are gentle to their families as a mother is gentle to her child; there is recorded for every man among them, every day and night, the reward of a hundred martyrs slain in the path of God, seeking reward and patient."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of God, how can a woman have the reward of a thousand martyrs and a man the reward of a hundred martyrs?" He said: "Do you not know that the woman has greater reward and more excellent recompense than the man, and that God, the Mighty and Majestic, raises the man in Paradise to degrees above his degrees because of his wife's contentment with him in this world and her supplication for him? Do you not know that the greatest burden after associating partners with God is the woman who covers her husband [with ingratitude]?

Beware, fear God regarding the two weak ones, for God will ask you about them: the orphan and the woman. Whoever is kind to them has reached God and His good pleasure, and whoever wrongs them has deserved God's anger. The right of the husband over the wife is like my right over you. Whoever neglects my right has neglected the right of God, and whoever neglects the right of God has returned with the wrath of God, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination."[144]

﴿In kindness; and men have a degree over them﴾, in excellence.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it is] by what he gives her of dowry and what he spends on her of wealth. It is also said: by reason; it is said: by inheritance; it is said: by rank. Qatada said: by jihad.

From Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: While we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was among a group of his companions, a woman approached and stood over his head, then said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. I am the envoy of the women to you. There is no woman who [has heard of my departure] to you except that she is pleased with it. O Messenger of God, God is the Lord of men and the Lord of women; Adam is the father of men and the father of women; Eve is the mother of men and the mother of women. When men go out in the path of God and are slain, ﴿they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾. When they go out, they have authority over us as you know; we [are kept back] from them and serve them; do we have any share of reward?" He said: "Yes. Convey my greetings to the women and say to them: 'Obedience to the husband and acknowledgment of his right equals all that; but few of you do it.'" [145] [al-Musannaf li-'Abd al-Razzaq: 8/463].

Thabit reported from Anas, who said: They came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, the men have taken the excellence through jihad in the path of God; what deed is there for us after you that equals a deed in the path of God?"

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani reported from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked: "Is there jihad upon women?" He said: "Yes, their jihad is jealousy; they struggle against themselves. If they are patient, they are strivers, and if they are patient, they are garrisoned, and they have two rewards." [146] [We have not found it in the sources.]

It is also said: [the degree is] by divorce and return; it is said: by testimony; it is said: by the strength of worship. Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by leadership. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is ﴿and men have a degree over them﴾, that is, a virtue of right.

﴿And God is Mighty, Wise﴾.

﴿Divorce is twice﴾

Hisham ibn Urwa narrated from his father, from Aisha, that a woman came to her and complained that her husband divorced her and then took her back in order to harm her by it. In the Jahiliyya, when a man divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period (*'iddah*) ended, he was entitled to do so. Even if he divorced her a thousand times, there was no limit to divorce among them. Aisha mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then there was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, and so Allah set the limit of divorce at three.

As for the third divorce, the words of Allah the Exalted apply: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾.

It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Divorce is twice, so where is the third?" He said: ﴿Then either keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾.

The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is that the divorce in which the husband has the right of return is twice. ﴿Then keep her in kindness﴾ means he must keep her in kindness, that is, he takes her back during the third pronouncement. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾ means after it, and he should not harm her. If he divorces her once or twice, he has the greater right to take her back as long as she is within the waiting period. When the waiting period ends, she has the right to herself. It is permissible for him to remarry her by mutual consent through a new marriage contract. If he divorces her a third time, she is separated from him and has the right to herself apart from him, and she is not lawful to him ﴿until she marries another husband﴾.

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them﴾, meaning during the time of exchange and divorce, any of the gifts, bridal payments (*mahr*) or other things you have given them. Then He made an exception for *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), saying: ﴿Except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾.

This verse was revealed concerning Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. She hated him intensely, and he loved her intensely. There was a dispute between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said to her: "Return to your husband, for by Allah, I dislike that a woman should always be raising her hand to complain about her husband." So she returned to him a second time with marks of beating on her, and she complained to him again. He said to her: "Return to your husband." When she saw that her father would not take up her complaint, she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complained to him about her husband, and showed him marks of beating on her, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Thabit ibn Qays and said: "O Thabit, what is your situation with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, there is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah when he asked her, so she said: "He speaks the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I feared that he would destroy me. Release me from him, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I have given her a garden of mine, so tell her to return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "What do you say? Will you return to him his garden and have authority over your own affair?" She said: "Yes, and I do not want him." He said: "No, only the garden."

Then she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I never told you a statement today that would be revealed to you contrary tomorrow. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I hate him, so neither he nor I [can continue]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." He did so. This was the first *khul'* in Islam. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear [that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾, where "fear" means "know."

[Footnote 147 and its note in the original: the hadith is mentioned by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/186), and likewise by al-Tabari in Jami' al-Bayan (2/626) and Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba (8/81), but all of them in abridged form.]

This is supported by the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿except that they both suspect﴾. Muhajjan said:

*"So do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear that when I die I will not taste it."*

[Footnote: Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari, 2/625.]

That is, "I know." Abu Ja'far, Hamza and Ya'qub read *yukhafa* with a dammed *ya'* (i.e., ﴿except that they both be made to fear﴾), meaning that this knowledge comes from them, by analogy with the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿except that they fear﴾. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, because of Allah's words: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. He said: "He made the fear belong to others and did not say 'if both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.'" The fear here is that the woman fears temptation for herself and so disobeys Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him he will transgress against her. Allah forbade the man to take anything from a woman without her consent, except when the disobedience (*nushuz*) and bad conduct come from her. For example, she says: "By Allah, I will not fulfill any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor let you lie with me," and similar things. When she does that to him, it is permissible for him to punish her, if she brings this upon herself. It is disliked for him to take from her more than he gave her, but in legal judgment it is permissible.

This is clarified by what al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna narrated: a woman showed *nushuz* toward her husband during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) admonished her and commanded her to obey her husband, but she refused and said: "If you return me to him, by Allah I will kill myself." So he ordered her to be confined in the stable of the animals, in the house of the fodder, for three nights. Then he summoned her and said: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I have not spent nights more pleasing to my eye than these, and I have not found rest since I was with him except these nights." He said: "This, by your father, is *nushuz*." Then he said to her husband: "Separate from her, even if it be for her earrings. Separate from her for less than the ornament of her head-band, for there is no good for you in her." This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾.

Al-Farra' said: He meant by it the husband, not the wife, but He mentioned both together because they are a pair, like His words: ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, when only the young man of Moses forgot, not Moses (peace be upon him). And His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾, when they come only from the salt water and not the sweet. A poet said:

*"If you reproach me, O son of Affan, I will be reproached; and if you call me, I will protect a defended honor."*

[Footnote: al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, 3/868; the verse is by Suwayd ibn Kura'.]

Others said its meaning is: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them﴾ together. There is no blame upon the woman for *nushuz* if she fears destruction and disobedience, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives of wealth, because she is prohibited from squandering wealth without right. Nor is there blame upon the man for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly, according to her wish.

The jurists have two opinions on *khul'*:

The first: it is a dissolution of the marriage without a divorce (*faskh*). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, and the view of al-Shafi'i in his old school in Iraq, from which he later retracted in Egypt.

The second: *khul'* is a single irrevocable divorce, unless the husband intends more than that. This is the view of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), and the new view of al-Shafi'i.

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, meaning do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 226–229 (part 1 of 2):

لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months﴾.

Qatada said: Ila' (oath of abstention) was the divorce of the people of the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: That was among the harms of the people of the Jahiliyya. A man would not desire a woman, nor would he like her to marry another; he would swear that he would never approach her, and he would leave her in that state, neither unmarried nor married. They did this in the Jahiliyya and in Islam. So God made the term by which a man would know about his wife four months, and God revealed: ﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "li-lladhina ala min nisa'ihim" (in the past tense). Ibn 'Abbas recited: "li-lladhina yuqsimuna min nisa'ihim" (those who swear).

Al-Ila' means the oath. It is said: "ala yuli, ila'" (he swore). al-Khansa' said:
"So I swore to grieve over the dead, or to ask the wailing woman about her possessions" [Zad al-Masir: 4/204; Kitab al-'Ayn: 8/349; Lisan al-'Arab: 15/465].

Its noun is al-alya. A poet said:
"Upon me is an oath and fasting; its wing-keeper refuses to restrain itself"

It has four dialect forms: aliyya, alwa, lalwa and alwa. The meaning of the verse, "for those who swear off," is that they withdraw from their wives. The object is omitted, the context being sufficient to indicate it. Al-tarabbus means waiting and pausing. Some claimed it is inverted (from al-tarassud), saying: al-tarabbus means patience. For example, a man swears that he will not approach his wife, saying to her: "By God, I will not have intercourse with you," or "my bed will not join your bed," and similar expressions of intercourse. Whenever a man swears to his wife and thereby refrains from intercourse with her for more than four months without any impediment in his body or wealth, that is an ila'. What is less than four months is not an ila'.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) used to say: "Ila' is an oath made in anger; if one swears in a state of contentment, it is not an ila'." The majority of jurists apply it to deliberate oaths, and they make ila' binding on every oath that prevents intercourse, whether in contentment or anger. If he swears an ila', and then has intercourse before four months pass, he expiates his oath and there is nothing upon him. The nukul (the penalty for failing to fulfil) applies if he does not have intercourse until four months have passed. The jurists differed regarding this. Some said: when four months pass and he does not fulfil it, she is divorced from him by a single revocable divorce, and she is free to decide her own affairs. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad ibn Thabit, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Kalbi and Abu Hanifa. Ibn 'Abbas's statement supports it: "The resolute divorce is the completion of four months."

Others said: when four months pass and the man is still refraining, if the woman is chaste and does not demand her right to intercourse, there is nothing upon the man and no divorce occurs, and they remain married as they were. If she demands her right, the judge stops her husband, and he must either fulfil or divorce. If he refuses both the return (to marital relations) and divorce, the judge divorces him on his behalf. It is said: he keeps him in detention indefinitely until he divorces. The whole of this view that they mention, of the stopping, is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Abu al-Darda', Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayda, Ahmad, Ishaq and the majority of the people of hadith.

Yunus al-Sawwaf said: I came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He said: "From where?" I said: "From Kufa." He said: "They say about ila', when four months have passed, [there is nothing upon him], and not four years, until if he returns [he should divorce]," and he disregards intercourse. If he is incapable of intercourse because of illness, impotence or the like, he returns by his tongue and calls witnesses.

He also said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say: "He is held to his word in every case; if he returns, he owes expiation for his oath according to the jurists." Except al-Hasan, Ibrahim and Qatada, who dropped the expiation from the one who swore if he returns, based on His saying: ﴿But if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibrahim said: "This applies to the forfeiture of the right by it, not to the expiation."

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾, that is, they are determined and sincere and intend it. Ibn 'Abbas recited: "wa in 'azamu al-sirah," which is also divorce.

﴿Then indeed God is All-Hearing of their saying, All-Knowing of their intentions﴾. This indicates that she is not divorced after the four months pass unless her husband or the ruler divorces her, because the verse makes the resolve a condition, and because hearing implies [ ... ] [[Unreadable word in the manuscript.]]. The saying is what is heard, and the hearing relates to the divorce; and God knows best.

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾. The verse was revealed concerning the case of... Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Kalbi said: At the beginning of Islam, if a man divorced his wife three times while she was pregnant, he had more right to take her back as long as she had not given birth, until God abrogated that with His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that﴾, and so on. Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah al-Ghifari divorced his wife Qutayla while she was pregnant.

Muqatil said: It was Malik ibn al-Ashdaq, a man from al-Ta'if. They all said: the man was unaware of this, and she did not inform him of it. When he learned of her pregnancy, he took her back and returned her to his house. She gave birth and died, and her child died. Concerning this God revealed this verse: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those released from the bonds of their husbands. It derives from the saying: "I released the thing from my hand" (atlaqtu al-shay' min yadi) and "I let it loose" (talaqtuhu) when I let it go. However, because the two words were used so much, they distinguished between them, so that tatliq is restricted to wives; and the Qur'an was revealed in that manner: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. The noun from it is talaq. It is said: "al-rajul talaqa al-mar'a" and "tallaqat" and "taliqat," all together. Its origin is from the saying: "inṭalaqa al-rajul" when a man goes forth unrestrained. The course that a horse or other animal runs without being restrained is called talq.

﴿Wait by themselves﴾: they await, and do not remarry. ﴿Three periods﴾: plural of qar', like qar' (sg.) and its small plural quru' and large plurals aqra' and qara'. The jurists differed regarding the qurū'.

Some people said: they are menstruations. This is the view of 'Ali, 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and the position of Sufyan, Abu Hanifa and the people of Kufa. They argued by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the woman suffering istihada: "Leave off prayer during the days of your menses" [141] [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/220]. Prayer is left only during menstruation. A rajaz verse recited by Tha'lab, from Ibn al-A'rabi, says:
"He has periods like the periods of the menstruating woman" [We have not found it with these words; see Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 1/484; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/448; Gharib al-Hadith: 1/34].
It means that his enmity flares up at known times, just as a woman menstruates at known times. Whoever holds this view says: a woman is not lawful to husbands and does not exit her 'idda until the third menstruation is complete. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Ali said concerning a man who divorces his wife once or twice: the husband may not take her back until she has bathed from the third menstruation and prayer becomes lawful for her.

Others said: they are the periods of purity (tuhr), the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i and the people of Medina. They argued by the saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their 'idda﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when Ibn 'Umar divorced a woman while she was menstruating, to 'Umar: "Tell him to take her back; when she becomes pure, let him divorce or keep her." The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them [at their waiting period]﴾. So he (ﷺ) informed that the 'idda is the periods of purity from menstruation, and he recited: "fa-tallaquhunna li-'iddatihinna" (divorce them for their waiting period), which means that he divorces her while she is pure, because then she begins her 'idda; if he divorced her during menstruation, she would not begin her 'idda until after the menstruation. What indicates that the qurū' are the periods of purity is the statement of the poet, al-A'sha:
"And every year you undertake a raid, and the determination of your raids pulls its farthest reach,
Leaving wealth behind, and in the tribe there is elevation, for what was lost among them of the quru' of your women."
[Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 2/603; al-Sihah li-l-Jawhari: 1/64].
The qar' in this verse means the purity, because he went out on raids and did not approach his women, so their quru' (periods of purity) were lost. Whoever holds this view says: when a woman has her third menstruation, her 'idda is complete and she is lawful for marriage. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa and 'Amra, from 'A'isha, who said: "When the divorced woman enters the third menstruation, she has separated from her husband and is lawful for husbands." 'Amra said: 'A'isha used to say: "The qar' is the purity, not the menstruation." Ibn Shihab said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: "I did not meet any of our jurists except that he says this," meaning the saying of 'A'isha: "The periods (aqra') are the purities."

This disagreement arose because qar' in the lexicon is one of the words with opposite meanings, suitable for both meanings together. One says: "aqra'at al-mar'a" when she menstruated, and "aqra'at" when she became pure; she is "tuqri" (in the state of menstruation or purity). They differed regarding its root. Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubayda said: it is the time of a thing's arrival and departure. It is said: "raja'a fulan li-qari'ihi" (he returned at his appointed time), i.e., the time at which he returns; and "hadha qari' al-riyah" (this is the time of the winds' blowing) [Zad al-Masir: 1/232].
Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:
"I disliked the slaughter of the Bani Shulayl, when the winds blow at their appointed time."
That is, at its time. It is said: "aqra'at al-nujum" when the stars rose, and "aqra'at" when they set.
Kathir said:
"When the Pleiades have risen, and the sky perceives that they have set."
So qar' applies to both, because menstruation comes at a time and purity comes at a time. It is also said: it is from [qara' al-ma' fi al-hawd, meaning gathering it], as in the verse of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:
"Two forearms of a she-camel when the young one has been weaned, white-skinned and lean, that has not carried a foetus."
That is, she did not conceive, and her womb did not close over a child. The Arabs say: "ma qara'at al-naqa bi-la qurt," meaning the she-camel does not close her womb over an offspring. From this is their saying: "qara'tu al-Qur'an," meaning I pronounced it collected. This is the choice of al-Zajjaj. He said: "From it is qaraytu al-ma' fi al-miqra' (I gathered the water in the cistern)," leaving out the hamza, though the original form has the hamza. So qar' is the retention and gathering of blood, and it occurs both in purity and in menstruation together; but the preference is for purity, because it collects and retains the blood, while menstruation loosens and releases it; and God knows best.

Ruling of the verse

Know that its wording is a report but its meaning is a command, like His saying: ﴿And mothers shall suckle their children﴾ and similar. The 'idda is of two kinds: the 'idda of a divorced woman and the 'idda of a widow. The 'idda of a divorced woman is of three types: the 'idda of a menstruating woman is three quru'; the 'idda of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth; and the 'idda of a young girl who has not menstruated and an elderly woman who has despaired of menstruation is three months. The 'idda of a widow is of two kinds: if she is pregnant, her 'idda is until she gives birth; otherwise her 'idda is four months and ten days. The 'idda of slave women is half of that which applies to free women, and among the periods there are two quru'; there is no half-'idda for one who has not been consummated when her husband dies, so her 'idda is four months and ten days ...

﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. 'Ikrima and Ibrahim said: this means menstruation, that is, a woman observing her 'idda while the man wishes to take her back, and she says: "I have menstruated a third time." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and Muqatil said: it means pregnancy in the child. So the meaning of the verse is: it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, of menstruation and pregnancy, to nullify the husband's right of return and the child, for a woman is trusted regarding her private parts.

﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾, and ﴿their husbands﴾, that is, their spouses. It is the plural of ba'l, like fuhula, dhukura, hazula and khayyuta. It is said: "tab'ala al-mar'a" when a woman marries, and from this intercourse is called ba'al. The husband is called ba'l because he takes charge of his wife's affairs. The root of ba'l is master and owner. God said: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾ Muslim ibn Muharib read "wa-bu'ulatuhunna" with the t vowel-less due to the many vowels; the full-vowel form is more eloquent, better, more suitable and preferable.

﴿Have more right to take them back﴾, that is, to their return ﴿in that case﴾, that is, during the 'idda ﴿if they desire reconciliation, not harm﴾. This is because when a man wants to harm his wife, he divorces her once and leaves her until near the end of her 'idda, then takes her back, then leaves her for a time, then divorces her again and leaves her as he did the first time, then takes her back, leaves her for a time, then divorces her.

﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them﴾, that is, women have over their husbands a right similar to what they owe.

It is reported that the wife of Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of God, what is the right of a wife over her husband?" He said: "That he does not strike her face, that he does not disfigure her, that he feeds her what he eats, clothes her with what he wears, and does not abandon her." [142] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/100].

Al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives who own nothing for themselves." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594, hadith 1851.] "You took them under the trust of God, and made lawful their private parts by the word of God." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/73.]

From Maymuna, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best of men of my community are those best to their women, and the best of women of my community are those best to their husbands. For every woman among them there is recorded every day and night the reward of a thousand martyrs who were slain in the path of God, patient and seeking reward; and the excellence of one of them over the dark-eyed houris is like the excellence of Muhammad over the lowest man among you. The best women of my community are those who come to their husbands' pleasure in all that he desires, short of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic. The best men of my community are those who are gentle to their families as a mother is gentle to her child; there is recorded for every man among them, every day and night, the reward of a hundred martyrs slain in the path of God, seeking reward and patient."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of God, how can a woman have the reward of a thousand martyrs and a man the reward of a hundred martyrs?" He said: "Do you not know that the woman has greater reward and more excellent recompense than the man, and that God, the Mighty and Majestic, raises the man in Paradise to degrees above his degrees because of his wife's contentment with him in this world and her supplication for him? Do you not know that the greatest burden after associating partners with God is the woman who covers her husband [with ingratitude]?

Beware, fear God regarding the two weak ones, for God will ask you about them: the orphan and the woman. Whoever is kind to them has reached God and His good pleasure, and whoever wrongs them has deserved God's anger. The right of the husband over the wife is like my right over you. Whoever neglects my right has neglected the right of God, and whoever neglects the right of God has returned with the wrath of God, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination."[144]

﴿In kindness; and men have a degree over them﴾, in excellence.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it is] by what he gives her of dowry and what he spends on her of wealth. It is also said: by reason; it is said: by inheritance; it is said: by rank. Qatada said: by jihad.

From Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: While we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was among a group of his companions, a woman approached and stood over his head, then said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. I am the envoy of the women to you. There is no woman who [has heard of my departure] to you except that she is pleased with it. O Messenger of God, God is the Lord of men and the Lord of women; Adam is the father of men and the father of women; Eve is the mother of men and the mother of women. When men go out in the path of God and are slain, ﴿they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾. When they go out, they have authority over us as you know; we [are kept back] from them and serve them; do we have any share of reward?" He said: "Yes. Convey my greetings to the women and say to them: 'Obedience to the husband and acknowledgment of his right equals all that; but few of you do it.'" [145] [al-Musannaf li-'Abd al-Razzaq: 8/463].

Thabit reported from Anas, who said: They came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, the men have taken the excellence through jihad in the path of God; what deed is there for us after you that equals a deed in the path of God?"

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani reported from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked: "Is there jihad upon women?" He said: "Yes, their jihad is jealousy; they struggle against themselves. If they are patient, they are strivers, and if they are patient, they are garrisoned, and they have two rewards." [146] [We have not found it in the sources.]

It is also said: [the degree is] by divorce and return; it is said: by testimony; it is said: by the strength of worship. Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by leadership. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is ﴿and men have a degree over them﴾, that is, a virtue of right.

﴿And God is Mighty, Wise﴾.

﴿Divorce is twice﴾

Hisham ibn Urwa narrated from his father, from Aisha, that a woman came to her and complained that her husband divorced her and then took her back in order to harm her by it. In the Jahiliyya, when a man divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period (*'iddah*) ended, he was entitled to do so. Even if he divorced her a thousand times, there was no limit to divorce among them. Aisha mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then there was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, and so Allah set the limit of divorce at three.

As for the third divorce, the words of Allah the Exalted apply: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾.

It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Divorce is twice, so where is the third?" He said: ﴿Then either keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾.

The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is that the divorce in which the husband has the right of return is twice. ﴿Then keep her in kindness﴾ means he must keep her in kindness, that is, he takes her back during the third pronouncement. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾ means after it, and he should not harm her. If he divorces her once or twice, he has the greater right to take her back as long as she is within the waiting period. When the waiting period ends, she has the right to herself. It is permissible for him to remarry her by mutual consent through a new marriage contract. If he divorces her a third time, she is separated from him and has the right to herself apart from him, and she is not lawful to him ﴿until she marries another husband﴾.

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them﴾, meaning during the time of exchange and divorce, any of the gifts, bridal payments (*mahr*) or other things you have given them. Then He made an exception for *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), saying: ﴿Except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾.

This verse was revealed concerning Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. She hated him intensely, and he loved her intensely. There was a dispute between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said to her: "Return to your husband, for by Allah, I dislike that a woman should always be raising her hand to complain about her husband." So she returned to him a second time with marks of beating on her, and she complained to him again. He said to her: "Return to your husband." When she saw that her father would not take up her complaint, she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complained to him about her husband, and showed him marks of beating on her, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Thabit ibn Qays and said: "O Thabit, what is your situation with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, there is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah when he asked her, so she said: "He speaks the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I feared that he would destroy me. Release me from him, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I have given her a garden of mine, so tell her to return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "What do you say? Will you return to him his garden and have authority over your own affair?" She said: "Yes, and I do not want him." He said: "No, only the garden."

Then she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I never told you a statement today that would be revealed to you contrary tomorrow. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I hate him, so neither he nor I [can continue]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." He did so. This was the first *khul'* in Islam. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear [that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾, where "fear" means "know."

[Footnote 147 and its note in the original: the hadith is mentioned by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/186), and likewise by al-Tabari in Jami' al-Bayan (2/626) and Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba (8/81), but all of them in abridged form.]

This is supported by the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿except that they both suspect﴾. Muhajjan said:

*"So do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear that when I die I will not taste it."*

[Footnote: Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari, 2/625.]

That is, "I know." Abu Ja'far, Hamza and Ya'qub read *yukhafa* with a dammed *ya'* (i.e., ﴿except that they both be made to fear﴾), meaning that this knowledge comes from them, by analogy with the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿except that they fear﴾. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, because of Allah's words: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. He said: "He made the fear belong to others and did not say 'if both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.'" The fear here is that the woman fears temptation for herself and so disobeys Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him he will transgress against her. Allah forbade the man to take anything from a woman without her consent, except when the disobedience (*nushuz*) and bad conduct come from her. For example, she says: "By Allah, I will not fulfill any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor let you lie with me," and similar things. When she does that to him, it is permissible for him to punish her, if she brings this upon herself. It is disliked for him to take from her more than he gave her, but in legal judgment it is permissible.

This is clarified by what al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna narrated: a woman showed *nushuz* toward her husband during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) admonished her and commanded her to obey her husband, but she refused and said: "If you return me to him, by Allah I will kill myself." So he ordered her to be confined in the stable of the animals, in the house of the fodder, for three nights. Then he summoned her and said: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I have not spent nights more pleasing to my eye than these, and I have not found rest since I was with him except these nights." He said: "This, by your father, is *nushuz*." Then he said to her husband: "Separate from her, even if it be for her earrings. Separate from her for less than the ornament of her head-band, for there is no good for you in her." This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾.

Al-Farra' said: He meant by it the husband, not the wife, but He mentioned both together because they are a pair, like His words: ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, when only the young man of Moses forgot, not Moses (peace be upon him). And His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾, when they come only from the salt water and not the sweet. A poet said:

*"If you reproach me, O son of Affan, I will be reproached; and if you call me, I will protect a defended honor."*

[Footnote: al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, 3/868; the verse is by Suwayd ibn Kura'.]

Others said its meaning is: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them﴾ together. There is no blame upon the woman for *nushuz* if she fears destruction and disobedience, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives of wealth, because she is prohibited from squandering wealth without right. Nor is there blame upon the man for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly, according to her wish.

The jurists have two opinions on *khul'*:

The first: it is a dissolution of the marriage without a divorce (*faskh*). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, and the view of al-Shafi'i in his old school in Iraq, from which he later retracted in Egypt.

The second: *khul'* is a single irrevocable divorce, unless the husband intends more than that. This is the view of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), and the new view of al-Shafi'i.

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, meaning do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 226–229 (part 1 of 2):

لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months﴾.

Qatada said: Ila' (oath of abstention) was the divorce of the people of the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period).

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: That was among the harms of the people of the Jahiliyya. A man would not desire a woman, nor would he like her to marry another; he would swear that he would never approach her, and he would leave her in that state, neither unmarried nor married. They did this in the Jahiliyya and in Islam. So God made the term by which a man would know about his wife four months, and God revealed: ﴿For those who swear off their wives﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "li-lladhina ala min nisa'ihim" (in the past tense). Ibn 'Abbas recited: "li-lladhina yuqsimuna min nisa'ihim" (those who swear).

Al-Ila' means the oath. It is said: "ala yuli, ila'" (he swore). al-Khansa' said:
"So I swore to grieve over the dead, or to ask the wailing woman about her possessions" [Zad al-Masir: 4/204; Kitab al-'Ayn: 8/349; Lisan al-'Arab: 15/465].

Its noun is al-alya. A poet said:
"Upon me is an oath and fasting; its wing-keeper refuses to restrain itself"

It has four dialect forms: aliyya, alwa, lalwa and alwa. The meaning of the verse, "for those who swear off," is that they withdraw from their wives. The object is omitted, the context being sufficient to indicate it. Al-tarabbus means waiting and pausing. Some claimed it is inverted (from al-tarassud), saying: al-tarabbus means patience. For example, a man swears that he will not approach his wife, saying to her: "By God, I will not have intercourse with you," or "my bed will not join your bed," and similar expressions of intercourse. Whenever a man swears to his wife and thereby refrains from intercourse with her for more than four months without any impediment in his body or wealth, that is an ila'. What is less than four months is not an ila'.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) used to say: "Ila' is an oath made in anger; if one swears in a state of contentment, it is not an ila'." The majority of jurists apply it to deliberate oaths, and they make ila' binding on every oath that prevents intercourse, whether in contentment or anger. If he swears an ila', and then has intercourse before four months pass, he expiates his oath and there is nothing upon him. The nukul (the penalty for failing to fulfil) applies if he does not have intercourse until four months have passed. The jurists differed regarding this. Some said: when four months pass and he does not fulfil it, she is divorced from him by a single revocable divorce, and she is free to decide her own affairs. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Muhammad ibn Thabit, Qatada, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, al-Kalbi and Abu Hanifa. Ibn 'Abbas's statement supports it: "The resolute divorce is the completion of four months."

Others said: when four months pass and the man is still refraining, if the woman is chaste and does not demand her right to intercourse, there is nothing upon the man and no divorce occurs, and they remain married as they were. If she demands her right, the judge stops her husband, and he must either fulfil or divorce. If he refuses both the return (to marital relations) and divorce, the judge divorces him on his behalf. It is said: he keeps him in detention indefinitely until he divorces. The whole of this view that they mention, of the stopping, is the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Abu al-Darda', Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sulayman ibn Yasar and Mujahid, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Abu 'Ubayda, Ahmad, Ishaq and the majority of the people of hadith.

Yunus al-Sawwaf said: I came to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He said: "From where?" I said: "From Kufa." He said: "They say about ila', when four months have passed, [there is nothing upon him], and not four years, until if he returns [he should divorce]," and he disregards intercourse. If he is incapable of intercourse because of illness, impotence or the like, he returns by his tongue and calls witnesses.

He also said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say: "He is held to his word in every case; if he returns, he owes expiation for his oath according to the jurists." Except al-Hasan, Ibrahim and Qatada, who dropped the expiation from the one who swore if he returns, based on His saying: ﴿But if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibrahim said: "This applies to the forfeiture of the right by it, not to the expiation."

﴿And if they resolve on divorce﴾, that is, they are determined and sincere and intend it. Ibn 'Abbas recited: "wa in 'azamu al-sirah," which is also divorce.

﴿Then indeed God is All-Hearing of their saying, All-Knowing of their intentions﴾. This indicates that she is not divorced after the four months pass unless her husband or the ruler divorces her, because the verse makes the resolve a condition, and because hearing implies [ ... ] [[Unreadable word in the manuscript.]]. The saying is what is heard, and the hearing relates to the divorce; and God knows best.

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾. The verse was revealed concerning the case of... Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Kalbi said: At the beginning of Islam, if a man divorced his wife three times while she was pregnant, he had more right to take her back as long as she had not given birth, until God abrogated that with His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ and His saying: ﴿And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that﴾, and so on. Isma'il ibn 'Abdullah al-Ghifari divorced his wife Qutayla while she was pregnant.

Muqatil said: It was Malik ibn al-Ashdaq, a man from al-Ta'if. They all said: the man was unaware of this, and she did not inform him of it. When he learned of her pregnancy, he took her back and returned her to his house. She gave birth and died, and her child died. Concerning this God revealed this verse: ﴿And divorced women﴾, that is, those released from the bonds of their husbands. It derives from the saying: "I released the thing from my hand" (atlaqtu al-shay' min yadi) and "I let it loose" (talaqtuhu) when I let it go. However, because the two words were used so much, they distinguished between them, so that tatliq is restricted to wives; and the Qur'an was revealed in that manner: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. The noun from it is talaq. It is said: "al-rajul talaqa al-mar'a" and "tallaqat" and "taliqat," all together. Its origin is from the saying: "inṭalaqa al-rajul" when a man goes forth unrestrained. The course that a horse or other animal runs without being restrained is called talq.

﴿Wait by themselves﴾: they await, and do not remarry. ﴿Three periods﴾: plural of qar', like qar' (sg.) and its small plural quru' and large plurals aqra' and qara'. The jurists differed regarding the qurū'.

Some people said: they are menstruations. This is the view of 'Ali, 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and the position of Sufyan, Abu Hanifa and the people of Kufa. They argued by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) to the woman suffering istihada: "Leave off prayer during the days of your menses" [141] [Sunan al-Daraqutni: 1/220]. Prayer is left only during menstruation. A rajaz verse recited by Tha'lab, from Ibn al-A'rabi, says:
"He has periods like the periods of the menstruating woman" [We have not found it with these words; see Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 1/484; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 1/448; Gharib al-Hadith: 1/34].
It means that his enmity flares up at known times, just as a woman menstruates at known times. Whoever holds this view says: a woman is not lawful to husbands and does not exit her 'idda until the third menstruation is complete. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from Ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Ali said concerning a man who divorces his wife once or twice: the husband may not take her back until she has bathed from the third menstruation and prayer becomes lawful for her.

Others said: they are the periods of purity (tuhr), the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn 'Umar, 'A'isha, and the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i and the people of Medina. They argued by the saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their 'idda﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when Ibn 'Umar divorced a woman while she was menstruating, to 'Umar: "Tell him to take her back; when she becomes pure, let him divorce or keep her." The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you divorce women, divorce them [at their waiting period]﴾. So he (ﷺ) informed that the 'idda is the periods of purity from menstruation, and he recited: "fa-tallaquhunna li-'iddatihinna" (divorce them for their waiting period), which means that he divorces her while she is pure, because then she begins her 'idda; if he divorced her during menstruation, she would not begin her 'idda until after the menstruation. What indicates that the qurū' are the periods of purity is the statement of the poet, al-A'sha:
"And every year you undertake a raid, and the determination of your raids pulls its farthest reach,
Leaving wealth behind, and in the tribe there is elevation, for what was lost among them of the quru' of your women."
[Jami' al-Bayan al-Tabari: 2/603; al-Sihah li-l-Jawhari: 1/64].
The qar' in this verse means the purity, because he went out on raids and did not approach his women, so their quru' (periods of purity) were lost. Whoever holds this view says: when a woman has her third menstruation, her 'idda is complete and she is lawful for marriage. Evidence for this is what al-Zuhri narrated from 'Urwa and 'Amra, from 'A'isha, who said: "When the divorced woman enters the third menstruation, she has separated from her husband and is lawful for husbands." 'Amra said: 'A'isha used to say: "The qar' is the purity, not the menstruation." Ibn Shihab said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman say: "I did not meet any of our jurists except that he says this," meaning the saying of 'A'isha: "The periods (aqra') are the purities."

This disagreement arose because qar' in the lexicon is one of the words with opposite meanings, suitable for both meanings together. One says: "aqra'at al-mar'a" when she menstruated, and "aqra'at" when she became pure; she is "tuqri" (in the state of menstruation or purity). They differed regarding its root. Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubayda said: it is the time of a thing's arrival and departure. It is said: "raja'a fulan li-qari'ihi" (he returned at his appointed time), i.e., the time at which he returns; and "hadha qari' al-riyah" (this is the time of the winds' blowing) [Zad al-Masir: 1/232].
Malik ibn al-Harith al-Hudhali said:
"I disliked the slaughter of the Bani Shulayl, when the winds blow at their appointed time."
That is, at its time. It is said: "aqra'at al-nujum" when the stars rose, and "aqra'at" when they set.
Kathir said:
"When the Pleiades have risen, and the sky perceives that they have set."
So qar' applies to both, because menstruation comes at a time and purity comes at a time. It is also said: it is from [qara' al-ma' fi al-hawd, meaning gathering it], as in the verse of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:
"Two forearms of a she-camel when the young one has been weaned, white-skinned and lean, that has not carried a foetus."
That is, she did not conceive, and her womb did not close over a child. The Arabs say: "ma qara'at al-naqa bi-la qurt," meaning the she-camel does not close her womb over an offspring. From this is their saying: "qara'tu al-Qur'an," meaning I pronounced it collected. This is the choice of al-Zajjaj. He said: "From it is qaraytu al-ma' fi al-miqra' (I gathered the water in the cistern)," leaving out the hamza, though the original form has the hamza. So qar' is the retention and gathering of blood, and it occurs both in purity and in menstruation together; but the preference is for purity, because it collects and retains the blood, while menstruation loosens and releases it; and God knows best.

Ruling of the verse

Know that its wording is a report but its meaning is a command, like His saying: ﴿And mothers shall suckle their children﴾ and similar. The 'idda is of two kinds: the 'idda of a divorced woman and the 'idda of a widow. The 'idda of a divorced woman is of three types: the 'idda of a menstruating woman is three quru'; the 'idda of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth; and the 'idda of a young girl who has not menstruated and an elderly woman who has despaired of menstruation is three months. The 'idda of a widow is of two kinds: if she is pregnant, her 'idda is until she gives birth; otherwise her 'idda is four months and ten days. The 'idda of slave women is half of that which applies to free women, and among the periods there are two quru'; there is no half-'idda for one who has not been consummated when her husband dies, so her 'idda is four months and ten days ...

﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾. 'Ikrima and Ibrahim said: this means menstruation, that is, a woman observing her 'idda while the man wishes to take her back, and she says: "I have menstruated a third time." Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and Muqatil said: it means pregnancy in the child. So the meaning of the verse is: it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, of menstruation and pregnancy, to nullify the husband's right of return and the child, for a woman is trusted regarding her private parts.

﴿If they believe in God and the Last Day﴾, and ﴿their husbands﴾, that is, their spouses. It is the plural of ba'l, like fuhula, dhukura, hazula and khayyuta. It is said: "tab'ala al-mar'a" when a woman marries, and from this intercourse is called ba'al. The husband is called ba'l because he takes charge of his wife's affairs. The root of ba'l is master and owner. God said: ﴿Do you call upon Ba'l?﴾ Muslim ibn Muharib read "wa-bu'ulatuhunna" with the t vowel-less due to the many vowels; the full-vowel form is more eloquent, better, more suitable and preferable.

﴿Have more right to take them back﴾, that is, to their return ﴿in that case﴾, that is, during the 'idda ﴿if they desire reconciliation, not harm﴾. This is because when a man wants to harm his wife, he divorces her once and leaves her until near the end of her 'idda, then takes her back, then leaves her for a time, then divorces her again and leaves her as he did the first time, then takes her back, leaves her for a time, then divorces her.

﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them﴾, that is, women have over their husbands a right similar to what they owe.

It is reported that the wife of Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of God, what is the right of a wife over her husband?" He said: "That he does not strike her face, that he does not disfigure her, that he feeds her what he eats, clothes her with what he wears, and does not abandon her." [142] [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/100].

Al-Mubarak ibn Fudala narrated from al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Treat women well, for they are with you as captives who own nothing for themselves." [Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/594, hadith 1851.] "You took them under the trust of God, and made lawful their private parts by the word of God." [143] [Musnad Ahmad: 5/73.]

From Maymuna, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), she said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The best of men of my community are those best to their women, and the best of women of my community are those best to their husbands. For every woman among them there is recorded every day and night the reward of a thousand martyrs who were slain in the path of God, patient and seeking reward; and the excellence of one of them over the dark-eyed houris is like the excellence of Muhammad over the lowest man among you. The best women of my community are those who come to their husbands' pleasure in all that he desires, short of disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic. The best men of my community are those who are gentle to their families as a mother is gentle to her child; there is recorded for every man among them, every day and night, the reward of a hundred martyrs slain in the path of God, seeking reward and patient."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of God, how can a woman have the reward of a thousand martyrs and a man the reward of a hundred martyrs?" He said: "Do you not know that the woman has greater reward and more excellent recompense than the man, and that God, the Mighty and Majestic, raises the man in Paradise to degrees above his degrees because of his wife's contentment with him in this world and her supplication for him? Do you not know that the greatest burden after associating partners with God is the woman who covers her husband [with ingratitude]?

Beware, fear God regarding the two weak ones, for God will ask you about them: the orphan and the woman. Whoever is kind to them has reached God and His good pleasure, and whoever wrongs them has deserved God's anger. The right of the husband over the wife is like my right over you. Whoever neglects my right has neglected the right of God, and whoever neglects the right of God has returned with the wrath of God, and his abode is Hell, and wretched is the destination."[144]

﴿In kindness; and men have a degree over them﴾, in excellence.

Ibn 'Abbas said: [it is] by what he gives her of dowry and what he spends on her of wealth. It is also said: by reason; it is said: by inheritance; it is said: by rank. Qatada said: by jihad.

From Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: While we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who was among a group of his companions, a woman approached and stood over his head, then said: "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. I am the envoy of the women to you. There is no woman who [has heard of my departure] to you except that she is pleased with it. O Messenger of God, God is the Lord of men and the Lord of women; Adam is the father of men and the father of women; Eve is the mother of men and the mother of women. When men go out in the path of God and are slain, ﴿they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision﴾. When they go out, they have authority over us as you know; we [are kept back] from them and serve them; do we have any share of reward?" He said: "Yes. Convey my greetings to the women and say to them: 'Obedience to the husband and acknowledgment of his right equals all that; but few of you do it.'" [145] [al-Musannaf li-'Abd al-Razzaq: 8/463].

Thabit reported from Anas, who said: They came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, the men have taken the excellence through jihad in the path of God; what deed is there for us after you that equals a deed in the path of God?"

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani reported from 'Imran ibn Husayn, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked: "Is there jihad upon women?" He said: "Yes, their jihad is jealousy; they struggle against themselves. If they are patient, they are strivers, and if they are patient, they are garrisoned, and they have two rewards." [146] [We have not found it in the sources.]

It is also said: [the degree is] by divorce and return; it is said: by testimony; it is said: by the strength of worship. Sufyan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by leadership. Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is ﴿and men have a degree over them﴾, that is, a virtue of right.

﴿And God is Mighty, Wise﴾.

﴿Divorce is twice﴾

Hisham ibn Urwa narrated from his father, from Aisha, that a woman came to her and complained that her husband divorced her and then took her back in order to harm her by it. In the Jahiliyya, when a man divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period (*'iddah*) ended, he was entitled to do so. Even if he divorced her a thousand times, there was no limit to divorce among them. Aisha mentioned this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then there was revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, and so Allah set the limit of divorce at three.

As for the third divorce, the words of Allah the Exalted apply: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾.

It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Divorce is twice, so where is the third?" He said: ﴿Then either keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾.

The exegetes said: the meaning of the verse is that the divorce in which the husband has the right of return is twice. ﴿Then keep her in kindness﴾ means he must keep her in kindness, that is, he takes her back during the third pronouncement. ﴿Or release her with good treatment﴾ means after it, and he should not harm her. If he divorces her once or twice, he has the greater right to take her back as long as she is within the waiting period. When the waiting period ends, she has the right to herself. It is permissible for him to remarry her by mutual consent through a new marriage contract. If he divorces her a third time, she is separated from him and has the right to herself apart from him, and she is not lawful to him ﴿until she marries another husband﴾.

﴿And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them﴾, meaning during the time of exchange and divorce, any of the gifts, bridal payments (*mahr*) or other things you have given them. Then He made an exception for *khul'* (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation), saying: ﴿Except when both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾.

This verse was revealed concerning Jamila bint Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was married to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. She hated him intensely, and he loved her intensely. There was a dispute between them, so she went to her father and complained to him about her husband, saying: "He mistreats me and beats me." He said to her: "Return to your husband, for by Allah, I dislike that a woman should always be raising her hand to complain about her husband." So she returned to him a second time with marks of beating on her, and she complained to him again. He said to her: "Return to your husband." When she saw that her father would not take up her complaint, she went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), complained to him about her husband, and showed him marks of beating on her, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, neither I nor he [can continue]."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Thabit ibn Qays and said: "O Thabit, what is your situation with your wife?" He said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, there is nothing on the face of the earth more beloved to me than her, except you." He said to her: "What do you say?" She disliked to lie to the Messenger of Allah when he asked her, so she said: "He speaks the truth, O Messenger of Allah, but I feared that he would destroy me. Release me from him, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I have given her a garden of mine, so tell her to return it to me, and I will release her." He said to her: "What do you say? Will you return to him his garden and have authority over your own affair?" She said: "Yes, and I do not want him." He said: "No, only the garden."

Then she said: "O Messenger of Allah, I never told you a statement today that would be revealed to you contrary tomorrow. He is among the most generous of people in his love for his wife, but I hate him, so neither he nor I [can continue]." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O Thabit, take back from her what you gave her and release her." He did so. This was the first *khul'* in Islam. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when both fear [that they will not keep within the limits of Allah]﴾, where "fear" means "know."

[Footnote 147 and its note in the original: the hadith is mentioned by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (6/186), and likewise by al-Tabari in Jami' al-Bayan (2/626) and Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba (8/81), but all of them in abridged form.]

This is supported by the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿except that they both suspect﴾. Muhajjan said:

*"So do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear that when I die I will not taste it."*

[Footnote: Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari, 2/625.]

That is, "I know." Abu Ja'far, Hamza and Ya'qub read *yukhafa* with a dammed *ya'* (i.e., ﴿except that they both be made to fear﴾), meaning that this knowledge comes from them, by analogy with the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿except that they fear﴾. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading, because of Allah's words: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. He said: "He made the fear belong to others and did not say 'if both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.'" The fear here is that the woman fears temptation for herself and so disobeys Allah regarding her husband's rights, and the husband fears that if his wife does not obey him he will transgress against her. Allah forbade the man to take anything from a woman without her consent, except when the disobedience (*nushuz*) and bad conduct come from her. For example, she says: "By Allah, I will not fulfill any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor let you lie with me," and similar things. When she does that to him, it is permissible for him to punish her, if she brings this upon herself. It is disliked for him to take from her more than he gave her, but in legal judgment it is permissible.

This is clarified by what al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna narrated: a woman showed *nushuz* toward her husband during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) admonished her and commanded her to obey her husband, but she refused and said: "If you return me to him, by Allah I will kill myself." So he ordered her to be confined in the stable of the animals, in the house of the fodder, for three nights. Then he summoned her and said: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I have not spent nights more pleasing to my eye than these, and I have not found rest since I was with him except these nights." He said: "This, by your father, is *nushuz*." Then he said to her husband: "Separate from her, even if it be for her earrings. Separate from her for less than the ornament of her head-band, for there is no good for you in her." This is the meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾.

Al-Farra' said: He meant by it the husband, not the wife, but He mentioned both together because they are a pair, like His words: ﴿They forgot their fish﴾, when only the young man of Moses forgot, not Moses (peace be upon him). And His words: ﴿From both of them come out pearls and coral﴾, when they come only from the salt water and not the sweet. A poet said:

*"If you reproach me, O son of Affan, I will be reproached; and if you call me, I will protect a defended honor."*

[Footnote: al-Sihah of al-Jawhari, 3/868; the verse is by Suwayd ibn Kura'.]

Others said its meaning is: ﴿So there is no blame upon either of them﴾ together. There is no blame upon the woman for *nushuz* if she fears destruction and disobedience, nor for what she ransoms herself with and gives of wealth, because she is prohibited from squandering wealth without right. Nor is there blame upon the man for what he takes from her of wealth if she gives it willingly, according to her wish.

The jurists have two opinions on *khul'*:

The first: it is a dissolution of the marriage without a divorce (*faskh*). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, and the view of al-Shafi'i in his old school in Iraq, from which he later retracted in Egypt.

The second: *khul'* is a single irrevocable divorce, unless the husband intends more than that. This is the view of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), and the new view of al-Shafi'i.

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: these are the commands and prohibitions of Allah. ﴿So do not transgress them﴾, meaning do not go beyond them. ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 230–232:

Then if he divorces her (meaning, a third time), she is not lawful to him after that (meaning, after the third pronouncement of divorce), and "after" is in the accusative as a terminal limit, "until she marries another husband" (zawjan ghayrahu), i.e. other than the one who divorced her, so that he has intercourse with her. The word nikah (marriage) encompasses both the contract and the sexual intercourse together.

This verse was revealed concerning Tamima, and it has been said: 'A'isha bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Atik al-Qurazi. She was married to Rifa'a ibn Wahb ibn 'Atik al-Qurazi, who was her cousin, and he divorced her three times. Then she married 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr, and with him was nothing but like the fringe of a garment. She said: He divorced me before he had touched me, so shall I return to my first husband, my cousin? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "Do you want to return to Rifa'a? No, not until you taste his honey (sweetness) and he tastes yours."

He said: Abu Bakr was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ), and Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As was sitting at the door of the chamber, and Khalid began calling out: "O Abu Bakr, will you not restrain this woman from what she is saying in the presence of the Messenger of Allah?"
