Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Zuhri and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: its highest is a servant, its middle is three garments: a shirt, a head-covering and a cloak, and a waist-wrap, and below that is maintenance, and below that clothing, and some silver. This is the school of al-Shafiʿi, who said: its highest is a servant for the wealthy, its middle is a garment, and its least is the least of what he possesses, its value. al-Hasan said: thirty dirhams. Shurayh provided five hundred dirhams. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf provided Umm Abi Salama, when he divorced her, a black slave girl.

al-Hasan ibn ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) provided a wife of his with ten thousand dirhams, and she said: "A small provision from a beloved who parts."

Abu Hanifa said: her provision, when husband and wife disagree about it, is the amount of half of her equivalent dowry, and it does not exceed that. The correct view is that what is obligatory of it depends on the husband's hardship and ease, as He, exalted, said. If the consideration were the dowry, He would have said: "Provide for them according to their measure and the measure of their equivalent dowry." When He said "according to the wealthy his measure and according to the straitened his measure," that shows that what is considered is the husband's condition, not the woman's. Ibn Abi Za'ida related from Subayh ibn Salih, who said: ʿAmir was asked: "How much does a man provide for his wife?" He said: "According to the measure of his wealth."

Detailed ruling of the verse

Whoever marries a woman without a named dowry, the marriage is valid. If she demands a fixed dowry, we instruct him to fix one for her. If he does not fix one for her and consummates with her, she has the equivalent dowry (mahr mithl). If he divorces her before consummation, she has the provision and no dowry. If he dies leaving her after consummation, she has the equivalent dowry. If he dies leaving her before consummation and before naming, there are two opinions:

One: she has the equivalent dowry. This is the view of the people of Iraq, and the proof is the hadith of Barwa' bint Washiq al-Ashja'iyya, when her husband died, he had not fixed for her and had not consummated with her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided with the dowry of her women, neither less nor excessive, and she observes the ʿiddah and has the inheritance.
[[Musnad Ahmad: 4/280.]]

The second opinion: she has the inheritance and observes the ʿiddah, and has no dowry, but only the provision, as if he had divorced her before consummation and naming. This is the view of ʿAli, and he used to say concerning the hadith of Barwa': "The word of a Bedouin from Ashja' is not accepted against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 235–237 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them (consummated the marriage)...﴾ This verse concerns a man who marries a woman and has already specified a bridal gift (sadaq) for her, then divorces her before he has touched her. She is due half of the bridal gift, and nothing more, and she has no waiting period ('idda). If he has not gone in to her and dies, there is no disagreement that she is due the full bridal gift and inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period. Here "touching" (al-mass) means intercourse (al-jima').

Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if a man is alone with a woman and does not have intercourse with her until he separates from her, the full bridal gift is binding on him, and the waiting period is binding on her, based on the report of Ibn Mas'ud: "The rightly-guided caliphs ruled concerning a man who closed a door and let down a curtain that she is due the bridal gift and must observe the waiting period." As for al-Shafi'i, he does not impose the full bridal gift or a waiting period, since there was no consummation according to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Shurayh said: "I have not heard God Most High mention in His Book a door or a curtain. He only said that if he has not touched her, she is due half the bridal gift." This is also the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

This verse abrogates (nasikh) the verse in Surah al-Ahzab: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women...﴾ up to His words ﴿then give them provision﴾. Previously she had the provision (mata'). When this verse was revealed, it abrogated what preceded it and made obligatory for the divorced woman, whose bridal gift was specified before touching, half of her specified bridal gift, and she has no provision, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾ (i.e., have intercourse with them).

﴿and you have already specified for them an obligation﴾ (i.e., you have made the bridal gift obligatory for them and specified a bridal gift for them). The root of fard is "cutting off," and from it is said of the notch of a balance or a bow: fardah; and of a portion: farida, because one cuts it off from the thing. ﴿then half of what you have specified﴾ means half of the bridal gift due. al-Sulami read fanisfun with a damma on the nun wherever it occurs; both are dialects.

Then He said: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, meaning the women. The position of ya'fun is in the accusative by [the particle] illa an, since the feminine plural in the present tense is the same in the nominative, accusative and jussive, and always takes the nun: you say hunna yadribna, and lan yadribna, and lam yadribna, because if the nun were dropped it would be confused with the masculine.

﴿or that he forgoes﴾: al-Hasan read it with a sukun on the waw, as if he found the fatha on the waw heavy, just as the damma on it was found heavy. ﴿He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾: the scholars differed concerning it. Some said: it is the guardian (wali), and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, i.e., they give up and leave the half, so that they do not demand it from their husbands if they are previously married, mature, rational, and have authority over their affairs; ﴿or he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾, who is her guardian, so that he leaves that half if she is a virgin or does not have authority over her affairs, and his forgoing is permissible for her even if she dislikes it. If the woman forgoes and the guardian refuses, the forgoing is permissible; if the guardian forgoes and the woman refuses, the forgoing is permissible provided she does not intend harm. This is the view of [Ali] and the companions of Abdullah, Ibrahim, 'Ata', al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Zayd, Rabi'a al-Ra'y, and a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn al-Hasan.

Ma'mar narrated from Ibn Tawus from his father, and from Isma'il ibn Shirwas, who both said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the guardian. 'Ikrima said: God Most High permitted him (He) to forgo, approved of it, and commanded it; so whichever woman forgoes, her forgoing is valid even if she is stingy and withholds, and whoever among her guardians forgoes, his forgoing is valid. This is the position of the jurists of the Hijaz, except that they said: the guardian's forgoing for a virgin is valid, but if she is previously married, his forgoing on her is not valid.

Others said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband, and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless the women forgo﴾, so they take nothing of the bridal gift, or ﴿the husband forgoes﴾, so he gives her the full bridal gift. This is the view of Ali, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Nafi', al-Rabi', Qatada, Ibn Hibban, al-Dahhak, and a narration of 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar from Ibn 'Abbas. This is the position of the people of Iraq, who see no way for the guardian over any part of her bridal gift without her permission, whether she is previously married or a virgin. They said: because all agree that if a woman's guardian released her husband from her bridal gift before divorce, that is not permitted; so likewise his release and forgoing after divorce is not permitted. And because they also agree that if her guardian gave her husband a single dirham of her property after separation, he would be sinful unless he had the right to do so, and that gift would be void, and the bridal gift is property of hers; so the ruling must be like the ruling on her release of her property. And because they agree that some guardians may not forgo on her behalf, by consensus, and these are the sons of brothers and the sons of paternal uncles; and what God distinguishes [some] in the verse.

From Isa ibn 'Asim, who said: I heard Shurayh narrate: 'Ali asked me about "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage." I said: the woman's guardian. He said: No, rather the husband. It is narrated that a man married his sister, and her husband divorced her before consummating the marriage, so her brother forgave the bridal gift, and Shurayh approved it. Then he said: "I forgive on behalf of the women of Banu Murra." Amir said: "No, by God, Shurayh has never issued a worse judgment, nor a more foolish one, than to permit the brother's forgiveness." He said: after Shurayh, he returned from his view and said: it is the husband.

From al-Qasim, who said: the elders of Kufa would come to Shurayh and dispute with him over his statement "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage," until he fell to his knees, and Shurayh would say: "It is the husband, it is the husband."

Shu'ba narrated from Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they said: it is the husband. Tawus and Mujahid said: it is the guardian. I spoke with them about it, and they returned from their view and followed Sa'id, saying: it is the husband.

Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated as a mursal report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage is the husband; he forgives and gives the full bridal gift."

From Salih ibn Kaysan: Jubayr ibn Mut'im married a woman, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, and completed the bridal gift for her, and said: "I have more right to forgiveness." He interpreted His words "or that he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" as meaning, on this interpretation, that "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband himself in every case, before and after divorce. Then, when the alif and lam were introduced, the pronoun was dropped, as in His words ﴿for the Garden is the refuge (al-ma'wa)﴾, meaning his refuge. And al-Nabigha said:

"They have a disposition which God has not given to any others among mankind, and their dreams are not disordered."

meaning "and their dreams." Likewise His words "the tie of marriage" mean the tie of his marriage.

﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety﴾. Sibawayh said: its position is nominative as the subject, i.e., "and forgoing is nearer to piety and more binding," with ila meaning "to," i.e., "to piety." The address here is to men and women, because when the masculine and feminine are combined, the masculine prevails. The meaning is: your forgoing of some of it is nearer to piety, because this forgoing is recommended; and when one hastens to it and does it, it is known that what is obligatory is more firmly practised, and what is prohibited is more firmly avoided. al-Sha'bi read "wa an ya'fu" with the ya', making it a predicate of "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage."

﴿And do not forget graciousness among yourselves﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Dawud and al-Nakha'i read "wa la tanasaw al-fadl" with the form of mufa'ala between two parties, like His words ﴿and do not call one another by nicknames﴾. Yahya ibn Ya'mur read "wa la tansawi al-fadl" with a kasra on the waw, and the rest read "wa la tansaw al-fadl" with a damma on the waw. The meaning of al-fadl is the man's completing the bridal gift or the woman's giving up of the half. God Most High urged both the husband and the wife toward graciousness and kindness, and commanded both of them to hasten to forgoing.

﴿Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 235–237 (part 1 of 2):

"And there is no blame upon you, O men, for what you hint at of proposing to the women in waiting (ʿiddah), and the root of taʿrīd (hinting, allusion) is to suggest something indirectly." The poet said:
"As one who writes Hebrew script with his right hand, in Taymāʾ, ink-marked, then lines up the rows [of writing]."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 3/1087; the verse was recited by al-Aṣmaʿi and attributed to al-Shammākh.]]

Taʿrīd in speech is that indirect allusion of speech by which the listener understands the meaning without explicit statement. Its root is from ʿarḍ al-shay', meaning its side; it is said: "He struck with it the side of the wall," as if he circles around it without making it manifest. The taʿrīd of proposal mentioned in this verse, according to what has come in the tafsir, is that he says to her while she is in her ʿiddah:
"Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are righteous, indeed you are beneficial, indeed I have resolved to marry, indeed I am desirous of you, indeed I am eager for you, and perhaps Allah will bring good to you, and if Allah brings us together in what is lawful, I would be pleased, and if I marry you I will give you and treat you well," and similar speech, without saying to her: "Marry me."

Ibrahim said: "There is no harm in his sending her a gift and attending to her affairs during her ʿiddah, if she is one of his concerns."

Ibn ʿAwf related from Muhammad, from ʿUbaydah, concerning this verse, that he said: "He says to her guardian, 'Let no one precede me to her.'" Mujahid said: "A man said to a woman at the funeral of her husband: 'Do not precede me with yourself.' She said: 'You have already preceded me.'"

Ibn al-Mubarak related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, from his maternal aunt, that Sukayna bint Handhala said: "Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli entered upon me while I was in my ʿiddah and said: 'O daughter of Handhala, you know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the right of my grandfather over me and his precedence in Islam.' She said: 'May Allah forgive you, Abu Jaʿfar! Do you propose to me during my ʿiddah while you are taken as a source of knowledge?' He said: 'Or did I actually do that? I only sought your favour by my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and my standing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm Salama, who had been married to her cousin Abu Salama, and when her husband died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued mentioning to her his station with Allah while he was leaning on his hand, until the mat left its mark on his hand from the intensity of his leaning on it. That was not a proposal.'"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/705.]]

Ibn Yazid said concerning this verse: "My father used to say: Everything that falls short of resolving the bond of marriage is zina." Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at of proposing to women," and khitbah (proposal) is a request for marriage, the verbal noun of your saying: "The man proposed to the woman, khatabahā khiṭbatan and khuṭbā."

Some people said: it is on the pattern of jilsah (sitting), qiʿdah (sitting), and rukbah (riding), and the meaning of their saying "So-and-so proposed to so-and-so" is: he asked her for a proposal regarding what was in her mind, that is, her needs and her affair, from their saying "What is your khaṭb?" i.e., your need and your affair. Allah said: "What is your affair, O Samiri?" [Q 20:95]

Al-Akhfash said: al-khuṭbah is mention, and al-khuṭbah is the gathering, so the meaning is: "in what you hint at, of those among whom you propose to women, in their presence." "Or you conceal within yourselves," i.e., you keep secret and hide in your souls, regarding their proposal and their marriage. It is said: "kanantu al-shay' and akannantuhu" are two dialects. Thaʿlab said: "akannat al-shay'" means I concealed it in my soul, and "kannatuhu" means I covered it. Al-Suddi said: it is that he enters and makes himself known to them as he wishes, without speaking anything.

"Allah knows that you will mention them in your hearts." Al-Hasan said: meaning the proposal. "But do not promise them secretly" [or: "do not make a pledge with them"] — some of them said: it is zina. A man would enter upon a woman for the sake of suspicion, while hinting at marriage, and say to her: "Leave me; when you complete your ʿiddah I will reveal my marriage to you." So Allah, exalted, forbade that. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibrahim, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ibn Abi Mujliz, al-Dahhak, al-Rabiʿ and ʿAtaʾ, and it is the narration of ʿAtiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas. What proves it is the saying of al-Aʿsha:

"Do not approach a neighbour's woman, for her secret is forbidden to you, [so marry her or remain forever]."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/625.]]

And al-Hutay'a said:
"He forbids the secret of their neighbour to them, and their neighbour eats the nose of the dishes."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/625.]]

Mujahid said: it is the man's saying to the woman: "Do not let yourself escape me, for I will marry you." Al-Shaʿbi and al-Suddi said: he does not take her pledge that she will not marry anyone else. ʿIkrima said: he does not propose to her during her ʿiddah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: he does not bargain with her for such and such amount of wealth on condition that she does not marry anyone else. All these interpretations are close in meaning, and the "secret" in these sayings is marriage. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Did not Bisasa claim today that I have grown old, and that those like me cannot do well with the secret?"
[[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/238; Lisan al-ʿArab: 15/259.]]

Al-Aʿsha said:
"They did not seek her secret for wealth, and they did not leave her for her asceticism."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 2/481.]]

That is, her marriage. Al-Kalbi said: "But do not promise them secretly" means: do not describe yourselves to them by frequent intercourse, so that he says to her, "I will come to you four or five times," and similar things. According to this view, the "secret" is intercourse itself. Al-Farazdaq said:

"Withholding the secrets except from their own people, and failing what the jealous, wasted lover supposed."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 4/1383.]]

He means that they are chaste in their hands from intercourse except with their husbands. Ru'ba said:

"He abstained from their secrets after the dusk, and did not place her between a rubbing and a passion."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 4/358.]]

He means he refrained from having relations with her after he had been bound to that.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "But do not promise them secretly" means: do not marry them secretly, then keep her until she is released, and then reveal it. The root of sirr is what you conceal in yourself, and marriage, adultery and intercourse are called sirr only because they occur between a man and a woman in secrecy. It is also said that the private part is called sirr because it is not made apparent. Thaʿlab related from Ibn al-Aʿrabi:

"When she saw my secret changed and bent, from beyond [its] desire, her secret when it turned away."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 4/358; attributed to al-Afwah al-Awdi, where it reads: "When she saw my secret change and turn, from beyond the desire of its ... when it turned away."]]

Then He excepted, saying: "Except that you say a fair word." It was said: a good promise. Mujahid said: it is allusion without explicit declaration or disclosure. The "an" [in "an taqūlū"] is in the place of an accusative, as a substitute for "secret." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: all of this is abrogated by His saying: "And do not resolve the bond of marriage," meaning do not validate the bond of marriage. Ibn al-Zajjaj said: "Do not resolve upon the bond of marriage," as it is said: "He struck the hand of purity and blessing." ʿAntara said:

"I have spent nights hungry, and its shade covered me, until I attain by it the generous feast."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 11/419; where it reads "generous food."]]

That is, and its shade was over me.

"Until the Book reaches its term" — until the ʿiddah ends. He called it "Book" because it is an obligation from Allah, exalted, like His saying: "Fasting is prescribed for you."

"And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him," i.e., fear Allah. "And know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing," who does not hasten to punishment. The Arabs say: "Place the howdah upon the most patient of the camels."

"There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them, [or] fixed for them an obligation," the verse.

It was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who married a woman from the Banu Hanifa, did not name a dowry for her, then divorced her before touching her. Allah revealed this verse, and when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Provide for her, even if it is with your cap." So this is His saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them," i.e., have not had intercourse with them.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "tamāssūhunna" with an alif, in the form of mufā'alah, because the body of each of them touches the body of the other, so both touch one another; its proof is His saying: "before they touch one another." The rest read "tamassūhunna" without alif, because the coming together is only from the action of the man; its proof is His saying: "No human has touched me."

"Or fix for them an obligation" — i.e., establish for them a dowry. It is said: "The ruler assigned for so-and-so," meaning he recorded for him a charity in the register. If it is asked: what is the reason for negating blame regarding one who divorces, and would there be blame on the man if he divorced after consummation, so that it is removed from him before consummation? It is answered:

It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "What is the matter with people who play with the limits of Allah, saying: 'I have divorced you, I have taken you back'?"
[[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/650, no. 2017.]]

And he ﷺ said: "Do not divorce your wives except because of suspicion, for Allah does not love those who taste [much] or the women who taste [much]."
[[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/335.]]

And he peace be upon him said: "The most detested of lawful things to Allah is divorce."
[[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/650, no. 2018.]]

And he peace be upon him said: "Indeed Allah detests every frequent divorcer who tastes [many]."
[[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 4/172, with variation.]]

When the Messenger said this, they thought they would sin by doing so, so Allah, exalted, informed them that there is no blame in divorcing women when it is done in the commendable manner, since separation is sometimes better than retention. It was also said: the meaning of His saying "There is no blame upon you" is that there is no way for the women against you if you divorce them, while you have not touched them and you have not fixed for them an obligation of dowry or maintenance.

It was also said: the meaning is "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them," at whatever time you wish, since there is no prescribed sunnah in their divorce. So a man may divorce them when he has not touched them, whether she is menstruating or pure, and at any time he likes. This is not the case for one who has been consummated with, because it is not permitted for her husband to divorce her if she is one of those with menstrual cycles, except in a ʿiddah, clearly, in a purity during which he has not had intercourse with her. If he divorces her while she is menstruating, or past the age [of menstruation], the divorce takes effect.

"And provide for them," i.e., furnish them and give them from your wealth what they may enjoy. Al-mutʿah and al-matāʿ are what one is provided with as provision. "According to the wealthy" (al-mūsiʿ), i.e., the rich, "his measure" (qadaruhu), "and according to the straitened" (al-muqtir), the poor, "his measure," i.e., his capacity and his ability. Abu Jaʿfar, Hafs, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Ibn Dhakwan read the dāl in both with a fatḥah, and Abu ʿUbayda chose it, saying: because of its grandeur in both. The others read the dāl in both with a sukūn, and Abu Hatim chose it. Both are dialects; he said: the Qur'an was recited with both. The confirmation of the fatḥah is His saying: "So the valleys flowed according to their measure" [Q 13:17], and the confirmation of the sukūn is His saying: "They did not measure Allah with His true measure" [Q 6:91]. The Arabs say: "al-qaḍāʾ and al-qadar." Abu Yazid al-Ansari said: "al-qaḍāʾ and al-qadr" with a sukūn on the dāl. The poet, al-Farazdaq, said:

"My sand was not poured into the iron of Mujashi', along with the decree, except for a need of mine that I wanted."

Some said: qadar (with fatḥah) is the verbal noun, and qadr (with sukūn) is the noun. "Matāʿan" is in the accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., "provide for them a provision." It may be accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, because matāʿ is indefinite and qadr is definite. "According to what is fair" (bil-maʿrūf), i.e., what Allah has commanded you, without injustice or procrastination. "Ḥaqqan" is in the accusative by way of reporting, its meaning: "I inform you of it as a truth." It was also said that it is in the accusative as a qualifier.

Ruling of the verse

The commentators said: it was said that this concerns a man who marries a woman and does not name a dowry for her, then divorces her before touching her; she has the mutʿah and no fixed dowry, by consensus of the scholars. They differed regarding the provision for a divorced woman in other than this case. Some said: every divorced woman has a provision, whoever she is and in whatever manner the divorce occurred. The provision is obligatory, to be paid from the divorcer's wealth as all other debts obligatory upon him are paid, whether he consummated with her or not, whether a dowry was fixed or not, provided the divorce came from him. As for when the separation comes from her, she has neither provision nor dowry. This is the view of al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-ʿAliya and Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: because of His saying:

"And for divorced women is provision according to what is fair, a duty upon the righteous." So He made the provision obligatory for all divorced women and did not distinguish. The meaning of the verse on this view is: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them, whether you have fixed for them an obligation or not," because every wife is either one for whom a dowry is named or one for whom none is named. From what they transmitted of His saying "or fix for them an obligation," we know that what is meant by "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women" is those for whom an obligation has been fixed, and those for whom none was fixed, for there is no sense in saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them or fixed for them an obligation," and then saying: "And provide for them," meaning all of them.

Others said: the provision is obligatory for every divorced woman except the one for whom an obligation was fixed when she is divorced before consummation; for her there is no provision, but she has half of the named dowry. This is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, Nafiʿ, ʿAtaʾ and Mujahid, and the school of al-Shafiʿi. The meaning of the verse on this view is: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them and have not fixed for them an obligation." The alif is extra, like His saying "or they increase" [Q 37:147] and similar. Then He commanded provision for them.

It is also possible that His saying "And provide for them" refers to divorced women for whom no obligation was fixed before touching, and not to those for whom it was fixed. Then His following saying "And if you divorce them before you touch them" is specific to that. The beginning of the verse follows the apparent generality for those for whom an obligation was fixed and those for whom none was fixed, while in "And provide for them" it is specific to those for whom none was fixed, in accordance with the following verse.

Al-Zuhri said: there are two kinds of provision, one of which the ruler adjudicates and the other he does not adjudicate, but it is binding upon him between himself and Allah. As for the one the ruler adjudicates, it is for one who divorced before a dowry was fixed and before consummation; he is compelled to pay the provision, which is His saying: "a duty upon the doers of good." The provision that is binding between him and Allah, which the ruler does not adjudicate, is for one who divorces after consummation and after a dowry was fixed, which is His saying: "a duty upon the righteous."

Others said: none of that is obligatory; rather, provision is a kindness, and the command to it is a command of recommendation and encouragement, not a command of obligation and requirement. This is the view of Abu Hanifa. Ibn Sirin related that a man divorced a woman after consummation, and she brought a case against him before Shurayh regarding the provision. Shurayh said: "It is not the case that you must be among the doers of good, nor that you must be among the righteous," and he did not compel him to it.

They differed regarding the amount and extent of the provision. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Zuhri and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: its highest is a servant, its middle is three garments: a shirt, a head-covering and a cloak, and a waist-wrap, and below that is maintenance, and below that clothing, and some silver. This is the school of al-Shafiʿi, who said: its highest is a servant for the wealthy, its middle is a garment, and its least is the least of what he possesses, its value. al-Hasan said: thirty dirhams. Shurayh provided five hundred dirhams. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf provided Umm Abi Salama, when he divorced her, a black slave girl.

al-Hasan ibn ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) provided a wife of his with ten thousand dirhams, and she said: "A small provision from a beloved who parts."

Abu Hanifa said: her provision, when husband and wife disagree about it, is the amount of half of her equivalent dowry, and it does not exceed that. The correct view is that what is obligatory of it depends on the husband's hardship and ease, as He, exalted, said. If the consideration were the dowry, He would have said: "Provide for them according to their measure and the measure of their equivalent dowry." When He said "according to the wealthy his measure and according to the straitened his measure," that shows that what is considered is the husband's condition, not the woman's. Ibn Abi Za'ida related from Subayh ibn Salih, who said: ʿAmir was asked: "How much does a man provide for his wife?" He said: "According to the measure of his wealth."

Detailed ruling of the verse

Whoever marries a woman without a named dowry, the marriage is valid. If she demands a fixed dowry, we instruct him to fix one for her. If he does not fix one for her and consummates with her, she has the equivalent dowry (mahr mithl). If he divorces her before consummation, she has the provision and no dowry. If he dies leaving her after consummation, she has the equivalent dowry. If he dies leaving her before consummation and before naming, there are two opinions:

One: she has the equivalent dowry. This is the view of the people of Iraq, and the proof is the hadith of Barwa' bint Washiq al-Ashja'iyya, when her husband died, he had not fixed for her and had not consummated with her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided with the dowry of her women, neither less nor excessive, and she observes the ʿiddah and has the inheritance.
[[Musnad Ahmad: 4/280.]]

The second opinion: she has the inheritance and observes the ʿiddah, and has no dowry, but only the provision, as if he had divorced her before consummation and naming. This is the view of ʿAli, and he used to say concerning the hadith of Barwa': "The word of a Bedouin from Ashja' is not accepted against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 235–237 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them (consummated the marriage)...﴾ This verse concerns a man who marries a woman and has already specified a bridal gift (sadaq) for her, then divorces her before he has touched her. She is due half of the bridal gift, and nothing more, and she has no waiting period ('idda). If he has not gone in to her and dies, there is no disagreement that she is due the full bridal gift and inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period. Here "touching" (al-mass) means intercourse (al-jima').

Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if a man is alone with a woman and does not have intercourse with her until he separates from her, the full bridal gift is binding on him, and the waiting period is binding on her, based on the report of Ibn Mas'ud: "The rightly-guided caliphs ruled concerning a man who closed a door and let down a curtain that she is due the bridal gift and must observe the waiting period." As for al-Shafi'i, he does not impose the full bridal gift or a waiting period, since there was no consummation according to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Shurayh said: "I have not heard God Most High mention in His Book a door or a curtain. He only said that if he has not touched her, she is due half the bridal gift." This is also the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

This verse abrogates (nasikh) the verse in Surah al-Ahzab: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women...﴾ up to His words ﴿then give them provision﴾. Previously she had the provision (mata'). When this verse was revealed, it abrogated what preceded it and made obligatory for the divorced woman, whose bridal gift was specified before touching, half of her specified bridal gift, and she has no provision, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾ (i.e., have intercourse with them).

﴿and you have already specified for them an obligation﴾ (i.e., you have made the bridal gift obligatory for them and specified a bridal gift for them). The root of fard is "cutting off," and from it is said of the notch of a balance or a bow: fardah; and of a portion: farida, because one cuts it off from the thing. ﴿then half of what you have specified﴾ means half of the bridal gift due. al-Sulami read fanisfun with a damma on the nun wherever it occurs; both are dialects.

Then He said: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, meaning the women. The position of ya'fun is in the accusative by [the particle] illa an, since the feminine plural in the present tense is the same in the nominative, accusative and jussive, and always takes the nun: you say hunna yadribna, and lan yadribna, and lam yadribna, because if the nun were dropped it would be confused with the masculine.

﴿or that he forgoes﴾: al-Hasan read it with a sukun on the waw, as if he found the fatha on the waw heavy, just as the damma on it was found heavy. ﴿He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾: the scholars differed concerning it. Some said: it is the guardian (wali), and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, i.e., they give up and leave the half, so that they do not demand it from their husbands if they are previously married, mature, rational, and have authority over their affairs; ﴿or he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾, who is her guardian, so that he leaves that half if she is a virgin or does not have authority over her affairs, and his forgoing is permissible for her even if she dislikes it. If the woman forgoes and the guardian refuses, the forgoing is permissible; if the guardian forgoes and the woman refuses, the forgoing is permissible provided she does not intend harm. This is the view of [Ali] and the companions of Abdullah, Ibrahim, 'Ata', al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Zayd, Rabi'a al-Ra'y, and a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn al-Hasan.

Ma'mar narrated from Ibn Tawus from his father, and from Isma'il ibn Shirwas, who both said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the guardian. 'Ikrima said: God Most High permitted him (He) to forgo, approved of it, and commanded it; so whichever woman forgoes, her forgoing is valid even if she is stingy and withholds, and whoever among her guardians forgoes, his forgoing is valid. This is the position of the jurists of the Hijaz, except that they said: the guardian's forgoing for a virgin is valid, but if she is previously married, his forgoing on her is not valid.

Others said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband, and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless the women forgo﴾, so they take nothing of the bridal gift, or ﴿the husband forgoes﴾, so he gives her the full bridal gift. This is the view of Ali, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Nafi', al-Rabi', Qatada, Ibn Hibban, al-Dahhak, and a narration of 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar from Ibn 'Abbas. This is the position of the people of Iraq, who see no way for the guardian over any part of her bridal gift without her permission, whether she is previously married or a virgin. They said: because all agree that if a woman's guardian released her husband from her bridal gift before divorce, that is not permitted; so likewise his release and forgoing after divorce is not permitted. And because they also agree that if her guardian gave her husband a single dirham of her property after separation, he would be sinful unless he had the right to do so, and that gift would be void, and the bridal gift is property of hers; so the ruling must be like the ruling on her release of her property. And because they agree that some guardians may not forgo on her behalf, by consensus, and these are the sons of brothers and the sons of paternal uncles; and what God distinguishes [some] in the verse.

From Isa ibn 'Asim, who said: I heard Shurayh narrate: 'Ali asked me about "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage." I said: the woman's guardian. He said: No, rather the husband. It is narrated that a man married his sister, and her husband divorced her before consummating the marriage, so her brother forgave the bridal gift, and Shurayh approved it. Then he said: "I forgive on behalf of the women of Banu Murra." Amir said: "No, by God, Shurayh has never issued a worse judgment, nor a more foolish one, than to permit the brother's forgiveness." He said: after Shurayh, he returned from his view and said: it is the husband.

From al-Qasim, who said: the elders of Kufa would come to Shurayh and dispute with him over his statement "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage," until he fell to his knees, and Shurayh would say: "It is the husband, it is the husband."

Shu'ba narrated from Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they said: it is the husband. Tawus and Mujahid said: it is the guardian. I spoke with them about it, and they returned from their view and followed Sa'id, saying: it is the husband.

Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated as a mursal report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage is the husband; he forgives and gives the full bridal gift."

From Salih ibn Kaysan: Jubayr ibn Mut'im married a woman, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, and completed the bridal gift for her, and said: "I have more right to forgiveness." He interpreted His words "or that he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" as meaning, on this interpretation, that "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband himself in every case, before and after divorce. Then, when the alif and lam were introduced, the pronoun was dropped, as in His words ﴿for the Garden is the refuge (al-ma'wa)﴾, meaning his refuge. And al-Nabigha said:

"They have a disposition which God has not given to any others among mankind, and their dreams are not disordered."

meaning "and their dreams." Likewise His words "the tie of marriage" mean the tie of his marriage.

﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety﴾. Sibawayh said: its position is nominative as the subject, i.e., "and forgoing is nearer to piety and more binding," with ila meaning "to," i.e., "to piety." The address here is to men and women, because when the masculine and feminine are combined, the masculine prevails. The meaning is: your forgoing of some of it is nearer to piety, because this forgoing is recommended; and when one hastens to it and does it, it is known that what is obligatory is more firmly practised, and what is prohibited is more firmly avoided. al-Sha'bi read "wa an ya'fu" with the ya', making it a predicate of "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage."

﴿And do not forget graciousness among yourselves﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Dawud and al-Nakha'i read "wa la tanasaw al-fadl" with the form of mufa'ala between two parties, like His words ﴿and do not call one another by nicknames﴾. Yahya ibn Ya'mur read "wa la tansawi al-fadl" with a kasra on the waw, and the rest read "wa la tansaw al-fadl" with a damma on the waw. The meaning of al-fadl is the man's completing the bridal gift or the woman's giving up of the half. God Most High urged both the husband and the wife toward graciousness and kindness, and commanded both of them to hasten to forgoing.

﴿Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 235–237 (part 1 of 2):

"And there is no blame upon you, O men, for what you hint at of proposing to the women in waiting (ʿiddah), and the root of taʿrīd (hinting, allusion) is to suggest something indirectly." The poet said:
"As one who writes Hebrew script with his right hand, in Taymāʾ, ink-marked, then lines up the rows [of writing]."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 3/1087; the verse was recited by al-Aṣmaʿi and attributed to al-Shammākh.]]

Taʿrīd in speech is that indirect allusion of speech by which the listener understands the meaning without explicit statement. Its root is from ʿarḍ al-shay', meaning its side; it is said: "He struck with it the side of the wall," as if he circles around it without making it manifest. The taʿrīd of proposal mentioned in this verse, according to what has come in the tafsir, is that he says to her while she is in her ʿiddah:
"Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are righteous, indeed you are beneficial, indeed I have resolved to marry, indeed I am desirous of you, indeed I am eager for you, and perhaps Allah will bring good to you, and if Allah brings us together in what is lawful, I would be pleased, and if I marry you I will give you and treat you well," and similar speech, without saying to her: "Marry me."

Ibrahim said: "There is no harm in his sending her a gift and attending to her affairs during her ʿiddah, if she is one of his concerns."

Ibn ʿAwf related from Muhammad, from ʿUbaydah, concerning this verse, that he said: "He says to her guardian, 'Let no one precede me to her.'" Mujahid said: "A man said to a woman at the funeral of her husband: 'Do not precede me with yourself.' She said: 'You have already preceded me.'"

Ibn al-Mubarak related from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, from his maternal aunt, that Sukayna bint Handhala said: "Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli entered upon me while I was in my ʿiddah and said: 'O daughter of Handhala, you know my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the right of my grandfather over me and his precedence in Islam.' She said: 'May Allah forgive you, Abu Jaʿfar! Do you propose to me during my ʿiddah while you are taken as a source of knowledge?' He said: 'Or did I actually do that? I only sought your favour by my kinship to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and my standing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm Salama, who had been married to her cousin Abu Salama, and when her husband died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued mentioning to her his station with Allah while he was leaning on his hand, until the mat left its mark on his hand from the intensity of his leaning on it. That was not a proposal.'"
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/705.]]

Ibn Yazid said concerning this verse: "My father used to say: Everything that falls short of resolving the bond of marriage is zina." Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at of proposing to women," and khitbah (proposal) is a request for marriage, the verbal noun of your saying: "The man proposed to the woman, khatabahā khiṭbatan and khuṭbā."

Some people said: it is on the pattern of jilsah (sitting), qiʿdah (sitting), and rukbah (riding), and the meaning of their saying "So-and-so proposed to so-and-so" is: he asked her for a proposal regarding what was in her mind, that is, her needs and her affair, from their saying "What is your khaṭb?" i.e., your need and your affair. Allah said: "What is your affair, O Samiri?" [Q 20:95]

Al-Akhfash said: al-khuṭbah is mention, and al-khuṭbah is the gathering, so the meaning is: "in what you hint at, of those among whom you propose to women, in their presence." "Or you conceal within yourselves," i.e., you keep secret and hide in your souls, regarding their proposal and their marriage. It is said: "kanantu al-shay' and akannantuhu" are two dialects. Thaʿlab said: "akannat al-shay'" means I concealed it in my soul, and "kannatuhu" means I covered it. Al-Suddi said: it is that he enters and makes himself known to them as he wishes, without speaking anything.

"Allah knows that you will mention them in your hearts." Al-Hasan said: meaning the proposal. "But do not promise them secretly" [or: "do not make a pledge with them"] — some of them said: it is zina. A man would enter upon a woman for the sake of suspicion, while hinting at marriage, and say to her: "Leave me; when you complete your ʿiddah I will reveal my marriage to you." So Allah, exalted, forbade that. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibrahim, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ibn Abi Mujliz, al-Dahhak, al-Rabiʿ and ʿAtaʾ, and it is the narration of ʿAtiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas. What proves it is the saying of al-Aʿsha:

"Do not approach a neighbour's woman, for her secret is forbidden to you, [so marry her or remain forever]."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/625.]]

And al-Hutay'a said:
"He forbids the secret of their neighbour to them, and their neighbour eats the nose of the dishes."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 2/625.]]

Mujahid said: it is the man's saying to the woman: "Do not let yourself escape me, for I will marry you." Al-Shaʿbi and al-Suddi said: he does not take her pledge that she will not marry anyone else. ʿIkrima said: he does not propose to her during her ʿiddah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: he does not bargain with her for such and such amount of wealth on condition that she does not marry anyone else. All these interpretations are close in meaning, and the "secret" in these sayings is marriage. Imru' al-Qays said:

"Did not Bisasa claim today that I have grown old, and that those like me cannot do well with the secret?"
[[Gharib al-Hadith: 1/238; Lisan al-ʿArab: 15/259.]]

Al-Aʿsha said:
"They did not seek her secret for wealth, and they did not leave her for her asceticism."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 2/481.]]

That is, her marriage. Al-Kalbi said: "But do not promise them secretly" means: do not describe yourselves to them by frequent intercourse, so that he says to her, "I will come to you four or five times," and similar things. According to this view, the "secret" is intercourse itself. Al-Farazdaq said:

"Withholding the secrets except from their own people, and failing what the jealous, wasted lover supposed."
[[al-Ṣiḥāḥ by al-Jawhari: 4/1383.]]

He means that they are chaste in their hands from intercourse except with their husbands. Ru'ba said:

"He abstained from their secrets after the dusk, and did not place her between a rubbing and a passion."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 4/358.]]

He means he refrained from having relations with her after he had been bound to that.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "But do not promise them secretly" means: do not marry them secretly, then keep her until she is released, and then reveal it. The root of sirr is what you conceal in yourself, and marriage, adultery and intercourse are called sirr only because they occur between a man and a woman in secrecy. It is also said that the private part is called sirr because it is not made apparent. Thaʿlab related from Ibn al-Aʿrabi:

"When she saw my secret changed and bent, from beyond [its] desire, her secret when it turned away."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 4/358; attributed to al-Afwah al-Awdi, where it reads: "When she saw my secret change and turn, from beyond the desire of its ... when it turned away."]]

Then He excepted, saying: "Except that you say a fair word." It was said: a good promise. Mujahid said: it is allusion without explicit declaration or disclosure. The "an" [in "an taqūlū"] is in the place of an accusative, as a substitute for "secret." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: all of this is abrogated by His saying: "And do not resolve the bond of marriage," meaning do not validate the bond of marriage. Ibn al-Zajjaj said: "Do not resolve upon the bond of marriage," as it is said: "He struck the hand of purity and blessing." ʿAntara said:

"I have spent nights hungry, and its shade covered me, until I attain by it the generous feast."
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 11/419; where it reads "generous food."]]

That is, and its shade was over me.

"Until the Book reaches its term" — until the ʿiddah ends. He called it "Book" because it is an obligation from Allah, exalted, like His saying: "Fasting is prescribed for you."

"And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him," i.e., fear Allah. "And know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing," who does not hasten to punishment. The Arabs say: "Place the howdah upon the most patient of the camels."

"There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them, [or] fixed for them an obligation," the verse.

It was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who married a woman from the Banu Hanifa, did not name a dowry for her, then divorced her before touching her. Allah revealed this verse, and when it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Provide for her, even if it is with your cap." So this is His saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them," i.e., have not had intercourse with them.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read "tamāssūhunna" with an alif, in the form of mufā'alah, because the body of each of them touches the body of the other, so both touch one another; its proof is His saying: "before they touch one another." The rest read "tamassūhunna" without alif, because the coming together is only from the action of the man; its proof is His saying: "No human has touched me."

"Or fix for them an obligation" — i.e., establish for them a dowry. It is said: "The ruler assigned for so-and-so," meaning he recorded for him a charity in the register. If it is asked: what is the reason for negating blame regarding one who divorces, and would there be blame on the man if he divorced after consummation, so that it is removed from him before consummation? It is answered:

It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "What is the matter with people who play with the limits of Allah, saying: 'I have divorced you, I have taken you back'?"
[[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/650, no. 2017.]]

And he ﷺ said: "Do not divorce your wives except because of suspicion, for Allah does not love those who taste [much] or the women who taste [much]."
[[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/335.]]

And he peace be upon him said: "The most detested of lawful things to Allah is divorce."
[[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/650, no. 2018.]]

And he peace be upon him said: "Indeed Allah detests every frequent divorcer who tastes [many]."
[[al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shayba: 4/172, with variation.]]

When the Messenger said this, they thought they would sin by doing so, so Allah, exalted, informed them that there is no blame in divorcing women when it is done in the commendable manner, since separation is sometimes better than retention. It was also said: the meaning of His saying "There is no blame upon you" is that there is no way for the women against you if you divorce them, while you have not touched them and you have not fixed for them an obligation of dowry or maintenance.

It was also said: the meaning is "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them," at whatever time you wish, since there is no prescribed sunnah in their divorce. So a man may divorce them when he has not touched them, whether she is menstruating or pure, and at any time he likes. This is not the case for one who has been consummated with, because it is not permitted for her husband to divorce her if she is one of those with menstrual cycles, except in a ʿiddah, clearly, in a purity during which he has not had intercourse with her. If he divorces her while she is menstruating, or past the age [of menstruation], the divorce takes effect.

"And provide for them," i.e., furnish them and give them from your wealth what they may enjoy. Al-mutʿah and al-matāʿ are what one is provided with as provision. "According to the wealthy" (al-mūsiʿ), i.e., the rich, "his measure" (qadaruhu), "and according to the straitened" (al-muqtir), the poor, "his measure," i.e., his capacity and his ability. Abu Jaʿfar, Hafs, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Ibn Dhakwan read the dāl in both with a fatḥah, and Abu ʿUbayda chose it, saying: because of its grandeur in both. The others read the dāl in both with a sukūn, and Abu Hatim chose it. Both are dialects; he said: the Qur'an was recited with both. The confirmation of the fatḥah is His saying: "So the valleys flowed according to their measure" [Q 13:17], and the confirmation of the sukūn is His saying: "They did not measure Allah with His true measure" [Q 6:91]. The Arabs say: "al-qaḍāʾ and al-qadar." Abu Yazid al-Ansari said: "al-qaḍāʾ and al-qadr" with a sukūn on the dāl. The poet, al-Farazdaq, said:

"My sand was not poured into the iron of Mujashi', along with the decree, except for a need of mine that I wanted."

Some said: qadar (with fatḥah) is the verbal noun, and qadr (with sukūn) is the noun. "Matāʿan" is in the accusative as a verbal noun, i.e., "provide for them a provision." It may be accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, because matāʿ is indefinite and qadr is definite. "According to what is fair" (bil-maʿrūf), i.e., what Allah has commanded you, without injustice or procrastination. "Ḥaqqan" is in the accusative by way of reporting, its meaning: "I inform you of it as a truth." It was also said that it is in the accusative as a qualifier.

Ruling of the verse

The commentators said: it was said that this concerns a man who marries a woman and does not name a dowry for her, then divorces her before touching her; she has the mutʿah and no fixed dowry, by consensus of the scholars. They differed regarding the provision for a divorced woman in other than this case. Some said: every divorced woman has a provision, whoever she is and in whatever manner the divorce occurred. The provision is obligatory, to be paid from the divorcer's wealth as all other debts obligatory upon him are paid, whether he consummated with her or not, whether a dowry was fixed or not, provided the divorce came from him. As for when the separation comes from her, she has neither provision nor dowry. This is the view of al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Abu al-ʿAliya and Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: because of His saying:

"And for divorced women is provision according to what is fair, a duty upon the righteous." So He made the provision obligatory for all divorced women and did not distinguish. The meaning of the verse on this view is: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them, whether you have fixed for them an obligation or not," because every wife is either one for whom a dowry is named or one for whom none is named. From what they transmitted of His saying "or fix for them an obligation," we know that what is meant by "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women" is those for whom an obligation has been fixed, and those for whom none was fixed, for there is no sense in saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them or fixed for them an obligation," and then saying: "And provide for them," meaning all of them.

Others said: the provision is obligatory for every divorced woman except the one for whom an obligation was fixed when she is divorced before consummation; for her there is no provision, but she has half of the named dowry. This is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, Nafiʿ, ʿAtaʾ and Mujahid, and the school of al-Shafiʿi. The meaning of the verse on this view is: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women while you have not touched them and have not fixed for them an obligation." The alif is extra, like His saying "or they increase" [Q 37:147] and similar. Then He commanded provision for them.

It is also possible that His saying "And provide for them" refers to divorced women for whom no obligation was fixed before touching, and not to those for whom it was fixed. Then His following saying "And if you divorce them before you touch them" is specific to that. The beginning of the verse follows the apparent generality for those for whom an obligation was fixed and those for whom none was fixed, while in "And provide for them" it is specific to those for whom none was fixed, in accordance with the following verse.

Al-Zuhri said: there are two kinds of provision, one of which the ruler adjudicates and the other he does not adjudicate, but it is binding upon him between himself and Allah. As for the one the ruler adjudicates, it is for one who divorced before a dowry was fixed and before consummation; he is compelled to pay the provision, which is His saying: "a duty upon the doers of good." The provision that is binding between him and Allah, which the ruler does not adjudicate, is for one who divorces after consummation and after a dowry was fixed, which is His saying: "a duty upon the righteous."

Others said: none of that is obligatory; rather, provision is a kindness, and the command to it is a command of recommendation and encouragement, not a command of obligation and requirement. This is the view of Abu Hanifa. Ibn Sirin related that a man divorced a woman after consummation, and she brought a case against him before Shurayh regarding the provision. Shurayh said: "It is not the case that you must be among the doers of good, nor that you must be among the righteous," and he did not compel him to it.

They differed regarding the amount and extent of the provision. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Shaʿbi, al-Zuhri and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: its highest is a servant, its middle is three garments: a shirt, a head-covering and a cloak, and a waist-wrap, and below that is maintenance, and below that clothing, and some silver. This is the school of al-Shafiʿi, who said: its highest is a servant for the wealthy, its middle is a garment, and its least is the least of what he possesses, its value. al-Hasan said: thirty dirhams. Shurayh provided five hundred dirhams. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf provided Umm Abi Salama, when he divorced her, a black slave girl.

al-Hasan ibn ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) provided a wife of his with ten thousand dirhams, and she said: "A small provision from a beloved who parts."

Abu Hanifa said: her provision, when husband and wife disagree about it, is the amount of half of her equivalent dowry, and it does not exceed that. The correct view is that what is obligatory of it depends on the husband's hardship and ease, as He, exalted, said. If the consideration were the dowry, He would have said: "Provide for them according to their measure and the measure of their equivalent dowry." When He said "according to the wealthy his measure and according to the straitened his measure," that shows that what is considered is the husband's condition, not the woman's. Ibn Abi Za'ida related from Subayh ibn Salih, who said: ʿAmir was asked: "How much does a man provide for his wife?" He said: "According to the measure of his wealth."

Detailed ruling of the verse

Whoever marries a woman without a named dowry, the marriage is valid. If she demands a fixed dowry, we instruct him to fix one for her. If he does not fix one for her and consummates with her, she has the equivalent dowry (mahr mithl). If he divorces her before consummation, she has the provision and no dowry. If he dies leaving her after consummation, she has the equivalent dowry. If he dies leaving her before consummation and before naming, there are two opinions:

One: she has the equivalent dowry. This is the view of the people of Iraq, and the proof is the hadith of Barwa' bint Washiq al-Ashja'iyya, when her husband died, he had not fixed for her and had not consummated with her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided with the dowry of her women, neither less nor excessive, and she observes the ʿiddah and has the inheritance.
[[Musnad Ahmad: 4/280.]]

The second opinion: she has the inheritance and observes the ʿiddah, and has no dowry, but only the provision, as if he had divorced her before consummation and naming. This is the view of ʿAli, and he used to say concerning the hadith of Barwa': "The word of a Bedouin from Ashja' is not accepted against the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 235–237 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them (consummated the marriage)...﴾ This verse concerns a man who marries a woman and has already specified a bridal gift (sadaq) for her, then divorces her before he has touched her. She is due half of the bridal gift, and nothing more, and she has no waiting period ('idda). If he has not gone in to her and dies, there is no disagreement that she is due the full bridal gift and inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period. Here "touching" (al-mass) means intercourse (al-jima').

Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if a man is alone with a woman and does not have intercourse with her until he separates from her, the full bridal gift is binding on him, and the waiting period is binding on her, based on the report of Ibn Mas'ud: "The rightly-guided caliphs ruled concerning a man who closed a door and let down a curtain that she is due the bridal gift and must observe the waiting period." As for al-Shafi'i, he does not impose the full bridal gift or a waiting period, since there was no consummation according to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

Shurayh said: "I have not heard God Most High mention in His Book a door or a curtain. He only said that if he has not touched her, she is due half the bridal gift." This is also the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

This verse abrogates (nasikh) the verse in Surah al-Ahzab: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women...﴾ up to His words ﴿then give them provision﴾. Previously she had the provision (mata'). When this verse was revealed, it abrogated what preceded it and made obligatory for the divorced woman, whose bridal gift was specified before touching, half of her specified bridal gift, and she has no provision, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾ (i.e., have intercourse with them).

﴿and you have already specified for them an obligation﴾ (i.e., you have made the bridal gift obligatory for them and specified a bridal gift for them). The root of fard is "cutting off," and from it is said of the notch of a balance or a bow: fardah; and of a portion: farida, because one cuts it off from the thing. ﴿then half of what you have specified﴾ means half of the bridal gift due. al-Sulami read fanisfun with a damma on the nun wherever it occurs; both are dialects.

Then He said: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, meaning the women. The position of ya'fun is in the accusative by [the particle] illa an, since the feminine plural in the present tense is the same in the nominative, accusative and jussive, and always takes the nun: you say hunna yadribna, and lan yadribna, and lam yadribna, because if the nun were dropped it would be confused with the masculine.

﴿or that he forgoes﴾: al-Hasan read it with a sukun on the waw, as if he found the fatha on the waw heavy, just as the damma on it was found heavy. ﴿He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾: the scholars differed concerning it. Some said: it is the guardian (wali), and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless they forgo﴾, i.e., they give up and leave the half, so that they do not demand it from their husbands if they are previously married, mature, rational, and have authority over their affairs; ﴿or he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage﴾, who is her guardian, so that he leaves that half if she is a virgin or does not have authority over her affairs, and his forgoing is permissible for her even if she dislikes it. If the woman forgoes and the guardian refuses, the forgoing is permissible; if the guardian forgoes and the woman refuses, the forgoing is permissible provided she does not intend harm. This is the view of [Ali] and the companions of Abdullah, Ibrahim, 'Ata', al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Zayd, Rabi'a al-Ra'y, and a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn al-Hasan.

Ma'mar narrated from Ibn Tawus from his father, and from Isma'il ibn Shirwas, who both said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the guardian. 'Ikrima said: God Most High permitted him (He) to forgo, approved of it, and commanded it; so whichever woman forgoes, her forgoing is valid even if she is stingy and withholds, and whoever among her guardians forgoes, his forgoing is valid. This is the position of the jurists of the Hijaz, except that they said: the guardian's forgoing for a virgin is valid, but if she is previously married, his forgoing on her is not valid.

Others said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband, and the meaning of the verse is: ﴿unless the women forgo﴾, so they take nothing of the bridal gift, or ﴿the husband forgoes﴾, so he gives her the full bridal gift. This is the view of Ali, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Nafi', al-Rabi', Qatada, Ibn Hibban, al-Dahhak, and a narration of 'Ammar ibn Abi 'Ammar from Ibn 'Abbas. This is the position of the people of Iraq, who see no way for the guardian over any part of her bridal gift without her permission, whether she is previously married or a virgin. They said: because all agree that if a woman's guardian released her husband from her bridal gift before divorce, that is not permitted; so likewise his release and forgoing after divorce is not permitted. And because they also agree that if her guardian gave her husband a single dirham of her property after separation, he would be sinful unless he had the right to do so, and that gift would be void, and the bridal gift is property of hers; so the ruling must be like the ruling on her release of her property. And because they agree that some guardians may not forgo on her behalf, by consensus, and these are the sons of brothers and the sons of paternal uncles; and what God distinguishes [some] in the verse.

From Isa ibn 'Asim, who said: I heard Shurayh narrate: 'Ali asked me about "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage." I said: the woman's guardian. He said: No, rather the husband. It is narrated that a man married his sister, and her husband divorced her before consummating the marriage, so her brother forgave the bridal gift, and Shurayh approved it. Then he said: "I forgive on behalf of the women of Banu Murra." Amir said: "No, by God, Shurayh has never issued a worse judgment, nor a more foolish one, than to permit the brother's forgiveness." He said: after Shurayh, he returned from his view and said: it is the husband.

From al-Qasim, who said: the elders of Kufa would come to Shurayh and dispute with him over his statement "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage," until he fell to his knees, and Shurayh would say: "It is the husband, it is the husband."

Shu'ba narrated from Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: they said: it is the husband. Tawus and Mujahid said: it is the guardian. I spoke with them about it, and they returned from their view and followed Sa'id, saying: it is the husband.

Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated as a mursal report that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage is the husband; he forgives and gives the full bridal gift."

From Salih ibn Kaysan: Jubayr ibn Mut'im married a woman, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, and completed the bridal gift for her, and said: "I have more right to forgiveness." He interpreted His words "or that he forgoes, He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" as meaning, on this interpretation, that "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage" is the husband himself in every case, before and after divorce. Then, when the alif and lam were introduced, the pronoun was dropped, as in His words ﴿for the Garden is the refuge (al-ma'wa)﴾, meaning his refuge. And al-Nabigha said:

"They have a disposition which God has not given to any others among mankind, and their dreams are not disordered."

meaning "and their dreams." Likewise His words "the tie of marriage" mean the tie of his marriage.

﴿And that you forgo is nearer to piety﴾. Sibawayh said: its position is nominative as the subject, i.e., "and forgoing is nearer to piety and more binding," with ila meaning "to," i.e., "to piety." The address here is to men and women, because when the masculine and feminine are combined, the masculine prevails. The meaning is: your forgoing of some of it is nearer to piety, because this forgoing is recommended; and when one hastens to it and does it, it is known that what is obligatory is more firmly practised, and what is prohibited is more firmly avoided. al-Sha'bi read "wa an ya'fu" with the ya', making it a predicate of "He in whose hand is the tie of marriage."

﴿And do not forget graciousness among yourselves﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Dawud and al-Nakha'i read "wa la tanasaw al-fadl" with the form of mufa'ala between two parties, like His words ﴿and do not call one another by nicknames﴾. Yahya ibn Ya'mur read "wa la tansawi al-fadl" with a kasra on the waw, and the rest read "wa la tansaw al-fadl" with a damma on the waw. The meaning of al-fadl is the man's completing the bridal gift or the woman's giving up of the half. God Most High urged both the husband and the wife toward graciousness and kindness, and commanded both of them to hasten to forgoing.

﴿Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 238–242 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾, meaning: be constant and persistent in the obligatory prayers, performing them at their appointed times, observing their limits, their bowing (rukū'), their prostrations (sujūd), their standing (qiyām) and their sitting (qu'ūd), and all that is required of them in their rights. Every prayer in the Qur'an that is joined with the command to guard is intended to refer to the five daily prayers. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them for special guarding, as a indication of its excellence, like His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mikal﴾ [2:98]. These two are part of the angels, yet they were singled out by mention. And His saying: ﴿In them are fruit and date-palms and pomegranates﴾ [55:68]. He singled them out from the whole by the conjunction "and," which indicates specification and detail. Likewise is His saying: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾.

ʿĀ'isha read ﴿wa-l-ṣalāta l-wusṭā﴾ with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (ighrā'). Qālūn narrated from Nāfiʿ that he read al-wuṣṭā with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭā' (in al-wusṭā), since the two belong to the same class. Both are dialectal variants, like aṣ-ṣirāṭ and as-sirāṭ, aṣ-ṣidgh and as-sidgh, al-biṣāq and al-bisāq, al-lu ṣūq and al-lusūq, aṣ-ṣundūq and as-sundūq, aṣ-ṣaqr and as-saqr.

Al-wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ (the middle). The "middle" (wasṭ) of a thing is its best and most just part, because the best of affairs is their middle. Allah says: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced community﴾ [2:143], meaning best and most just. He also says: ﴿The most moderate of them said﴾ [68:28], meaning the best and most excellent of them. An Arab bedouin praised the Prophet (ﷺ) saying:

*"O the most central of people in all their glories,
and the most generous of people in mothers and fathers."* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/2098]

The scholars differed concerning the middle prayer and which prayer it is. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning it in this manner," and he interlaced his fingers. Some said: it is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). This is the view of Muʿādh, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād. It is narrated from Mūsā ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abū Umāma, when asked about the middle prayer, say: "I do not think it is other than the dawn prayer." Maʿmar ibn Ṭāwūs narrated from his father, and Ismāʿīl ibn Shurūs from ʿIkrima, both said: "It is the dawn prayer, meaning the middle prayer." This is the choice of Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shāfiʿī. Evidence for this is what al-Rabīʿ narrated from Abū al-ʿĀliya, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they finished, he said: "I asked them: Which of the prayers is the middle prayer? They said: The one you have just prayed." It is also said: because it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "It is the dawn prayer. It was made the middle, so it lies between night and day. It is prayed in the darkness of night and the brightness of day. It is the greatest of the prayers in that people miss it. It is also not shortened and not combined with another prayer, and it lies between two prayers that are combined." Confirmation of this interpretation from the revelation, which indicates specification and excellence, is His saying: ﴿and the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [17:78], meaning that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, recorded in the register of the night and the register of the day. Another evidence from the context of the verse is that He follows it with: ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [2:238], meaning: stand for Allah in it, devoutly obedient. They said: there is no obligatory prayer in which qunūt (devout standing) is performed except the dawn prayer, so it is known that this is the one. In it is evidence for the establishment of qunūt.

Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī said: "Ibn ʿAbbās led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Basra. He performed qunūt before the bowing and raised his hands. When he finished he said: This is the middle prayer that we were commanded to stand in devoutly obedient." The evidence for this is what Ḥanẓala narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt for a month, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to perform qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world."

Ibn Abī Layla narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar until he died, and ʿUthmān until he died, and ʿAlī until he died."

Others said: it is the noon prayer (ṣalāt al-ẓuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿĀʾisha.

ʿUrwa narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at the time of midday heat (al-hājira), and it was the heaviest of the prayers upon his companions, so that behind him there would only be a row or two rows, and most people would be in their afternoon rest (qā'ila) and in their trade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I had intended to burn the houses of people who do not attend the prayer." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾.

Their evidence that it is the middle of the day is what Abū Dharr narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has a gate in the lowest heaven through which the sun passes. When the sun declines, everything glorifies our Lord, and Allah commanded the prayer at that hour. It is the hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and they are not closed until the noon prayer is prayed, and supplication is answered at it."

Also because it is the middle of the day's prayers. Among its distinctions is that it was the first prayer made obligatory, and it was the first prayer toward which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions turned to the Kaʿba. It is also the one on account of which all prayers and congregations are lifted on Friday.

Some said: it is the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). This is the view of ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿī, Zurr ibn Ḥubaysh, Qatāda, Abū Ayyūb, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and Muqātil, and the choice of Abū Ḥanīfa. Evidence for this is what al-Ḥasan narrated from Samura ibn Jundub, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

It is mentioned in some reports that it is the one about which Sulaymān (peace be upon him) was negligent.

Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib who said: "The verse ﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾ was revealed, and the afternoon prayer was recited by us during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it (nasakhahā) with ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Someone said to him: "So it is the afternoon prayer?" He said: "Did I inform you how it was revealed and how it was abrogated? And Allah knows best."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ḥafṣa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me so that I may tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." When he informed her, she said: "Write: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer."

Hishām narrated from ʿUrwa from his father who said: "In the copy of ʿĀʾisha was: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾." Likewise used to recite it Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from ʿAlī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb): "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May Allah fill their houses, or their graves, with fire."

He said: then he prayed it between the two evening prayers.

In some reports, a man said in the assembly of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar sent me, when I was a small boy, to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my small finger and said: 'This is the dawn prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the noon prayer.' Then he folded the thumb and said: 'This is the sunset prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the night prayer.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'The afternoon prayer.' He said: 'It is the afternoon prayer.'"
