They said: it is also because it lies between the two day prayers and the two night prayers. The Prophet (ﷺ) was lenient, so he prayed it and emphasised it.

Abū Tamīm al-Ḥabashānī narrated from Abū Baṣra al-Ghifārī who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer with us, and when he finished he said: 'This prayer was made obligatory upon those before you, and they were lax in it and abandoned it. Whoever among you prays it and guards it will be given its reward twice, and there is no prayer after it until the witness appears.'" The witness is the star.

Abū Qilāba narrated from Abū al-Muhājir from Buraida who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds are nullified."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer, it suffices him regarding his family and his wealth."

Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb said: "It is the sunset prayer. Do you not see that it is a middle prayer, neither the least nor the most in number, and it is not shortened during travel, and it is the odd-numbered prayer (witr) of the day?"

Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father from ʿĀʾisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent of the prayers is the sunset prayer. Allah did not remove it from the traveller or the resident. Through it Allah opens the night prayer and closes the day. Whoever prays the sunset prayer and then prays two rak'as after it, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise. Whoever prays four rak'as after it, Allah forgives him the sins of twenty years, or he said forty years."

Shaykh Abū Maytham Sahl ibn Muḥammad related from some people that it is the last night prayer (al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhira), and he said: "Because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the night prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for half the night, and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for the whole night."

Some said: it is one of the five prayers, and we do not know its specific identity. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was asked about the middle prayer, and he said to the questioner: "[Are you eager] that if I teach you it, you will guard it and neglect the rest?" He said: "No." He said: "If you guard all of them, you have guarded it." This was also said by Abū Bakr al-Warrāq, who said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed, He would have made it clear. But He, glorified be He, wanted to alert the creation to performing the prayers."

Al-Thaʿlabī said: "Both of these two views are excellent. Allah, exalted be He, concealed the middle prayer among all the obligatory prayers so that they would guard all of them in hope of hitting the middle, just as He concealed the Night of Power among the nights of Ramadan, His greatest Name among all the names, and the hour of response among the hours of Friday, as wisdom from Him in His doing and mercy upon His creation."

In His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and the middle prayer﴾ there is evidence that the witr prayer is not obligatory. This is because the Muslims agreed that the obligatory prayers are fewer than seven and more than three, and among the numbers between three and seven there is no odd number except five, and even numbers have no middle. So it is established that it is five.

Qatāda narrated from Anas who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prayers has Allah made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "Five prayers." He asked: "Is there anything before them or after them that Allah has made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "No." The man swore by Allah that he would neither add to them nor subtract from them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If the man is truthful, he will enter Paradise."

It is narrated from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Najd, with dishevelled hair, his voice heard but he could not be understood, until he came close and it became clear that he was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Five prayers in the day and night." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And fasting the month of Ramadan." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." He mentioned to him the zakat, and he said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." Then the man turned away saying: "By Allah, I will neither add to this nor subtract from it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He will prosper if he is truthful."

It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥayyān from Ibn Jarīr that a man from the tribe of Kināna called al-Muḥdajī used to hear a man in Syria, known as Abū Muḥammad, say: "The witr is obligatory." Al-Muḥdajī said: "I went to ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and waylaid him as he was going to the mosque, and I told him what Abū Muḥammad had said. ʿUbāda said: 'Abū Muḥammad lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Five prayers Allah has prescribed for the servants. Whoever comes with them, not neglecting any of them out of disregard for their right, has a covenant with Allah that He will admit him to Paradise. Whoever does not come with them has no covenant with Allah. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will admit him to Paradise."'"

It is narrated from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The witr is not obligatory, because there is no takbīr in it, but it is a sunna which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established." The evidence that the witr is not obligatory is what Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform the witr on his mount. Nāfiʿ also narrated that Ibn ʿUmar used to perform the witr on his camel, and mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do that. The jurists agreed that an obligatory prayer on a mount in a state of safety is not valid.

﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: obedient. This was said by al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir ibn Zayd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs and Ibn ʿAbbās through the narration of ʿIkrima, ʿAṭiyya and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: for every people of a religion there is a prayer in which they stand while disobedient, so stand you in your prayers for Allah in obedience. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every qunūt in the two midday prayers is obedience."

Some said: qunūt is silence regarding what it is not permissible to speak in the prayer. Zayd ibn Arqam said: "We used to speak during the prayer in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of us would speak to the person beside him, and a comer would enter and greet, and they would return the greeting, and he would ask them: 'How many [rak'as] have you prayed?' and they would reply telling him how many they had prayed. A man's servant would come while he was praying and speak to him about his need, like the practice of the People of the Book. We continued like this until ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ was revealed, and we were commanded to silence and forbidden to speak."

Mujāhid said: "Humble (khāshiʿīn)." He said: "Among qunūt is prolonging the bowing, lowering the gaze, stillness and lowering the wing. The scholars, when one of them stood to pray, would be so awed before the Most Merciful that he would not turn, nor move pebbles, nor fidget with anything, nor occupy his mind with any matter of this world, except inadvertently."

Al-Ḥasan and al-Rabīʿ said: "Standing in the prayer." Evidence for this is the hadith of Jābir that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which prayer is best?" He said: "Long qunūt."

Ibn ʿAbbās, in a narration from Rajāʾ, said: "Supplicating in their prayer." The evidence is that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed qunūt against a man and mentioned that whatever supplication was against them [was made]. It was said: "Praying." The evidence is His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ [39:9], meaning one who prays. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the one who strives in the cause of Allah is like the one who is devoutly obedient, fasting," meaning the one who prays and fasts.

﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾, meaning: on foot. It is said: rājil and rijāl, like ṣāḥib and ṣiḥāb, ṣā'im and ṣiyām, qā'im and qiyām. Allah says: ﴿they will come to you on foot﴾ [22:27]. Al-Akhṭal said:

*"The sons of Ghadāna, their eyes fixed,
walking beneath their bellies on foot."* [Tāj al-ʿArūs: 7/336]

It is reported that they bent down as captives, with their eyes fixed upon their children. ﴿Or riding﴾ upon their mounts, which is the plural of rākib (rider). Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "Rākib is only said of the owner of a camel. The owner of a horse is called fāris, the rider of a donkey is ḥammār, the rider of a mule is baghghāl." The word is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), meaning: pray on foot or riding.

The meaning of the verse: if you cannot pray devoutly obedient, observing the prayer in its full rights because of fear, then pray on foot, that is, walking on your feet, or riding on the backs of your mounts; that will suffice you.

The commentators said: this applies to the situation of pursuit and flight. One prays wherever he turns, facing the qibla or not, riding or on foot, and makes the prostration lower than the bowing, signalling with gestures. This is the prayer of extreme fear. Prayer in a state of fear is of two kinds, and we will mention them in Surat al-Nisā'. The prayer of extreme fear is this one. The fear which permits the worshipper to pray on horseback or on foot, wherever his direction is, is that of fighting and pursuit, the fighting against an enemy or a warrior, or the fear of a raging beast, an attacking camel, or a flowing torrent, or where the most likely outcome is destruction. If he prays the prayer of safety, he is permitted to pray the prayer of extreme fear, which is two rak'as. If he prays it as one rak'a, that is permitted, because of what Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet: four in residence, two when travelling, and one in fear."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If you are in battle, and the two armies meet, and people strike one another, then say: 'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest,' and remember Allah, and that is your prayer." al-Zuhrī said: "If he is unable, he should not leave off its remembrance in his heart."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 238–242 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then when you are secure, remember God,﴾ that is, perform the five prayers in full, observing their requirements, ﴿as He taught you what you did not know.﴾ ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind,﴾ addressing the men, ﴿and who leave wives behind﴾ meaning wives.

Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs most often say "zawjah" (wife) for a woman, but in the Qur'an it is "zawj" (spouse).

﴿A bequest for their wives﴾ — al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Abu 'Amir, al-A'mash and Hamzah read "waṣiyyatan" in the accusative, meaning: "let them bequeath a bequest." The rest read it in the nominative, meaning: "the bequest is prescribed for them." It is also said that the meaning is "for their wives is a bequest," and it is said: "let there be a bequest." The evidence for this reading is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "A bequest has been prescribed for them, for their wives."

And Ubayy read: "and leave wives, a provision for their wives." Abu 'Ubayd said: Yet we have found this meaning, all of it, in the Qur'an in the nominative, such as His saying ﴿half of what you have decreed﴾ and ﴿a payment of blood money delivered﴾ and similar.

"Matā'an" (provision) is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: "provide for them a provision." It is also said: God, Mighty and Majestic, made that a provision for them. It is also said it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative governed by the bequest, like His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾. "Al-matā'" means maintenance for a year for her food and clothing, or her housing, or what she needs. ﴿Without expulsion, for a full year﴾ — "ghayra ikhrāj" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative by removing the preposition, meaning: "without expulsion."

As for the interpretation of the verse and its ruling:

Ibn 'Abbas and the rest of the exegetes said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the people of al-Ta'if called Hakim ibn al-Harith, who emigrated to Medina. He had children, and his parents and his wife were with him. He died, and the matter was referred to the Prophet ﷺ, so God the Exalted revealed this verse. The Messenger of God ﷺ gave his parents and children from his inheritance, and did not give his wife anything, except that he commanded them to maintain her from the estate of her husband for a year.

This was because when a man died and left a wife, she would observe a year's waiting period in her husband's house without leaving it. When the year was over, she would leave and throw a dung-pellet at a dog, meaning by this that her sitting after her husband was easier for her than a dung-pellet thrown at a dog. The poets also mentioned this in their verse. Labid said:

"And the widows when their year stretches long."

Her lodging and maintenance were obligatory from her husband's property for this year, as long as she did not leave. That was her share of her husband's estate, and she had no inheritance. If she left her husband's house, she had no maintenance. The man would bequeath this. It remained so until the verse of inheritance was revealed, and God abrogated the year's maintenance by the quarter and the eighth, and abrogated the year's waiting period by His saying ﴿who wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

God the Exalted said ﴿But if they leave﴾, meaning of their own accord, before the year is over, without being expelled by the heirs, ﴿then there is no blame upon you, O guardians of the deceased, for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾, meaning their desire for marriage. Regarding the meaning of lifting blame from the men for the women's action, there are two views:

The first: there is no blame on you in cutting off maintenance from them if they leave before the year is complete.

The second: there is no blame on you in not preventing them from leaving, because their remaining for a year in their husband's house was not obligatory upon them. God gave them the choice in this until four months and ten days abrogated it, for if it had been obligatory upon her, it would not have been permissible for the husband's guardians to prevent her from that. So God lifted the blame from them and from her, and permitted her to leave if she wished. Then the maintenance was abrogated by inheritance, and the year's stay by four months and ten days. ﴿And God is Mighty and Wise.﴾

﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing.﴾ We have already discussed the ruling on provision at length, so there is no need to repeat it. It was mentioned again here because it adds a meaning not found elsewhere: what came before explains the ruling for a divorced woman who has not been touched, whereas here it explains the ruling for all divorced women regarding provision.

Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed because when God revealed His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ up to His saying ﴿upon the good-doers﴾, a man among the Muslims said: "If I do good, I will do it, and if I do not wish to, I will not do it." God the Exalted said ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾, meaning the believing God-fearing ones who avoid polytheism, clarifying that every divorced woman has a provision. We have already mentioned the disagreement concerning it.

Ayyas ibn 'Amir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) who said: "Every believing divorced woman, free or a slave, has a provision," and he recited ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness﴾ — the verse.

﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may understand.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 238–242 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾, meaning: be constant and persistent in the obligatory prayers, performing them at their appointed times, observing their limits, their bowing (rukū'), their prostrations (sujūd), their standing (qiyām) and their sitting (qu'ūd), and all that is required of them in their rights. Every prayer in the Qur'an that is joined with the command to guard is intended to refer to the five daily prayers. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them for special guarding, as a indication of its excellence, like His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mikal﴾ [2:98]. These two are part of the angels, yet they were singled out by mention. And His saying: ﴿In them are fruit and date-palms and pomegranates﴾ [55:68]. He singled them out from the whole by the conjunction "and," which indicates specification and detail. Likewise is His saying: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾.

ʿĀ'isha read ﴿wa-l-ṣalāta l-wusṭā﴾ with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (ighrā'). Qālūn narrated from Nāfiʿ that he read al-wuṣṭā with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭā' (in al-wusṭā), since the two belong to the same class. Both are dialectal variants, like aṣ-ṣirāṭ and as-sirāṭ, aṣ-ṣidgh and as-sidgh, al-biṣāq and al-bisāq, al-lu ṣūq and al-lusūq, aṣ-ṣundūq and as-sundūq, aṣ-ṣaqr and as-saqr.

Al-wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ (the middle). The "middle" (wasṭ) of a thing is its best and most just part, because the best of affairs is their middle. Allah says: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced community﴾ [2:143], meaning best and most just. He also says: ﴿The most moderate of them said﴾ [68:28], meaning the best and most excellent of them. An Arab bedouin praised the Prophet (ﷺ) saying:

*"O the most central of people in all their glories,
and the most generous of people in mothers and fathers."* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/2098]

The scholars differed concerning the middle prayer and which prayer it is. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning it in this manner," and he interlaced his fingers. Some said: it is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). This is the view of Muʿādh, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād. It is narrated from Mūsā ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abū Umāma, when asked about the middle prayer, say: "I do not think it is other than the dawn prayer." Maʿmar ibn Ṭāwūs narrated from his father, and Ismāʿīl ibn Shurūs from ʿIkrima, both said: "It is the dawn prayer, meaning the middle prayer." This is the choice of Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shāfiʿī. Evidence for this is what al-Rabīʿ narrated from Abū al-ʿĀliya, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they finished, he said: "I asked them: Which of the prayers is the middle prayer? They said: The one you have just prayed." It is also said: because it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "It is the dawn prayer. It was made the middle, so it lies between night and day. It is prayed in the darkness of night and the brightness of day. It is the greatest of the prayers in that people miss it. It is also not shortened and not combined with another prayer, and it lies between two prayers that are combined." Confirmation of this interpretation from the revelation, which indicates specification and excellence, is His saying: ﴿and the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [17:78], meaning that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, recorded in the register of the night and the register of the day. Another evidence from the context of the verse is that He follows it with: ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [2:238], meaning: stand for Allah in it, devoutly obedient. They said: there is no obligatory prayer in which qunūt (devout standing) is performed except the dawn prayer, so it is known that this is the one. In it is evidence for the establishment of qunūt.

Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī said: "Ibn ʿAbbās led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Basra. He performed qunūt before the bowing and raised his hands. When he finished he said: This is the middle prayer that we were commanded to stand in devoutly obedient." The evidence for this is what Ḥanẓala narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt for a month, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to perform qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world."

Ibn Abī Layla narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar until he died, and ʿUthmān until he died, and ʿAlī until he died."

Others said: it is the noon prayer (ṣalāt al-ẓuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿĀʾisha.

ʿUrwa narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at the time of midday heat (al-hājira), and it was the heaviest of the prayers upon his companions, so that behind him there would only be a row or two rows, and most people would be in their afternoon rest (qā'ila) and in their trade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I had intended to burn the houses of people who do not attend the prayer." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾.

Their evidence that it is the middle of the day is what Abū Dharr narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has a gate in the lowest heaven through which the sun passes. When the sun declines, everything glorifies our Lord, and Allah commanded the prayer at that hour. It is the hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and they are not closed until the noon prayer is prayed, and supplication is answered at it."

Also because it is the middle of the day's prayers. Among its distinctions is that it was the first prayer made obligatory, and it was the first prayer toward which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions turned to the Kaʿba. It is also the one on account of which all prayers and congregations are lifted on Friday.

Some said: it is the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). This is the view of ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿī, Zurr ibn Ḥubaysh, Qatāda, Abū Ayyūb, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and Muqātil, and the choice of Abū Ḥanīfa. Evidence for this is what al-Ḥasan narrated from Samura ibn Jundub, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

It is mentioned in some reports that it is the one about which Sulaymān (peace be upon him) was negligent.

Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib who said: "The verse ﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾ was revealed, and the afternoon prayer was recited by us during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it (nasakhahā) with ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Someone said to him: "So it is the afternoon prayer?" He said: "Did I inform you how it was revealed and how it was abrogated? And Allah knows best."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ḥafṣa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me so that I may tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." When he informed her, she said: "Write: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer."

Hishām narrated from ʿUrwa from his father who said: "In the copy of ʿĀʾisha was: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾." Likewise used to recite it Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from ʿAlī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb): "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May Allah fill their houses, or their graves, with fire."

He said: then he prayed it between the two evening prayers.

In some reports, a man said in the assembly of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar sent me, when I was a small boy, to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my small finger and said: 'This is the dawn prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the noon prayer.' Then he folded the thumb and said: 'This is the sunset prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the night prayer.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'The afternoon prayer.' He said: 'It is the afternoon prayer.'"

They said: it is also because it lies between the two day prayers and the two night prayers. The Prophet (ﷺ) was lenient, so he prayed it and emphasised it.

Abū Tamīm al-Ḥabashānī narrated from Abū Baṣra al-Ghifārī who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer with us, and when he finished he said: 'This prayer was made obligatory upon those before you, and they were lax in it and abandoned it. Whoever among you prays it and guards it will be given its reward twice, and there is no prayer after it until the witness appears.'" The witness is the star.

Abū Qilāba narrated from Abū al-Muhājir from Buraida who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds are nullified."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer, it suffices him regarding his family and his wealth."

Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb said: "It is the sunset prayer. Do you not see that it is a middle prayer, neither the least nor the most in number, and it is not shortened during travel, and it is the odd-numbered prayer (witr) of the day?"

Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father from ʿĀʾisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent of the prayers is the sunset prayer. Allah did not remove it from the traveller or the resident. Through it Allah opens the night prayer and closes the day. Whoever prays the sunset prayer and then prays two rak'as after it, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise. Whoever prays four rak'as after it, Allah forgives him the sins of twenty years, or he said forty years."

Shaykh Abū Maytham Sahl ibn Muḥammad related from some people that it is the last night prayer (al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhira), and he said: "Because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the night prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for half the night, and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for the whole night."

Some said: it is one of the five prayers, and we do not know its specific identity. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was asked about the middle prayer, and he said to the questioner: "[Are you eager] that if I teach you it, you will guard it and neglect the rest?" He said: "No." He said: "If you guard all of them, you have guarded it." This was also said by Abū Bakr al-Warrāq, who said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed, He would have made it clear. But He, glorified be He, wanted to alert the creation to performing the prayers."

Al-Thaʿlabī said: "Both of these two views are excellent. Allah, exalted be He, concealed the middle prayer among all the obligatory prayers so that they would guard all of them in hope of hitting the middle, just as He concealed the Night of Power among the nights of Ramadan, His greatest Name among all the names, and the hour of response among the hours of Friday, as wisdom from Him in His doing and mercy upon His creation."

In His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and the middle prayer﴾ there is evidence that the witr prayer is not obligatory. This is because the Muslims agreed that the obligatory prayers are fewer than seven and more than three, and among the numbers between three and seven there is no odd number except five, and even numbers have no middle. So it is established that it is five.

Qatāda narrated from Anas who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prayers has Allah made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "Five prayers." He asked: "Is there anything before them or after them that Allah has made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "No." The man swore by Allah that he would neither add to them nor subtract from them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If the man is truthful, he will enter Paradise."

It is narrated from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Najd, with dishevelled hair, his voice heard but he could not be understood, until he came close and it became clear that he was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Five prayers in the day and night." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And fasting the month of Ramadan." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." He mentioned to him the zakat, and he said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." Then the man turned away saying: "By Allah, I will neither add to this nor subtract from it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He will prosper if he is truthful."

It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥayyān from Ibn Jarīr that a man from the tribe of Kināna called al-Muḥdajī used to hear a man in Syria, known as Abū Muḥammad, say: "The witr is obligatory." Al-Muḥdajī said: "I went to ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and waylaid him as he was going to the mosque, and I told him what Abū Muḥammad had said. ʿUbāda said: 'Abū Muḥammad lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Five prayers Allah has prescribed for the servants. Whoever comes with them, not neglecting any of them out of disregard for their right, has a covenant with Allah that He will admit him to Paradise. Whoever does not come with them has no covenant with Allah. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will admit him to Paradise."'"

It is narrated from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The witr is not obligatory, because there is no takbīr in it, but it is a sunna which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established." The evidence that the witr is not obligatory is what Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform the witr on his mount. Nāfiʿ also narrated that Ibn ʿUmar used to perform the witr on his camel, and mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do that. The jurists agreed that an obligatory prayer on a mount in a state of safety is not valid.

﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: obedient. This was said by al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir ibn Zayd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs and Ibn ʿAbbās through the narration of ʿIkrima, ʿAṭiyya and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: for every people of a religion there is a prayer in which they stand while disobedient, so stand you in your prayers for Allah in obedience. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every qunūt in the two midday prayers is obedience."

Some said: qunūt is silence regarding what it is not permissible to speak in the prayer. Zayd ibn Arqam said: "We used to speak during the prayer in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of us would speak to the person beside him, and a comer would enter and greet, and they would return the greeting, and he would ask them: 'How many [rak'as] have you prayed?' and they would reply telling him how many they had prayed. A man's servant would come while he was praying and speak to him about his need, like the practice of the People of the Book. We continued like this until ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ was revealed, and we were commanded to silence and forbidden to speak."

Mujāhid said: "Humble (khāshiʿīn)." He said: "Among qunūt is prolonging the bowing, lowering the gaze, stillness and lowering the wing. The scholars, when one of them stood to pray, would be so awed before the Most Merciful that he would not turn, nor move pebbles, nor fidget with anything, nor occupy his mind with any matter of this world, except inadvertently."

Al-Ḥasan and al-Rabīʿ said: "Standing in the prayer." Evidence for this is the hadith of Jābir that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which prayer is best?" He said: "Long qunūt."

Ibn ʿAbbās, in a narration from Rajāʾ, said: "Supplicating in their prayer." The evidence is that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed qunūt against a man and mentioned that whatever supplication was against them [was made]. It was said: "Praying." The evidence is His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ [39:9], meaning one who prays. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the one who strives in the cause of Allah is like the one who is devoutly obedient, fasting," meaning the one who prays and fasts.

﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾, meaning: on foot. It is said: rājil and rijāl, like ṣāḥib and ṣiḥāb, ṣā'im and ṣiyām, qā'im and qiyām. Allah says: ﴿they will come to you on foot﴾ [22:27]. Al-Akhṭal said:

*"The sons of Ghadāna, their eyes fixed,
walking beneath their bellies on foot."* [Tāj al-ʿArūs: 7/336]

It is reported that they bent down as captives, with their eyes fixed upon their children. ﴿Or riding﴾ upon their mounts, which is the plural of rākib (rider). Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "Rākib is only said of the owner of a camel. The owner of a horse is called fāris, the rider of a donkey is ḥammār, the rider of a mule is baghghāl." The word is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), meaning: pray on foot or riding.

The meaning of the verse: if you cannot pray devoutly obedient, observing the prayer in its full rights because of fear, then pray on foot, that is, walking on your feet, or riding on the backs of your mounts; that will suffice you.

The commentators said: this applies to the situation of pursuit and flight. One prays wherever he turns, facing the qibla or not, riding or on foot, and makes the prostration lower than the bowing, signalling with gestures. This is the prayer of extreme fear. Prayer in a state of fear is of two kinds, and we will mention them in Surat al-Nisā'. The prayer of extreme fear is this one. The fear which permits the worshipper to pray on horseback or on foot, wherever his direction is, is that of fighting and pursuit, the fighting against an enemy or a warrior, or the fear of a raging beast, an attacking camel, or a flowing torrent, or where the most likely outcome is destruction. If he prays the prayer of safety, he is permitted to pray the prayer of extreme fear, which is two rak'as. If he prays it as one rak'a, that is permitted, because of what Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet: four in residence, two when travelling, and one in fear."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If you are in battle, and the two armies meet, and people strike one another, then say: 'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest,' and remember Allah, and that is your prayer." al-Zuhrī said: "If he is unable, he should not leave off its remembrance in his heart."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 238–242 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then when you are secure, remember God,﴾ that is, perform the five prayers in full, observing their requirements, ﴿as He taught you what you did not know.﴾ ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind,﴾ addressing the men, ﴿and who leave wives behind﴾ meaning wives.

Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs most often say "zawjah" (wife) for a woman, but in the Qur'an it is "zawj" (spouse).

﴿A bequest for their wives﴾ — al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Abu 'Amir, al-A'mash and Hamzah read "waṣiyyatan" in the accusative, meaning: "let them bequeath a bequest." The rest read it in the nominative, meaning: "the bequest is prescribed for them." It is also said that the meaning is "for their wives is a bequest," and it is said: "let there be a bequest." The evidence for this reading is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "A bequest has been prescribed for them, for their wives."

And Ubayy read: "and leave wives, a provision for their wives." Abu 'Ubayd said: Yet we have found this meaning, all of it, in the Qur'an in the nominative, such as His saying ﴿half of what you have decreed﴾ and ﴿a payment of blood money delivered﴾ and similar.

"Matā'an" (provision) is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: "provide for them a provision." It is also said: God, Mighty and Majestic, made that a provision for them. It is also said it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative governed by the bequest, like His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾. "Al-matā'" means maintenance for a year for her food and clothing, or her housing, or what she needs. ﴿Without expulsion, for a full year﴾ — "ghayra ikhrāj" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative by removing the preposition, meaning: "without expulsion."

As for the interpretation of the verse and its ruling:

Ibn 'Abbas and the rest of the exegetes said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the people of al-Ta'if called Hakim ibn al-Harith, who emigrated to Medina. He had children, and his parents and his wife were with him. He died, and the matter was referred to the Prophet ﷺ, so God the Exalted revealed this verse. The Messenger of God ﷺ gave his parents and children from his inheritance, and did not give his wife anything, except that he commanded them to maintain her from the estate of her husband for a year.

This was because when a man died and left a wife, she would observe a year's waiting period in her husband's house without leaving it. When the year was over, she would leave and throw a dung-pellet at a dog, meaning by this that her sitting after her husband was easier for her than a dung-pellet thrown at a dog. The poets also mentioned this in their verse. Labid said:

"And the widows when their year stretches long."

Her lodging and maintenance were obligatory from her husband's property for this year, as long as she did not leave. That was her share of her husband's estate, and she had no inheritance. If she left her husband's house, she had no maintenance. The man would bequeath this. It remained so until the verse of inheritance was revealed, and God abrogated the year's maintenance by the quarter and the eighth, and abrogated the year's waiting period by His saying ﴿who wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

God the Exalted said ﴿But if they leave﴾, meaning of their own accord, before the year is over, without being expelled by the heirs, ﴿then there is no blame upon you, O guardians of the deceased, for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾, meaning their desire for marriage. Regarding the meaning of lifting blame from the men for the women's action, there are two views:

The first: there is no blame on you in cutting off maintenance from them if they leave before the year is complete.

The second: there is no blame on you in not preventing them from leaving, because their remaining for a year in their husband's house was not obligatory upon them. God gave them the choice in this until four months and ten days abrogated it, for if it had been obligatory upon her, it would not have been permissible for the husband's guardians to prevent her from that. So God lifted the blame from them and from her, and permitted her to leave if she wished. Then the maintenance was abrogated by inheritance, and the year's stay by four months and ten days. ﴿And God is Mighty and Wise.﴾

﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing.﴾ We have already discussed the ruling on provision at length, so there is no need to repeat it. It was mentioned again here because it adds a meaning not found elsewhere: what came before explains the ruling for a divorced woman who has not been touched, whereas here it explains the ruling for all divorced women regarding provision.

Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed because when God revealed His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ up to His saying ﴿upon the good-doers﴾, a man among the Muslims said: "If I do good, I will do it, and if I do not wish to, I will not do it." God the Exalted said ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾, meaning the believing God-fearing ones who avoid polytheism, clarifying that every divorced woman has a provision. We have already mentioned the disagreement concerning it.

Ayyas ibn 'Amir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) who said: "Every believing divorced woman, free or a slave, has a provision," and he recited ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness﴾ — the verse.

﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may understand.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 238–242 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾, meaning: be constant and persistent in the obligatory prayers, performing them at their appointed times, observing their limits, their bowing (rukū'), their prostrations (sujūd), their standing (qiyām) and their sitting (qu'ūd), and all that is required of them in their rights. Every prayer in the Qur'an that is joined with the command to guard is intended to refer to the five daily prayers. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them for special guarding, as a indication of its excellence, like His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mikal﴾ [2:98]. These two are part of the angels, yet they were singled out by mention. And His saying: ﴿In them are fruit and date-palms and pomegranates﴾ [55:68]. He singled them out from the whole by the conjunction "and," which indicates specification and detail. Likewise is His saying: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾.

ʿĀ'isha read ﴿wa-l-ṣalāta l-wusṭā﴾ with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (ighrā'). Qālūn narrated from Nāfiʿ that he read al-wuṣṭā with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭā' (in al-wusṭā), since the two belong to the same class. Both are dialectal variants, like aṣ-ṣirāṭ and as-sirāṭ, aṣ-ṣidgh and as-sidgh, al-biṣāq and al-bisāq, al-lu ṣūq and al-lusūq, aṣ-ṣundūq and as-sundūq, aṣ-ṣaqr and as-saqr.

Al-wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ (the middle). The "middle" (wasṭ) of a thing is its best and most just part, because the best of affairs is their middle. Allah says: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced community﴾ [2:143], meaning best and most just. He also says: ﴿The most moderate of them said﴾ [68:28], meaning the best and most excellent of them. An Arab bedouin praised the Prophet (ﷺ) saying:

*"O the most central of people in all their glories,
and the most generous of people in mothers and fathers."* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/2098]

The scholars differed concerning the middle prayer and which prayer it is. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning it in this manner," and he interlaced his fingers. Some said: it is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). This is the view of Muʿādh, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād. It is narrated from Mūsā ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abū Umāma, when asked about the middle prayer, say: "I do not think it is other than the dawn prayer." Maʿmar ibn Ṭāwūs narrated from his father, and Ismāʿīl ibn Shurūs from ʿIkrima, both said: "It is the dawn prayer, meaning the middle prayer." This is the choice of Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shāfiʿī. Evidence for this is what al-Rabīʿ narrated from Abū al-ʿĀliya, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they finished, he said: "I asked them: Which of the prayers is the middle prayer? They said: The one you have just prayed." It is also said: because it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "It is the dawn prayer. It was made the middle, so it lies between night and day. It is prayed in the darkness of night and the brightness of day. It is the greatest of the prayers in that people miss it. It is also not shortened and not combined with another prayer, and it lies between two prayers that are combined." Confirmation of this interpretation from the revelation, which indicates specification and excellence, is His saying: ﴿and the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [17:78], meaning that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, recorded in the register of the night and the register of the day. Another evidence from the context of the verse is that He follows it with: ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [2:238], meaning: stand for Allah in it, devoutly obedient. They said: there is no obligatory prayer in which qunūt (devout standing) is performed except the dawn prayer, so it is known that this is the one. In it is evidence for the establishment of qunūt.

Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī said: "Ibn ʿAbbās led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Basra. He performed qunūt before the bowing and raised his hands. When he finished he said: This is the middle prayer that we were commanded to stand in devoutly obedient." The evidence for this is what Ḥanẓala narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt for a month, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to perform qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world."

Ibn Abī Layla narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar until he died, and ʿUthmān until he died, and ʿAlī until he died."

Others said: it is the noon prayer (ṣalāt al-ẓuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿĀʾisha.

ʿUrwa narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at the time of midday heat (al-hājira), and it was the heaviest of the prayers upon his companions, so that behind him there would only be a row or two rows, and most people would be in their afternoon rest (qā'ila) and in their trade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I had intended to burn the houses of people who do not attend the prayer." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾.

Their evidence that it is the middle of the day is what Abū Dharr narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has a gate in the lowest heaven through which the sun passes. When the sun declines, everything glorifies our Lord, and Allah commanded the prayer at that hour. It is the hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and they are not closed until the noon prayer is prayed, and supplication is answered at it."

Also because it is the middle of the day's prayers. Among its distinctions is that it was the first prayer made obligatory, and it was the first prayer toward which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions turned to the Kaʿba. It is also the one on account of which all prayers and congregations are lifted on Friday.

Some said: it is the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). This is the view of ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿī, Zurr ibn Ḥubaysh, Qatāda, Abū Ayyūb, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and Muqātil, and the choice of Abū Ḥanīfa. Evidence for this is what al-Ḥasan narrated from Samura ibn Jundub, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

It is mentioned in some reports that it is the one about which Sulaymān (peace be upon him) was negligent.

Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib who said: "The verse ﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾ was revealed, and the afternoon prayer was recited by us during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it (nasakhahā) with ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Someone said to him: "So it is the afternoon prayer?" He said: "Did I inform you how it was revealed and how it was abrogated? And Allah knows best."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ḥafṣa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me so that I may tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." When he informed her, she said: "Write: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer."

Hishām narrated from ʿUrwa from his father who said: "In the copy of ʿĀʾisha was: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾." Likewise used to recite it Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from ʿAlī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb): "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May Allah fill their houses, or their graves, with fire."

He said: then he prayed it between the two evening prayers.

In some reports, a man said in the assembly of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar sent me, when I was a small boy, to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my small finger and said: 'This is the dawn prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the noon prayer.' Then he folded the thumb and said: 'This is the sunset prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the night prayer.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'The afternoon prayer.' He said: 'It is the afternoon prayer.'"

They said: it is also because it lies between the two day prayers and the two night prayers. The Prophet (ﷺ) was lenient, so he prayed it and emphasised it.

Abū Tamīm al-Ḥabashānī narrated from Abū Baṣra al-Ghifārī who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer with us, and when he finished he said: 'This prayer was made obligatory upon those before you, and they were lax in it and abandoned it. Whoever among you prays it and guards it will be given its reward twice, and there is no prayer after it until the witness appears.'" The witness is the star.

Abū Qilāba narrated from Abū al-Muhājir from Buraida who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds are nullified."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer, it suffices him regarding his family and his wealth."

Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb said: "It is the sunset prayer. Do you not see that it is a middle prayer, neither the least nor the most in number, and it is not shortened during travel, and it is the odd-numbered prayer (witr) of the day?"

Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father from ʿĀʾisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent of the prayers is the sunset prayer. Allah did not remove it from the traveller or the resident. Through it Allah opens the night prayer and closes the day. Whoever prays the sunset prayer and then prays two rak'as after it, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise. Whoever prays four rak'as after it, Allah forgives him the sins of twenty years, or he said forty years."

Shaykh Abū Maytham Sahl ibn Muḥammad related from some people that it is the last night prayer (al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhira), and he said: "Because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the night prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for half the night, and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for the whole night."

Some said: it is one of the five prayers, and we do not know its specific identity. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was asked about the middle prayer, and he said to the questioner: "[Are you eager] that if I teach you it, you will guard it and neglect the rest?" He said: "No." He said: "If you guard all of them, you have guarded it." This was also said by Abū Bakr al-Warrāq, who said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed, He would have made it clear. But He, glorified be He, wanted to alert the creation to performing the prayers."

Al-Thaʿlabī said: "Both of these two views are excellent. Allah, exalted be He, concealed the middle prayer among all the obligatory prayers so that they would guard all of them in hope of hitting the middle, just as He concealed the Night of Power among the nights of Ramadan, His greatest Name among all the names, and the hour of response among the hours of Friday, as wisdom from Him in His doing and mercy upon His creation."

In His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and the middle prayer﴾ there is evidence that the witr prayer is not obligatory. This is because the Muslims agreed that the obligatory prayers are fewer than seven and more than three, and among the numbers between three and seven there is no odd number except five, and even numbers have no middle. So it is established that it is five.

Qatāda narrated from Anas who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how many prayers has Allah made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "Five prayers." He asked: "Is there anything before them or after them that Allah has made obligatory upon His servants?" He said: "No." The man swore by Allah that he would neither add to them nor subtract from them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If the man is truthful, he will enter Paradise."

It is narrated from Ṭalḥa ibn ʿUbayd Allāh who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the people of Najd, with dishevelled hair, his voice heard but he could not be understood, until he came close and it became clear that he was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Five prayers in the day and night." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And fasting the month of Ramadan." He said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." He mentioned to him the zakat, and he said: "Is there anything else obligatory upon me?" He said: "No, unless you voluntarily do more." Then the man turned away saying: "By Allah, I will neither add to this nor subtract from it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He will prosper if he is truthful."

It is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Ḥayyān from Ibn Jarīr that a man from the tribe of Kināna called al-Muḥdajī used to hear a man in Syria, known as Abū Muḥammad, say: "The witr is obligatory." Al-Muḥdajī said: "I went to ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit and waylaid him as he was going to the mosque, and I told him what Abū Muḥammad had said. ʿUbāda said: 'Abū Muḥammad lied. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Five prayers Allah has prescribed for the servants. Whoever comes with them, not neglecting any of them out of disregard for their right, has a covenant with Allah that He will admit him to Paradise. Whoever does not come with them has no covenant with Allah. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will admit him to Paradise."'"

It is narrated from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The witr is not obligatory, because there is no takbīr in it, but it is a sunna which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established." The evidence that the witr is not obligatory is what Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to perform the witr on his mount. Nāfiʿ also narrated that Ibn ʿUmar used to perform the witr on his camel, and mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to do that. The jurists agreed that an obligatory prayer on a mount in a state of safety is not valid.

﴿And stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: obedient. This was said by al-Shaʿbī, ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir ibn Zayd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs and Ibn ʿAbbās through the narration of ʿIkrima, ʿAṭiyya and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muqātil and al-Kalbī said: for every people of a religion there is a prayer in which they stand while disobedient, so stand you in your prayers for Allah in obedience. The evidence for this interpretation is what Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Every qunūt in the two midday prayers is obedience."

Some said: qunūt is silence regarding what it is not permissible to speak in the prayer. Zayd ibn Arqam said: "We used to speak during the prayer in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of us would speak to the person beside him, and a comer would enter and greet, and they would return the greeting, and he would ask them: 'How many [rak'as] have you prayed?' and they would reply telling him how many they had prayed. A man's servant would come while he was praying and speak to him about his need, like the practice of the People of the Book. We continued like this until ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ was revealed, and we were commanded to silence and forbidden to speak."

Mujāhid said: "Humble (khāshiʿīn)." He said: "Among qunūt is prolonging the bowing, lowering the gaze, stillness and lowering the wing. The scholars, when one of them stood to pray, would be so awed before the Most Merciful that he would not turn, nor move pebbles, nor fidget with anything, nor occupy his mind with any matter of this world, except inadvertently."

Al-Ḥasan and al-Rabīʿ said: "Standing in the prayer." Evidence for this is the hadith of Jābir that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which prayer is best?" He said: "Long qunūt."

Ibn ʿAbbās, in a narration from Rajāʾ, said: "Supplicating in their prayer." The evidence is that the Prophet (ﷺ) performed qunūt against a man and mentioned that whatever supplication was against them [was made]. It was said: "Praying." The evidence is His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night﴾ [39:9], meaning one who prays. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the one who strives in the cause of Allah is like the one who is devoutly obedient, fasting," meaning the one who prays and fasts.

﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾, meaning: on foot. It is said: rājil and rijāl, like ṣāḥib and ṣiḥāb, ṣā'im and ṣiyām, qā'im and qiyām. Allah says: ﴿they will come to you on foot﴾ [22:27]. Al-Akhṭal said:

*"The sons of Ghadāna, their eyes fixed,
walking beneath their bellies on foot."* [Tāj al-ʿArūs: 7/336]

It is reported that they bent down as captives, with their eyes fixed upon their children. ﴿Or riding﴾ upon their mounts, which is the plural of rākib (rider). Al-Mufaḍḍal said: "Rākib is only said of the owner of a camel. The owner of a horse is called fāris, the rider of a donkey is ḥammār, the rider of a mule is baghghāl." The word is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), meaning: pray on foot or riding.

The meaning of the verse: if you cannot pray devoutly obedient, observing the prayer in its full rights because of fear, then pray on foot, that is, walking on your feet, or riding on the backs of your mounts; that will suffice you.

The commentators said: this applies to the situation of pursuit and flight. One prays wherever he turns, facing the qibla or not, riding or on foot, and makes the prostration lower than the bowing, signalling with gestures. This is the prayer of extreme fear. Prayer in a state of fear is of two kinds, and we will mention them in Surat al-Nisā'. The prayer of extreme fear is this one. The fear which permits the worshipper to pray on horseback or on foot, wherever his direction is, is that of fighting and pursuit, the fighting against an enemy or a warrior, or the fear of a raging beast, an attacking camel, or a flowing torrent, or where the most likely outcome is destruction. If he prays the prayer of safety, he is permitted to pray the prayer of extreme fear, which is two rak'as. If he prays it as one rak'a, that is permitted, because of what Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet: four in residence, two when travelling, and one in fear."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: "If you are in battle, and the two armies meet, and people strike one another, then say: 'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is greatest,' and remember Allah, and that is your prayer." al-Zuhrī said: "If he is unable, he should not leave off its remembrance in his heart."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 238–242 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then when you are secure, remember God,﴾ that is, perform the five prayers in full, observing their requirements, ﴿as He taught you what you did not know.﴾ ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind,﴾ addressing the men, ﴿and who leave wives behind﴾ meaning wives.

Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs most often say "zawjah" (wife) for a woman, but in the Qur'an it is "zawj" (spouse).

﴿A bequest for their wives﴾ — al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Abu 'Amir, al-A'mash and Hamzah read "waṣiyyatan" in the accusative, meaning: "let them bequeath a bequest." The rest read it in the nominative, meaning: "the bequest is prescribed for them." It is also said that the meaning is "for their wives is a bequest," and it is said: "let there be a bequest." The evidence for this reading is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "A bequest has been prescribed for them, for their wives."

And Ubayy read: "and leave wives, a provision for their wives." Abu 'Ubayd said: Yet we have found this meaning, all of it, in the Qur'an in the nominative, such as His saying ﴿half of what you have decreed﴾ and ﴿a payment of blood money delivered﴾ and similar.

"Matā'an" (provision) is in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning: "provide for them a provision." It is also said: God, Mighty and Majestic, made that a provision for them. It is also said it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative governed by the bequest, like His saying ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger an orphan﴾. "Al-matā'" means maintenance for a year for her food and clothing, or her housing, or what she needs. ﴿Without expulsion, for a full year﴾ — "ghayra ikhrāj" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state. It is also said it is in the accusative by removing the preposition, meaning: "without expulsion."

As for the interpretation of the verse and its ruling:

Ibn 'Abbas and the rest of the exegetes said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the people of al-Ta'if called Hakim ibn al-Harith, who emigrated to Medina. He had children, and his parents and his wife were with him. He died, and the matter was referred to the Prophet ﷺ, so God the Exalted revealed this verse. The Messenger of God ﷺ gave his parents and children from his inheritance, and did not give his wife anything, except that he commanded them to maintain her from the estate of her husband for a year.

This was because when a man died and left a wife, she would observe a year's waiting period in her husband's house without leaving it. When the year was over, she would leave and throw a dung-pellet at a dog, meaning by this that her sitting after her husband was easier for her than a dung-pellet thrown at a dog. The poets also mentioned this in their verse. Labid said:

"And the widows when their year stretches long."

Her lodging and maintenance were obligatory from her husband's property for this year, as long as she did not leave. That was her share of her husband's estate, and she had no inheritance. If she left her husband's house, she had no maintenance. The man would bequeath this. It remained so until the verse of inheritance was revealed, and God abrogated the year's maintenance by the quarter and the eighth, and abrogated the year's waiting period by His saying ﴿who wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

God the Exalted said ﴿But if they leave﴾, meaning of their own accord, before the year is over, without being expelled by the heirs, ﴿then there is no blame upon you, O guardians of the deceased, for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable﴾, meaning their desire for marriage. Regarding the meaning of lifting blame from the men for the women's action, there are two views:

The first: there is no blame on you in cutting off maintenance from them if they leave before the year is complete.

The second: there is no blame on you in not preventing them from leaving, because their remaining for a year in their husband's house was not obligatory upon them. God gave them the choice in this until four months and ten days abrogated it, for if it had been obligatory upon her, it would not have been permissible for the husband's guardians to prevent her from that. So God lifted the blame from them and from her, and permitted her to leave if she wished. Then the maintenance was abrogated by inheritance, and the year's stay by four months and ten days. ﴿And God is Mighty and Wise.﴾

﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing.﴾ We have already discussed the ruling on provision at length, so there is no need to repeat it. It was mentioned again here because it adds a meaning not found elsewhere: what came before explains the ruling for a divorced woman who has not been touched, whereas here it explains the ruling for all divorced women regarding provision.

Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed because when God revealed His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ up to His saying ﴿upon the good-doers﴾, a man among the Muslims said: "If I do good, I will do it, and if I do not wish to, I will not do it." God the Exalted said ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾, meaning the believing God-fearing ones who avoid polytheism, clarifying that every divorced woman has a provision. We have already mentioned the disagreement concerning it.

Ayyas ibn 'Amir narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) who said: "Every believing divorced woman, free or a slave, has a provision," and he recited ﴿For divorced women there is provision in kindness﴾ — the verse.

﴿Thus God makes clear to you His signs, that you may understand.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 238–242 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾, meaning: be constant and persistent in the obligatory prayers, performing them at their appointed times, observing their limits, their bowing (rukū'), their prostrations (sujūd), their standing (qiyām) and their sitting (qu'ūd), and all that is required of them in their rights. Every prayer in the Qur'an that is joined with the command to guard is intended to refer to the five daily prayers. Then He singled out the middle prayer from among them for special guarding, as a indication of its excellence, like His saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers, and Jibril and Mikal﴾ [2:98]. These two are part of the angels, yet they were singled out by mention. And His saying: ﴿In them are fruit and date-palms and pomegranates﴾ [55:68]. He singled them out from the whole by the conjunction "and," which indicates specification and detail. Likewise is His saying: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾.

ʿĀ'isha read ﴿wa-l-ṣalāta l-wusṭā﴾ with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (ighrā'). Qālūn narrated from Nāfiʿ that he read al-wuṣṭā with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭā' (in al-wusṭā), since the two belong to the same class. Both are dialectal variants, like aṣ-ṣirāṭ and as-sirāṭ, aṣ-ṣidgh and as-sidgh, al-biṣāq and al-bisāq, al-lu ṣūq and al-lusūq, aṣ-ṣundūq and as-sundūq, aṣ-ṣaqr and as-saqr.

Al-wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ (the middle). The "middle" (wasṭ) of a thing is its best and most just part, because the best of affairs is their middle. Allah says: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced community﴾ [2:143], meaning best and most just. He also says: ﴿The most moderate of them said﴾ [68:28], meaning the best and most excellent of them. An Arab bedouin praised the Prophet (ﷺ) saying:

*"O the most central of people in all their glories,
and the most generous of people in mothers and fathers."* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/2098]

The scholars differed concerning the middle prayer and which prayer it is. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) differed concerning it in this manner," and he interlaced his fingers. Some said: it is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). This is the view of Muʿādh, ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrima, al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād. It is narrated from Mūsā ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abū Umāma, when asked about the middle prayer, say: "I do not think it is other than the dawn prayer." Maʿmar ibn Ṭāwūs narrated from his father, and Ismāʿīl ibn Shurūs from ʿIkrima, both said: "It is the dawn prayer, meaning the middle prayer." This is the choice of Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shāfiʿī. Evidence for this is what al-Rabīʿ narrated from Abū al-ʿĀliya, that he prayed the morning prayer with the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and when they finished, he said: "I asked them: Which of the prayers is the middle prayer? They said: The one you have just prayed." It is also said: because it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "It is the dawn prayer. It was made the middle, so it lies between night and day. It is prayed in the darkness of night and the brightness of day. It is the greatest of the prayers in that people miss it. It is also not shortened and not combined with another prayer, and it lies between two prayers that are combined." Confirmation of this interpretation from the revelation, which indicates specification and excellence, is His saying: ﴿and the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [17:78], meaning that it is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, recorded in the register of the night and the register of the day. Another evidence from the context of the verse is that He follows it with: ﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾ [2:238], meaning: stand for Allah in it, devoutly obedient. They said: there is no obligatory prayer in which qunūt (devout standing) is performed except the dawn prayer, so it is known that this is the one. In it is evidence for the establishment of qunūt.

Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī said: "Ibn ʿAbbās led us in the dawn prayer in the mosque of Basra. He performed qunūt before the bowing and raised his hands. When he finished he said: This is the middle prayer that we were commanded to stand in devoutly obedient." The evidence for this is what Ḥanẓala narrated from Anas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt for a month, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to perform qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world."

Ibn Abī Layla narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunūt until he died, and Abū Bakr until he died, and ʿUmar until he died, and ʿUthmān until he died, and ʿAlī until he died."

Others said: it is the noon prayer (ṣalāt al-ẓuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thābit, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Usāma ibn Zayd and ʿĀʾisha.

ʿUrwa narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at the time of midday heat (al-hājira), and it was the heaviest of the prayers upon his companions, so that behind him there would only be a row or two rows, and most people would be in their afternoon rest (qā'ila) and in their trade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I had intended to burn the houses of people who do not attend the prayer." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾.

Their evidence that it is the middle of the day is what Abū Dharr narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has a gate in the lowest heaven through which the sun passes. When the sun declines, everything glorifies our Lord, and Allah commanded the prayer at that hour. It is the hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and they are not closed until the noon prayer is prayed, and supplication is answered at it."

Also because it is the middle of the day's prayers. Among its distinctions is that it was the first prayer made obligatory, and it was the first prayer toward which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions turned to the Kaʿba. It is also the one on account of which all prayers and congregations are lifted on Friday.

Some said: it is the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). This is the view of ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Hurayra, al-Nakhaʿī, Zurr ibn Ḥubaysh, Qatāda, Abū Ayyūb, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and Muqātil, and the choice of Abū Ḥanīfa. Evidence for this is what al-Ḥasan narrated from Samura ibn Jundub, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

It is mentioned in some reports that it is the one about which Sulaymān (peace be upon him) was negligent.

Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib who said: "The verse ﴿Guard strictly the prayers﴾ was revealed, and the afternoon prayer was recited by us during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it (nasakhahā) with ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." Someone said to him: "So it is the afternoon prayer?" He said: "Did I inform you how it was revealed and how it was abrogated? And Allah knows best."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ḥafṣa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me so that I may tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." When he informed her, she said: "Write: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer."

Hishām narrated from ʿUrwa from his father who said: "In the copy of ʿĀʾisha was: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾." Likewise used to recite it Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from ʿAlī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Aḥzāb): "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May Allah fill their houses, or their graves, with fire."

He said: then he prayed it between the two evening prayers.

In some reports, a man said in the assembly of ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Marwān: "Abū Bakr and ʿUmar sent me, when I was a small boy, to the Prophet (ﷺ) to ask him about the middle prayer. He took my small finger and said: 'This is the dawn prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the noon prayer.' Then he folded the thumb and said: 'This is the sunset prayer.' Then he folded the one next to it and said: 'This is the night prayer.' Then he said: 'Which of your fingers remains?' I said: 'The middle one.' He said: 'Which prayer remains?' I said: 'The afternoon prayer.' He said: 'It is the afternoon prayer.'"

They said: it is also because it lies between the two day prayers and the two night prayers. The Prophet (ﷺ) was lenient, so he prayed it and emphasised it.

Abū Tamīm al-Ḥabashānī narrated from Abū Baṣra al-Ghifārī who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed the afternoon prayer with us, and when he finished he said: 'This prayer was made obligatory upon those before you, and they were lax in it and abandoned it. Whoever among you prays it and guards it will be given its reward twice, and there is no prayer after it until the witness appears.'" The witness is the star.

Abū Qilāba narrated from Abū al-Muhājir from Buraida who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hasten to the prayer on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the afternoon prayer, his deeds are nullified."

Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer, it suffices him regarding his family and his wealth."

Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb said: "It is the sunset prayer. Do you not see that it is a middle prayer, neither the least nor the most in number, and it is not shortened during travel, and it is the odd-numbered prayer (witr) of the day?"

Hishām ibn ʿUrwa narrated from his father from ʿĀʾisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most excellent of the prayers is the sunset prayer. Allah did not remove it from the traveller or the resident. Through it Allah opens the night prayer and closes the day. Whoever prays the sunset prayer and then prays two rak'as after it, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise. Whoever prays four rak'as after it, Allah forgives him the sins of twenty years, or he said forty years."

Shaykh Abū Maytham Sahl ibn Muḥammad related from some people that it is the last night prayer (al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhira), and he said: "Because it lies between two prayers that are not shortened."

ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿUmar narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Whoever prays the night prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for half the night, and whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation is as one who stands in prayer for the whole night."

Some said: it is one of the five prayers, and we do not know its specific identity. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym was asked about the middle prayer, and he said to the questioner: "[Are you eager] that if I teach you it, you will guard it and neglect the rest?" He said: "No." He said: "If you guard all of them, you have guarded it." This was also said by Abū Bakr al-Warrāq, who said: "If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had willed, He would have made it clear. But He, glorified be He, wanted to alert the creation to performing the prayers."

Al-Thaʿlabī said: "Both of these two views are excellent.
