Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 265–267:

﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah﴾ — seeking the pleasure of Allah — ﴿and as a reinforcement from their own souls﴾. Al-Sha'bi, al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: meaning, confirmation from their own selves; they pay zakat willingly, their souls being content with it, knowing that what they gave out is better for them than what they kept back.

Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Rawq, Ibn Zayd and al-Mufaddal said: with certainty that Allah will replace it for them. Qatadah said: seeking reward with faith from themselves. ʿAta' and Mujahid said: ﴿mutharrabun﴾ (firmly established), meaning they do not waste their wealth. Mujahid also read it as ﴿wa-tathbitan li-anfusihim﴾ (and to make firm for their souls).

Al-Hasan said: when a man intended to give charity, he made sure (tathabbut); if it was for Allah, he gave; if anything else mixed into it, he withheld. According to this view, the tathbit (تثبيت) carries the meaning of tathabbut (تثبت), like the words of the Exalted: ﴿wa-tabattal ilayhi tabtila﴾ [[Surah al-Muzzammil: 8.]], meaning tabattulan (devotion).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik said: a lightening of their sins. Ibn Kaysan said: sincerity, and settling their souls to obey Allah the Exalted in their expenditures. Al-Zajjaj said: they spend while acknowledging that Allah the Exalted is watchful over them.

The origin of this word is from the saying of the questioner: "Thabata fulan fi hadha al-amr" (so-and-so was firm in this matter) when he verified it, and "thabata 'alayhi" and his resolve was strong and he was powerful in it by himself.

﴿Fa-thabbata Allahu ma atakа min husn... tathbit Musa wa-nasran ka-alladhi nasaru﴾ [[Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/276.]]

﴿Like the example of a garden﴾, i.e., an orchard (bustan). Al-Farra' said: if there are palm trees in the orchard, it is a janna, and if it is vines, it is a firdaws.

As for Mujahid's statement, "kamathali habbatin" (with ḥā' and bā'), ﴿upon a height﴾ (bi-rabwah): al-Sulami, al-ʿAtaridi, al-Hasan, ʿAsim and Ibn ʿAmir read ﴿bi-rabwatin﴾ with a fatha on the rā' here and in Surat al-Mu'minun, and this is the dialect of the Banu Tamim.

Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi', Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read it with a ḍamma on the rā' in both places. Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd chose this, because it is the most complete and most well-known of the dialects; and Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i and Ibn Abi Ishaq read ﴿bi-rabwah﴾. Ashhab al-'Uqayli read ﴿bi-rabawah﴾ with an alif and a kasra on the rā'. All of them mean a raised, level place where rivers flow and which does not lack water. It was called rabwah because it grew and rose high (rabat wa-tayyabat wa-'alat), from the saying "raba al-shay'u yarbu" when a thing swells and grows large. He placed it on a rabwah because vegetation on it is finest and most pure.

﴿Which a heavy rain struck﴾ — intense, abundant rain — ﴿so it brought forth its produce twofold﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿ukulaha﴾ with a light pronunciation, while the rest read it with emphasis; it means the fruit.

Al-Mufaddal said: the ukl is the abundance of what is in a thing by which it is improved and strengthened; it is said, "a garment of abundant ukl," meaning of abundant spinning. Its meaning: it gave its fruit twofold, and the "double" refers to the load.

ʿAta' said: it bore in one season of spring what others bear in two years. ʿIkrimah said: it bore twice a year.

﴿But if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain (tall)﴾, i.e., a drizzle, which is the weakest and gentlest rain.

Al-Suddi said: it is the dew.

Abu Salam ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salam, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His words ﴿but if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain﴾, said: it is the land of Egypt; if rain does not strike it, it still yields well, and if rain strikes it, it is weakened. This is a parable God the Exalted struck for the deed of the sincere believer. He says: just as this garden yields in every condition and does not fail or disappoint its owner, whether the rain is little or much, so Allah the Exalted multiplies the reward of the sincere believer's charity, who neither reminds nor injures, whether his expenditure and charity are small or great; it is never disappointed in any state.

﴿And Allah is seeing of what you do.﴾ ﴿Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾. This verse is connected to His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and injury﴾ — the verse: ﴿Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow; for him therein is every kind of fruit, and old age has overtaken him﴾. He said ﴿aṣābahu﴾ (it struck him) in the past tense in response to the future, because the Arabs say "waddadtu" once with "law" which is in the past tense, saying "waddadtu law dhahabat ʿanna" (I wished that you had gone from us), and once with "an" which is for the future, saying "waddadtu an tadhhaba ʿanna" (I wish that you would go from us). "Law" and "an" are both verbs with the sense of a conditional. Do you not see that the Arabs, when they combined "law" and "an," the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever evil it has done, it wishes that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [[Surat Al ʿImran: 30.]] — the verse, just as they combine "ma" and "an," and both are negation.

The poet said:

*Mā an raʾaytu wa-lā samiʿtu bi-mithlihi / ka-l-yawmi ṭāli ʾaynuqin jarab*
*(I have neither seen nor heard of its like / like today, the she-camels mangy...)* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/267, where it reads "sami'tu bihi" instead of "sami'tu bi-mithlihi."]]

Since that is permissible, it is acceptable to say "fa'ala" with the sense of "yaf'alu," and "yaf'alu" with the sense of "fa'ala," and to pronounce "law" in place of "an" and "an" in place of "law."

So the meaning of the verse: ﴿Would any of you wish that he had a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, for him therein every kind of fruit, and old age has overtaken him, and he has weak offspring, so a whirlwind struck it, which is the violent wind that blows from the earth to the sky like a column.﴾

Al-Kumayt said:

*[Tusaddi al-riyāḥu bihā dhayla wa-tulḥimuhu / dhā maʿtawin min daqīq al-turbi mawwār / fī minkhalin jāʾa min hayfin yamāniyyihi / bi-l-sāfiyāti wa-fī ghirbālin iʿṣār]*

Its plural is aʿasir.

Yazid ibn al-Miqra' al-Himyari said:

*Unāsun ajārūnā wa-kāna jiwāruhum / aʿāṣīru min Fasw al-ʿIrāq al-mubaddhar*

[[Fasw is a tribe of ʿAbd al-Qays; in al-Aghani it is "Qasw."]]

This is a parable God the Exalted struck for the expenditure of the hypocrite who shows off. He says: the deed of this showoff appears good to him for the time of the garden, so he benefits from it as the owner of the garden benefits from it. But when he grows old and weak, and has small children, a whirlwind strikes his garden, ﴿in which is fire, so it is burned﴾. He has spent on it and is too weak to repair it because of his age, and his children are too weak to repair it because of their youth; and he himself does not find what he could return to his children, nor do his children find what they could return to their father; so he and his children are left in poverty and helplessness, bewildered, unable to find any remedy. Likewise, Allah voids the deeds of this hypocrite and showoff at a time when there is no one to seek forgiveness for him, no repentance and no pardon, from their examples and their debts.

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: [I struck a parable for the deed that begins and does good deeds, so it becomes a parable for the garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, for him therein every kind of fruit; then he does evil at the end of his life], and continues in the evil until he dies upon it; so the whirlwind in which is fire that burned the garden becomes a parable for his evil by which he died [upon it] [[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 1/340 and Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/106; the bracketed text is from it.]].

﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, that you may give thought.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things⁠﴾ — give charity from the best and finest — similar to His saying: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾ [[Al ʿImran: 92.]]. Ibn Mas'ud and Mujahid said: lawful things, as evidence for His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ [[Surat al-Mu'minun: 51.]].

﴿O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 172.]].

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has divided your characters among you as He has divided your provisions among you, and Allah is good and accepts only what is good. A servant does not earn wealth from what is unlawful and then give charity from it, and it is accepted from him, nor does he spend from it, and it is blessed for him, nor does he leave it behind his back except that it becomes his provision to the Fire. And evil is not erased by evil, but evil is erased by good; the wicked does not erase the wicked." [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/387 and Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/53, with variation.]]

﴿What you have earned﴾ — through trade and craft — of gold and silver.

ʿUbayd ibn Rifa'ah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said: "O assembly of merchants, you are wicked, except one who fears Allah, and is righteous and truthful, and said [this and this and this]." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 2/191.]]

Qays ibn ʿUrwah al-Ghifari said: We were in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah, calling ourselves "al-samasirah" (brokers), and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named us with a name better than our name, and said: "O assembly of merchants, this selling is attended by idle talk, lying and oaths, so mix it with charity." [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/6.]]

Makhul, from Abu Umamah, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Goodness is of ten parts, the best of which is trade when one takes what is due and gives what is due."

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Nine-tenths of provision is in trade, and the remaining part is in the saba' [[al-Sabaya': offspring/produce; it is said to be the water that flows over the head of a newborn, and it is said to be the membrane in which it is born. See Gharib al-Hadith 1/299.]] [[al-Nihayah: 2/341.]]."

Ibn Juraij, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let these clients not overcome you in trade, for blessing is in trade, and its owner does not become poor, except the merchant who swears much and is contemptible."

ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, said: A dirham from trade is dearer to me than ten from my stipend.

Al-Aʿmash, from Abu Ibrahim, from ʿAishah, said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best a man eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings." [192] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/42.]]

Sa'id ibn ʿUmayr said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked: Which earning of a man is best?

He said: "A man's work with his hand, and every sale that is accepted (mabrur)."

Muhammad ibn al-Radibi said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i passed by a woman from Mazad who was spinning at her door, and he said: "O Umm Bakr, have you not grown old? Is it not time for you to give this up?" She said: "How can I give it up when I have heard ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) say: it is from the good provision."

﴿And from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾ — meaning the grains and fruits that are eaten and stored, of which zakat is due.

ʿUmar ibn Dinar said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm Maʿbad's orchard and said: "O Umm Maʿbad, who planted this, a Muslim or a disbeliever?" She said: "A Muslim." He said: "A Muslim does not plant a plant from which a person, animal or bird eats except that it is charity for him until the Day of Resurrection." [[Sahih Muslim: 5/28.]]

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAishah: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seek provision in the hidden places of the earth."

Malik ibn Dinar said: I read in the Torah: Blessed is he who eats from the fruit of his own hands.

﴿And do not aim﴾ — Ibn Mas'ud read: "wa-la ta'ammamu" with hamza. Ibn ʿAbbas read: ﴿wa-la tuyammimu﴾ with the first letter ḍamma and the first mim kasra, meaning do not direct yourselves.

Ibn Kathir read: ﴿wa-la tayyammamu﴾ with shadda on the yā' and a fatha on it, in this and its sister forms, which are thirty-one places in the Qur'an, restoring the dropped letter and assimilating it, because originally there are two tā's: the tā' of the addressee and the tā' of the imperative, so the tā' of the verb was dropped.

The rest read: ﴿wa-la tayammamu﴾ with a fatha and light pronunciation.

They are all dialects with one meaning. It is said: "amamtu fulanan," "tayammamtuhu," and "ta'ammamtuhu," meaning I aimed at him and intended him.

Al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays said:

*Tayammamtu Qaysan wa-kam dunahu / min al-ardi min mahmahin dhi shazan*
[[al-Mahmah: a distant desert; dhu shazan: rough; the verse is in Lisan al-ʿArab: 12/23.]]

Al-Suddi, from ʿAli ibn Thabit, from al-Farra', said: This verse was revealed concerning the Ansar, who used to bring out, when the palm harvest was cut from their gardens, bunches of dates and unripe dates, and hang them on a rope between two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the poor emigrants would eat from it. A man would deliberately bring out a cluster of ḥashf [[al-Ḥashf: the worst dates.]], thinking that it would be accepted from him amid the great number of bunches placed there; so this verse was revealed concerning those who did this.

﴿And do not aim at the bad of it to spend from it﴾ — meaning the cluster containing ḥashf; and if it were given to you as a gift, you would not accept it.

From Badhan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding this verse, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Indeed, Allah has a right in your wealth; when the right of Allah in your wealth is reached, give from it." And people used to bring their charities to the people of charity and place them in the mosque; when they were gathered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided them among them.

He said: A man came one day, after the people of the mosque had grown thin and their heads had scattered, with a bunch of ḥashf, and placed it in the charity. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, he saw it and said: "Who brought this bunch of ḥashf?" They said: "We do not know, O Messenger of Allah."

He said: "Evil is what the owner of this ḥashf has done." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: They used to give charity from the worst of their fruits and the dregs of their wealth, setting aside the good for themselves. So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿and do not aim at the bad﴾, meaning the inferior of your wealth, the ḥashf of the dates, the rotten and the darnel of the grains, and the counterfeit dirhams and dinars.

﴿And you would not accept it except with closing your eyes regarding it﴾. The place of "an" is in the accusative by removing the preposition, meaning: unless you close your eyes to it.

Al-Zuhri read: ﴿tughmiḍū﴾ with a fatha on the tā' and a ḍamma on the mim. Al-Hasan read with a fatha on the tā' and a kasra on the mim; both are dialects: ghamiḍa yaghmiḍu and yaghmuḍu. Qatadah read ﴿tughammaḍū﴾ from the tafʿīl form. Abu Majlan read ﴿tughmaḍū﴾ with a fatha on the mim and a ḍamma on the tā', meaning unless it is closed to you. The rest read ﴿tughmiḍū﴾.

Al-Ighmad is lowering the gaze and closing one eyelid over another. Ru'bah said:

*Arraqa ʿaynayya ʿani al-ighmadi / barqun sara fi ʿaridin nahhadi*
[[Arraqahu: kept him awake; ʿarid nahhad: a high cloud. The verse is in Lisan al-ʿArab: 7/1995, where it reads "ʿaynayka ʿan al-ghamad"; similarly in Taj al-ʿArus: 5/63.]]

Here it means permissibility, leniency and indulgence. This is because when a man sees what he dislikes, he closes his eye so as not to see all that is done; then this became common until every overlooking and leniency in sale was called ighmad.

Al-Tirimmah said:

*Lam yaftinaa bi-l-watr qawmun wa-lil-ḍaymi / rijālun yarḍawna bi-l-ighmāḍi*
[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/116.]]

ʿAli and al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib said: The meaning: if one of you had a right over a man and he came to him with this, he would not take it except while seeing that he had overlooked part of his right.

This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Walibi narrated from him: "And you would not accept this bad (thing) if one of you had a right over the other by the reckoning of the good, until you diminish it."

Al-Hasan and Qatadah: If you found it sold in the market, you would not take it at the price of the good unless some of its price were reduced for you.

It is also narrated from al-Farra': If that were given to you as a gift, you would not accept it except with shame before its owner and anger that he sent you what you had no need of. So how do you accept for me what you would not accept for yourselves?! Allah the Exalted informed that the recipients of the shares are partners of the owner of the wealth in his wealth; so if all his wealth is good, they are his partners in the good. But when all the wealth is bad, there is no harm in giving the bad, because the obligation in it is that, unless one volunteers.

﴿And know that Allah is Rich (ghani) beyond your expenditures and charities, Praiseworthy (hamid), praised in His actions.﴾

It is narrated from Ma'bad ibn Minqadh that Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi, companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: If you see me giving charity of the worst of what I have, then cover me and know that I am mad.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 265–267:

﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah﴾ — seeking the pleasure of Allah — ﴿and as a reinforcement from their own souls﴾. Al-Sha'bi, al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: meaning, confirmation from their own selves; they pay zakat willingly, their souls being content with it, knowing that what they gave out is better for them than what they kept back.

Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Rawq, Ibn Zayd and al-Mufaddal said: with certainty that Allah will replace it for them. Qatadah said: seeking reward with faith from themselves. ʿAta' and Mujahid said: ﴿mutharrabun﴾ (firmly established), meaning they do not waste their wealth. Mujahid also read it as ﴿wa-tathbitan li-anfusihim﴾ (and to make firm for their souls).

Al-Hasan said: when a man intended to give charity, he made sure (tathabbut); if it was for Allah, he gave; if anything else mixed into it, he withheld. According to this view, the tathbit (تثبيت) carries the meaning of tathabbut (تثبت), like the words of the Exalted: ﴿wa-tabattal ilayhi tabtila﴾ [[Surah al-Muzzammil: 8.]], meaning tabattulan (devotion).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik said: a lightening of their sins. Ibn Kaysan said: sincerity, and settling their souls to obey Allah the Exalted in their expenditures. Al-Zajjaj said: they spend while acknowledging that Allah the Exalted is watchful over them.

The origin of this word is from the saying of the questioner: "Thabata fulan fi hadha al-amr" (so-and-so was firm in this matter) when he verified it, and "thabata 'alayhi" and his resolve was strong and he was powerful in it by himself.

﴿Fa-thabbata Allahu ma atakа min husn... tathbit Musa wa-nasran ka-alladhi nasaru﴾ [[Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/276.]]

﴿Like the example of a garden﴾, i.e., an orchard (bustan). Al-Farra' said: if there are palm trees in the orchard, it is a janna, and if it is vines, it is a firdaws.

ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Abu Wa'il, said: A dirham from trade is dearer to me than ten from my stipend.

He said: "A man's work with his hand, and every sale that is accepted (mabrur)."

﴿And from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾ — meaning the grains and fruits that are eaten and stored, of which zakat is due.

ʿUmar ibn Dinar said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon Umm Maʿbad's orchard and said: "O Umm Maʿbad, who planted this, a Muslim or a disbeliever?" ﴿And do not aim﴾ — Ibn Mas'ud read: "wa-la ta'ammamu" with hamza. Ibn ʿAbbas read: ﴿wa-la tuyammimu﴾ with the first letter ḍamma and the first mim kasra, meaning do not direct yourselves.

Al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays said:

﴿And do not aim at the bad of it to spend from it﴾ — meaning the cluster containing ḥashf; and if it were given to you as a gift, you would not accept it.

From Badhan, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding this verse, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Indeed, Allah has a right in your wealth; when the right of Allah in your wealth is reached, give from it." And people used to bring their charities to the people of charity and place them in the mosque; when they were gathered, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided them among them.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out, he saw it and said: "Who brought this bunch of ḥashf?" They said: "We do not know, O Messenger of Allah."

He said: "Evil is what the owner of this ḥashf has done." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Ighmad is lowering the gaze and closing one eyelid over another. Ru'bah said:

*Arraqa ʿaynayya ʿani al-ighmadi / barqun sara fi ʿaridin nahhadi*

[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/116.]]

ʿAli and al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib said: The meaning: if one of you had a right over a man and he came to him with this, he would not take it except while seeing that he had overlooked part of his right.

﴿And know that Allah is Rich (ghani) beyond your expenditures and charities, Praiseworthy (hamid), praised in His actions.﴾

It is narrated from Ma'bad ibn Minqadh that Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi, companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: If you see me giving charity of the worst of what I have, then cover me and know that I am mad.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 265–267:

﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah﴾ — seeking the pleasure of Allah — ﴿and as a reinforcement from their own souls﴾. Al-Sha'bi, al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak said: meaning, confirmation from their own selves; they pay zakat willingly, their souls being content with it, knowing that what they gave out is better for them than what they kept back.

Al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Rawq, Ibn Zayd and al-Mufaddal said: with certainty that Allah will replace it for them. Qatadah said: seeking reward with faith from themselves. ʿAta' and Mujahid said: ﴿mutharrabun﴾ (firmly established), meaning they do not waste their wealth. Mujahid also read it as ﴿wa-tathbitan li-anfusihim﴾ (and to make firm for their souls).

Al-Hasan said: when a man intended to give charity, he made sure (tathabbut); if it was for Allah, he gave; if anything else mixed into it, he withheld. According to this view, the tathbit (تثبيت) carries the meaning of tathabbut (تثبت), like the words of the Exalted: ﴿wa-tabattal ilayhi tabtila﴾ [[Surah al-Muzzammil: 8.]], meaning tabattulan (devotion).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik said: a lightening of their sins. Ibn Kaysan said: sincerity, and settling their souls to obey Allah the Exalted in their expenditures. Al-Zajjaj said: they spend while acknowledging that Allah the Exalted is watchful over them.

The origin of this word is from the saying of the questioner: "Thabata fulan fi hadha al-amr" (so-and-so was firm in this matter) when he verified it, and "thabata 'alayhi" and his resolve was strong and he was powerful in it by himself.

﴿Fa-thabbata Allahu ma atakа min husn... tathbit Musa wa-nasran ka-alladhi nasaru﴾ [[Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya: 4/276.]]

﴿Like the example of a garden﴾, i.e., an orchard (bustan). Al-Farra' said: if there are palm trees in the orchard, it is a janna, and if it is vines, it is a firdaws.

As for Mujahid's statement, "kamathali habbatin" (with ḥā' and bā'), ﴿upon a height﴾ (bi-rabwah): al-Sulami, al-ʿAtaridi, al-Hasan, ʿAsim and Ibn ʿAmir read ﴿bi-rabwatin﴾ with a fatha on the rā' here and in Surat al-Mu'minun, and this is the dialect of the Banu Tamim.

Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi', Ibn Kathir, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read it with a ḍamma on the rā' in both places. Abu Hatim and Abu 'Ubayd chose this, because it is the most complete and most well-known of the dialects; and Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i and Ibn Abi Ishaq read ﴿bi-rabwah﴾. Ashhab al-'Uqayli read ﴿bi-rabawah﴾ with an alif and a kasra on the rā'. All of them mean a raised, level place where rivers flow and which does not lack water. It was called rabwah because it grew and rose high (rabat wa-tayyabat wa-'alat), from the saying "raba al-shay'u yarbu" when a thing swells and grows large. He placed it on a rabwah because vegetation on it is finest and most pure.

﴿Which a heavy rain struck﴾ — intense, abundant rain — ﴿so it brought forth its produce twofold﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿ukulaha﴾ with a light pronunciation, while the rest read it with emphasis; it means the fruit.

Al-Mufaddal said: the ukl is the abundance of what is in a thing by which it is improved and strengthened; it is said, "a garment of abundant ukl," meaning of abundant spinning. Its meaning: it gave its fruit twofold, and the "double" refers to the load.

ʿAta' said: it bore in one season of spring what others bear in two years. ʿIkrimah said: it bore twice a year.

﴿But if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain (tall)﴾, i.e., a drizzle, which is the weakest and gentlest rain.

Al-Suddi said: it is the dew.

Abu Salam ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salam, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His words ﴿but if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain﴾, said: it is the land of Egypt; if rain does not strike it, it still yields well, and if rain strikes it, it is weakened. This is a parable God the Exalted struck for the deed of the sincere believer. He says: just as this garden yields in every condition and does not fail or disappoint its owner, whether the rain is little or much, so Allah the Exalted multiplies the reward of the sincere believer's charity, who neither reminds nor injures, whether his expenditure and charity are small or great; it is never disappointed in any state.

﴿And Allah is seeing of what you do.﴾ ﴿Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾. This verse is connected to His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and injury﴾ — the verse: ﴿Would any of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾.

﴿Beneath which rivers flow; for him therein is every kind of fruit, and old age has overtaken him﴾. He said ﴿aṣābahu﴾ (it struck him) in the past tense in response to the future, because the Arabs say "waddadtu" once with "law" which is in the past tense, saying "waddadtu law dhahabat ʿanna" (I wished that you had gone from us), and once with "an" which is for the future, saying "waddadtu an tadhhaba ʿanna" (I wish that you would go from us). "Law" and "an" are both verbs with the sense of a conditional. Do you not see that the Arabs, when they combined "law" and "an," the Exalted said: ﴿And whatever evil it has done, it wishes that between it and that were a great distance﴾ [[Surat Al ʿImran: 30.]] — the verse, just as they combine "ma" and "an," and both are negation.

The poet said:

*Mā an raʾaytu wa-lā samiʿtu bi-mithlihi / ka-l-yawmi ṭāli ʾaynuqin jarab*
*(I have neither seen nor heard of its like / like today, the she-camels mangy...)* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 26/267, where it reads "sami'tu bihi" instead of "sami'tu bi-mithlihi."]]

Since that is permissible, it is acceptable to say "fa'ala" with the sense of "yaf'alu," and "yaf'alu" with the sense of "fa'ala," and to pronounce "law" in place of "an" and "an" in place of "law."

So the meaning of the verse: ﴿Would any of you wish that he had a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, for him therein every kind of fruit, and old age has overtaken him, and he has weak offspring, so a whirlwind struck it, which is the violent wind that blows from the earth to the sky like a column.﴾

Al-Kumayt said:

*[Tusaddi al-riyāḥu bihā dhayla wa-tulḥimuhu / dhā maʿtawin min daqīq al-turbi mawwār / fī minkhalin jāʾa min hayfin yamāniyyihi / bi-l-sāfiyāti wa-fī ghirbālin iʿṣār]*

Its plural is aʿasir.

[[Fasw is a tribe of ʿAbd al-Qays; in al-Aghani it is "Qasw."]]

*"When they slander me with their tongues, I am not one who is weakened by poverty."* [[Taj al-'Arus: 9/334.]]

The meaning of the verse is: Satan frightens you with poverty and tells a man, "Keep your wealth, for if you give charity you will become poor."

﴿God promises you﴾, that is, He rewards you. The promise of God is inspiration and revelation, while the promise of Satan is whispering and imagination.

﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Al-Suddi said: it is prophethood. Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari: wisdom is the Sunnah.

Some people of allusion (*ahl al-ishara*) said: it is divine knowledge. It was said: it is allusion without cause. It was said: it is the witnessing of the Real, Exalted, in all states.

Abu 'Uthman: it is the light that distinguishes between inspiration (*ilham*) and whispering (*waswas*). It was said: it is the stripping of the secret for the arrival of inspiration.

Al-Qasim: that the thought of the Truth judges over you, and your desire does not judge over you.

Bundar ibn al-Husayn, when asked about God's saying ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾, said: "Quickness of response together with correctness of the right answer." The lexicographers said: every excellence that draws you, whether in speech or deed, and it is the judgments of the excelled thing.

[ ... ] [[Illegible word in the manuscript.]] Wisdom is returning to what is correct, and the wisdom of the animal (*hikmat al-dabba*, the bridle) derives from this, because it returns it to the straight path.

Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah said: I heard the Kitabi say: "Indeed God sent the messengers with sincere counsel for the souls of His creatures. Ya'qub recited *wa man yu'ti* with a kasra on the *ta'*, meaning "whom God gives it to." The rest recited *wa man yu'ta* with a fatha on the *ta'*, as a passive verb.

*Man* is in the nominative position as the subject of the passive verb that has not named its agent, and *al-hikmah* is its predicate. Al-Hasan ibn Dinar reported from al-Hasan concerning God's saying ﴿whoever is given wisdom﴾: it is scrupulousness (*wara'*) in the religion of God, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿then he has been given much good﴾. ﴿And none remember (*yadhdhakkaru*, take heed) except those of understanding﴾, meaning those of intellect. *Al-lubb* is the intellect that is free from the impulses of desire.

﴿And whatever expense you spend﴾, in what God has obligated upon you, ﴿or whatever vow you vow﴾, or what you have made obligatory upon yourselves, and then fulfilled.

﴿indeed God knows it﴾, and preserves it until He recompenses you for it. Whoever puts a kasra on the *nun* and the *'ayn* makes the kasra follow the kasra, so that two sukuns do not meet: the sukun of the *'ayn* and the sukun of the assimilation.

﴿And if you conceal them﴾, you keep them secret, ﴿and give them to the poor﴾ in secret, ﴿then it is better for you﴾ and more excellent. Every charity is accepted when the intention is sincere, but secret charity is better.

﴿God promises you﴾, that is, He rewards you. The promise of God is inspiration and revelation, while the promise of Satan is whispering and imagination.

﴿forgiveness from Him for your sins and bounty﴾, that is, provision and replacement. ﴿God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning Rich and Knowing. It is said that it is written in the Torah: "My servant, spend from My provision, and I will extend to you from My bounty."

﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾. Al-Suddi said: it is prophethood. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and Abu al-'Aliyah said: it is knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated verses (*nasikh wa mansukh*; *naskh* means abrogation), its clear and ambiguous verses, its earlier and later parts, and its lawful and unlawful matters.

Al-Dahhak said: it is the Qur'an and the judgment in it. He said: "In the Qur'an there are one hundred and nine abrogating and abrogated verses, and a thousand [verses] [[In the manuscript: verses.]] of the lawful and unlawful. The believers may not neglect them until they learn them and teach them. Do not be like the people of Nahrawan, who interpreted verses of the Qur'an concerning the People of the Qibla, though they were revealed concerning the People of the Book. They were ignorant of their knowledge, so they shed blood by them, testified against us with misguidance, and plundered wealth. So hold fast to the knowledge of the Qur'an, for whoever knows what has been revealed, nothing in it will be disputed by him, and he benefits and is benefited."

Mujahid said: "Indeed, it is not prophethood, but it is the Qur'an, knowledge and understanding (*fiqh*)."

Ibn Abi Najih narrated: it is correctness in speech and deed. Ibn Zayd: intellect. Ibn al-Muqaffa': every saying or deed whose soundness intellect bears witness to. Ibrahim: understanding. 'Ata': knowledge of God, Mighty and Majestic. Rabi': fear of God.

Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tustari: wisdom is the Sunnah.

Some people of allusion (*ahl al-ishara*) said: it is divine knowledge. It was said: it is allusion without cause. It was said: it is the witnessing of the Real, Exalted, in all states.

Abu 'Uthman: it is the light that distinguishes between inspiration (*ilham*) and whispering (*waswas*). It was said: it is the stripping of the secret for the arrival of inspiration.

Al-Qasim: that the thought of the Truth judges over you, and your desire does not judge over you.

Bundar ibn al-Husayn, when asked about God's saying ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾, said: "Quickness of response together with correctness of the right answer." The lexicographers said: every excellence that draws you, whether in speech or deed, and it is the judgments of the excelled thing.

[ ... ] [[Illegible word in the manuscript.]] Wisdom is returning to what is correct, and the wisdom of the animal (*hikmat al-dabba*, the bridle) derives from this, because it returns it to the straight path.

Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah said: I heard the Kitabi say: "Indeed God sent the messengers with sincere counsel for the souls of His creatures. He revealed the books to alert their hearts, and He revealed wisdom for the tranquility of their spirits. The Messenger is a caller to God, the Book is a caller to His rulings, and wisdom points to His grace."

﴿Whoever is given wisdom﴾. Al-Rabi' ibn Khaytham recited *tuti al-hikmata* (with the verb in the active feminine form), and *man tu'ti al-hikmata* with a *ta'* in it.

Ya'qub recited *wa man yu'ti* with a kasra on the *ta'*, meaning "whom God gives it to." The rest recited *wa man yu'ta* with a fatha on the *ta'*, as a passive verb.

*Man* is in the nominative position as the subject of the passive verb that has not named its agent, and *al-hikmah* is its predicate. Al-Hasan ibn Dinar reported from al-Hasan concerning God's saying ﴿whoever is given wisdom﴾: it is scrupulousness (*wara'*) in the religion of God, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿then he has been given much good﴾. ﴿And none remember (*yadhdhakkaru*, take heed) except those of understanding﴾, meaning those of intellect. *Al-lubb* is the intellect that is free from the impulses of desire.

﴿And whatever expense you spend﴾, in what God has obligated upon you, ﴿or whatever vow you vow﴾, or what you have made obligatory upon yourselves, and then fulfilled.

Vows are of two kinds: a vow in obedience and a vow in disobedience. If it is for God, fulfilling it is obligatory, and neglecting it incurs expiation. What is for Satan has neither fulfillment nor expiation.

﴿indeed God knows it﴾, and preserves it until He recompenses you for it. He said *ya'lamuhu* (He knows it, masculine) and not *ya'lamuha* (feminine), because He returned it to the nearer part of it, as in His saying ﴿and whoever earns a fault or a sin and then throws it upon an innocent one﴾ [[Surah al-Nisa': 112.]]. This was said by al-Akhfash. If you wish, you may take it as referring to *ma* (what), as in His saying: ﴿What He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom, He admonishes you with it﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 231.]], where He did not say *biha* (with it, feminine).

﴿The wrongdoers have no helpers﴾, those who place expenditure and vows in other than their proper place, through showing-off and disobedience, ﴿helpers﴾, those who ward off the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic, from them. *Ansar* is the plural of *nasir* (helper), like *sharif* and *ashraf*, and *habib* and *ahbab*.

﴿If you disclose the charities, then excellent is it﴾. The reason: they said, "O Messenger of God, is secret charity better, or public charity?" So God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿If you disclose the charities﴾, that is, display and proclaim them, ﴿then excellent is it﴾.

That is, an excellent quality it is. *Ma* is in the nominative position, and *hiya* is in the accusative position, as you say *ni'ma al-rajulu rajulan* (what an excellent man, a man). When it is definite, you use the nominative and say *ni'ma al-rajulu Zayd* (what an excellent man is Zayd).

Its original form is *ni'ma ma*, then they were joined and assimilated. Al-Hasan used to recite it as *fa-ni'ma ma* separated, according to the original. Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi' (except the transmission of Warsh), 'Asim (in the transmission of Abu Bakr), Abu 'Amr and Abu Bahriyya recited *fa-ni'ma* with a kasra on the *nun* and a sukun on the *'ayn*, similarly in Surah al-Nisa'. Ibn 'Amir, Yahya ibn Thabit, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited with a fatha on the *nun* and the *'ayn* in both places.

Talha, Ibn Kathir, Ya'qub and Ayyub recited with a kasra on the *nun* and the *'ayn*, and Abu Hatim chose this. These are all sound dialects. *Ni'ma* and *ni'ma* are two good forms. Whoever puts a kasra on the *nun* and the *'ayn* makes the kasra follow the kasra, so that two sukuns do not meet: the sukun of the *'ayn* and the sukun of the assimilation.

﴿And if you conceal them﴾, you keep them secret, ﴿and give them to the poor﴾ in secret, ﴿then it is better for you﴾ and more excellent. Every charity is accepted when the intention is sincere, but secret charity is better.

It is in a hadith: "Secret charity extinguishes the anger of the Lord, and extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire, and it averts seventy doors of calamity."

Hafs ibn 'Asim reported from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Seven whom God will shade under His shade on a day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler; a young man who grew up in the worship of God, Mighty and Majestic; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who loved each other for God's sake, gathered for Him and separated for Him; a man whom a woman of rank and beauty invited to herself, and he said, 'Indeed I fear God'; a man who gave charity and concealed it, so that his left hand does not know what his right hand gives; and a man who remembered God in solitude and his eyes overflowed." [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/190.]] [193]

﴿And will expiate from you﴾. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he recited *wa-yukaffiru* with a *ya'* and a *raf'* (nominative), meaning "God expiates." ﴿of your misdeeds﴾. *Min* (of) is used for partiality (*tab'id*). Its reason is the will of God, so that the servants remain in awe and do not become complacent. The grammarians of Basra said: its meaning is removal (*al-isqat*), its estimate being "and We expiate your misdeeds."

﴿And God is Aware of what you do﴾. 'Ammar al-Dhahabi reported from Abu Ja'far, that he said concerning His saying ﴿If you disclose the charities, then excellent is it﴾: "He means the obligatory zakat. ﴿And if you conceal them and give them to the poor, then it is better for you﴾ means voluntary charity."

From Ma'add ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi, raised to the Prophet: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about reciting aloud and reciting quietly, and he said: "It is like charity: ﴿then excellent is it, and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, then it is better for you﴾."

Kathir ibn Murrah reported from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "One who recites the Qur'an quietly is like one who gives charity quietly, and one who recites the Qur'an aloud is like one who gives charity openly." [194] [[Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 3/304.]]

'Ali ibn Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this, who said: God, Mighty and Majestic, made voluntary charity given in secret surpass its public form by seventy times, and obligatory charity surpass its public form by twenty-five times, and likewise all obligations and supererogatory acts.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 272–273:

لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ

Al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed the ʿUmrat al-Qaḍāʾ (the makeup ʿumrah), and with him on that ʿumrah was Asma bint Abi Bakr. Her mother Qutayla and her grandmother came to her asking for something, and they were both polytheists. She said: "I will not give you anything until I seek the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for you are not upon my religion." So she sought his permission regarding that, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. After the revelation of this verse, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to give charity to them, so she gave them and maintained ties with them.

Al-Kalbi said: It has another aspect. Some Muslims had foster relations among the Jews, and they used to support them before they embraced Islam. When they embraced Islam, they disliked spending on them and wanted them to become Muslims, so they sought the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed, and they gave to them after its revelation.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They used to give charity to the poor among the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimma). When the poor among the Muslims increased, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not give charity except to the people of your religion." [195] [[Zad al-Masir: 1/283.]] So Allah revealed: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ, so that they would not be denied charity in order to enter Islam, out of their need for it.

وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ. By guidance (al-huda) he meant divine success and acquaintance, because upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only the guidance of clarification and invitation.

It is narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz who said: It reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man from the People of the Covenant asking at the doors of the Muslims, and he said: "We have not been fair to you; they took the jizya from you while you were young, then we neglected you today." So he commanded that his sustenance be provided from the public treasury (bayt al-mal).

وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ is a conditional sentence with its response (shart wa-jaza'), and "khayr" here means wealth. The verb تُنْفِقُوا in وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ is a conditional like the first, so the nun is dropped from it [in both places].

يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ: its reward is given to you; as if its meaning is: it is paid to you. So likewise I entered "ilā" into it. وَأَنْتُمْ لا تُظْلَمُونَ: you will not be wronged in the reward of your deeds in any way.

Know that this verse concerns voluntary charity (ṣadaqat al-taṭawwuʿ). Allah permitted a Muslim to give charity to a Muslim and to a dhimmi. As for obligatory charity (ṣadaqat al-farḍ), it is not permitted except to Muslims, and they are the people of the two shares that Allah mentioned in Surat al-Tawba. Then He directed them to the best of charities and the most excellent expenditures, so Allah the Exalted said:

لِلْفُقَراءِ. The scholars differed concerning the position of this lām. Some of them said: it is linked to the position of the lām in His words فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ, as if He said: "And whatever you spend of good, it is for the poor," and you spend only for yourselves, its reward returns to you. But when the statement was interrupted by His words فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ and the fāʾ which is the response of the conditional was placed in it, its repetition was omitted in His words لِلْفُقَراءِ, since the meaning of the statement is understood.

Others said: it is a omitted predicate, its estimate being: لِلْفُقَراءِ الَّذِينَ صفتهم كذا, a right that is obligatory,

and they are the poor emigrants (fuqarāʾ al-muhājirīn), who were about four hundred men, having no dwellings in Medina nor tribes. They made themselves in the mosque, learning the Qur'an at night and gathering (firewood/ labour) by day [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] and they used to go out in every expedition (sariyya) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent. [So he went out] [[Illegible in the manuscript; what has been recorded seems to be correct.]] one day to the companions of the Suffa, saw their poverty and hardship, and strengthened their hearts, and said: "Rejoice, O companions of the Suffa, for whoever among my nation remains upon the description you are upon, content with what it contains, they are my companions."

It is reported that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) sent to Saʿid ibn ʿAmir a thousand dirhams, and he came grieved and sorrowful. His wife said to him: "Has some matter occurred?" He said: "Worse than that." Then he said: "Show me your worn-out garment," and he tore it and made it into bundles, then he stood praying and weeping until morning. When it was morning, he stood on the road and began to distribute each bundle until he reached the last of them. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The poor emigrants will come on the Day of Resurrection for the reckoning, and they will say: 'Did you give us anything for which you will call us to account?' and they will enter Paradise five hundred years before the rich. Even a rich man will enter among them and be taken out and seized." So Umar wanted to make me that man, and it would not please me that I were that man, even if I had the world and all that is in it. The poet said:

Little wealth is set right by it, and it remains, while much does not remain with corruption.
The preservation of wealth is easier than seeking it, [and travelling] in the lands without provision. [[Tarikh Dimashq: 11/372, where it reads: "wa-ʿasf fi al-bilad", and similarly in al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Kathir: 1/112.]]

The rest read it with a kasra. Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Ḥātim chose it, and it is said it is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ).

[197] [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/33; al-Mustadrak: 2/233.]]

الْجاهِلُ بأمرهم وحالهم أَغْنِياءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ: from their abstention from asking. Al-taʿaffuf is a reflexive form (tafaʿʿul) from ʿiffa, which means restraint: one says ʿaffa ʿan al-shayʾ when he refrains from it, and ʿafīf when he exerts effort in restraint.

Ru'ba said:

So he refrained from its secrets after the dusk.

Muhammad ibn al-Fadl said: their lofty aspirations prevent them from raising their need to their master.

Al-Thawri: their joy in their poverty and the soundness of their states at the points where afflictions reach them. [Al-Murtaḍā]: their zeal for their poverty and their constant adherence to it. Abu ʿUthman: preferring what they own while being in need of it.

Some said: their hearts are content, their faces radiant, their states good, the light of their secrets, and their spirits roaming in the dominion of their Lord.

And al-Zajjaj recited:

On a camel path with no landmark to be guided by, when the Nabataean driver drives it onward, it brays.

Hisham said: al-Hasan said: the owner of fifty dirhams [is rich].

ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār narrated from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The poor man is not the one turned away by a morsel or two morsels, a date or two dates; rather the poor man is the one who restrains himself." [[As it is in the manuscript, and so in Tafsir Majma al-Bayan: 2/203.]]

لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ

Al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed the ʿUmrat al-Qaḍāʾ (the makeup ʿumrah), and with him on that ʿumrah was Asma bint Abi Bakr. Her mother Qutayla and her grandmother came to her asking for something, and they were both polytheists. She said: "I will not give you anything until I seek the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for you are not upon my religion." So she sought his permission regarding that, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. After the revelation of this verse, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to give charity to them, so she gave them and maintained ties with them.

Al-Kalbi said: It has another aspect. Some Muslims had foster relations among the Jews, and they used to support them before they embraced Islam. When they embraced Islam, they disliked spending on them and wanted them to become Muslims, so they sought the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed, and they gave to them after its revelation.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: They used to give charity to the poor among the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimma). When the poor among the Muslims increased, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not give charity except to the people of your religion." [195] [[Zad al-Masir: 1/283.]] So Allah revealed: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ, so that they would not be denied charity in order to enter Islam, out of their need for it.

It is narrated from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz who said: It reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab saw a man from the People of the Covenant asking at the doors of the Muslims, and he said: "We have not been fair to you; they took the jizya from you while you were young, then we neglected you today." So he commanded that his sustenance be provided from the public treasury (bayt al-mal).

يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ: its reward is given to you; as if its meaning is: it is paid to you. So likewise I entered "ilā" into it. وَأَنْتُمْ لا تُظْلَمُونَ: you will not be wronged in the reward of your deeds in any way.

Whoever asks while he has what suffices him, his asking will come on the Day of Resurrection as scratches, or scrapes, or gashes [[Al-kadḥ is less than the khadsh, and the khadsh is less than the khamsh.]] on his face." It was said: "What is the sufficiency, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Fifty dirhams, or its equivalent in gold." [[With variation in al-Muʿjam al-Kabir: 10/129.]]

وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ: He said, فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ, and upon that He will reward him.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 274–276:

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly…﴾ (the verse).

Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, said:

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, had four dirhams and possessed nothing other than them. He gave one dirham in secret, one dirham openly, one dirham by night and one dirham by day. So there was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day﴾ (the verse) [[Maʿani al-Qurʾan of al-Nahhas: 1/305; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 58.]].

And from Yazid ibn Rawan, who said: No verse of the Qur'an was revealed concerning anyone as was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dirham outstrips a hundred thousand." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can a dirham outstrip a hundred thousand?" He said: "A man has two dirhams, takes one of them and gives it in charity; and a man [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] takes out of his wealth a hundred thousand and gives it in charity" [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/360, no. 16059, with slight variation.]].

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾ (the verse), ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf sent many dinars to the People of the Suffah until he enriched them, and ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, sent in the depth of the night a wasq of dates—and the wasq is sixty ṣaʿ. The most beloved of the two charities to Allah, mighty and majestic, was the charity of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. So Allah revealed concerning both: ﴿Those who spend their wealth﴾ (the verse). Thus by "by day, openly" is meant the charity of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, and by "by night, secretly" is meant the charity of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him [[See Zad al-Masir: 1/285.]].

Abu Umamah, Abu al-Darda', Makhul, al-Awza'i and Rabah ibn Yazid said: They are those who tether [[In Asbab al-Nuzul: "who tie up" (yartabitun).]] horses in the way of Allah, spending upon them by night and by day, secretly and openly. It was revealed concerning those who did not tether horses out of pride or vanity. What supports this is what

Sa'id ibn Sinan narrated from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Gharib, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾, that he said: "It was revealed concerning the owners of horses."

Gharib said: The jinn do not approach a house in which there is a noble horse. And it is narrated that he pointed to some horses that were among those kept for the cause, and he pointed to the noble ones among those horses and said: "These are those who spend their wealth by night and by day" (the verse).

And from Habis ibn ʿAbd Allah al-San'ani, who said that Ibn ʿAbbas, speaking about this verse, ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾, said: It refers to the fodder of horses [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 57.]]. And from Abu Surayh, from one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Faqih, who said: Whoever keeps a horse, its concealment will be a screen for him from the Fire, [and a good deed fell from him]. [[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/196.]] And Abu Hurayrah, whenever he passed by a fat horse, would recite this verse, and whenever he passed by a lean horse, he would remain silent.

Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever ties up a horse in the way of Allah and spends upon it seeking reward, its satiety and its hunger, its drinking and its thirst, its urine and its dung will be in his scale on the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Jabir, from Makhul, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who spends upon his horse in the way of Allah is like one who extends his palms with charity" [201] [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 57; Musnad Ahmad: 6/458.]].

﴿So for them is their reward﴾. Al-Akhfash [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] said: He made the predicate follow with "fa" when the subject that is connected [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]], because it carries the sense of "man" and the answer of "man" in a conditional, with "fa" as in the apodosis of a condition; and the meaning of the verse is: whoever spends, for him is his reward.

﴿with their Lord, and no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ Those who consume usury (riba). The meaning of riba is an increase over the principal of wealth in a non-sale transaction; it is said: "rabba al-shay'" when it increases, and "arba ʿalayhi" and "ʿamala ʿalayhi" when he increases upon it in riba. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Do not sell gold for gold except like for like, and do not sell silver for silver except like for like, and do not sell gold for gold where one of them is absent and the other present; and if he asks you for time until he enters his house, do not grant him time except hand to hand. Say: "Take it." Indeed I fear for you riba [[al-Majmuʿ of Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi: 10/73.]].

They said: The analogical writing of it with the letter ya' is due to the kasrah on its first letter, but they wrote it in the Qur'an with the waw. Al-Farra' said: They wrote it thus because the people of the Hijaz learned writing from the people of al-Hira, and their dialect was "al-ribaw," so they taught them the form of the letter according to their dialect, and they took it thus from them. Likewise al-Dahhak read it [al-ribaw] with waw.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with imalah in place of the kasrah of the rā'. The rest read with tafkhim, with a fatḥah on the bā'. They said: Today you are free in it: if you wish, write it according to what is in the muṣḥaf, in agreement with it; and if you wish, with a ya', and if you wish, with an alif. The meaning of His words ﴿those who consume riba﴾ [consume it] is consuming in the true sense, because it is the greater part of the matter.

Riba occurs in four things: gold, silver, foodstuffs and drink. So it is not permissible to exchange some of them for others except like for like and hand to hand. When the two kinds differ, excess is permitted in ready exchange and forbidden in deferred exchange. It is not permissible to exchange a ṣaʿ of wheat for two ṣaʿ, neither in ready nor in deferred exchange, because they are one genus. Likewise gold for gold, a mithqal for two, neither ready nor deferred; likewise silver for silver. Likewise a ṣaʿ of wheat for two ṣaʿ of barley, and a ṣaʿ of barley for two ṣaʿ of wheat, in ready exchange, and not in deferred exchange. It is permissible to exchange a mithqal for twenty dirhams, or less or more, in ready exchange, and not in deferred exchange. The summary of what people commonly agreed upon is three categories: first, what is consumed as food or drink; second, what serves as price for things and value for destroyed goods, namely gold and silver—in these two riba applies, so it is not permitted to sell one thing for more of its kind, whether ready or deferred; third, what is other than these two, which is not eaten, not drunk, and is not a price, in which there is no riba, so it is permitted to sell some of it for more of the same kind, whether ready or deferred. This is the sum of the discussion of what contains riba according to the school of al-Shafiʿi.

Malik said: Every price, or what is eaten as staple, or what makes staple suitable, is that in which there is riba [[See al-Mughni: 4/127.]].

The people of Iraq said: Every measured or weighed item has riba. The people of the Hijaz said: what

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from Muslim ibn Yasar and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbak, who both said: A gathering brought together ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit and Muʿawiyah, and ʿUbadah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from selling gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, and dates for dates; one of them said: and salt for salt; and the other said: except like for like and hand to hand; and he commanded us to sell gold for silver, and silver for gold, wheat for barley and barley for wheat, hand to hand, however we wish. One of them said: whoever increases or seeks more has committed riba.

The Exalted said: ﴿They will not rise﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, ﴿except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch﴾, i.e., throws down and strikes. The root of "khabt" is striking and trampling; it is said: a "khabut" she-camel is one that tramples people and strikes the earth with her legs. Zuhayr said:

I saw death like a blind camel's stumbling; whoever it strikes, it kills; whoever it misses, lives long and grows old.
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 7/281.]]

﴿from the touch﴾, i.e., madness. It is said: "massa al-rajul" and "alasa," so he is "mamsus" and "malus," when he is insane; its origin is the touch of Satan upon him. The meaning of the verse: the one who consumes riba will be raised by Allah on the Day of Resurrection insane [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]], and that is the sign of the people of riba: they are raised while there is madness from Satan in them. Said by Qatadah.

Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the story of the Night Journey, said:

"Then Gabriel took me to many men, each of whom had a belly like a large house, positioned along the road of the people of Pharaoh, and the people of Pharaoh are presented to the Fire morning and evening. They come like thirsty camels, trampling stones [they neither hear nor understand]; when those with those bellies sense them, they rise, and their bellies tilt them and they fall; then one of them rises and his belly tilts him and he falls, and they cannot move until the people of Pharaoh overtake them, trampling them coming and going. That is their punishment in the barzakh between this world and the Hereafter." He said: "And the people of Pharaoh say: O Allah, do not establish the Hour ever." He said: "And on the day when it is said to them: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾ [[Surat Ghafir: 46.]]." I said: "O Gabriel, who are these?" He said: "They are those who consume riba: ﴿they will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch﴾" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/355.]].

Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu Hurayrah: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he saw in the sky men whose bellies were like houses, with snakes visible outside their bellies. I said: "Who are these, O Gabriel?" He said: "These are the devourers of riba."

﴿That is because they say: trade is only like riba﴾, i.e., that punishment which came upon them is because of their saying this and their considering it lawful.

That is because the people of the Jahiliyyah, when one of them had a debt due from his debtor and demanded it, the debtor would say to the creditor: "Increase the term for me and grant me time, and I will increase your wealth." They would agree, and say: "It is the same for us whether the increase is at the beginning of the sale as profit, or at the due date of the money for delay." So Allah, exalted, refuted them, saying: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba.﴾ ﴿So whoever has received an admonition﴾, i.e., a reminder and warning, ﴿from his Lord and desists﴾ from consuming riba, ﴿for him is what has passed﴾, i.e., what was past of his sin before the prohibition, so he is forgiven; ﴿and his affair is with Allah﴾, meaning the prohibition: if He wills, He protects him so he remains steadfast in desisting; and if He wills, He forsakes him so he returns. It was also said: ﴿and his affair is with Allah﴾ regarding what He commands him and forbids him, and makes lawful for him and prohibits for him, and he has no say in the matter of himself at all. Mahmud al-Warraq said concerning this:

To Allah belongs all the affair of every creature; and to the creature there is nothing of the affair.

﴿And whoever returns [after the prohibition and the admonition] to consuming riba, considering it lawful, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy gates, the least of which is like a man who marries his mother" [202] [[Al-Muntaqa min al-Sunan al-Musnadah of Ibn al-Jarud al-Naysaburi: 163, in full; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 4/108, no. 9774, with slight variation.]].

And from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who feeds it, its scribe, and its witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/110, no. 3333.]].

Al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah intends destruction for a town, He causes riba to appear among them" [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 4/104, no. 9751.]].

﴿Allah destroys riba﴾, i.e., diminishes it, destroys it, and removes its blessing, even if it is much, as the moon is effaced.

And from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed riba, even if it increases, its outcome is to decline" [203] [[Fath al-Bari: 8/152.]].

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Allah destroys﴾ means He does not accept from him charity, nor struggle, nor pilgrimage, nor kinship-maintenance.

﴿And He causes charities to grow﴾, i.e., He increases them, multiplies them, and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense in the Hereafter even if they are small. The Mighty One said: ﴿He will multiply it for him many times over﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 245.]].

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charities, and accepts from them only the good; He takes them in His right hand and makes them grow just as one of you raises his foal or [weaning camel], until a morsel becomes like Mount Uhud" [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 3/115.]].

And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ [[Surat al-Tawbah: 104.]]

﴿Allah destroys riba and causes charities to grow.﴾ Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: I know of no grain that weighs the mountains of this world except the grain of charity. ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, by prohibiting riba, one who deems it lawful, [persisting in sin] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari: 19/153.]].
