So Allah, exalted, refuted them, saying: ﴿But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba.﴾ ﴿So whoever has received an admonition﴾, i.e., a reminder and warning, ﴿from his Lord and desists﴾ from consuming riba, ﴿for him is what has passed﴾, i.e., what was past of his sin before the prohibition, so he is forgiven; ﴿and his affair is with Allah﴾, meaning the prohibition: if He wills, He protects him so he remains steadfast in desisting; and if He wills, He forsakes him so he returns. It was also said: ﴿and his affair is with Allah﴾ regarding what He commands him and forbids him, and makes lawful for him and prohibits for him, and he has no say in the matter of himself at all. Mahmud al-Warraq said concerning this:

To Allah belongs all the affair of every creature; and to the creature there is nothing of the affair.

﴿And whoever returns [after the prohibition and the admonition] to consuming riba, considering it lawful, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy gates, the least of which is like a man who marries his mother" [202] [[Al-Muntaqa min al-Sunan al-Musnadah of Ibn al-Jarud al-Naysaburi: 163, in full; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 4/108, no. 9774, with slight variation.]].

And from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who feeds it, its scribe, and its witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/110, no. 3333.]].

Al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah intends destruction for a town, He causes riba to appear among them" [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 4/104, no. 9751.]].

﴿Allah destroys riba﴾, i.e., diminishes it, destroys it, and removes its blessing, even if it is much, as the moon is effaced.

And from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed riba, even if it increases, its outcome is to decline" [203] [[Fath al-Bari: 8/152.]].

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Allah destroys﴾ means He does not accept from him charity, nor struggle, nor pilgrimage, nor kinship-maintenance.

﴿And He causes charities to grow﴾, i.e., He increases them, multiplies them, and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense in the Hereafter even if they are small. The Mighty One said: ﴿He will multiply it for him many times over﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 245.]].

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charities, and accepts from them only the good; He takes them in His right hand and makes them grow just as one of you raises his foal or [weaning camel], until a morsel becomes like Mount Uhud" [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 3/115.]].

And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ [[Surat al-Tawbah: 104.]]

﴿Allah destroys riba and causes charities to grow.﴾ Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: I know of no grain that weighs the mountains of this world except the grain of charity. ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, by prohibiting riba, one who deems it lawful, [persisting in sin] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari: 19/153.]].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 274–276:

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly…﴾ (the verse).

Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, said:

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, had four dirhams and possessed nothing other than them. He gave one dirham in secret, one dirham openly, one dirham by night and one dirham by day. So there was revealed: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day﴾ (the verse) [[Maʿani al-Qurʾan of al-Nahhas: 1/305; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 58.]].

And from Yazid ibn Rawan, who said: No verse of the Qur'an was revealed concerning anyone as was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A dirham outstrips a hundred thousand." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, how can a dirham outstrip a hundred thousand?" He said: "A man has two dirhams, takes one of them and gives it in charity; and a man [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] takes out of his wealth a hundred thousand and gives it in charity" [[Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 6/360, no. 16059, with slight variation.]].

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿For the poor who are restricted in the way of Allah﴾ (the verse), ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf sent many dinars to the People of the Suffah until he enriched them, and ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, sent in the depth of the night a wasq of dates—and the wasq is sixty ṣaʿ. The most beloved of the two charities to Allah, mighty and majestic, was the charity of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. So Allah revealed concerning both: ﴿Those who spend their wealth﴾ (the verse). Thus by "by day, openly" is meant the charity of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, and by "by night, secretly" is meant the charity of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him [[See Zad al-Masir: 1/285.]].

Abu Umamah, Abu al-Darda', Makhul, al-Awza'i and Rabah ibn Yazid said: They are those who tether [[In Asbab al-Nuzul: "who tie up" (yartabitun).]] horses in the way of Allah, spending upon them by night and by day, secretly and openly. It was revealed concerning those who did not tether horses out of pride or vanity. What supports this is what

Sa'id ibn Sinan narrated from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Gharib, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾, that he said: "It was revealed concerning the owners of horses."

Gharib said: The jinn do not approach a house in which there is a noble horse. And it is narrated that he pointed to some horses that were among those kept for the cause, and he pointed to the noble ones among those horses and said: "These are those who spend their wealth by night and by day" (the verse).

And from Habis ibn ʿAbd Allah al-San'ani, who said that Ibn ʿAbbas, speaking about this verse, ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly﴾, said: It refers to the fodder of horses [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 57.]]. And from Abu Surayh, from one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Faqih, who said: Whoever keeps a horse, its concealment will be a screen for him from the Fire, [and a good deed fell from him]. [[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/196.]] And Abu Hurayrah, whenever he passed by a fat horse, would recite this verse, and whenever he passed by a lean horse, he would remain silent.

Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever ties up a horse in the way of Allah and spends upon it seeking reward, its satiety and its hunger, its drinking and its thirst, its urine and its dung will be in his scale on the Day of Resurrection."

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Jabir, from Makhul, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who spends upon his horse in the way of Allah is like one who extends his palms with charity" [201] [[Asbab al-Nuzul: 57; Musnad Ahmad: 6/458.]].

﴿So for them is their reward﴾. Al-Akhfash [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]] said: He made the predicate follow with "fa" when the subject that is connected [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]], because it carries the sense of "man" and the answer of "man" in a conditional, with "fa" as in the apodosis of a condition; and the meaning of the verse is: whoever spends, for him is his reward.

﴿with their Lord, and no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ Those who consume usury (riba). The meaning of riba is an increase over the principal of wealth in a non-sale transaction; it is said: "rabba al-shay'" when it increases, and "arba ʿalayhi" and "ʿamala ʿalayhi" when he increases upon it in riba. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Do not sell gold for gold except like for like, and do not sell silver for silver except like for like, and do not sell gold for gold where one of them is absent and the other present; and if he asks you for time until he enters his house, do not grant him time except hand to hand. Say: "Take it." Indeed I fear for you riba [[al-Majmuʿ of Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi: 10/73.]].

They said: The analogical writing of it with the letter ya' is due to the kasrah on its first letter, but they wrote it in the Qur'an with the waw. Al-Farra' said: They wrote it thus because the people of the Hijaz learned writing from the people of al-Hira, and their dialect was "al-ribaw," so they taught them the form of the letter according to their dialect, and they took it thus from them. Likewise al-Dahhak read it [al-ribaw] with waw.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read with imalah in place of the kasrah of the rā'. The rest read with tafkhim, with a fatḥah on the bā'. They said: Today you are free in it: if you wish, write it according to what is in the muṣḥaf, in agreement with it; and if you wish, with a ya', and if you wish, with an alif. The meaning of His words ﴿those who consume riba﴾ [consume it] is consuming in the true sense, because it is the greater part of the matter.

Riba occurs in four things: gold, silver, foodstuffs and drink. So it is not permissible to exchange some of them for others except like for like and hand to hand. When the two kinds differ, excess is permitted in ready exchange and forbidden in deferred exchange. It is not permissible to exchange a ṣaʿ of wheat for two ṣaʿ, neither in ready nor in deferred exchange, because they are one genus. Likewise gold for gold, a mithqal for two, neither ready nor deferred; likewise silver for silver. Likewise a ṣaʿ of wheat for two ṣaʿ of barley, and a ṣaʿ of barley for two ṣaʿ of wheat, in ready exchange, and not in deferred exchange. It is permissible to exchange a mithqal for twenty dirhams, or less or more, in ready exchange, and not in deferred exchange. The summary of what people commonly agreed upon is three categories: first, what is consumed as food or drink; second, what serves as price for things and value for destroyed goods, namely gold and silver—in these two riba applies, so it is not permitted to sell one thing for more of its kind, whether ready or deferred; third, what is other than these two, which is not eaten, not drunk, and is not a price, in which there is no riba, so it is permitted to sell some of it for more of the same kind, whether ready or deferred. This is the sum of the discussion of what contains riba according to the school of al-Shafiʿi.

Malik said: Every price, or what is eaten as staple, or what makes staple suitable, is that in which there is riba [[See al-Mughni: 4/127.]].

The people of Iraq said: Every measured or weighed item has riba. The people of the Hijaz said: what

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from Muslim ibn Yasar and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbak, who both said: A gathering brought together ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit and Muʿawiyah, and ʿUbadah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from selling gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, and dates for dates; one of them said: and salt for salt; and the other said: except like for like and hand to hand; and he commanded us to sell gold for silver, and silver for gold, wheat for barley and barley for wheat, hand to hand, however we wish. One of them said: whoever increases or seeks more has committed riba.

The Exalted said: ﴿They will not rise﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection from their graves, ﴿except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch﴾, i.e., throws down and strikes. The root of "khabt" is striking and trampling; it is said: a "khabut" she-camel is one that tramples people and strikes the earth with her legs. Zuhayr said:

I saw death like a blind camel's stumbling; whoever it strikes, it kills; whoever it misses, lives long and grows old.
[[Lisan al-ʿArab: 7/281.]]

﴿from the touch﴾, i.e., madness. It is said: "massa al-rajul" and "alasa," so he is "mamsus" and "malus," when he is insane; its origin is the touch of Satan upon him. The meaning of the verse: the one who consumes riba will be raised by Allah on the Day of Resurrection insane [ ... ] [[Illegible in the manuscript.]], and that is the sign of the people of riba: they are raised while there is madness from Satan in them. Said by Qatadah.

Abu Harun al-ʿAbdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the story of the Night Journey, said:

"Then Gabriel took me to many men, each of whom had a belly like a large house, positioned along the road of the people of Pharaoh, and the people of Pharaoh are presented to the Fire morning and evening. They come like thirsty camels, trampling stones [they neither hear nor understand]; when those with those bellies sense them, they rise, and their bellies tilt them and they fall; then one of them rises and his belly tilts him and he falls, and they cannot move until the people of Pharaoh overtake them, trampling them coming and going. That is their punishment in the barzakh between this world and the Hereafter." He said: "And the people of Pharaoh say: O Allah, do not establish the Hour ever." He said: "And on the day when it is said to them: ﴿Admit the people of Pharaoh to the most severe punishment﴾ [[Surat Ghafir: 46.]]." I said: "O Gabriel, who are these?" He said: "They are those who consume riba: ﴿they will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has driven to madness by his touch﴾" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 3/355.]].

Hammad ibn Salamah, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu Hurayrah: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he saw in the sky men whose bellies were like houses, with snakes visible outside their bellies. I said: "Who are these, O Gabriel?" He said: "These are the devourers of riba."

﴿That is because they say: trade is only like riba﴾, i.e., that punishment which came upon them is because of their saying this and their considering it lawful.

That is because the people of the Jahiliyyah, when one of them had a debt due from his debtor and demanded it, the debtor would say to the creditor: "Increase the term for me and grant me time, and I will increase your wealth." They would agree, and say: "It is the same for us whether the increase is at the beginning of the sale as profit, or at the due date of the money for delay." It was also said: ﴿and his affair is with Allah﴾ regarding what He commands him and forbids him, and makes lawful for him and prohibits for him, and he has no say in the matter of himself at all. Mahmud al-Warraq said concerning this:

To Allah belongs all the affair of every creature; and to the creature there is nothing of the affair.

﴿And whoever returns [after the prohibition and the admonition] to consuming riba, considering it lawful, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Riba has seventy gates, the least of which is like a man who marries his mother" [202] [[Al-Muntaqa min al-Sunan al-Musnadah of Ibn al-Jarud al-Naysaburi: 163, in full; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 4/108, no. 9774, with slight variation.]].

And from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the one who consumes riba, the one who feeds it, its scribe, and its witnesses [[Sunan Abi Dawud: 2/110, no. 3333.]].

﴿Allah destroys riba﴾, i.e., diminishes it, destroys it, and removes its blessing, even if it is much, as the moon is effaced.

And from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed riba, even if it increases, its outcome is to decline" [203] [[Fath al-Bari: 8/152.]].

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Allah destroys﴾ means He does not accept from him charity, nor struggle, nor pilgrimage, nor kinship-maintenance.

﴿And He causes charities to grow﴾, i.e., He increases them, multiplies them, and blesses them in this world, and multiplies the reward and recompense in the Hereafter even if they are small. The Mighty One said: ﴿He will multiply it for him many times over﴾ [[Surat al-Baqarah: 245.]].

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charities, and accepts from them only the good; He takes them in His right hand and makes them grow just as one of you raises his foal or [weaning camel], until a morsel becomes like Mount Uhud" [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin: 3/115.]].

And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ [[Surat al-Tawbah: 104.]]

﴿Allah destroys riba and causes charities to grow.﴾ Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: I know of no grain that weighs the mountains of this world except the grain of charity. ﴿And Allah does not love every ungrateful sinner﴾, by prohibiting riba, one who deems it lawful, [persisting in sin] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari: 19/153.]].

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 277–281:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve. O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest (riba).﴾

Ata' and Ikrimah said: This verse was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Uthman ibn Affan, who had extended credit (aslafa) for dates. When the harvest time came, the owner of the dates said to them: "My dependents will have nothing left if you take all your due. Instead, take half now and defer half, and I will double it for you." They agreed. But when the time came, the two sought the increase, and this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, so they listened and obeyed, and took back their capital.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Khalid ibn al-Walid, who were partners in the Jahiliyyah, extending loans at interest to the Banu Amr ibn Umayr, people of Thaqif, and they had great wealth from interest. Allah the Exalted then revealed this verse, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed every interest from the interest of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first interest I abolish is the interest of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Every blood from the blood of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first blood I abolish is the blood of Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He was nursing among the Banu Layth, and Hudhayl killed him."

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqif: Mas'ud, Abd Yalil, Habib and Rabi'ah, who were the sons of Amr ibn Umayr ibn Awf al-Thaqafi. They used to lend to al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum, and they took interest. When the Prophet (ﷺ) prevailed over al-Ta'if and made peace with Thaqif, these four brothers embraced Islam and demanded their interest from the Banu al-Mughirah. The Banu al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, we will not pay interest in Islam, for Allah and His Messenger have abolished it for the believers, so will this make us the most wretched of people?" They brought the dispute before Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-Is ibn Umayyah.

He was the governor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over Makkah, and [the Prophet] had said: "I appoint you over the people of Allah." Attab wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the case of the two parties, and the sum was great. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest.﴾

"Dhar" is an expression of threat. Al-Hasan read "ma baqiya" with an alif, which is the dialect of Tayy, who say "jaraat" for "jariyah" and "naasaat" for "naasiyah." A poet of theirs said:

"By your life, I do not fear poverty while there remains on earth a man of Qays driving camels."

﴿If you are believers﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And you will be the superior ones if you are believers﴾ (Surah Al Imran: 139). ﴿But if you do not do so﴾ means: if you do not give up what remains of interest, ﴿then be informed﴾ (fa-'dhanu). Asim, Hamzah, and the narration of Abu Bakr from Asim, read ﴿fa-'adhanu﴾ with a madd, on the pattern of "amanu." The rest read ﴿fa-'dhanu﴾ shortened, with the dhal fatha, which is the reading of Ali and the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Whoever reads it shortened, its meaning is: "Know, you and hear." It is said: "adhina al-shay'a ya'dhanu adhanan wa adhanatan" when he hears it and knows it. Allah said: ﴿And it listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (Surah Al-Inshiqaq: 2). Whoever reads it with madd, its meaning is: "Inform others." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said: We have informed You that none of us is a witness﴾ (Surah Fussilat: 47).

The root of the word is from "udhun" (ear), i.e., "make them hear it" (aqʻuhu fi al-adhan), that is, announce it.

﴿War from Allah and His Messenger.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said: "Do not eat interest; take your weapon for war." Al-Walibi narrated from him: Whoever persists in interest and does not desist from it, it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims to ask him to repent; if he desists, well and good, otherwise his neck is struck.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The war of Allah is the Fire, and the war of His Messenger is the sword. ﴿But if you repent, then you have your capital, neither wronging nor being wronged﴾: you do not wrong by seeking increase, nor are you wronged by a decrease below the capital. Aban and al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim with a damma on the first taa' and a fatha on the second. The scholars of meanings said: this is the condition of repentance, for if they do not repent they disbelieve by rejecting the judgment of Allah and making lawful what Allah has forbidden, and their wealth becomes spoils (fay') for the Muslims.

When these verses were revealed, the Banu Amr ibn Umayr [said] to the Banu al-Mughirah: "Rather, we repent to Allah, for we have no power to fight the war of Allah and His Messenger." So they accepted the capital and submitted to the command of Allah. But the Banu al-Mughirah complained of hardship and said: "Delay us until we gather the harvests." They refused to delay, so Allah revealed:

﴿And if there is one in hardship﴾: the statement has the noun of "kana" as its subject without a predicate, which is permissible with an indefinite noun. The Arabs say: "If there is a righteous man, honor him." It is also said: "kana" here indicates the occurrence of the event, and then it needs no predicate.

Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas read: ﴿in kana dha 'usratin﴾ with the noun of the debtor or the one owed understood as "in al-gharim aw al-matlub dha 'usratin." Aban ibn Uthman read: ﴿wa man kana dha 'usratin﴾ for this produce. Al-A'mash read: ﴿wa in kana mu'sir﴾, which is evidence for the common reading.

"Al-usrah" means poverty, constraint and hardship. Abu Ja'far read ﴿'usrun﴾ with a damma on the sin; both are dialects.

﴿Then let there be postponement﴾: this is a command in the form of a statement, and the fa' in it answers the conditional; its implied meaning is: "then for him is postponement," that is, he said:

It is obligatory to respect him, with nasb in the sense of "then let him wait with patience," which would be correct, like His saying ﴿so strike the necks﴾. "Nazirah" means granting respite.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan and Qatadah read ﴿fa-nazirah﴾ with kasrah on the dad and raf' on the ra' and ha', meaning "waiting." Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read ﴿fa-nazrah﴾ with the zay sakin; it is a verbal noun which may be from "nazar" (seeing) or "intizar" (waiting), both.

﴿To a time of ease.﴾ Ata', Shaybah, Nafi' and Humayd ibn Muhays read: ﴿maysurah﴾ with damma on the sin and tanwin.

Umar, Ali, Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Muslim, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Abu Amr, Ya'qub and Ayyub read: ﴿maysarah﴾ with tanwin and fatha on the sin. This is the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because it is the prevailing dialect. Mujahid and Abu Sarra al-Hudhali read: ﴿maysurihi﴾ with damma on the sin in construct form with a pronoun. Zayd narrated from Ya'qub. Al-A'mash narrated from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah that he used to read it: "fa-nazirawhu ila maysurah." All of these are dialects with the meaning of ease, wealth and abundance.

﴿But that you give it as charity [remit your capitals] to the debtor in hardship is better for you, if you knew.﴾ Asim read: ﴿tasaddaqu﴾ with the sad lightened; the rest read it with the sad doubled.

**Mention of the ruling of the verse**

Allah the Exalted commanded granting respite to the one in hardship. Whenever a man becomes poor and his poverty is clear, the owner of property has no way to demand his money until his wealth appears. When his wealth appears, it becomes obligatory on him to deliver the right to the owner of property, and he knows that rights [are due]. Every right that falls on a person as a substitute for property that came into his hand, such as a loan or the purchase of goods, if he claims poverty he must prove his poverty, because the original state of such a person is wealth by the acquisition of what came into his hand. And every right that falls on him without property coming into his hand, such as dower or guarantee, if he claims poverty, the owner of property must prove that he is wealthy, because the original state of people is poverty. If no state of wealth is known for him, the ruling is to remain on the original state until his wealth becomes clear.

Al-Hasan said: If he says, "I am destitute," his word is accepted with his oath, and it is incumbent on him to make his property apparent by evidence or by inspection.

Abu Hanifah held that he should be imprisoned for two or three months, then inquiry should be made about him in secret; if it becomes clear that he is poor, he is released.

The evidence of those who say he should not be imprisoned:

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man suffered losses in fruits and his debt increased, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take what you find; you have nothing but that."

Abu Hurayrah was in charge of the judiciary of Madinah, and a man came to him with a debtor and said: "I want you to imprison him."

He said: "Do you know of any property of his that we can take from him and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Do you know of any origin of wealth that we can sell and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Then what do you want?" He said: "I want you to imprison him." He said: "But I will leave him to seek for you and for himself and his dependents; when he becomes wealthy, he will be obliged to pay the debt."

Abu al-Zinad al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Delay by the wealthy is injustice. When one of you is referred to a wealthy person, let him follow."

And from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves that his supplication be answered and his distress be relieved, let him ease the one in hardship."

He said: "Allah said: ﴿And if there is one in hardship, then let there be postponement to a time of ease,﴾" so he brought out his document and erased it.

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Abu Bahriyyah, Abu Amr, Salam and Ya'qub read: ﴿turja'un﴾ with fatha on the ta'; they took as evidence the reading of Ubayy: "fa-ttaqu yawman tasirna fihi ila Allah." ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve. O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest (riba).﴾

Ata' and Ikrimah said: This verse was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Uthman ibn Affan, who had extended credit (aslafa) for dates. When the harvest time came, the owner of the dates said to them: "My dependents will have nothing left if you take all your due. Instead, take half now and defer half, and I will double it for you." They agreed. But when the time came, the two sought the increase, and this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, so they listened and obeyed, and took back their capital.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Khalid ibn al-Walid, who were partners in the Jahiliyyah, extending loans at interest to the Banu Amr ibn Umayr, people of Thaqif, and they had great wealth from interest. Allah the Exalted then revealed this verse, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed every interest from the interest of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first interest I abolish is the interest of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Every blood from the blood of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first blood I abolish is the blood of Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He was nursing among the Banu Layth, and Hudhayl killed him."

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqif: Mas'ud, Abd Yalil, Habib and Rabi'ah, who were the sons of Amr ibn Umayr ibn Awf al-Thaqafi. They used to lend to al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum, and they took interest. When the Prophet (ﷺ) prevailed over al-Ta'if and made peace with Thaqif, these four brothers embraced Islam and demanded their interest from the Banu al-Mughirah. The Banu al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, we will not pay interest in Islam, for Allah and His Messenger have abolished it for the believers, so will this make us the most wretched of people?" They brought the dispute before Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-Is ibn Umayyah.

He was the governor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over Makkah, and [the Prophet] had said: "I appoint you over the people of Allah." Attab wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the case of the two parties, and the sum was great. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest.﴾

"Dhar" is an expression of threat. Al-Hasan read "ma baqiya" with an alif, which is the dialect of Tayy, who say "jaraat" for "jariyah" and "naasaat" for "naasiyah." A poet of theirs said:

"By your life, I do not fear poverty while there remains on earth a man of Qays driving camels."

﴿If you are believers﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And you will be the superior ones if you are believers﴾ (Surah Al Imran: 139). ﴿But if you do not do so﴾ means: if you do not give up what remains of interest, ﴿then be informed﴾ (fa-'dhanu). Asim, Hamzah, and the narration of Abu Bakr from Asim, read ﴿fa-'adhanu﴾ with a madd, on the pattern of "amanu." The rest read ﴿fa-'dhanu﴾ shortened, with the dhal fatha, which is the reading of Ali and the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Whoever reads it shortened, its meaning is: "Know, you and hear." It is said: "adhina al-shay'a ya'dhanu adhanan wa adhanatan" when he hears it and knows it. Allah said: ﴿And it listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (Surah Al-Inshiqaq: 2). Whoever reads it with madd, its meaning is: "Inform others." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said: We have informed You that none of us is a witness﴾ (Surah Fussilat: 47).

The root of the word is from "udhun" (ear), i.e., "make them hear it" (aqʻuhu fi al-adhan), that is, announce it.

﴿War from Allah and His Messenger.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said: "Do not eat interest; take your weapon for war." Al-Walibi narrated from him: Whoever persists in interest and does not desist from it, it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims to ask him to repent; if he desists, well and good, otherwise his neck is struck.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The war of Allah is the Fire, and the war of His Messenger is the sword. ﴿But if you repent, then you have your capital, neither wronging nor being wronged﴾: you do not wrong by seeking increase, nor are you wronged by a decrease below the capital. Aban and al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim with a damma on the first taa' and a fatha on the second. The scholars of meanings said: this is the condition of repentance, for if they do not repent they disbelieve by rejecting the judgment of Allah and making lawful what Allah has forbidden, and their wealth becomes spoils (fay') for the Muslims.

When these verses were revealed, the Banu Amr ibn Umayr [said] to the Banu al-Mughirah: "Rather, we repent to Allah, for we have no power to fight the war of Allah and His Messenger." So they accepted the capital and submitted to the command of Allah. But the Banu al-Mughirah complained of hardship and said: "Delay us until we gather the harvests." They refused to delay, so Allah revealed:

﴿And if there is one in hardship﴾: the statement has the noun of "kana" as its subject without a predicate, which is permissible with an indefinite noun. The Arabs say: "If there is a righteous man, honor him." It is also said: "kana" here indicates the occurrence of the event, and then it needs no predicate.

Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas read: ﴿in kana dha 'usratin﴾ with the noun of the debtor or the one owed understood as "in al-gharim aw al-matlub dha 'usratin." Aban ibn Uthman read: ﴿wa man kana dha 'usratin﴾ for this produce. Al-A'mash read: ﴿wa in kana mu'sir﴾, which is evidence for the common reading.

"Al-usrah" means poverty, constraint and hardship. Abu Ja'far read ﴿'usrun﴾ with a damma on the sin; both are dialects.

﴿Then let there be postponement﴾: this is a command in the form of a statement, and the fa' in it answers the conditional; its implied meaning is: "then for him is postponement," that is, he said:

It is obligatory to respect him, with nasb in the sense of "then let him wait with patience," which would be correct, like His saying ﴿so strike the necks﴾. "Nazirah" means granting respite.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan and Qatadah read ﴿fa-nazirah﴾ with kasrah on the dad and raf' on the ra' and ha', meaning "waiting." Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read ﴿fa-nazrah﴾ with the zay sakin; it is a verbal noun which may be from "nazar" (seeing) or "intizar" (waiting), both.

﴿To a time of ease.﴾ Ata', Shaybah, Nafi' and Humayd ibn Muhays read: ﴿maysurah﴾ with damma on the sin and tanwin.

Umar, Ali, Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Muslim, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Abu Amr, Ya'qub and Ayyub read: ﴿maysarah﴾ with tanwin and fatha on the sin. This is the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because it is the prevailing dialect. Mujahid and Abu Sarra al-Hudhali read: ﴿maysurihi﴾ with damma on the sin in construct form with a pronoun. Zayd narrated from Ya'qub. Al-A'mash narrated from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah that he used to read it: "fa-nazirawhu ila maysurah." All of these are dialects with the meaning of ease, wealth and abundance.

﴿But that you give it as charity [remit your capitals] to the debtor in hardship is better for you, if you knew.﴾ Asim read: ﴿tasaddaqu﴾ with the sad lightened; the rest read it with the sad doubled.

**Mention of the ruling of the verse**

Allah the Exalted commanded granting respite to the one in hardship. Whenever a man becomes poor and his poverty is clear, the owner of property has no way to demand his money until his wealth appears. When his wealth appears, it becomes obligatory on him to deliver the right to the owner of property, and he knows that rights [are due]. Every right that falls on a person as a substitute for property that came into his hand, such as a loan or the purchase of goods, if he claims poverty he must prove his poverty, because the original state of such a person is wealth by the acquisition of what came into his hand. And every right that falls on him without property coming into his hand, such as dower or guarantee, if he claims poverty, the owner of property must prove that he is wealthy, because the original state of people is poverty. If no state of wealth is known for him, the ruling is to remain on the original state until his wealth becomes clear.

Al-Hasan said: If he says, "I am destitute," his word is accepted with his oath, and it is incumbent on him to make his property apparent by evidence or by inspection.

Abu Hanifah held that he should be imprisoned for two or three months, then inquiry should be made about him in secret; if it becomes clear that he is poor, he is released.

The evidence of those who say he should not be imprisoned:

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man suffered losses in fruits and his debt increased, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take what you find; you have nothing but that."

Abu Hurayrah was in charge of the judiciary of Madinah, and a man came to him with a debtor and said: "I want you to imprison him."

He said: "Do you know of any property of his that we can take from him and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Do you know of any origin of wealth that we can sell and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Then what do you want?" He said: "I want you to imprison him." He said: "But I will leave him to seek for you and for himself and his dependents; when he becomes wealthy, he will be obliged to pay the debt."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever walks to his creditor with his right, the creatures of the earth and the fish of the water will bless him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for every step a tree planted for him in Paradise and a sin forgiven him. But if he does not do so and delays, then he is a transgressor."

Abu al-Zinad al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Delay by the wealthy is injustice. When one of you is referred to a wealthy person, let him follow."

And from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves that his supplication be answered and his distress be relieved, let him ease the one in hardship."

Rib'i ibn Khirash narrated from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman that he said: On the Day of Resurrection Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will bring His servant and say: "O my Lord, I did no good deed for You ever, except that You gave me wealth and I used to be generous to the one in hardship and grant him respite." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I have more right to that than you; forgive My servant."

He said: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari said: "I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of Allah."

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Dawud from Buraydah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day." Then he said after that: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day equal to what he granted respite." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you said: whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day; then you said: whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day equal to what he granted respite."

He said: "My saying 'a charity every day' is before the due date, and my saying 'a charity every day equal to what he granted respite' is after the due date."

And from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id from his brother from his father: Jabir ibn Abdullah went out to a debtor of his, seeking repayment. He said: "My right is here." They said: "No." He withdrew, then came out ashamed of him and said: "What prevented you from holding back my right and hiding your face from me?" He said: "Hardship." He said: "Allah said: ﴿And if there is one in hardship, then let there be postponement to a time of ease,﴾" so he brought out his document and erased it.

**Chapter on debt**

He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far used to say to his treasurer: "Go and take a debt for us, for I dislike to spend a night without Allah, Mighty and Majestic, being with me, since I heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ata' ibn Yasar narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes a debt intending not to pay it is a thief."

Uthman ibn Abdullah narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah from his father: A man was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray over him, and he said: "Pray over your companion, for he has a debt." And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I seek refuge in Allah from disbelief and debt." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is debt equated with disbelief?" He said: "Yes."

And from Aisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Debt is the banner of Allah on earth; when He wishes to humble His servant, He afflicts him with debt and places it on his neck."

And from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no sin greater before Allah after the major sins than that a man dies with the wealth of people as a debt upon his neck, for which there is no payment."

Yazid ibn Abi Khalid narrated from Ibn Ayyub from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of debt, for it is worry by night and humiliation by day."

Rib'i ibn Khirash narrated from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman that he said: On the Day of Resurrection Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will bring His servant and say: "O my Lord, I did no good deed for You ever, except that You gave me wealth and I used to be generous to the one in hardship and grant him respite." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I have more right to that than you; forgive My servant."

He said: Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari said: "I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of Allah."

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Dawud from Buraydah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day." Then he said after that: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day equal to what he granted respite." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, you said: whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day; then you said: whoever grants respite to one in hardship, for him is a charity every day equal to what he granted respite."

He said: "My saying 'a charity every day' is before the due date, and my saying 'a charity every day equal to what he granted respite' is after the due date."

And from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id from his brother from his father: Jabir ibn Abdullah went out to a debtor of his, seeking repayment. He said: "My right is here." They said: "No." He withdrew, then came out ashamed of him and said: "What prevented you from holding back my right and hiding your face from me?" He said: "Hardship." He said: "Allah said: ﴿And if there is one in hardship, then let there be postponement to a time of ease,﴾" so he brought out his document and erased it.

**Chapter on debt**

Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father from Abdullah ibn Ja'far that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is with the creditor until he repays his debt, so long as it is not in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dislikes." He said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far used to say to his treasurer: "Go and take a debt for us, for I dislike to spend a night without Allah, Mighty and Majestic, being with me, since I heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ata' ibn Yasar narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes a debt intending not to pay it is a thief."

Uthman ibn Abdullah narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah from his father: A man was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ) to pray over him, and he said: "Pray over your companion, for he has a debt." Abu Qatadah said: "I will guarantee it." He said: "With fulfilment." He said: "With fulfilment," and he prayed over him. He owed eighteen or seventeen dirhams.

And from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "I seek refuge in Allah from disbelief and debt." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, is debt equated with disbelief?" He said: "Yes."

And from Aisha who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Debt is the banner of Allah on earth; when He wishes to humble His servant, He afflicts him with debt and places it on his neck."

And from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no sin greater before Allah after the major sins than that a man dies with the wealth of people as a debt upon his neck, for which there is no payment."

Yazid ibn Abi Khalid narrated from Ibn Ayyub from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Beware of debt, for it is worry by night and humiliation by day."

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah.﴾ Abu Bahriyyah, Abu Amr, Salam and Ya'qub read: ﴿turja'un﴾ with fatha on the ta'; they took as evidence the reading of Ubayy: "fa-ttaqu yawman tasirna fihi ila Allah." The others read with damma on the ta', taking as evidence the reading of Abdullah: "wa-ttaqu yawman turaddun fihi ila Allah."

﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah in it﴾: he said: This is the last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Jibril said: "Place it at the top of two hundred and eighty verses of al-Baqarah."

Sufyan narrated from Asim from al-Sha'bi from Ibn Abbas who said: [This is] the last verse revealed upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

**Chapter on another account of the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an**

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ (Surah Az-Zumar: 30), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I wish I knew when that will be." Then Allah revealed Surah An-Nasr, and after the revelation of this surah the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pause from takbir and recitation, saying in it: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdih, astaghfir Allah wa atubu ilayh." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, you did not used to say this before." He said: "It is my soul; I have been informed of my death." Then he wept intensely. It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you weep at death when Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?" He said: "Where is the terror of the moment of standing, where is the narrowness of the grave and the darkness of the tomb, where are the Resurrection and its terrors?"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived six months. Then when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out for the Farewell Pilgrimage, on the road there was revealed to him: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-kalalah﴾ (Surah An-Nisa': 176) to its end, and it was called "the verse of summer."

Then there was revealed to him while standing at Arafat: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾ (Surah Al-Ma'idah: 3), and he lived after it eighty-one days. Then the verses on interest were revealed to him, then after them: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah in it,﴾ which is the last verse revealed from the heaven. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived after it twenty-one days.

Ibn Jurayj said: nine nights. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Muqatil said: seven nights. Then he died on Monday, two nights remaining of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the sun had passed its zenith, in the eleventh year after the Hijrah, the first year of the reign of Ardashir Shirawayh ibn Abarwiz ibn Hurmuz ibn Nushirwan.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verses 277–281:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve. O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest (riba).﴾

Ata' and Ikrimah said: This verse was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Uthman ibn Affan, who had extended credit (aslafa) for dates. When the harvest time came, the owner of the dates said to them: "My dependents will have nothing left if you take all your due. Instead, take half now and defer half, and I will double it for you." They agreed. But when the time came, the two sought the increase, and this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who forbade them. Then Allah revealed this verse, so they listened and obeyed, and took back their capital.

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Khalid ibn al-Walid, who were partners in the Jahiliyyah, extending loans at interest to the Banu Amr ibn Umayr, people of Thaqif, and they had great wealth from interest. Allah the Exalted then revealed this verse, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed every interest from the interest of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first interest I abolish is the interest of al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Every blood from the blood of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first blood I abolish is the blood of Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib. He was nursing among the Banu Layth, and Hudhayl killed him."

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning four brothers from Thaqif: Mas'ud, Abd Yalil, Habib and Rabi'ah, who were the sons of Amr ibn Umayr ibn Awf al-Thaqafi. They used to lend to al-Mughirah ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum, and they took interest. When the Prophet (ﷺ) prevailed over al-Ta'if and made peace with Thaqif, these four brothers embraced Islam and demanded their interest from the Banu al-Mughirah. The Banu al-Mughirah said: "By Allah, we will not pay interest in Islam, for Allah and His Messenger have abolished it for the believers, so will this make us the most wretched of people?" They brought the dispute before Attab ibn Asid ibn Abi al-Is ibn Umayyah.

He was the governor of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over Makkah, and [the Prophet] had said: "I appoint you over the people of Allah." Attab wrote to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the case of the two parties, and the sum was great. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest.﴾

"Dhar" is an expression of threat. Al-Hasan read "ma baqiya" with an alif, which is the dialect of Tayy, who say "jaraat" for "jariyah" and "naasaat" for "naasiyah." A poet of theirs said:

"By your life, I do not fear poverty while there remains on earth a man of Qays driving camels."

﴿If you are believers﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And you will be the superior ones if you are believers﴾ (Surah Al Imran: 139). ﴿But if you do not do so﴾ means: if you do not give up what remains of interest, ﴿then be informed﴾ (fa-'dhanu). Asim, Hamzah, and the narration of Abu Bakr from Asim, read ﴿fa-'adhanu﴾ with a madd, on the pattern of "amanu." The rest read ﴿fa-'dhanu﴾ shortened, with the dhal fatha, which is the reading of Ali and the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Whoever reads it shortened, its meaning is: "Know, you and hear." It is said: "adhina al-shay'a ya'dhanu adhanan wa adhanatan" when he hears it and knows it. Allah said: ﴿And it listened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ (Surah Al-Inshiqaq: 2). Whoever reads it with madd, its meaning is: "Inform others." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said: We have informed You that none of us is a witness﴾ (Surah Fussilat: 47).

The root of the word is from "udhun" (ear), i.e., "make them hear it" (aqʻuhu fi al-adhan), that is, announce it.

﴿War from Allah and His Messenger.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said: "Do not eat interest; take your weapon for war." Al-Walibi narrated from him: Whoever persists in interest and does not desist from it, it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims to ask him to repent; if he desists, well and good, otherwise his neck is struck.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The war of Allah is the Fire, and the war of His Messenger is the sword. ﴿But if you repent, then you have your capital, neither wronging nor being wronged﴾: you do not wrong by seeking increase, nor are you wronged by a decrease below the capital. Aban and al-Mufaddal narrated from Asim with a damma on the first taa' and a fatha on the second. The scholars of meanings said: this is the condition of repentance, for if they do not repent they disbelieve by rejecting the judgment of Allah and making lawful what Allah has forbidden, and their wealth becomes spoils (fay') for the Muslims.

When these verses were revealed, the Banu Amr ibn Umayr [said] to the Banu al-Mughirah: "Rather, we repent to Allah, for we have no power to fight the war of Allah and His Messenger." So they accepted the capital and submitted to the command of Allah. But the Banu al-Mughirah complained of hardship and said: "Delay us until we gather the harvests." They refused to delay, so Allah revealed:

﴿And if there is one in hardship﴾: the statement has the noun of "kana" as its subject without a predicate, which is permissible with an indefinite noun. The Arabs say: "If there is a righteous man, honor him." It is also said: "kana" here indicates the occurrence of the event, and then it needs no predicate.

Ubayy, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas read: ﴿in kana dha 'usratin﴾ with the noun of the debtor or the one owed understood as "in al-gharim aw al-matlub dha 'usratin." Aban ibn Uthman read: ﴿wa man kana dha 'usratin﴾ for this produce. Al-A'mash read: ﴿wa in kana mu'sir﴾, which is evidence for the common reading.

"Al-usrah" means poverty, constraint and hardship. Abu Ja'far read ﴿'usrun﴾ with a damma on the sin; both are dialects.

﴿Then let there be postponement﴾: this is a command in the form of a statement, and the fa' in it answers the conditional; its implied meaning is: "then for him is postponement," that is, he said:

It is obligatory to respect him, with nasb in the sense of "then let him wait with patience," which would be correct, like His saying ﴿so strike the necks﴾. "Nazirah" means granting respite.

Abu Raja', al-Hasan and Qatadah read ﴿fa-nazirah﴾ with kasrah on the dad and raf' on the ra' and ha', meaning "waiting." Ata' ibn Abi Rabah read ﴿fa-nazrah﴾ with the zay sakin; it is a verbal noun which may be from "nazar" (seeing) or "intizar" (waiting), both.

﴿To a time of ease.﴾ Ata', Shaybah, Nafi' and Humayd ibn Muhays read: ﴿maysurah﴾ with damma on the sin and tanwin.

Umar, Ali, Abu Raja', al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Muslim, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Asim, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Abu Amr, Ya'qub and Ayyub read: ﴿maysarah﴾ with tanwin and fatha on the sin. This is the preference of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim, because it is the prevailing dialect. Mujahid and Abu Sarra al-Hudhali read: ﴿maysurihi﴾ with damma on the sin in construct form with a pronoun. Zayd narrated from Ya'qub. Al-A'mash narrated from Asim, from Zirr, from Abdullah that he used to read it: "fa-nazirawhu ila maysurah." All of these are dialects with the meaning of ease, wealth and abundance.

﴿But that you give it as charity [remit your capitals] to the debtor in hardship is better for you, if you knew.﴾ Asim read: ﴿tasaddaqu﴾ with the sad lightened; the rest read it with the sad doubled.

**Mention of the ruling of the verse**

Allah the Exalted commanded granting respite to the one in hardship. Whenever a man becomes poor and his poverty is clear, the owner of property has no way to demand his money until his wealth appears. When his wealth appears, it becomes obligatory on him to deliver the right to the owner of property, and he knows that rights [are due]. Every right that falls on a person as a substitute for property that came into his hand, such as a loan or the purchase of goods, if he claims poverty he must prove his poverty, because the original state of such a person is wealth by the acquisition of what came into his hand. And every right that falls on him without property coming into his hand, such as dower or guarantee, if he claims poverty, the owner of property must prove that he is wealthy, because the original state of people is poverty. If no state of wealth is known for him, the ruling is to remain on the original state until his wealth becomes clear.

Al-Hasan said: If he says, "I am destitute," his word is accepted with his oath, and it is incumbent on him to make his property apparent by evidence or by inspection.

Abu Hanifah held that he should be imprisoned for two or three months, then inquiry should be made about him in secret; if it becomes clear that he is poor, he is released.

The evidence of those who say he should not be imprisoned:

The hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: A man suffered losses in fruits and his debt increased, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Take what you find; you have nothing but that."

Abu Hurayrah was in charge of the judiciary of Madinah, and a man came to him with a debtor and said: "I want you to imprison him."

He said: "Do you know of any property of his that we can take from him and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Do you know of any origin of wealth that we can sell and give to you?"

He said: "No." He said: "Then what do you want?" He said: "I want you to imprison him." He said: "But I will leave him to seek for you and for himself and his dependents; when he becomes wealthy, he will be obliged to pay the debt."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever walks to his creditor with his right, the creatures of the earth and the fish of the water will bless him, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for every step a tree planted for him in Paradise and a sin forgiven him. But if he does not do so and delays, then he is a transgressor."

Abu al-Zinad al-A'raj narrated from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Delay by the wealthy is injustice. When one of you is referred to a wealthy person, let him follow."

Zayd ibn Aslam narrated from Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever grants respite to one in hardship, or remits for him, Allah will shade him in the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade but His shade."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 1 of 2)

﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt...﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: When Allah prohibited riba (usury), He permitted salam (advance sale), and so He said:

﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt...﴾ That is, when some of you deal in debt with one another. Al-dayn (debt) is that which is deferred, and al-'ayn is that which is present. It is said: "Dana fulanan yadinuhu" when he gives him a debt; so the one who gives is called "dā'in" (creditor), and the one who receives is "mudayan" and "madyun" (debtor). His saying ﴿when you contract a debt﴾ includes debt, credit sales, salam, and whatever rights are deferred.

He said "with a debt" (bi-dayn), and mudayana (dealing in debt) can only be with a debt, because mudayana may [be] [[The word is not legible in the manuscript; the apparent reading is what we have established.]] a reciprocal recompense, and may be a mutual exchange; so He made this clear and restricted it by His saying "with a debt."

It has also been said that it is in the sense of emphasis, like His saying: ﴿nor any bird that flies with its two wings﴾ [[Surah al-An'am: 38.]] and His saying: ﴿so the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ [[Surah al-Hijr: 30.]].

﴿for a specified term﴾ That is, a known time. ﴿then write it down﴾ That is, write down that which you have contracted, whether a sale or a loan, so that there is no denial, no forgetting, and no disputing in it.

They differed regarding this writing: is it obligatory or not? Some of them said: it is an obligatory duty. Ibn Jurayj said: "Whoever incurs a debt, let him write; and whoever sells, let him call witnesses." This is the view chosen by Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, and what supports it is what al-Sha'bi narrated from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Three persons supplicate Allah and are not answered: a man whose wife has a bad character and he does not divorce her; a man who had a debt and did not call witnesses; and a man who gave his property to a foolish person." And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And do not give to the foolish your property﴾ [[al-Mustadrak: 2/302.]].

Others said: it is a command of recommendation and option; if he writes, it is good, and if he leaves it, there is no harm. Like His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 2.]], and His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [[Surah al-Jumu'ah: 10.]]. This is the view chosen by al-Farra'.

Others said: the writing of the debt, the calling of witnesses, and the pledge were obligatory, then this was abrogated (naskh) by His saying: ﴿But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted fulfill his trust﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 283.]]. This is the view of al-Sha'bi.

Then He explained the manner of writing, so He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿and let a scribe write between you justly﴾. Al-Hasan read ﴿wal-yaktib﴾ with a kasra on the lam, and this lam is the lam of command, which is used only with the third person absent. When it stands alone, there is only the vowel; but when a waw, fa' or thumma precedes it, most of the Arabs make it sukun for lightness, while some of them keep the kasra according to the original form.

The meaning of the verse: ﴿and let the scribe write the debt document between the seller and the buyer, the creditor and the debtor﴾. ﴿a scribe with justice﴾ That is, with truth and equity, so that he adds nothing to it, nor reduces anything from it, nor advances the term or delays it, nor writes anything that nullifies a right of either of them that he himself does not know.

﴿And let not the scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him, so let him write﴾. This was because scribes were few at the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The scholars differed concerning the obligation upon the scribe to write and upon the witness to testify. Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: it is obligatory upon the scribe to write, since he has been commanded. Al-Hasan said: this applies in the situation where no other scribe can be found, so that the creditor would be harmed if he refused; in that case it is an obligation, but if another scribe is available, he is in latitude when another takes it up.

Al-Dahhak said: this was a binding obligation upon the scribe and the witness, then His saying abrogated it: ﴿Let neither scribe nor witness be harmed﴾. Al-Suddi said: it is obligatory upon him when he is free.

﴿And let the one upon whom the truth is due dictate﴾. The debtor, the one who owes, acknowledges with his tongue what is upon him, so that he knows what he owes. Al-Imla' and al-Imla (both forms) are two eloquent dialects, and the Qur'an came with both.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And it is dictated to him morning and evening﴾ [[Surah al-Furqan: 5.]].

The root of al-imlal is repeating a thing time after time and insisting upon it. The poet said:

"Alla ya diyara al-hayyi bi-al-Sab'an... amilla 'alayha bi-al-bila al-malawan" [[al-Sihah: 3/1227.]]

Then He warned him, saying: ﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it﴾. That is, he should not reduce anything of the right that is upon him. It is said: "bakhasahu haqqahu" and "bakhasahu" when he diminished it; and similar expressions in the Qur'an are numerous.

﴿But if the one upon whom the truth is due is foolish﴾. That is, if the debtor who owes the money is foolish, ﴿or weak﴾, that is, an old man, ﴿or unable to dictate himself﴾. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: that is, incapable, a fool. Mujahid said: ignorant regarding property; al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: a small child; ﴿or unable to dictate himself﴾ due to muteness, or inarticulateness, or absence, or non-Arabic speech, or infirmity, or imprisonment, which prevents him from attending the document, or ignorance of what he owes him. ﴿then let his guardian dictate﴾, that is, his trustee and his heir.

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Rabi' and Muqatil said: that is, let the guardian of the right and the creditor dictate, because he knows his own debt best. ﴿with justice﴾, with truth, equity and fairness. ﴿And call to witness﴾: this "sin" is for request and demand. ﴿two witnesses﴾

﴿from among your men﴾. That is, free adult males, not slaves, not children, and not non-Muslim free persons. This is the position of Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifah, Sufyan and most jurists.

Shurayh and Ibn Sirin allowed the testimony of a slave, and this is the view of Anas ibn Malik. Some allowed their testimony in trivial matters.

﴿And if there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾. That is, if the two witnesses are not two men, then a man and two women, or let a man and two women testify.

The jurists agreed that the testimony of women alongside men is permissible in property matters, and they differed regarding matters other than property. Malik, al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Abu 'Ubayd, Abu Thawr and Ahmad did not permit it except in property. Abu Hanifah, Sufyan and their companions permitted the testimony of two women with a man in everything except hudud and qisas.

﴿of those whom you accept as witnesses﴾. That is, those who are acceptable in their religion, trustworthiness and competence.

'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Whoever shows us good, we think good of him and respond to him accordingly; and whoever shows us evil, we think evil of him and dislike him for it. And when a man is praised by his neighbour, his relatives and his companion, then do not doubt his righteousness.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "Just" (al-'adl) is one in whom no suspicion has appeared. al-Sha'bi said: "Just" is one about whom no fault has been raised concerning his stomach or his private parts.

al-Hasan said: it is one whose disgrace is not known.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The testimony of a treacherous man or a treacherous woman is not permitted, nor of one punished with a hadd, nor of one with a grudge against his brother, nor of one known to give false testimony, nor of a dependent (servant) in the household — meaning a servant to them — [nor of one suspected in clientage or kinship]." [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/15, no. 17747.]]

The summary concerning whose testimony is accepted: ten qualities must be combined in him: he must be free, adult, Muslim, just, knowledgeable of what he testifies to, he must not gain by his testimony any benefit to himself, nor avert from himself any harm, he must not be known for frequent error, he must not abandon manliness (muruwwah), he must not have softness [nor] his slave testify against him. When these qualities are combined in him, his word is accepted and his testimony permitted.

The testimony of women alone, without a man with them, is accepted in four situations: defects of women, which is what is a defect in a place that is their private part — in a free woman, her entire body except her face and palms, and for a slave woman, what is between her navel and her knees; and in breastfeeding, in childbirth, and in the crying out of a newborn (istihlal).

There is no disagreement about all of this except regarding breastfeeding. Abu Hanifah held that the testimony of women alone is not accepted in it until two men or one man and two women testify.

As for the manner of testimony: Tawus narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about testimony, and he said: "Do you see the sun?" He said: Yes. He said: "Upon the like of it, testify or leave it."
[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/23, no. 17782.]]

And from 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Honour the witnesses, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic brings forth rights through them and repels injustice through them" [208] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/12, no. 17733.]].

Kharijah ibn Nur, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ubayd, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever withholds the mention of a right after the document has been handed over for three [days], upon him is a qirat of sin" [209].

﴿that if one of them errs, the other may remind her﴾. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read ﴿in﴾ with a kasra on the alif, with ﴿fa-tudhakkiru﴾ in the nominative, and its meaning is conditional and inceptive; the place of ﴿tadilla﴾ is jussive for the conditional, except that it is not apparent in the doubled form; ﴿fa-tudhakkira﴾ is nominative because what follows the conditional fa' is a subject (mubtada').

The reading of the majority is with a fatha on the alif, the fa' being connected to the preceding statement, and the place of ﴿an﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, meaning "because"; ﴿tadilla﴾ in its place is accusative by ﴿an﴾, and ﴿fa-tudhakkira﴾ is subordinated to it. The meaning of the verse: "then a man and two women, so that one of them may remind the other if she errs."

This is from the inverted order (muqaddam wa-mu'akhkhar), like your saying: "It pleases me that he asks and is given," meaning: it pleases me that you give the asker when he asks, because the giving is what is pleasing, not the asking. Allah said: ﴿And had it not been that a misfortune should afflict them for what their hands have sent forth, and they should say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger..."﴾ [[Surah al-Qasas: 47.]], and so on.

Its meaning: "Had it not been that they would say, when a misfortune afflicts them: Why did You not send us a messenger?"

As for His saying ﴿an tadilla﴾: that is, forget, like His saying: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [[Surah Ta-Ha: 52.]], and His saying: ﴿He said, "I did it then, and I was of those who err"﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 20.]], and ﴿the misguidance was justified upon him, so travel﴾ [[Surah al-Nahl: 36.]], and the Arab saying "the water has strayed into the milk," and Allah said: ﴿And they say, "When we are lost in the earth..."﴾ [[Surah al-Sajdah: 10.]]. Asim al-Jahdari read ﴿an tudilla ahaduhuma﴾ with a damma on the taa' and a fatha on the daad, in the passive. Zayd ibn Aslam read ﴿fa-tudhakkira﴾ from al-mudhakara (mutual remembering).

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub, Abu Hatim and Qutaybah read ﴿fa-tudhakkira﴾ with the light form, and the rest read it with doubling.

"Dhakkara" and "adhkara" have the same meaning, as one says "nazzala" and "anzala," "karrama" and "akrama." Both carry the sense of remembering, which is the opposite of forgetting. A poet said:

"Tudhakkiruniyhi al-shamsu 'inda tuluu'iha... wa-ta'riḍu dhikraha idha gharabuha afal" [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 14/118.]]

Abu 'Ubayd said: I was told from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah that he said: it is from the root "dhikr" (remembrance), meaning that when she testifies with another, their testimony becomes like the testimony of a man. I say: this view does not please me, because it is coordinated with forgetting, and Allah knows best.

﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾. Some said: this concerns the bearing of testimony, and it is a command of obligation.

Qatadah and al-Rabi' said: a man would go around a large tribe in which there were people, calling them to testify, and none of them would follow him, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Al-Sha'bi said: he has the choice in bearing testimony when he finds another; if he wishes he testifies, and if he wishes he does not testify; but if no one else is found and he refrains, then he has neglected what was obligatory upon him. Others said: this is a command of recommendation, and he has the choice in all circumstances: if he wishes he testifies, and if he wishes he does not. This is the view of 'Ata' and 'Atiyyah.

Abu Bahriyyah said: I said to al-Hasan: I am called to testify, and I am averse. He said: Then do not be obligated; do not testify if you wish. Mughirah said: I said to Ibrahim: I am called to testify, and I fear I will forget. He said: Then do not testify, if you love.

Others said: this is about the establishment and delivery of testimony, and the meaning of the verse: ﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾ for the establishment of testimony, if they had testified before that. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. Sufyan narrated from Jabir, from 'Amir, who said: the witness has the choice as long as he has not testified. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: this verse applies to both matters, bearing and establishing, when he is free.

﴿And do not be weary﴾, that is, do not become bored. It is said: "sa'imtu asam sa'aman wa-sa'amatan." Zuhayr said:

"Sa'imtu takalif al-hayati wa-man ya'ish... thamanina hawlan la aba laka yas'am"

And Labid said:

"Wa-laqad sa'imtu min al-hayati wa-tuluha... wa-su'al hadha al-nasi kayfa Labid"

And "an" is in the accusative position in two respects: if you wish, make it with the verb a verbal noun and let the weariness fall upon it, its estimate being: "and do not be weary of writing it"; and if you wish, make it accusative by removing the prepositions, its estimate being: "and do not be weary of writing it." The pronoun refers to the right.

Al-Sulami read ﴿wa-la yas'amu﴾ with a ya'.

﴿small﴾, that is, the right; ﴿or large﴾, that is, little or much of property. The accusative of "small" and "large" is in two respects: one, as a circumstantial accusative (hal) and a qata' from the pronoun; the second, that you make it the predicate of "kana" with a suppressed subject, meaning:

"And do not be weary of writing it, whether small, the right, or large, up to its term," to the place of the right.

﴿That is⟩, the document, ﴿more just⟩, more equitable, ﴿in the sight of Allah⟩, because He commanded it, and following His command is more just than abandoning it; ﴿and more upright⟩, more correct, ﴿for testimony⟩; ﴿and more likely⟩, more appropriate and nearer ﴿to avoid doubt⟩, that you doubt about the testimony, the amount of the right and the term when it is written, similar to His saying: ﴿That is nearer that they will bring the testimony in its proper form﴾ [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 107.]], and it is the superlative from "nearness."

Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿except that it be a present trade...﴾. 'Asim read it with the accusative as the predicate of "kana," with the subject suppressed, its estimate: "except that the trade be a trade, and the exchange a trade." al-Farra' recited:

"Li-llahi qawmi ayya qawmi bahratin... idha kana yawman dha kawakiba ashna'a" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 3/180.]]

meaning: "when the day was a day." He also recited:

"A'ayyaya hal tabkiyani 'afaqan... idha kana tana'an baynahum wa-'inaqan" [[Jami' al-Bayan: 3/179.]]

meaning: "when the matter was."

The rest read it in the nominative in two ways: one, that "kana" means "to occur," meaning: "except that a trade occurs," and then it has no predicate. The second, that the subject is placed in the trade and the predicate in the verb, which is His saying: ﴿you conduct it among yourselves﴾, its estimate: "except that there be a present trade, circulating among you." The meaning of the verse: ﴿except that it be a present trade, which you conduct among yourselves hand to hand﴾, having no deferment or credit in it.

﴿Then there is no blame upon you that you do not write it﴾, meaning the trade. ﴿And call witnesses when you engage in trade.﴾ al-Dahhak said: this is a command from Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and calling witnesses is obligatory for small and large rights, whether cash or credit, even for a bunch of herbs; this is the view chosen by Muhammad ibn Jarir.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: the matter in it is left to trustworthiness. Allah said: ﴿But if one of you trusts another...﴾. Others said: it is a command of recommendation: if he wishes he calls witnesses, and if he does not wish, he does not.

Then He said: ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed.﴾ This is a prohibition in the third person absent, its original form being "yudarrir," so the first ra' was assimilated into the second ra' and vocalized with a fatha, for the doubling, because of the meeting of two sukuns; the fatha is the lightest of the vowels, so it was moved to it.

As for the explanation of the verse, some took it according to the active verb and said: its original form is "yudarir" with a kasra on the ra', and they made the doer the scribe and the witness, meaning: "let no scribe be harmed," so that he writes what was not dictated to him, adding or reducing or distorting; "nor a witness," so that he testifies to what he did not witness or refuses to establish testimony. This is the view of Tawus, al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd. Others took it according to the passive verb and made the scribe and the witness the objects, saying: its original form is "la yudarra."

The meaning of the verse: a man calls upon the scribe or the witness while they are engaged in an important need, and they say: "We are occupied, seek others." The one who calls them says: "Allah commanded you both to respond in writing and testimony," and he insists upon them and distracts them from their need. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic forbade [harming them] and commanded that others be sought.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And let not a scribe refuse to write it down as Allah has taught him, so let him write﴾ and ﴿let not the witnesses refuse when they are called﴾, one of the two parties would come to the scribe and say to him: "Write for me." He would say: "I am busy, or I have a need," and he would go off to someone else. So the first would cling to him and say: "You have been commanded to write," and he would not leave him alone, harming him thereby while he could find someone else. The same would be done with the witness. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾.

The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of ʿUmar, Ubayy, Ibn Masʿud and Mujahid: "wa-la yudarir katibun wa-la shahidun," with the doubling shown by spelling it out, on the pattern of "mā lam yamnaʿ" (wa-la yuḍārra), i.e. ﴿let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾.

Abu Jaʿfar read: "wa-la yuḍār," jussive and lightened, dropping one of the rāʾ entirely. Al-Hasan read "wa-la yuḍārri" with a kasra on the rāʾ and shaddah.

﴿And if you do it﴾, i.e. what I have forbidden you of harming, ﴿then it is indeed a transgression (fusuq) in you﴾, meaning a departure from the command. ﴿And fear Allah; Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knower of all things.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 2, verse 283–286 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Abu al-'Aliyah and Mujahid read kitaban (a written document), and they said: "Sometimes a scribe may be found but not the ink or the page." They also said: "There was no tribe among the Arabs without a scribe among them, but they were unable to obtain the pen and inkwell."

Al-Dahhak read kuttaban, the plural of katib (scribe). The rest read katiban in the singular, which is more fitting with the Mushaf.

﴿fa-rihanun maqbudah﴾ (then pledges taken in hand). Ibn 'Abbas, Ibrahim, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read furuhun with a ḍammah on the rā’ and the hā’. 'Ikrimah, al-Minhal and 'Abd al-Warith read furuhn with a ḍammah on the rā’ and a sukun on the hā’. The rest read farihanun, which is the plural of rahn (pledge). This pattern is like fa'l and fi'al (as in ḥabl and ḥibāl, kabsh and kibāsh, and ka'b and ka''ab).
